cards.answer: Huguenots were Protestant like England's political class and brought silk-weaving skills needed to compete with French and Dutch textiles.

cards.front: How did the Ulster Plantation lead to long-term sectarian division?
cards.answer: Catholic Irish were pushed onto poorer land, sparking the 1641 rising and Cromwell's 1649-50 reconquest, leaving Ulster with a Protestant majority.

cards.front: Name the three main types of physical promotion described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Appearances – launch parties, TV and interviews / Performances – gigs, tours and festivals / Materials – posters, billboards and flyers
items: Appearances – launch parties, TV and interviews

cards.front: Name the four media products artists can release, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Single / EP / Album / Music video

cards.front: Why does strong branding make an artist instantly recognisable?
cards.answer: It creates a consistent visual identity through logos, colour schemes and typography used across all their releases.

cards.front: Why does physical distribution require significant upfront investment?
cards.answer: It involves manufacturing, such as pressing vinyl or printing CDs, then shipping products to retailers before they can be sold.

cards.front: Name the five physical conditions the lesson gives that push UK rivers towards flooding.
cards.answer: Heavy or prolonged rainfall / Saturated soil / Steep upland slopes / Impermeable rocks / Sparse vegetation cover

cards.front: Name the four human land-use changes the lesson gives that increase flood risk.
cards.answer: Building on a floodplain / Drains moving water to rivers fast / Deforestation in upland catchments / Ploughing fields up and down slopes
items: Drains moving water to rivers fast
Ploughing fields up and down slopes

cards.front: Why does building on a floodplain increase flood risk?
cards.answer: It replaces grass and soil with roofs, roads and concrete, so a city centre rejects 70–90% of rainfall as overland flow that drains reach quickly.

cards.front: Why do UK rivers show higher discharge in winter than in summer?
cards.answer: Low evaporation and saturated soils in winter mean even moderate rain causes high discharge, while summer plants intercept and transpire more water leaving spare soil capacity.

cards.front: Name the four targets of Austen's social satire in Pride and Prejudice.
cards.answer: The marriage market / Class snobbery / Female dependence / The gap between manners and morality
items: The gap between manners and morality

cards.front: Besides Darcy's letter, name the three other letters the lesson says advance the plot.
cards.answer: Mr Collins's letter reveals his character before he appears / Jane's letters express her heartbreak with restraint / Mrs Gardiner's letter reveals Darcy's secret rescue of Lydia
items: Mr Collins's letter reveals his character before he appears
Jane's letters express her heartbreak with restraint
Mrs Gardiner's letter reveals Darcy's secret rescue of Lydia

cards.front: How does free indirect discourse let Austen expose Mr Collins's foolishness when he explains his reasons for marrying?
cards.answer: It lets the reader hear both his pompous self-justification and the narrator's amusement at it, without the narrator directly commenting.

cards.front: Why is Austen's satire through understatement more effective than satire through anger?
cards.answer: Her narrator seems amused rather than outraged, which invites the reader to feel superior to the targets, making the criticism sharper.

title: The Nature of Reality and Cosmology
subject: religious-studies-ocr

cards.front: Name the four yugas that make up a Mahayuga, in order of decreasing spiritual quality.
cards.answer: Satya Yuga / Treta Yuga / Dwapara Yuga / Kali Yuga

cards.front: Name the three heavenly realms of the Trimurti described in Hindu cosmology.
cards.answer: Brahma-Loka / Shiva-Loka / Vishnu-Loka (Vaikuntha)

cards.front: Why does confusing purusha with prakriti lead to spiritual bondage in Samkhya thought?
cards.answer: Because consciousness mistakenly identifies with the material processes of body and mind, becoming caught up in samsara.

cards.front: Why is birth in the human realm considered rare and valuable in Hindu cosmology?
cards.answer: Because it is one of the few realms from which liberation (moksha) can be achieved directly.

cards.front: Why does the boys' democratic assembly on the island matter for Golding's message?
cards.answer: It mirrors adult society like Parliament, so its collapse into tribal warfare reflects how civilisations throughout history break down.

cards.front: Why did many writers after WWII question whether humanity was capable of progress?
cards.answer: Because two World Wars, the Holocaust and the atomic bombings showed 'civilised' nations committing industrial-scale atrocities.

cards.front: Name the 6Rs framework used to evaluate textile sustainability.
cards.answer: Reduce / Reuse / Recycle / Rethink / Refuse / Repair

cards.front: List the six features designed into a professional cycling jersey described in the sportswear case study.
cards.answer: Polyester-elastane weft-knit panels / Sublimation printing / Flatlock overlocked seams / Silicone gripper banding at hem / UV-protective finish / Recycled polyester construction

cards.front: Why does batch production have lower unit costs than one-off production but still involve downtime?
cards.answer: Set-up costs are spread across the whole batch, but machinery must be reconfigured between different batches, causing downtime.

cards.front: Why does France's Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) scheme drive circular fashion effectively?
cards.answer: It requires brands to fund collection and recycling infrastructure, internalising costs previously pushed onto society and the environment.

title: Enforcing law and order: medieval to early modern
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Why did the Anglo-Saxon tithing system give men an incentive to police their neighbours?
cards.answer: Because if a member committed a crime and could not be produced, the whole tithing was collectively fined.

cards.front: Why did the end of trial by ordeal in 1215 lead to jury trial?
cards.answer: Without the Church's support for ordeal, guilt had to be decided another way, so twelve local men judged cases using knowledge of the accused and circumstances.

cards.front: Name the four non-hormonal contraceptive methods given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Condoms / Diaphragms / Copper IUDs / Surgical sterilisation

cards.front: Name the three functions of healthy kidneys stated in the lesson.
cards.answer: Filter blood and remove waste / Maintain ion balance / Regulate water content

cards.front: How does dialysis remove waste products from the blood?
cards.answer: Blood flows through a membrane into dialysate solution and waste products like urea move across by diffusion.

cards.front: Why is a liver transplant sometimes possible using a living donor, unlike most other organ transplants?
cards.answer: Because the liver can partially regenerate, so a living donor can donate just a segment of it.

title: Salvation, Eschatology and the Problem of Evil
subject: religious-studies-b-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three divergent views Christians hold about the nature of hell.
cards.answer: Eternal conscious punishment / Final ending of the unrepentant / Ultimate reconciliation of all people to God
items: Ultimate reconciliation of all people to God

cards.front: Name the three types of response Christians give to the problem of evil.
cards.answer: Biblical / Theoretical / Practical

cards.front: Why do critics say the free will defence fails to fully solve the problem of evil?
cards.answer: It explains moral suffering caused by human choice, but not natural suffering, which is not caused by human choice at all.

cards.front: Why do Christians believe the atonement is necessary for salvation?
cards.answer: Because without Christ's atoning death, sin would remain an unbridgeable barrier between people and God.

cards.front: How does Mrs Hepworth's praise of Willie's boots help Maggie's case for leaving Hobson's shop?
cards.answer: It proves Willie's talent is objectively valuable, not just useful within Hobson's shop, giving Maggie evidence to act on.

cards.front: Why do Alice and Vickey refuse to care for Hobson in Act 4?
cards.answer: Their genteel, respectable values don't extend to real family loyalty, showing they benefit from Maggie's rebellion without her courage.

cards.front: Name three disadvantages (Nachteile) of technology given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Cyberbullying (Online-Mobbing) / It can be dangerous / You spend too much time online / Unhealthy to sit long at the screen / You can become addicted / Personal data isn't always safe
items: You spend too much time online
Unhealthy to sit long at the screen

cards.front: Name three advantages (Vorteile) of technology given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Stay in contact with friends / Find information quickly / It is fun / Download music / Practical and useful / Share videos with friends

cards.front: How does a separable verb like 'herunterladen' work in the present tense in German?
cards.answer: The prefix splits off and goes to the end of the clause, e.g. Ich lade Musik herunter.

cards.front: How is 'zu' placed when using the um...zu construction with a separable verb like 'herunterladen'?
cards.answer: Zu goes between the prefix and the stem, e.g. um Fotos herunterzuladen.

cards.front: According to the lesson, what four factors drove the development of Germ Theory?
cards.answer: Science and technology (better microscopes) / Individuals (Pasteur's curiosity, Koch's method) / Attitudes in society (doctor resistance) / Institutions (government/university funding, rivalry)

cards.front: The lesson says Germ Theory opened the door to which three developments?
cards.answer: Vaccinations / Antiseptic surgery / Antibiotics

cards.front: Why did Germ Theory face opposition even after Pasteur published his findings?
cards.answer: Doctors dismissed Pasteur as a chemist not a physician, and critics said he'd only proved germs caused decay, not disease.

cards.front: How did Germ Theory support the argument for the Public Health Act of 1875?
cards.answer: If germs in dirty water and sewage caused disease, governments had a responsibility to provide clean water and sanitation.

title: The King's Great Matter and Wolsey's Fall
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three historians (and their views) the lesson gives on why Wolsey fell.
cards.answer: John Guy: failure of the annulment was the sufficient cause / Eric Ives: Anne Boleyn poisoned Henry against him / C.S.L. Davies: predictable end of one-minister system
items: John Guy: failure of the annulment was the sufficient cause
Eric Ives: Anne Boleyn poisoned Henry against him
C.S.L. Davies: predictable end of one-minister system

cards.front: Name the four overlapping pressures the lesson says led to the eventual break with Rome.
cards.answer: The succession crisis / Henry's claim to royal supremacy / Fiscal opportunity from church wealth / An evangelical current led by Cranmer and Cromwell
items: An evangelical current led by Cranmer and Cromwell

cards.front: Why did Henry believe it was dangerous for England to be left with only a female heir?
cards.answer: England had never had a settled ruling queen, and the closest precedent, Empress Matilda, produced years of civil war.

cards.front: How did the Boleyn faction help bring about Wolsey's downfall?
cards.answer: Thomas Boleyn and the Duke of Norfolk resented Wolsey's monopoly of patronage and blamed him for failing to deliver the annulment quickly.

cards.front: Why can't a solid ionic compound be electrolysed?
cards.answer: Its ions are held in fixed positions in the lattice and cannot move to carry the current.

cards.front: Why does electrolysis of aqueous copper sulfate produce oxygen rather than chlorine at the anode?
cards.answer: No concentrated halide ions are present, so hydroxide ions are oxidised instead, releasing oxygen gas.

cards.front: Why does extracting aluminium by electrolysis cost a lot of money?
cards.answer: Melting aluminium oxide needs huge amounts of energy and the carbon anodes burn away and must be replaced.

title: Jazz and Blues Ensembles: Roles, Riffs and Improvisation
subject: music-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four rhythm section roles the lesson describes for drums, bass, piano and guitar.
cards.answer: Drums keep swung pulse and add fills / Bass plays walking bass outlining changes / Piano/guitar comp with syncopated chord stabs / All three react to soloist and shape dynamics
items: Drums keep swung pulse and add fills
Bass plays walking bass outlining changes
Piano/guitar comp with syncopated chord stabs
All three react to soloist and shape dynamics

cards.front: How does a walking bass line create swing-style momentum?
cards.answer: It moves in a smooth, mostly stepwise sequence of quarter notes, one per beat, outlining the chord changes and driving the music forward.

cards.front: Why can musicians from different backgrounds improvise together confidently over a 12-bar blues?
cards.answer: Because every musician knows the shared 12-bar chord pattern by ear, allowing the band to play together spontaneously without written parts.

cards.front: How does swing feel differ from straight classical rhythm?
cards.answer: Swing feel plays quaver pairs unevenly, long-short, combined with syncopation, giving forward-leaning energy unlike evenly-divided classical rhythms.

title: Staging and Design: The Garden, the Bulbs and the Lifts
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: Name the two halves the stage was split into by Geoff Cobham's design.
cards.answer: Downstage slippery black floor / Upstage garden with real water pool
items: Upstage garden with real water pool

cards.front: Why was the stage floor built slippery and black downstage?
cards.answer: It was built for sliding furniture and for Frantic Assembly's physical sequences.

cards.front: Why is Pip lit in a tight, isolated lighting state during her autumn announcement?
cards.answer: A narrow warm wash holds her alone against the tree so the audience reads instantly that she is apart from the family.

cards.front: Why did the creative team keep the play's Australian working-class setting when it was remade for a British cast?
cards.answer: They judged the social class, not the Australian setting, was the essential thing to preserve, so nothing was reset.

cards.front: Name the 5 steps in the 5-Minute Planning Template for the anthology comparison question.
cards.answer: Write a one-sentence thesis / Point 1: language feature per poem / Point 2: form/structure per poem / Point 3: context point per poem / Write out chosen poem quotations from memory
items: Write out chosen poem quotations from memory

cards.front: Name the 4 poems suggested as a thematic pairing for 'Social criticism' and 'Displacement' combined.
cards.answer: London / Nothing's Changed / Presents from my Aunts in Pakistan / Hurricane Hits England
items: Presents from my Aunts in Pakistan

cards.front: Why should you learn short quotations of 3-6 words rather than long passages?
cards.answer: Short quotations are easier to memorise accurately and can be embedded smoothly into analytical sentences, showing precise selection.

cards.front: Why does a slightly misquoted word matter in the exam?
cards.answer: Because it can undermine your credibility, so accuracy in quotations is important.

cards.front: Name the four stages of energy flow in a food chain, from producer onward.
cards.answer: Producer / Primary consumer / Secondary consumer / Tertiary consumer

cards.front: Name the four human activities the lesson says are reducing biodiversity worldwide.
cards.answer: Deforestation / Pollution / Global warming / Overexploitation

cards.front: Why does removing one species from a food chain affect all the other organisms in it?
cards.answer: Because organisms in a community are interdependent, relying on each other for food and resources, so losing one disrupts the rest.

cards.front: How does global warming reduce biodiversity?
cards.answer: Rising temperatures alter habitats, causing species to migrate or become extinct.

title: Rhythms of the World: Eastern Mediterranean and Middle Eastern Folk Music
subject: music-ocr

cards.front: Name the three connected folk music traditions this lesson focuses on.
cards.answer: Greek folk music / Palestinian folk music / Israeli folk music

cards.front: Name the three instruments described in the Instruments section (oud, darbuka, riq).
cards.answer: Oud / Darbuka / Riq

cards.front: Why is the oud well suited to playing maqam melodies?
cards.answer: Its lack of frets lets performers slide smoothly between pitches, essential for playing maqam's microtonal inflections.

cards.front: Why does dabke dancing create a rhythmic texture of its own?
cards.answer: The dancers' stamping locks together so tightly it functions almost like a percussion ensemble made of feet.

cards.front: What three steps does the lesson recommend for correctly identifying the fulcrum, load and effort in a lever?
cards.answer: Identify the joint first (this is always the fulcrum) / Identify what is being moved (the load) / Identify where the muscle pulls (the effort)
items: Identify the joint first (this is always the fulcrum)
Identify what is being moved (the load)
Identify where the muscle pulls (the effort)

cards.front: What three things should a good exam answer on mechanical advantage include?
cards.answer: State whether the effort arm or load arm is longer / Say whether this gives MA greater or less than 1 / Explain what that means for force or speed
items: State whether the effort arm or load arm is longer
Say whether this gives MA greater or less than 1
Explain what that means for force or speed

cards.front: Why does a bicep curl need more muscular effort than the load it is lifting?
cards.answer: The effort arm is shorter than the load arm, giving a mechanical advantage less than 1, so more effort is needed.

cards.front: Why can the calf muscles lift the whole body weight during a calf raise with relatively little effort?
cards.answer: The effort arm is longer than the load arm, giving a mechanical advantage greater than 1, so effort is amplified into greater force.

cards.front: What are the 4 things the lesson says top-band analysis needs?
cards.answer: Choosing unexpected or subtle features / Explaining connotations and effects / Showing how language and structure work together / Offering a personal response beyond generic statements
items: Choosing unexpected or subtle features, not just obvious ones
Explaining connotations and effects, not just naming techniques
Showing how language and structure work together
Offering a personal response beyond generic statements

cards.front: What are the 3 stages of the default Part (ii) comparison structure?
cards.answer: Paragraphs 1-2: compare a technique from each poem / Paragraph 3: compare structure / Paragraph 4: compare tone or the endings
items: Paragraphs 1-2: compare a technique from each poem
Paragraph 4: compare tone or the endings

cards.front: Why does the lesson say three deep paragraphs beat five shallow ones in Part (i)?
cards.answer: Depth of analysis scores higher marks than feature-spotting, which just names techniques without explaining their effect.

cards.front: Why is tone always analysable even if you don't fully understand a poem's meaning?
cards.answer: You can identify the speaker's emotion (happy, sad, angry etc.) and the words or images creating it without needing full meaning.

cards.front: Name the three processes the lesson gives that Earth has but the Moon lacks, which destroy impact craters.
cards.answer: Active weathering and erosion by water and wind / Plate tectonics (subduction and mountain building) / Abundant vegetation covering topography
items: Active weathering and erosion by water and wind

cards.front: Why do the lunar highlands have more craters than the maria?
cards.answer: The maria formed later from volcanic eruptions (about 3.9-3.0 billion years ago) which resurfaced the area, burying older craters.

cards.front: How can an ancient impact crater on Earth become a valuable mineral deposit, as at the Sudbury Basin?
cards.answer: The impact melted and redistributed metal-rich rocks, concentrating them into a nickel-copper ore deposit.

title: The Lunar Disc: Features, Rotation and Libration
subject: astronomy-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three prominent craters that form an observational triangle in the southern highlands.
cards.answer: Tycho / Copernicus / Kepler

cards.front: Name the three causes of libration described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Libration in longitude / Libration in latitude / Diurnal libration

cards.front: Why do the maria appear darker than the terrae?
cards.answer: Because the maria are basaltic lava plains, and basalt reflects less sunlight than the highland rock of the terrae.

cards.front: Why is the far side of the Moon more heavily cratered than the near side?
cards.answer: Its crust is thicker, which prevented the volcanic flooding that created the maria seen on the near side.

cards.front: Name the seven main cybersecurity threats the lesson says you must know.
cards.answer: Malware / Phishing / Social engineering / Brute-force attacks / DoS/DDoS / Data interception / SQL injection

cards.front: Name the three social engineering techniques (other than plain phishing) described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Spear phishing / Pretexting / Baiting

cards.front: How does a Trojan attack work?
cards.answer: It disguises itself as legitimate software to trick users into installing it, then opens a backdoor for the attacker.

cards.front: Why does the principle of least privilege reduce the damage from a compromised account?
cards.answer: It grants users only the permissions needed for their role, limiting what an attacker can access if the account is hacked.

title: Other explorers: Diaz, da Gama, Vespucci and Magellan
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: What two problems did Vasco da Gama face when he tried to trade at Calicut in 1498?
cards.answer: The Zamorin was unimpressed by Portugal's cloth and trinkets / Arab merchants worked to undermine Portuguese trade
items: The Zamorin was unimpressed by Portugal's cloth and trinkets
Arab merchants worked to undermine Portuguese trade

cards.front: Why did Bartolomeu Dias's 1488 voyage matter even though he didn't reach India?
cards.answer: He proved Africa had an end and that a sea route to the Indian Ocean existed, making da Gama's voyage possible.

cards.front: Why did spice prices fall in Europe after da Gama's voyage to India?
cards.answer: Portuguese ships bypassed Arab and Ottoman middlemen, creating a direct sea route to Asian spices.

cards.front: Why did Magellan's circumnavigation prove the Americas were separate from Asia?
cards.answer: By sailing right around the globe via a long Pacific crossing, the voyage showed the Americas were not part of Asia.

cards.front: Name the three functions castles served for the Normans, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Housed garrisons to suppress rebellion / Provided bases for rapid military response / Demonstrated Norman lords' dominance over locals
items: Provided bases for rapid military response
Demonstrated Norman lords' dominance over locals

cards.front: Why did royal authority collapse during The Anarchy (1135-54)?
cards.answer: Matilda and Stephen each granted concessions to win baronial support, so central authority collapsed and lords acted as local warlords.

cards.front: How did William I use the Harrying of the North to control England?
cards.answer: He launched a scorched-earth campaign destroying settlements and food supplies to crush repeated northern rebellions against Norman rule.

cards.front: What four sensory details make Fezziwig's Christmas ball full of imagery?
cards.answer: Fiddles / Mince pies / Dancing / Shining faces

cards.front: Why is Belle described as Scrooge's moral turning point in the lesson?
cards.answer: Her accusation of a 'golden idol' is the first explicit link between Scrooge's greed and spiritual damnation, giving the Ghost's lesson emotional bite.

cards.front: What does Scrooge's exhaustion and heavy sleep at the end of Stave 2 show about his development?
cards.answer: He has moved from denial to grief, showing the Ghost's reminders have forced him to feel again.

title: Minority Rights: Windrush, Brixton and Beyond, 1948-Present
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: What four things did the 1981 Scarman Report recommend?
cards.answer: Community policing / Better recruitment of Black officers / Scrapping of the sus law / Clearer rules on stop and search
items: Clearer rules on stop and search

cards.front: Name the five factors this lesson traces through minority rights history from Windrush to Black Lives Matter.
cards.answer: Government / Economy / Ideas / Communication / Role of the individual

cards.front: Why did the Windrush scandal happen in 2017-18?
cards.answer: Home Office policies wrongly threatened, detained and sometimes deported British citizens who could not produce paperwork the system now demanded.

cards.front: Why does the lesson argue that modern protest only seems more violent than protest in the past?
cards.answer: Earlier protests like Peterloo and the Newport Rising killed more people, but media saturation now makes every modern confrontation feel immediate and widespread.

cards.front: Name the three theories the lesson says readers construct in the eight chapters before Chapter 9 reveals the truth.
cards.answer: Blackmail / Murder / A secret relative

cards.front: Why did Jekyll's potion fail to create a purely good version of himself?
cards.answer: The transformation only worked one way, releasing evil but never able to isolate or preserve virtue.

cards.front: Why does Hyde kill himself rather than face justice at the end?
cards.answer: To avoid facing the consequences of his crimes, not out of remorse — even his final act is selfish.

title: The Third and Fourth Noble Truths
subject: religious-studies-ocr

cards.front: Name the eight factors of the Noble Eightfold Path.
cards.answer: Right View / Right Intention / Right Speech / Right Action / Right Livelihood / Right Effort / Right Mindfulness / Right Concentration

cards.front: Name the six Perfections (paramitas) a Bodhisattva cultivates in Mahayana Buddhism.
cards.answer: Generosity / Ethics / Patience / Energy / Meditation / Wisdom

cards.front: Why must Sila (ethical conduct) be developed before Samadhi (meditation) can succeed?
cards.answer: Without ethical conduct the mind is agitated by guilt, conflict and harmful consequences, making meditation impossible.

cards.front: How does panna (wisdom) bring about Nibbana?
cards.answer: Panna directly uproots the three poisons of moha, lobha and dosa, producing the Enlightenment that is Nibbana.

cards.front: Name the three castles the Normans used to control London, as given in the lesson.
cards.answer: White Tower / Baynard's Castle / Montfichet's Tower

cards.front: The lesson says the White Tower's vertical layout stacked four functions under one roof. What were they?
cards.answer: Fortress / Palace / Treasury / Prison

cards.front: Why did William choose the south-east corner of London's Roman walls for the White Tower?
cards.answer: The surviving Roman walls protected two sides so builders could work securely, and the site commanded the Thames river route.

cards.front: Why was the White Tower built with such massive scale and stone, rather than a quick timber castle?
cards.answer: It was permanence made of stone, declaring the conquest finished and overawing Londoners' minds as well as their walls.

cards.front: Name the seven renewable energy resources given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Wind / Solar / Hydroelectric / Tidal / Geothermal / Wave / Bio-fuel

cards.front: Name the three drivers of the global shift towards renewable energy given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Concerns about climate change / Energy security / Falling cost of renewable technologies

cards.front: Why does doubling an object's speed quadruple its kinetic energy?
cards.answer: Because kinetic energy depends on speed squared, so doubling speed multiplies energy by four.

cards.front: Why do mechanical processes waste energy through friction?
cards.answer: Friction causes a rise in temperature, heating the surroundings and dissipating energy to the thermal store.

cards.front: Name the four smart transport strategies the lesson gives for reducing traffic congestion in cities.
cards.answer: Integrated transport systems / Park-and-ride sites / Congestion charging / Pedestrianised streets, cycle highways and Low Traffic Neighbourhoods
items: Pedestrianised streets, cycle highways and Low Traffic Neighbourhoods

cards.front: Name the three ways homes in sustainable cities cut water use, as given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Water meters / Low-flush toilets, aerated taps and dual-flush systems / Rainwater harvesting and grey water recycling
items: Low-flush toilets, aerated taps and dual-flush systems
Rainwater harvesting and grey water recycling

cards.front: Why does traffic congestion cause serious air-quality problems in UK cities?
cards.answer: Petrol and diesel engines stuck in jams emit nitrogen dioxide and particulates, linked to thousands of early deaths yearly.

cards.front: How does Bristol's closed-loop scheme make food waste recycling sustainable?
cards.answer: It turns school food waste into compost used on city allotments, so nutrients re-enter the local food system.

cards.front: Name the five colours used in the Olympic rings, as stated in the lesson.
cards.answer: Blue / Yellow / Black / Green / Red

cards.front: At which three levels does the lesson say Olympic and Paralympic values can be seen through campaigns?
cards.answer: Local / Regional / National

cards.front: Why is Determination especially significant for Paralympic athletes, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Because they often face greater obstacles than non-disabled athletes in accessing coaching, funding and facilities to reach elite level.

cards.front: How did the Paris 2024 Olympic Village demonstrate the Olympic value of Friendship?
cards.answer: It housed athletes and staff from 206 delegations in one location, creating connections across borders.

cards.front: Name the three things ayahs lacked once abandoned in London, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: No money / No language skills / No legal rights

cards.front: Name the three ways the lesson says lascars were treated worse than white sailors.
cards.answer: Paid far less than white sailors / Housed in the worst quarters / No legal protection if abandoned at port
items: Paid far less than white sailors
No legal protection if abandoned at port

cards.front: Why did Gupta set The Empress between 1887 and 1901 even though she wrote it in 2013?
cards.answer: To draw parallels between Victorian racism and modern attitudes towards immigration.

cards.front: Why does Gupta stage Queen Victoria comforting Abdul Karim while Rani is left destitute at the docks?
cards.answer: It is a structural choice that reinforces the play's themes of inequality and absence of justice.

cards.front: Name the six steps the lesson gives for constructing a ranking matrix.
cards.answer: List all specification criteria in rows / Assign a weighting 1-5 to each criterion / List each design concept in columns / Score each concept against each criterion / Multiply each score by the weighting / Sum the weighted scores for each concept
items: List all specification criteria in rows
Assign a weighting 1-5 to each criterion
List each design concept in columns
Score each concept against each criterion
Multiply each score by the weighting
Sum the weighted scores for each concept

cards.front: Why must engineers evaluate design ideas objectively against the design brief and specification instead of relying on preference?
cards.answer: Without systematic evaluation, decisions risk selecting a design that fails user needs, exceeds budget, or fails safety requirements.

cards.front: Name the three anthology poems the lesson compares with 'Holy Thursday'.
cards.answer: Theme for English B / Happy Birthday Moon / Tea With Our Grandmothers

cards.front: Why does the poem suddenly shift from description to direct address in the final couplet?
cards.answer: Because the poem's real purpose is to instruct wealthy adults on how they should treat poor children, not just admire the ceremony.

cards.front: How do the similes comparing the children to Thames water and wind affect how they seem?
cards.answer: They make the children seem larger than themselves, like a natural force rather than just a crowd of individuals.

cards.front: How does the poem's structure work like a sermon?
cards.answer: It builds through description in the middle, then suddenly addresses the reader at the end, so we observe before being told what it means.

title: Opposition, resistance and Germany at war
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the five categories of opposition to Nazi rule described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Private grumbling / Subcultural resistance (youth movements) / Religious resistance / Political resistance (underground networks) / Conservative-military resistance

cards.front: What happened to the weekly rations of bread, meat and fat between 1939 and 1945?
cards.answer: Bread: 2,400g to 1,700g / Meat: 700g to 250g / Fat: 270g to 80g

cards.front: Why did Goebbels give his 'total war' speech in February 1943?
cards.answer: After the defeat at Stalingrad, he called for full mobilisation of German society for war production.

cards.front: Why does the lesson argue that opposition to the Nazis mattered, even though it failed to remove Hitler?
cards.answer: Because it preserved the idea of an alternative Germany that resisted, shaping how post-war Germany understood its responsibility.

cards.front: What three broad economic sectors do minerals extracted from the Earth serve?
cards.answer: Construction / Industrial manufacturing / Energy generation

cards.front: What are the four stages of the staged prospecting approach, in order from cheapest to most expensive?
cards.answer: Geological mapping / Geophysical surveys / Geochemical surveys / Borehole drilling

cards.front: Why is a uranium deposit deep beneath the Antarctic ice sheet classed as a resource but not a reserve?
cards.answer: Current technology and extraction costs make it impractical to extract the uranium profitably right now.

cards.front: How do seismic surveys help locate oil and gas deposits?
cards.answer: They send acoustic waves into the ground and record reflections, revealing structures like anticlines or faults that trap oil and gas.

title: Life in Nazi Germany: Women, Youth & Persecution
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: What four main methods did the Nazis use to reduce unemployment?
cards.answer: National Labour Service (RAD) / Autobahns / Rearmament / Conscription

cards.front: What four reasons does the lesson give for why so few Germans opposed the persecution of Jewish people?
cards.answer: Anti-Semitism had deep roots in European culture / Nazi propaganda reinforced existing prejudices / The police state made protest dangerous / Some Germans benefited by buying Jewish property/businesses cheaply
items: Anti-Semitism had deep roots in European culture
The police state made protest dangerous
Some Germans benefited by buying Jewish property/businesses cheaply

cards.front: Why did the Nazis reverse their policy of keeping women out of work by the late 1930s?
cards.answer: Rearmament created labour shortages, forcing the Nazis to encourage women back into the workforce despite their own ideology.

cards.front: Why did Nazi maths textbooks include questions about the cost of caring for disabled people?
cards.answer: To make students accept disabled people as a burden on society, preparing public opinion for the later euthanasia programme.

cards.front: How does increasing temperature affect the rate of diffusion?
cards.answer: Higher temperature gives particles more kinetic energy, which increases the rate of diffusion.

cards.front: Why do potato cylinders lose mass when placed in a concentrated sugar solution?
cards.answer: Water inside the cells moves out by osmosis into the more concentrated sugar solution outside.

cards.front: Name the five criteria scored in the Apgar score.
cards.answer: Appearance (skin colour) / Pulse (heart rate) / Grimace (reflex response) / Activity (muscle tone) / Respiration (breathing)

cards.front: Name the two technologies used in the newborn hearing test.
cards.answer: Otoacoustic emission (OAE) test / Automated auditory brainstem response (AABR) test

cards.front: Why is kangaroo care (skin-to-skin contact) actively promoted for babies in SCBU?
cards.answer: It stabilises the baby's heart rate and temperature and supports bonding and breastfeeding.

cards.front: Why do premature babies often need care in a Special Care Baby Unit?
cards.answer: They have underdeveloped lungs, poor temperature regulation, difficulty feeding, and a weakened immune system.

title: Food Commodities & Their Place in the Diet
subject: food-preparation-and-nutrition-eduqas

cards.front: Why does freezing preserve the nutritional value of fruit and vegetables well?
cards.answer: Freezing halts enzyme activity almost completely, preserving micronutrients effectively.

cards.front: Why does wrapping bread and keeping it at room temperature (not the fridge) keep it fresher for longer?
cards.answer: Bread stales through starch retrogradation, which the refrigerator actually speeds up, so room temperature slows staling.

cards.front: Why are sugar and syrup shelf-stable without refrigeration?
cards.answer: Their high sugar concentration reduces water activity, which inhibits microbial growth.

cards.front: Why does chicken breast become firm and opaque when roasted?
cards.answer: Heat causes the proteins to denature, uncoiling their molecular chains and making the flesh firm and opaque.

cards.front: What four reasons does the lesson give for China launching the First Five-Year Plan?
cards.answer: Defence against modern US military power / Ideology valuing heavy industry as proof of socialism / Alliance access to Soviet engineers and credit / Prestige of catching up with imperial powers
items: Defence against modern US military power
Ideology valuing heavy industry as proof of socialism
Alliance access to Soviet engineers and credit
Prestige of catching up with imperial powers

cards.front: Why did the Korean War push Mao to industrialise China quickly?
cards.answer: Chinese soldiers fought a modern American army with First World War-era equipment, showing China urgently needed heavy industry for defence.

cards.front: Why was Mao personally uncomfortable with the success of the First Five-Year Plan?
cards.answer: It was designed mainly by Soviet planners and run by Liu Shaoqi, Zhou Enlai and Chen Yun, making Mao chafe at dependence on cautious bureaucratic Soviet-style planning.

cards.front: Name the four magnetic materials given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Iron / Steel / Cobalt / Nickel

cards.front: Name the three ways to increase the strength of a solenoid's magnetic field.
cards.answer: Increase the current / Add more turns of wire / Place an iron core inside

cards.front: Why does a compass needle point towards geographic north?
cards.answer: It aligns with the Earth's magnetic field, whose south pole is near geographic north, attracting the compass's north-seeking pole.

cards.front: Why is the magnetic field strong inside a solenoid but weak outside?
cards.answer: Inside, the fields from each coil turn add together; outside, the fields mostly cancel each other out.

cards.front: Name the three purposes of family life given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Procreation / Stability and protection / Educating children in a faith

cards.front: Name the five family types found in modern Britain according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Nuclear family / Extended family / Single-parent family / Blended (step) family / Same-sex parent family

cards.front: Why does Islam not accept same-sex parenting?
cards.answer: Because homosexual relationships are considered haram (forbidden) in Islam.

cards.front: Why do some Christians argue against full equality of gender roles?
cards.answer: They believe God gave men and women different but complementary roles, citing St Paul's teaching that women should not have authority over men.

title: Creation, Evolution and the Sanctity of Human Life
subject: religious-studies-eduqas

cards.front: What two consequences does creation ex nihilo have, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: The universe is entirely dependent on God / Creation is fundamentally good
items: The universe is entirely dependent on God

cards.front: Why does the Catholic Church say science and theology do not simply contradict each other on creation?
cards.answer: Because they operate at different levels of enquiry: science asks 'how?', theology asks 'why?' and 'who?'

cards.front: How did Pope John Paul II reconcile evolution with Catholic teaching in his 1996 message?
cards.answer: He accepted biological evolution as God's method for producing human life, but said the soul is directly created by God, not evolved.

cards.front: Why does Peter Singer challenge the idea that human life is automatically more valuable than animal life?
cards.answer: Because he argues moral worth depends on capacity to feel pain and have interests, not on belonging to the human species.

cards.front: Why did the ill-appearing victim in Piliavin's study receive help more often than the drunk-appearing victim?
cards.answer: Because an ill victim seemed less dangerous, making the cost of helping lower and increasing bystanders' willingness to help.

cards.front: Why might Piliavin's subway study findings not generalise beyond that specific setting?
cards.answer: The study took place in one urban subway environment, so results may not apply to different cultures or types of emergency.

cards.front: Why is Enid's palm reading in Scene 8 significant for her character?
cards.answer: It is her own act of acceptance, allowing the Obeah she once dismissed as backward to reach her.

cards.front: Why does Enid's strategy of suppression fail in Scene 8?
cards.answer: She is forced to see she cannot control Del's choices, prevent grief or loss, or maintain her silence.

cards.front: Name the three key figures the lesson identifies as central to non-violent action in the 20th century.
cards.answer: Mahatma Gandhi / Martin Luther King Jr / Desmond Tutu

cards.front: What four arguments do defenders of pacifism give against the criticism that non-violence is ineffective?
cards.answer: Violence often escalates conflict rather than resolving it / It corrupts those who use it / Non-violent methods can achieve profound social change / Christian ethics requires living out Kingdom of God's values now
items: Violence often escalates conflict rather than resolving it
It corrupts those who use it
Non-violent methods can achieve profound social change
Christian ethics requires living out Kingdom of God's values now

cards.front: Why does the philosopher Reinhold Niebuhr call pacifism 'irresponsible perfectionism'?
cards.answer: Because Christians who refuse all use of force are failing their responsibility to protect the innocent.

cards.front: How does the command to love your enemies act as a foundation for Christian pacifism?
cards.answer: If you genuinely love someone, you cannot wish harm on them even if they are harming you.

title: Historic environment: Glastonbury Festival c.1970 to the present day
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the seven fallow years at Glastonbury Festival given in the lesson.
Why did the crowd problems of the early 1990s lead to major security changes at Glastonbury?
cards.answer: The rave/free party movement brought huge numbers of gatecrashers, with 1992 crowds of 70,000-80,000 exceeding licenced capacity, threatening the festival's future.

cards.front: How did the Super Fence change the nature of Glastonbury Festival in 2002?
cards.answer: It ended free entry for those who couldn't pay or climbed in, making Glastonbury a secure, ticketed event with defined entrances.

cards.front: Name the three legal restrictions the lesson gives on Elizabethan women.
cards.answer: Could not own property independently / Could not vote / Marriages typically arranged by fathers

cards.front: Name the three things Elizabethan courtship typically required, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Father's consent / Negotiation over the dowry / Public betrothal before the wedding

cards.front: Why is Claudio's accusation against Hero so catastrophic in honour culture terms?
cards.answer: He accuses her publicly at the wedding to destroy her reputation and restore his own honour, not just end the engagement.

cards.front: How does the community interpret Hero's fainting after the accusation?
cards.answer: Her silence is taken as guilt, so the community assumes she is ashamed because she is guilty; only Beatrice and the Friar resist this.

cards.front: The lesson gives four areas of ethical treatment a business must consider. Name them.
cards.answer: Treatment of workers / Treatment of suppliers / Treatment of customers / Sourcing of materials and marketing

cards.front: Why can acting ethically sometimes still be profitable for a business in the long term?
cards.answer: It can win loyal customers who care and build brand reputation, even though it usually raises costs.

cards.front: How did social media change the risk for businesses that behave unethically?
cards.answer: A single factory-scandal video can reach millions of people before a company can respond with PR.

cards.front: Why do big supermarkets face challenge for delaying supplier payments by 60 or 90 days?
cards.answer: Delaying payments squeezes small farmers financially, leading to legal and reputational challenge.

title: Regional Instability After the Iran-Iraq War
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the four legacies the lesson says the Iran-Iraq War bequeathed directly to the 1990 Kuwait crisis.
cards.answer: Massive debt / An oversized army / Normalised use of chemical weapons / An unforgiving Saddam Hussein

cards.front: Why did Iraq's oil revenue collapse during the Iran-Iraq War, worsening its debt problem?
cards.answer: The Tanker War saw both sides attack Gulf shipping, frightening off insurance markets and crushing oil revenue.

cards.front: Why did Saddam Hussein believe he could justify invading a neighbour by 1990?
cards.answer: He had the military hardware, the financial pressure to need money, and a story of being an Arab defender betrayed by ungrateful neighbours.

cards.front: How did Saddam try to solve Iraq's post-war unemployment and debt crisis instead of demobilising?
cards.answer: Rather than disband his army, he kept it under arms and eighteen months later pointed it at Kuwait.

cards.front: Why does Kelly structure Mark and Jan as always appearing together, finishing each other's sentences?
cards.answer: Their shared narration acts as a Greek chorus, contrasting with the isolation of characters like Brian and Richard.

cards.front: How does the length of Leah's monologues change across the play, and what does this show?
cards.answer: They get longer and more frantic, mirroring the group's moral disintegration.

cards.front: Why is Leah's speech to Phil not a soliloquy or a dialogue?
cards.answer: Phil is present so it isn't a soliloquy, but he never replies so it isn't a dialogue either.

cards.front: Why does Kelly use minimal stage directions in DNA?
cards.answer: It gives directors freedom in staging and focuses audience attention on language and character rather than spectacle.

cards.front: What are the five key themes of DNA identified in the lesson?
cards.answer: Guilt and responsibility / Leadership and power / Peer pressure / Silence and complicity / Morality

cards.front: What four forms does silence take in DNA?
cards.answer: Phil's silence is strategic power / Adam's silence is imposed powerlessness / The group's silence is complicity / Leah's talk is effectively silence since nobody listens
items: Leah's talk is effectively silence since nobody listens

cards.front: Why does Kelly present collective guilt as more dangerous than individual guilt in DNA?
cards.answer: Because within a group everyone can convince themselves that someone else is really to blame.

cards.front: What is the devastating irony of Adam's fall in DNA?
cards.answer: Adam's need to belong destroys him, while the group's need to hold together after his fall destroys their morality.

title: Product and the Product Life Cycle
subject: business-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three elements of the design mix.
cards.answer: Function / Aesthetics / Cost

cards.front: Name the four extension strategies a business can use to boost sales.
cards.answer: New markets / Product modification / Promotional campaigns / Price reductions

cards.front: Why does failing to differentiate risk squeezing a business's profit margins?
cards.answer: Without differentiation the business ends up competing purely on price, causing a race to the bottom that erodes margins.

cards.front: Why might an extension strategy fail to revive sales for an obsolete product?
cards.answer: If new technology has genuinely made the product obsolete, even a large marketing budget may not revive demand.

cards.front: Name the four factors the lesson gives for green design.
cards.answer: Materials needing less energy to extract or process / Reduced volume and type of packaging / Materials that are easy to recycle at end of life / Designing products to last longer
items: Materials needing less energy to extract or process
Reduced volume and type of packaging
Materials that are easy to recycle at end of life

cards.front: Name the five stages of a life cycle analysis (LCA).
cards.answer: Raw material extraction / Manufacture / Transportation / Use / Disposal

cards.front: Why should carbon offsetting be used alongside real emission cuts rather than instead of them?
cards.answer: Offsetting does not reduce emissions at the source, so it only works well combined with genuine reductions in energy use and transport.

cards.front: Why is switching from a mixed-material carton to a single-polymer bottle easier to recycle?
cards.answer: Recycling plants can process one plastic type directly, without needing to separate different layers of material first.

title: Watching Theatre Critically: Taking Useful Notes
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: Name the four things the lesson says to note during a live performance.
cards.answer: Performer moments / Design moments / Audience reaction / Stage configuration

cards.front: Name the three questions you should answer in full sentences during the interval.
cards.answer: Most striking performer choice so far / Design element that most affected your mood / What the director wants you to think about themes
items: Most striking performer choice so far
Design element that most affected your mood
What the director wants you to think about themes

cards.front: Why does a plot summary earn little credit in a live theatre review?
cards.answer: Because the exam asks you to analyse how meaning was communicated, not retell what happened, and the reader already knows the plot.

cards.front: Why is audience reaction useful to note during a performance?
cards.answer: Audience reaction such as gasping, laughing or falling silent is evidence that a theatrical choice worked.

cards.front: Name the four kinds of tool an IDE usually provides.
cards.answer: Editor / Error diagnostics / Run-time environment / Translator

cards.front: Name the four features an IDE editor uses to make code easier to write and read.
cards.answer: Syntax highlighting / Automatic indentation / Auto-complete / Line numbering

cards.front: Why is a compiler a good choice for finished software you want to share with others?
cards.answer: The executable runs fast, works without the source code, and keeps the source code hidden from users.

cards.front: Why does an interpreter suit writing and testing a program during development?
cards.answer: Errors are caught one at a time and the same source code runs on any device with the right interpreter.

cards.front: Name the three parallel crises that drive Scenes 4–7 of Leave Taking.
cards.answer: Del deepens her bond with Mai and moves into her bedsit / Del's pregnancy becomes apparent / Viv walks out of an A-level exam
items: Del deepens her bond with Mai and moves into her bedsit
Viv walks out of an A-level exam

cards.front: Why is Mai in a hurry to prepare Del during Scenes 4–7?
cards.answer: Mai is physically declining, has a dizzy spell in Scene 5, and uses the time she has left to make sure Del is ready to inherit her role.

cards.front: Why does Brod's account of Del's father also reveal Brod's own disillusionment?
cards.answer: Brod, like Del's father, has watched the Windrush promise of a better life corroded by racism and poverty in England.

title: Functional Areas and the Supply Chain
subject: l12-retail-business

cards.front: Name the three stages of the retail supply chain given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Sourcing (finding suppliers) / Logistics (transporting and storing products) / Stock control (managing stock levels, recording movements and maintaining supply)
items: Stock control (managing stock levels, recording movements and maintaining supply)

cards.front: Name the four benefits of using technology in stock control listed in the lesson.
cards.answer: Greater accuracy / Reduced waste / Lower storage costs / Improved availability for customers

cards.front: Why does an online retailer like ASOS place enormous emphasis on its ICT department?
cards.answer: Because ICT maintains the website, app and payment systems that the whole online business depends on.

cards.front: Why is good HR practice especially important in retail businesses?
cards.answer: It reduces staff turnover, which is particularly common and expensive in the retail sector.

cards.front: Name the three wires inside a UK three-pin plug, with their colours.
cards.answer: Live (brown) - carries the AC supply at about 230V / Neutral (blue) - completes the circuit, normally at 0V / Earth (green and yellow striped) - safety wire to the metal casing
items: Live (brown) - carries the AC supply at about 230V
Neutral (blue) - completes the circuit, normally at 0V
Earth (green and yellow striped) - safety wire to the metal casing

cards.front: Name the four electrical safety features described for appliances and circuits.
cards.answer: Fuse / Earth wire / Residual current device (RCD) / Double insulation

cards.front: Why is the live wire dangerous even when an appliance's switch is turned off?
cards.answer: It stays connected to the mains supply and carries 230V relative to earth, so touching it creates a dangerous potential difference through your body.

cards.front: Why do transformers only work with alternating current, not direct current?
cards.answer: They rely on a changing magnetic field in the core to induce a voltage in the secondary coil, which only AC produces.

cards.front: Name the four tragedies in the novel that the lesson says all flow from Victor's abandonment of the Creature.
cards.answer: William's murder / Justine's execution / Clerval's death / Elizabeth's murder

cards.front: Why does the Creature turn to violence, according to the theme of isolation?
cards.answer: Its plea for companionship is denied by humanity, and isolation drives it to violence when this is refused.

cards.front: How does Victor's abandonment of the Creature contrast with God's creation of Adam?
cards.answer: God gives Adam companionship and a home, while Victor gives the Creature nothing after creating it.

cards.front: Why does Shelley say ambition itself is not the real problem in the novel?
cards.answer: The problem is ambition without limits, compassion, or responsibility, not striving or ambition itself.

title: The Covenant: Abraham, Moses and the Promised Land
subject: religious-studies-aqa

cards.front: Name the five commandments in the first group of the Ten Commandments, which concern duties to God.
cards.answer: I am the Lord your God / No other gods or idols / Not taking God's name in vain / Keeping Shabbat holy / Honouring your father and mother
items: I am the Lord your God
Not taking God's name in vain

cards.front: Name the five commandments in the second group of the Ten Commandments, which concern duties between people.
cards.answer: Do not murder / Do not commit adultery / Do not steal / Do not give false witness / Do not covet

cards.front: Why can't Yom Kippur forgiveness alone resolve a wrong committed against another person?
cards.answer: Because for mitzvot between man and man, God's forgiveness cannot substitute for making direct amends to the person wronged.

cards.front: Why do some Orthodox Jews make aliyah (move permanently to Israel)?
cards.answer: Because they understand the promise of the land as literal and ongoing, so moving to Israel fulfils the covenant as a religious act.

cards.front: Name the five main air masses that influence UK weather.
cards.answer: Tropical Maritime / Tropical Continental / Polar Maritime / Polar Continental / Arctic Maritime

cards.front: Name the three stages a depression passes over the UK in, in order.
cards.answer: Warm front / Warm sector / Cold front

cards.front: Why does the UK have such changeable weather?
cards.answer: The UK sits under the polar front, where warm tropical air meets cold polar air, causing rapid weather changes.

cards.front: How does a warm front appear on a synoptic chart?
cards.answer: As a red line with semicircles pointing in the direction the front is travelling.

cards.front: Name the six functions of the skeleton given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Support / Protection / Movement / Attachment for muscles / Mineral storage / Blood cell production

cards.front: Why does the shape of the femur's head allow movement in all directions at the hip?
cards.answer: Its rounded head fits into the cup-shaped socket of the pelvis, allowing movement in all directions.

cards.front: Why is movement at the elbow restricted to a single plane?
cards.answer: The pulley-shaped end of the humerus fits into the groove of the ulna, restricting movement to flexion and extension only.

cards.front: How does the radius allow the forearm to turn palm-up or palm-down?
cards.answer: The radius rotates around the ulna, allowing the forearm to turn palm-up or palm-down.

cards.front: Why does Magwitch's appearance create sympathy despite him seizing Pip in the graveyard?
cards.answer: His violent appearance is undercut by his desperation, as he is shivering, hungry, and hunted.

cards.front: Why does Pip become ashamed of Joe and the forge after visiting Satis House?
cards.answer: Estella's contempt made Pip see himself through upper-class eyes, filling him with shame at being 'common'.

cards.front: Why has Miss Havisham raised Estella to be incapable of love?
cards.answer: She uses Estella as a weapon of revenge, to inflict on men the pain inflicted on her when jilted.

cards.front: What two formative encounters define Pip's childhood, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Meeting the convict Magwitch / Meeting the decaying Miss Havisham

cards.front: What three arguments does Rochester give to justify his hidden marriage to Bertha?
cards.answer: It was forced on him by his family for money / Bertha was already showing signs of madness / He has suffered for years
items: It was forced on him by his family for money
Bertha was already showing signs of madness

cards.front: What three earlier mysteries at Thornfield are explained once Bertha is revealed?
cards.answer: The laughter / The fire / The torn veil

cards.front: Why does Jane turn back at Rochester's door before finally leaving Thornfield?
cards.answer: Brontë shows her hesitation and pain to prove her moral strength comes from choosing principle over desire, not indifference.

cards.front: How can Bertha Mason be read as more than just a Gothic monster?
cards.answer: She can symbolise everything Victorian society repressed — female anger, sexuality, and women locked away when inconvenient.

cards.front: Name the four angels with specific named roles described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Jibril – angel of revelation / Izra'il – angel of death / Mika'il – bringer of rain and sustenance / Israfil – blows the trumpet on Judgement Day
items: Mika'il – bringer of rain and sustenance
Israfil – blows the trumpet on Judgement Day

cards.front: Name the six key prophets highlighted in the lesson from Adam onwards.
cards.answer: Adam / Ibrahim / Isma'il / Musa / Dawud / Isa

cards.front: How does belief in recording angels affect the way Muslims behave?
cards.answer: Knowing every action, even private ones, is recorded encourages honesty, compassion and avoiding wrongdoing even without human witnesses.

cards.front: Where do Sunni Muslims believe guidance comes from after the Prophet, since they reject infallible Imams?
cards.answer: From the Qur'an, the Sunnah (the Prophet's example), and the scholarly community (Ulema).

title: Plot and Structure: A Tale Across Two Countries
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: Name the four precise historical markers the lesson gives for events in The Great Wave.
According to the lesson, what three design methods does Turnly use to signal time leaps in The Great Wave?
cards.answer: lighting state changes / sound cues / costume alteration

cards.front: Why does Turnly choose a two-act, twin-timeline structure for The Great Wave?
cards.answer: It gives the audience a form that mirrors the content: separation, parallel endurance, and the impossibility of easy reunion.

cards.front: Why does episodic, Brechtian-style structure stop the audience fully surrendering to one storyline in The Great Wave?
cards.answer: Cutting between Japan and North Korea reminds the audience another equally real world is running parallel, preventing total emotional identification with either side.

title: Mission, Evangelism, Ecumenism and the Persecuted Church
subject: religious-studies-ocr

cards.front: Name the four ecumenical organisations and communities named in the lesson.
cards.answer: World Council of Churches (WCC) / Taizé / Iona / Corrymeela

cards.front: What forms of persecution does the lesson say Christians can face because of their faith?
cards.answer: Arrest / Violence / Imprisonment / Loss of employment / Death

cards.front: Why do evangelical Christians see verbal proclamation as the highest priority in mission?
cards.answer: They believe sharing that Jesus is the only path to salvation, as in John 14:6, is an act of love, not imposition.

cards.front: Why do Catholics and liberal Protestants often emphasise social action as their form of mission?
cards.answer: Because Jesus identifies himself with the poor and vulnerable in Matthew 25:31-46, so deeds serving them serve Christ himself.

cards.front: Name the four types of trenches that made up the Western Front system.
cards.answer: Front-line trenches / Communication trenches / Reserve trenches / Supply lines

cards.front: Name the four symptoms of shell shock the lesson lists.
cards.answer: Nightmares / Trembling / Inability to speak or move / Emotional breakdown

cards.front: Why was shell shock a controversial issue during WWI?
cards.answer: The military establishment was slow to recognise it as a genuine condition, so many sufferers were accused of cowardice.

cards.front: How does Sherriff show psychological damage in the play without ever using the term 'shell shock'?
cards.answer: Stanhope drinks to forget, Hibbert invents physical ailments to escape, and even steady Osborne shows quiet anxiety.

cards.front: Name the five bullet points in the sample restaurant role-play scenario.
cards.answer: Book a table for four people / Order a starter and a main course / Ask what drinks they have / Say what you ate last time you visited / Unexpected problem with your order
items: Book a table for four people
Order a starter and a main course
Say what you ate last time you visited

cards.front: Name the three polite ways to order food given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Para mí… / Quisiera… / Me gustaría…

cards.front: Why should you avoid using 'quiero' on its own when ordering in a restaurant?
cards.answer: Because it can sound rude, so polite forms like 'Quisiera' or 'Me gustaría' should be used instead.

cards.front: Why is it important to use the usted form when speaking to a waiter in a role-play?
cards.answer: It shows cultural awareness and earns marks for using the correct register.

cards.front: Name the six plosive consonants the lesson lists.
cards.answer: b / d / p / t / k / g

cards.front: Name the four verbs the lesson uses to show how verb choice reveals a speaker's state of mind.
cards.answer: walks / drifts / trudges / strides

cards.front: How does the personification of the cliff work in Wordsworth's 'Boat Stealing'?
cards.answer: The cliff hasn't actually moved; the boy's guilt makes it seem to, turning the landscape into an image of his conscience.

cards.front: How does vowel length create pace in Keats' line 'Bright star, would I were stedfast as thou art'?
cards.answer: The long open vowels hold the line steady, imitating the fixed star the speaker envies, whereas short vowels would hurry it.

title: Wolsey's Foreign Policy: Peacemaker or Warmonger?
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: What three aims did Henry VIII have for foreign policy, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Military glory / Recovery of English claims in France / A male heir whose rule could not be threatened
items: Recovery of English claims in France
A male heir whose rule could not be threatened

cards.front: Name the three events the lesson gives that eroded the 1518 peace settlement.
cards.answer: Charles V's election as Holy Roman Emperor (1519) / Renewal of Habsburg-Valois war from 1521 / The Sack of Rome (1527)
items: Charles V's election as Holy Roman Emperor (1519)

cards.front: Why does the lesson argue the Treaty of London was a triumph even though it only lasted four years?
cards.answer: Judged by what England could realistically achieve, it made Henry a European arbiter, and its collapse came from events outside Wolsey's control.

cards.front: Why did the Field of the Cloth of Gold fail to prevent renewed conflict with France?
cards.answer: It was theatre rather than policy, so it did not change the underlying Habsburg-Valois rivalry that soon dragged England back into war.

cards.front: Name the four false assumptions Pip loses by the end of this stage of the novel, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Benefactor is a convict not a lady / Hopes of marrying Estella are a fantasy / Gentlemanly status funded by criminal money / His treatment of Joe was cruel and unnecessary
items: Benefactor is a convict not a lady
Hopes of marrying Estella are a fantasy
Gentlemanly status funded by criminal money
His treatment of Joe was cruel and unnecessary

cards.front: Why does Pip feel revulsion when he first realises Magwitch is his benefactor?
cards.answer: Pip has absorbed Victorian class prejudice that criminals are contemptible, so he cannot reconcile this with the gratitude he should feel.

cards.front: Why does Dickens have Miss Havisham's dress catch fire after Pip confronts her about his suffering?
cards.answer: The fire symbolises that a life built on bitterness and revenge, surrounded by decaying, flammable relics, is inherently self-destructive.

cards.front: Name the six contextual layers the lesson says you need to understand to write analytically about Brontë's intentions.
cards.answer: Class / Gender / The governess role / The Gothic / Romanticism / Religion

cards.front: Name the four Gothic conventions the lesson says writers like Ann Radcliffe and Mary Shelley pioneered.
cards.answer: Dark secrets / Haunted buildings / Imprisoned women / Blurred boundary between the natural and the supernatural
items: Blurred boundary between natural and supernatural

cards.front: Why did governesses occupy an uncomfortable social position in Victorian households?
cards.answer: They were too educated to mix with servants but too poor to be treated as equals by employers, leaving them isolated and dependent.

cards.front: Why does Jane leave Rochester after discovering his secret?
cards.answer: Her deeply Christian morality gives her the strength to leave him despite her feelings.

title: User Interaction Methods and Digital Interactivity
subject: it-ocr

cards.front: Name the four disadvantages the lesson gives for voice input.
cards.answer: Unreliable in noisy environments / Raises privacy concerns (always listening) / May not work with accents or speech impairments / May not work for quiet voices
items: May not work with accents or speech impairments
May not work for quiet voices

cards.front: Name the four disadvantages the lesson gives for touch input.
cards.answer: Needs a clean surface and dry hands / Leaves fingerprints on the screen / Small elements hard to tap precisely / Prolonged use on vertical screens causes arm fatigue
items: Needs a clean surface and dry hands
Small elements hard to tap precisely
Prolonged use on vertical screens causes arm fatigue

cards.front: Why is voice input the ideal interaction method for a kitchen smart speaker?
cards.answer: The cook's hands may be wet or covered in food and their eyes are focused on cooking, so hands-free voice control suits best.

cards.front: Why is mouse input best for a graphic design workstation rather than touch?
cards.answer: Fine pixel-level manipulation needs the mouse's high precision, while touch is not accurate enough for such detailed editing.

cards.front: Name the three strange events at Thornfield that build suspense about its hidden secret.
cards.answer: Curious mirthless laugh from third storey / Rochester's bed curtains set on fire / Wedding veil torn by mysterious figure
items: Curious mirthless laugh from third storey
Rochester's bed curtains set on fire
Wedding veil torn by mysterious figure

cards.front: Why does Brontë strip away formality in Jane and Rochester's first meeting on the icy lane?
cards.answer: To show them meeting as equals in physical need, establishing their relationship won't follow conventional master-servant power dynamics.

cards.front: Why does Jane force herself to compare her plain self-portrait with an imagined portrait of Blanche?
cards.answer: To manage her hope by reminding herself that wealth and beauty, which she lacks, supposedly determine who deserves love.

cards.front: Name the three examples the lesson gives of Godfrey Cass's moral cowardice.
cards.answer: Marries Molly in secret / Refuses to claim Eppie / Only confesses when forced

cards.front: Name the three ways Dolly Winthrop shows kindness to Silas, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Brings food when he's a stranger / Helps him raise Eppie / Supports him without asking anything in return
items: Brings food when he's a stranger
Supports him without asking anything in return

cards.front: Why is Dunstan Cass's death in the stone-pit symbolic?
cards.answer: He is buried alongside the gold he stole, showing wealth cannot protect someone from the consequences of their own moral failures.

cards.front: How does Nancy Lammeter respond when Godfrey finally confesses about Eppie?
cards.answer: She responds with calm dignity, hurt but not vindictive, accepting responsibility rather than running from it like Godfrey.

title: The Effects of Mental Health Problems
subject: psychology-ocr

cards.front: Name the three examples the lesson gives of discrimination someone might face after being diagnosed with a mental health problem.
cards.answer: Being turned down for a job / Having a promotion blocked / Being excluded from social events
items: Being turned down for a job

cards.front: Name the three ways the lesson says other people might treat someone differently once they know about their diagnosis.
cards.answer: Avoiding them socially / Gossiping about them / Assuming they are unpredictable or incapable
items: Assuming they are unpredictable or incapable

cards.front: Why can self-stigma be as damaging as stigma from other people?
cards.answer: Because it can stop the person believing that recovery or a normal life is even possible for them.

cards.front: Why did care in the community replace long-stay psychiatric hospitals as a policy?
cards.answer: Attitudes changed and hospitals were seen as isolating, so the policy aimed to let people keep independence, relationships and their place in the community.

cards.front: Name the three examples of giant covalent structures given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Diamond / Graphite / Silicon dioxide

cards.front: Name the three examples of simple molecules given in the lesson.
cards.answer: H2O / CO2 / O2

cards.front: Why do larger simple molecules tend to have higher boiling points?
cards.answer: As molecules get bigger, the intermolecular forces between them become stronger, needing more energy to overcome.

cards.front: Why are polymers usually solid at room temperature?
cards.answer: Polymers have relatively strong intermolecular forces between their long chains, keeping them solid at room temperature.

cards.front: Name the three types of desire the lesson identifies across Browning, Mew, and Nagra's poems.
cards.answer: Possessive and fatal (Browning) / Frustrated and potentially dangerous (Mew) / Mutual, playful, and life-affirming (Nagra)

cards.front: How does the storm at the start of 'Porphyria's Lover' link to the speaker's mind?
cards.answer: The pathetic fallacy of the storm mirrors the speaker's inner turmoil before Porphyria arrives.

cards.front: Why does the word 'chose' in 'The Farmer's Bride' suggest an unequal marriage?
cards.answer: It suggests the wife had no say, showing marriage as a transaction rather than a partnership.

cards.front: How does Mew use nature imagery to present the farmer's wife?
cards.answer: She is compared to a mouse, a leveret and a hunted hare, reducing her to a frightened animal.

cards.front: Name the five uses of glucose produced during photosynthesis in plants.
cards.answer: Respiration (to release energy) / Converting to starch for storage / Producing cellulose for cell walls / Producing amino acids for proteins / Producing lipids for storage in seeds
items: Producing lipids for storage in seeds

cards.front: Name the three ways the body responds during exercise to meet increased energy demand.
cards.answer: Heart rate increases / Breathing rate and depth increase / Blood is redirected to the muscles
items: Blood is redirected to the muscles

cards.front: Why does increasing light intensity only increase the rate of photosynthesis up to a point?
cards.answer: The rate increases with light intensity until another factor, such as CO2 or temperature, becomes limiting.

cards.front: How does raising temperature beyond the optimum affect the rate of photosynthesis?
cards.answer: Enzymes controlling the reaction denature above the optimum temperature, causing the rate to drop sharply.

cards.front: Name the three grounds Christians give in response to the indoctrination charge.
cards.answer: All upbringings involve values / Good Christian education invites questioning / Adult who freely continues has made an informed choice
items: Adult who freely continues has made an informed choice

cards.front: Name the three Christian festivals the lesson says give rhythm to a child's year.
cards.answer: Christmas / Easter / Pentecost

cards.front: How does attending church as a child help lead to lasting belief?
cards.answer: It gives the child a community of believers who reinforce Christian identity and show faith practised by adults they love and respect.

cards.front: How does prayer at home shape a child's faith?
cards.answer: Saying grace and bedtime prayers models an ongoing relationship with God as natural and routine.

cards.front: Name the four main types of fault covered in this lesson.
cards.answer: Normal fault / Reverse fault / Thrust fault / Strike-slip fault

cards.front: What are the three types of tectonic stress that produce faults?
cards.answer: Tensional stress / Compressional stress / Shear stress

cards.front: Why are younger rocks exposed on the downthrown side of a normal fault?
cards.answer: The fault cuts out part of the rock succession, so younger rocks appear on the downthrown side and older rocks on the upthrown side.

cards.front: How does movement along a fault cause an earthquake?
cards.answer: Blocks lock together due to friction until stress overcomes it, then slip rapidly, releasing energy as seismic waves.

cards.front: How does the blood imagery reversal between Act 2 and Act 5 show guilt cannot be escaped?
cards.answer: Macbeth says the ocean can't clean his hands and Lady Macbeth says water clears them, but by Act 5 she obsessively washes invisible blood, showing guilt destroys both.

cards.front: How does Macduff's reaction to Duncan's murder contrast with Macbeth's performance of grief?
cards.answer: Macduff's simple 'O horror, horror, horror!' shows genuine speechless shock, unlike Macbeth's elaborate, rehearsed-sounding metaphor about 'golden blood'.

cards.front: The lesson lists three qualities Shakespeare gives to sleep to show what Macbeth has lost. Name them.
cards.answer: the death of each day's life / sore labour's bath / balm of hurt minds
items: the death of each day's life

title: Types of Data and Research Methods
subject: sociology-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three types of interview described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Structured interview / Unstructured interview / Semi-structured interview

cards.front: Why do official crime statistics likely understate the true level of offending?
cards.answer: They only count crimes that are reported to and recorded by the police, missing unreported offences.

cards.front: Why might a researcher 'go native' during participant observation?
cards.answer: They may over-identify with the group they are studying and lose their objectivity.

cards.front: Why do questionnaires tend to have low validity even though they are reliable?
cards.answer: Closed questions impose the researcher's categories and cannot probe unexpected answers, reducing accuracy of real behaviour captured.

cards.front: Name the four key figures/organisations in the history of American independent cinema given in the lesson.
cards.answer: John Cassavetes / Sundance Film Festival / Miramax / A24

cards.front: Name the five A24 films listed in the lesson as showing its director-driven slate.
cards.answer: Moonlight / Lady Bird / The Florida Project / Hereditary / Everything Everywhere All at Once

cards.front: Why does a low budget paradoxically allow independent filmmakers to take more creative risks?
cards.answer: Without needing to recoup a huge investment, filmmakers can experiment with non-linear structure, unusual casting or unresolved endings.

cards.front: How did mumblecore's naturalistic, overlapping dialogue style originate?
