cards.front: Why does crowd funding reduce financial risk for a designer launching a new product?
cards.answer: Backers only pledge money before manufacturing, and if the target isn't reached no money changes hands, avoiding wasted production costs.

cards.front: How does JIT (just in time) manufacturing reduce storage costs?
cards.answer: Materials are ordered only when they are needed for production, so less stock has to be stored.

cards.front: How does the shift from comedy to tragedy in Act 3 make the play more devastating?
cards.answer: Shakespeare builds a comic structure in Acts 1–2 then violently dismantles it after Mercutio's death, making the tragedy hit harder than one that starts tragic.

cards.front: How does the balcony scene's staging create a visual metaphor?
cards.answer: Juliet stands above in the upper gallery and Romeo below, physically showing the separation between the lovers.

cards.front: Why is the tomb scene the ultimate example of dramatic irony?
cards.answer: Juliet's lips are crimson and her cheeks flushed because she is alive, but Romeo mistakes this for death's cruel beauty and kills himself.

cards.front: Name the four spaces the lesson gives as examples of where love and violence happen in the play.
cards.answer: public streets (brawls, duels) / the ball / the balcony / the bedchamber

cards.front: The lesson gives five sources of error that can enter a system. Name them.
cards.answer: Transcription error / Transmission error / Original source error / Data loss / Deliberate falsification

cards.front: Name the two main verification methods described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Double entry / Proof reading

cards.front: How does a check digit detect an error when a barcode is scanned at a till?
cards.answer: The system recalculates the check digit from the other digits; if it doesn't match the scanned digit, it alerts the operator.

cards.front: Why might a data entry system use both validation and verification together?
cards.answer: Validation checks each field is reasonable as it's typed, then verification (proof reading) confirms the record matches the source, reducing errors.

cards.front: Name the four physical/working properties of paper and board discussed, apart from porosity and tear resistance.
cards.answer: Stiffness / Opacity / Whiteness / Tensile strength

cards.front: The lesson gives six examples of specialist papers and their uses. Name them.
cards.answer: Cartridge paper / Layout paper / Tracing paper / Grid paper / Bleed-proof paper / Sugar paper

cards.front: Why does chemical pulping (the kraft process) produce a stronger sheet of paper than mechanical pulping?
cards.answer: Chemical pulping removes more lignin, giving a stronger, more durable sheet than the weaker, more acidic mechanically pulped paper.

cards.front: Why should the grain direction run parallel to the longest fold lines when cutting a packaging net?
cards.answer: Paper folds more cleanly and creases more crisply along the grain, preventing cracking and giving a neater carton.

cards.front: Besides the agonist and antagonist, the lesson names two other types of muscle involved in movement. Name all four types.
cards.answer: Agonist (prime mover) / Antagonist (relaxes to allow movement) / Synergist (assists the agonist) / Fixator (stabilises the joint)

cards.front: What are the three functions of the muscular system given in the lesson?
cards.answer: Movement through contraction / Maintaining posture / Generating heat

cards.front: Why does vasoconstriction happen when the body is cold?
cards.answer: Blood vessels near the skin narrow, redirecting warm blood to vital organs and muscles to conserve core temperature.

cards.front: How does expiration force air out of the lungs?
cards.answer: The diaphragm and intercostal muscles relax, the ribcage drops, volume decreases, pressure rises, pushing air out.

cards.front: Name the four factors that affect the rate of a reaction.
cards.answer: Temperature / Concentration (or pressure for gases) / Surface area to volume ratio / Catalysts

cards.front: How can the rate of a gas-producing reaction be measured experimentally?
cards.answer: By collecting the gas in a gas syringe or measuring the loss of mass on a balance over time.

cards.front: How is the rate of the sodium thiosulfate and hydrochloric acid reaction measured?
cards.answer: By timing how long it takes the yellow sulfur precipitate to make the solution opaque, hiding a cross beneath the flask.

cards.front: Name the five physical factors the lesson says interact to produce a flood.
cards.answer: Rainfall intensity / Soil saturation (antecedent conditions) / Slope / Geology / Drainage basin shape

cards.front: Name the four human causes the lesson gives for rivers becoming flashier.
cards.answer: Urbanisation / Deforestation / Modern arable farming / River straightening

cards.front: Why do round, compact drainage basins flood more quickly than long, thin basins?
cards.answer: Round, compact basins concentrate water at the outlet faster, giving a shorter lag time and higher flood peak.

cards.front: Why does straightening a river channel protect upstream areas but increase flood risk downstream?
cards.answer: Straightening speeds water through the channel, protecting upstream fields but raising flood peaks for towns further downstream.

title: Beyond Earth: Solar System, Stars and the Universe
subject: separate-sciences-ocr

cards.front: Name the six types of objects that make up the solar system.
cards.answer: The Sun / Eight planets / Moons / Dwarf planets (e.g. Pluto) / Asteroids / Comets

cards.front: Name the four outer planets of the solar system in order from the Sun.
cards.answer: Jupiter / Saturn / Uranus / Neptune

cards.front: Why does a satellite stay in a stable orbit rather than flying off or falling in?
cards.answer: Its tendency to move in a straight line is balanced by the gravitational pull curving its path inwards.

cards.front: Why must satellites in lower orbits travel faster than those in higher orbits?
cards.answer: Closer orbits experience a stronger gravitational field, so the satellite must travel faster to maintain that orbit.

cards.front: Name the two core purposes Catholic teaching gives to the family.
cards.answer: Procreation / Security and education of children in the faith
items: Security and education of children in the faith

cards.front: Name the five practical ways local Catholic parishes support families, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Family worship / The sacraments / Classes for parents / Groups for children / Counselling

cards.front: Why does the Catholic Church say cohabitation lacks what marriage provides?
cards.answer: Without a binding vow, a relationship lacks the security needed for a true and total gift of self.

cards.front: Why does the Catholic Church teach that removing the procreative dimension breaks the meaning of sex?
cards.answer: The marital, unitive and procreative dimensions cannot be pulled apart without breaking the full meaning of the act.

title: Energy Futures: Reducing Reliance on Fossil Fuels
subject: geography-edexcel-b

cards.front: Name the three types of unconventional fossil fuels the lesson describes.
cards.answer: Canadian tar sands / Shale gas / Arctic offshore oil

cards.front: Name the six different groups with competing views on energy futures mentioned in the lesson.
cards.answer: Consumers / TNCs like Shell or BP / Governments / Climate scientists / Environmental groups / Indigenous communities

cards.front: Why are biofuels seen as a problematic renewable energy source?
cards.answer: They require large amounts of land that could instead be used to grow food.

cards.front: Why is nuclear power controversial even though it produces almost no operating CO₂ emissions?
cards.answer: It raises long-term waste storage concerns and has high upfront costs.

title: Logic Gates, Truth Tables and Boolean Algebra
subject: electronics-eduqas

cards.front: Name the five logic gates covered for the exam.
cards.answer: NOT / AND / OR / NAND / NOR

cards.front: Why is the NAND gate called a universal gate?
cards.answer: Because any logic function can be built using only NAND gates.

cards.front: How does a NAND gate behave as a NOT gate when both inputs are tied together?
cards.answer: Both inputs equal A, so the output becomes NOT(A AND A), which equals NOT A.

cards.front: Why should truth table rows for a three-input circuit be listed in binary counting order?
cards.answer: Listing rows as 000 to 111 in order guarantees every input combination is included and none is missed.

cards.front: Name the four disadvantages of being a sole trader given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Unlimited liability / Limited access to finance / Business depends entirely on the owner / No one to share workload or skills
items: Business depends entirely on the owner
No one to share workload or skills

cards.front: Name the three disadvantages of a private limited company compared to a sole trader, according to the lesson's key fact.
cards.answer: More complex and costly to set up / Accounts are public / Owners must share control with other shareholders
items: More complex and costly to set up
Owners must share control with other shareholders

cards.front: Why is start-up capital easier to raise in a partnership than for a sole trader?
cards.answer: Because there are multiple owners who can each contribute personal funds.

cards.front: Why does franchising allow a franchisor to expand rapidly?
cards.answer: It expands the brand without the capital cost of opening company-owned sites.

cards.front: Name the four studio hazards and their main risks given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Noise → hearing loss / Displays/screens → eye strain / Slip/trip/fall → sprains and injuries / Electrical → electrocution

cards.front: Name the four key features of an audio interface given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Phantom power / Balanced and unbalanced inputs / Pre-amps / DAW connectivity

cards.front: How does a DI box reduce noise on long cable runs?
cards.answer: It converts the instrument's unbalanced, high-impedance signal into a balanced, low-impedance signal at mic level.

cards.front: Why must gain be optimised during the recording process?
cards.answer: So the input level is strong enough to record clearly but does not clip or distort.

title: Earth's Resources, Potable Water and Life-Cycle Assessment
subject: separate-sciences-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three ways the lesson says chemistry helps with sustainable development.
cards.answer: Finding alternatives to finite resources (biofuels, bioplastics) / Improving recycling / Designing more efficient processes that generate less waste
items: Finding alternatives to finite resources (biofuels, bioplastics)
Designing more efficient processes that generate less waste

cards.front: What three things does the raw material extraction stage of a life-cycle assessment consider?
cards.answer: Energy used / Land disturbed / Waste generated

cards.front: Why is desalination essential in some parts of the Middle East despite its high energy cost?
cards.answer: These regions have limited rainfall and no major rivers, so treating fresh water isn't an option.

cards.front: Why does recycling still have an environmental cost even though it conserves resources?
cards.answer: Collection, sorting, transport and reprocessing all require energy and produce some waste.

cards.front: Why does Shakespeare use dramatic irony in Benedick's declaration against love?
cards.answer: The more emphatically Benedick rejects love, the more certain the audience becomes he will fall in it.

cards.front: How does the masked ball show that characters react to appearances rather than reality?
cards.answer: Everyone wears masks, so characters observe, misinterpret, and react to disguised or false appearances instead of the truth.

title: Bank of England, East India Company and the trade revolution
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Name the three interlocking innovations the lesson says gave England its commercial advantage.
cards.answer: Bank of England (1694) enabling cheap state borrowing / East India Company controlling Asian trade / Joint-stock investment spreading risk across many investors
items: Bank of England (1694) enabling cheap state borrowing
East India Company controlling Asian trade
Joint-stock investment spreading risk across many investors

cards.front: Name the three major battles the lesson says John Churchill, Duke of Marlborough, commanded English and allied forces in.
cards.answer: Blenheim (1704) / Ramillies (1706) / Oudenarde (1708)

cards.front: How did the growing habit of tea-drinking link Asian trade to the Atlantic slave economy?
cards.answer: Tea-drinking created demand for sugar, which came from the Atlantic slave economy, tying Asian trade to that system.

cards.front: Why did the Treaty of Methuen (1703) shift England's wine trade from France to Portugal?
cards.answer: France was England's enemy in war, so trade shifted to allied Portugal, which also opened up Brazilian trade routes.

cards.front: Name the three legal privileges the Vestal Virgins gained from being freed from a male guardian's authority.
cards.answer: Could make wills / Could own property / Could give testimony in court without an oath
items: Could give testimony in court without an oath

cards.front: Why did Athenian law codes in the fifth century BC try to restrict female lamentation in public?
cards.answer: Because it was seen as too emotionally excessive, showing how powerful and public women's religious mourning actually was.

cards.front: What happened to a Vestal Virgin found guilty of breaking her vow of chastity?
cards.answer: She was buried alive in a small underground chamber sealed with earth.

cards.front: Why was the Bona Dea ceremony considered scandalous when Publius Clodius Pulcher attended in 62 BC?
cards.answer: Because he disguised himself as a woman to infiltrate a rite from which men were strictly forbidden.

cards.front: Why do carbon anodes need to be replaced regularly during aluminium extraction?
cards.answer: Oxygen produced at the anode reacts with the carbon at high temperature, burning the anodes away.

cards.front: Why does aluminium appear unreactive in everyday life despite being high in the reactivity series?
cards.answer: It quickly forms a thin, tightly bonded, impermeable oxide layer that seals the surface and prevents further oxidation.

cards.front: Why does copper metal form at the cathode when copper sulfate solution is electrolysed?
cards.answer: Copper is less reactive than hydrogen, so Cu²⁺ ions are preferentially discharged instead of H⁺ ions.

cards.front: Name the two electrode products in the worked example of copper sulfate solution electrolysis with carbon electrodes.
cards.answer: Copper metal at cathode / Oxygen gas at anode

cards.front: What are Piaget's four invariant stages of cognitive development, in order, with their approximate ages?
cards.answer: Sensori-motor (0–2 years) / Pre-operational (2–7 years) / Concrete-operational (7–11 years) / Formal-operational (11 years onwards)

cards.front: What three abilities does the lesson say adolescents gain in the formal-operational stage?
cards.answer: Reason about hypothetical situations / Plan ahead / Think about possibilities rather than only actualities
items: Think about possibilities rather than only actualities

cards.front: Why did younger children in Piaget's (1952) study say the spread-out row of counters now had more?
cards.answer: They judged number by the length of the row rather than by logic, not yet able to decentre from the obvious visual change.

cards.front: Why does a baby stop looking for a toy once it is hidden, before object permanence develops?
cards.answer: They have not yet understood that objects continue to exist when out of sight, so it seems to have vanished.

cards.front: Name the four non-specific (first-line) defences the body uses against pathogens.
cards.answer: Skin / Mucus and cilia / Stomach acid / Lysozyme in tears/saliva

cards.front: Why does cholera cause severe diarrhoea and dehydration?
cards.answer: The bacteria produce a toxin that makes the intestinal wall secrete massive amounts of water.

cards.front: How does cilia damage from cutting through mucus normally protect the airways?
cards.answer: Cilia beat rhythmically to sweep mucus and trapped pathogens up to the throat to be swallowed and destroyed by stomach acid.

cards.front: Why can HIV progress to AIDS if untreated?
cards.answer: HIV attacks helper T lymphocytes, progressively damaging the immune system until it can't fight off infections.

cards.front: Name the four carbon allotropes described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Diamond / Graphite / Fullerenes / Graphene

cards.front: Name the four properties of metals given in the lesson.
cards.answer: High melting points / Conduct electricity / Malleable / Good conductors of heat

cards.front: Why are metals malleable?
cards.answer: Layers of positive ions can slide over each other without breaking the metallic bond because delocalised electrons adjust to the new positions.

cards.front: Why do larger molecules have higher boiling points than smaller ones?
cards.answer: Larger molecules have more electrons, giving stronger intermolecular forces that need more energy to overcome.

title: Prayer and Masses for the Dead
subject: religious-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four communal forms prayer for the dead takes in British Catholic parishes, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Prayers for the dead at every Mass / All Souls' Day Masses reading names of the dead / A 'book of the dead' for names in November / Candlelit vigils and visiting family graves
items: Prayers for the dead at every Mass
All Souls' Day Masses reading names of the dead
A 'book of the dead' for names in November
Candlelit vigils and visiting family graves

cards.front: Why does a Humanist reject prayer for the dead, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Because consciousness ceases at death, so there is no soul left for prayer to assist.

title: The Exclusion Crisis and the Succession
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the three groups the lesson gives as the base of support for the Whigs.
cards.answer: Dissenters / London merchants / Many of the gentry

cards.front: Name the three groups the lesson gives as the base of support for the Tories.
cards.answer: Country squires / Cathedral clergy / The universities

cards.front: Why was Charles II able to risk dissolving Parliament instead of relying on it for money?
cards.answer: Louis XIV secretly paid him a subsidy and customs revenue from booming trade had improved the Crown's finances.

cards.front: Why did Charles II refuse to make the Duke of Monmouth his heir?
cards.answer: He refused absolutely to acknowledge any marriage to Monmouth's mother, Lucy Walter, so would not legitimise him.

cards.front: Name the five named ethical issues researchers must deal with.
cards.answer: Informed consent / Deception / Confidentiality / Right to withdraw / Protection of participants

cards.front: Name the six lenses used for evaluating any psychological study.
cards.answer: Validity / Reliability / Generalisability / Ethics / Objectivity / Subjectivity

cards.front: Why can a repeated measures design improve validity?
cards.answer: Using the same participants in every condition removes participant variables as an explanation for any difference found.

cards.front: Why can volunteer sampling reduce how far findings generalise?
cards.answer: Volunteers may be more motivated or confident than the average person, producing a biased sample.

cards.front: Why does Jekyll's experiment not actually create Hyde as a new being?
cards.answer: Jekyll was always divided and concealed his desires; the potion just releases a self that already existed.

cards.front: How does Utterson's respect for privacy end up harming Jekyll?
cards.answer: His deference to social convention stops him investigating aggressively enough to uncover the truth and save his friend.

cards.front: What event triggers the mockumentary frame to start dissolving in District 9?
cards.answer: Wikus is exposed to alien biotechnical fluid during the eviction-notice door-to-door sequence.

cards.front: How does District 9 shift the spectator's identification from bureaucrat to refugee?
cards.answer: Restricted narration aligns the spectator with Wikus as his body transforms, shifting identification from oppressor to oppressed.

cards.front: Name the three diegetic sound sources layered simultaneously in the eviction-notice sequence.
cards.answer: Wikus's camcorder narration / alien clicks and growls / MNU agents shouting procedural instructions

cards.front: Why does the rack focus in the MNU laboratory transformation sequence keep Wikus's hands sharp while the scientists blur?
cards.answer: It shows what Wikus sees so the spectator shares his horror without the scientists' analytical viewpoint.

title: Convergence and the Cross-Platform Media Landscape
subject: media-studies-aqa

cards.front: Name the three levels at which convergence operates, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Technological level / Industrial level / Cultural level

cards.front: What three advantages does a 'vertical stack' give an organisation?
cards.answer: Favour its own content / Control terms of competitor access to the platform / Collect audience data at every stage
items: Control terms of competitor access to the platform
Collect audience data at every stage

cards.front: Why can a streaming service based in one country reach subscribers in over 150 countries so easily?
cards.answer: It bypasses the national distribution infrastructure that once made global media expansion slow and expensive.

cards.front: Why do media organisations design campaigns to encourage second-screen participation?
cards.answer: To extend audience engagement beyond the primary screen using hashtags, live polls and social media tie-ins.

cards.front: Name the four near-rhyme endings Douglas uses in 'Vergissmeinnicht' instead of exact rhymes.
cards.answer: gone / ground / found / sun

cards.front: Name the four other Conflict poems (besides 'Songs for the People') that this lesson compares with 'Vergissmeinnicht'.
cards.answer: Colonization in Reverse by Louise Bennett / Papa-T by Fred D'Aguiar / We Lived Happily during the War by Ilya Kaminsky / The Destruction of Sennacherib by Byron
items: Colonization in Reverse by Louise Bennett
We Lived Happily during the War by Ilya Kaminsky
The Destruction of Sennacherib by Byron

cards.front: Why does Douglas use near-rhyme rather than exact rhyme in 'Vergissmeinnicht'?
cards.answer: It unsettles the reader instead of soothing them, unlike a neat rhyme scheme would.

cards.front: Why does the poem call the soldier's equipment 'hard and good when he's decayed'?
cards.answer: It shows the irony that his gun and gear have outlasted him, more durable than the man who used them.

cards.front: Why does Ross confirming Macbeth as Thane of Cawdor matter for the rest of the prophecies?
cards.answer: It fulfils the first prophecy, making the remaining prophecy of kingship seem possible to Macbeth.

cards.front: Why does Macbeth bring the bloody daggers back with him instead of leaving them to frame the guards?
cards.answer: He is so traumatised and guilt-ridden after the murder that his mental state fractures and he cannot complete the plan.

cards.front: Name the six input switch types listed for input devices.
cards.answer: SPST / Push-to-make / Push-to-break / Tilt switch / Reed switch / QTC switch

cards.front: Name the six input sensor types listed for input devices.
cards.answer: LDR / Photodiode / NTC thermistor / Pressure sensor / Infrared sensor / Smart sensor

cards.front: How does an NPN transistor allow a small current to switch a much larger current?
cards.answer: A small current flowing into the base allows a much larger current to flow between the collector and emitter, switching the load.

cards.front: Why do higher-power output devices need driver components such as transistors or relays?
cards.answer: Microcontrollers can only supply a few milliamps, so drivers are needed to switch loads that need much larger currents.

cards.front: Name the two types of reaction based on energy change described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Exothermic reactions / Endothermic reactions

cards.front: Why does an exothermic reaction cause the temperature to rise?
cards.answer: Because the energy released forming new bonds exceeds the energy needed to break the existing bonds, releasing energy to the surroundings.

cards.front: Why might a reaction that produces gas in an open container seem to lose mass?
cards.answer: Because the gas produced escapes into the air, so it isn't included when the remaining mass is measured.

cards.front: In the equation 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO, why does this confirm conservation of mass?
cards.answer: Because 48g of magnesium plus 32g of oxygen equals 80g of magnesium oxide, so reactant mass equals product mass.

cards.front: Name the six high-value passages the lesson says are most frequently examined in Silas Marner.
cards.answer: Lantern Yard betrayal (drawing of lots) / Silas counting his gold by firelight / The theft discovery ('wild ringing scream') / Eppie's arrival (golden curls mistaken for gold) / Eppie's choice ('I can't feel as I've got any father but one') / The return of the gold (Silas's indifference)
items: Silas counting his gold by firelight
Eppie's arrival (golden curls mistaken for gold)
Eppie's choice ('I can't feel as I've got any father but one')
The return of the gold (Silas's indifference)

cards.front: Name the four key methods the lesson lists for analysing Eliot's writing under AO2.
cards.answer: Symbolism / Dual plot structure / Omniscient narrative voice / Use of dialect

cards.front: Why does Eliot use dialect in Silas Marner, such as in Dolly's speech?
cards.answer: To create warmth and authenticity.

cards.front: Why should every paragraph connect the extract to the wider novel rather than staying isolated?
cards.answer: Cross-text connections demonstrate the sustained critical style that marks out the highest bands.

title: Summing Amplifiers and Audio Mixer Systems
subject: electronics-eduqas

cards.front: What four common errors do students make in block diagram questions about audio systems?
cards.answer: Placing the mixer before the preamplifiers / Placing the power amplifier before the mixer / Adding an unjustified block (e.g. a pulse generator) / Forgetting to label each block clearly
items: Placing the mixer before the preamplifiers
Placing the power amplifier before the mixer
Adding an unjustified block (e.g. a pulse generator)
Forgetting to label each block clearly

cards.front: Name the three other practical systems (besides audio) that use summing amplifiers.
cards.answer: Data-acquisition circuits combining sensor readings / Digital-to-analogue converters summing binary-weighted voltages / Automatic control systems blending error signals from sensors
items: Automatic control systems blending error signals from sensors

cards.front: How does virtual earth let each input resistor in a summing amplifier set its own contribution to the output?
cards.answer: Negative feedback holds the inverting input near 0V, so each resistor's current depends only on its own input voltage, independent of the others.

cards.front: Why is it wrong to place the power amplifier before the mixer in an audio block diagram?
cards.answer: The power amplifier must boost a single already-combined signal, but before the mixer there are still several separate signals.

title: Magazine Front Covers: Vogue and GQ
subject: media-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four colours in the limited colour palette used on the Vogue July 2021 cover.
cards.answer: Red / Silver-grey / Black / White

cards.front: Name the four genres of content mixed together on the GQ August 2019 cover.
cards.answer: Fashion advice / Sport / Politics / Celebrity gossip

cards.front: Why is Malala's mode of address on the Vogue cover described as personal and confident rather than just inviting the viewer to look at her?
cards.answer: She is shot in medium close-up with direct eye contact and a slight smile, inviting the reader to admire her as a role model.

cards.front: Why does GQ show Sterling topless and muscular on its August 2019 cover?
cards.answer: It reflects the body-conscious, consumerist 'spornosexual' model of modern masculinity that GQ sells to its readers.

cards.front: Name the four contact forces the lesson gives as examples.
cards.answer: Friction / Air resistance / Tension / Normal contact force

cards.front: Name the three non-contact forces the lesson gives as examples.
cards.answer: Gravitational force / Electrostatic force / Magnetic force

cards.front: How do you work out the resultant force when two forces act on an object in the same direction?
cards.answer: Add the two forces together; the resultant acts in that same direction.

cards.front: Why does an astronaut's weight change between Earth and the Moon even though their mass stays the same?
cards.answer: Weight depends on gravitational field strength, which is lower on the Moon, while mass never changes with location.

title: Resistance and Rebellion: Slavery and the Colonies
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four everyday acts of resistance the lesson gives for enslaved people in the fields and towns.
cards.answer: Work slowdowns / Breaking tools / Setting fire to barns / Feigning illness / Refusing to work on Sundays

cards.front: Why did Spain offer freedom to enslaved Africans who reached Spanish Florida?
cards.answer: It was strategic: freeing them undermined the British plantation system and weakened a rival empire on Spain's border.

cards.front: Why did South Carolina planters push for harsher slave codes after the Stono Rebellion?
cards.answer: The rebellion showed how seriously enslaved people threatened the plantation system, so planters sought tighter control to prevent further unrest.

cards.front: Why do historians disagree about whether the New York Conspiracy of 1741 was a real plot?
cards.answer: Some see it as panic driven by fear and expanding testimony, like Salem, while others point to real Atlantic radical networks linking enslaved people and labourers.

title: Freedom Rides to the Civil Rights Act 1964
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Name the three legal tools state authorities used to slow the civil rights movement.
cards.answer: Injunctions against marches / Arrests on technical charges / Economic pressure on Black employers and landlords
items: Economic pressure on Black employers and landlords

cards.front: Name the three civil rights workers murdered in Mississippi during Freedom Summer, June 1964.
cards.answer: James Chaney / Andrew Goodman / Michael Schwerner

cards.front: Why was Johnson able to pass the Civil Rights Act in 1964 when Kennedy had not managed to?
cards.answer: He used the nation's grief after Kennedy's assassination and his mastery of Senate procedure to push it through Congress.

cards.front: Why did the FBI under Hoover fail to properly investigate violent crimes against civil rights workers?
cards.answer: Hoover was reluctant to investigate and preferred to monitor the movement as a potential Communist subversion instead.

cards.front: Name the three types of organism the lesson says can reproduce asexually.
cards.answer: Plants / Bacteria / Some animals (e.g. starfish)

cards.front: Name the three benefits of the Human Genome Project given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Identify genes linked to diseases / Develop personalised medicines / Trace human migration and evolutionary relationships
items: Trace human migration and evolutionary relationships

cards.front: Why is the genetic variation produced by sexual reproduction important?
cards.answer: It is important for natural selection, helping populations survive and adapt.

cards.front: What happens to the zygote after fertilisation to form an embryo?
cards.answer: The zygote divides by mitosis to form an embryo.

cards.front: The lesson describes three practical steps for systematic sampling. What are they?
cards.answer: Calculate the interval k (population ÷ sample size) / Choose a random start between 1 and k / Select every k-th member after the start
items: Calculate the interval k (population ÷ sample size)
Choose a random start between 1 and k
Select every k-th member after the start

cards.front: Name the four biased sampling methods the lesson lists alongside their main weakness.
cards.answer: Opportunity - highly biased / Judgement - depends on researcher's assumptions / Cluster - clusters may not be typical / Quota - not random within each quota
items: Cluster - clusters may not be typical
Quota - not random within each quota

cards.front: Why can systematic sampling accidentally produce an all-male or all-female sample?
cards.answer: If the register alternates by gender, sampling every k-th name can hit a hidden pattern and pick only one gender.

cards.front: Why might a biased sample from opportunity or judgement sampling still be useful in research?
cards.answer: In early exploratory research speed matters more than perfect representativeness, so a quick convenient sample can help identify variables worth investigating.

cards.front: Name the five discourse markers the lesson gives for making a balanced argument in German writing.
cards.answer: Einerseits / Andererseits / Außerdem / Jedoch / Trotzdem

cards.front: Name four arguments the lesson gives against marriage (Nachteile).
cards.answer: Es kostet zu viel / Es ist nur ein Blatt Papier / Viele Menschen werden geschieden / Ich möchte unabhängig bleiben
items: Es ist nur ein Blatt Papier

cards.front: Why is using the conditional tense important for reaching Grade 5+ on the writing paper?
cards.answer: Because the conditional counts as a separate time frame alongside present, past and future, which is needed for AO3.

cards.front: Why do hätte and wäre not need an infinitive at the end of the sentence, unlike möchten or würde?
cards.answer: Because hätte and wäre are standalone conditional verbs that don't pair with an infinitive.

cards.front: Name the three questions the lesson's quick self-check asks before moving on to conclusions.
cards.answer: Did you choose the right type of graph for the data? / Did you use the right summary statistic, and explain why? / Did you describe the pattern with figures from your results, including anomalies?
items: Did you choose the right type of graph for the data?
Did you use the right summary statistic, and explain why?
Did you describe the pattern with figures from your results, including anomalies?

cards.front: Why does pebble size typically decrease downstream, according to the Bradshaw model?
cards.answer: Attrition smooths and breaks pebbles as they are transported, so they get smaller and rounder away from the source.

cards.front: Why is extrapolation from a line of best fit risky?
cards.answer: Because you are reading a value beyond the range of the data collected, and the trend may not continue.

cards.front: Why does Armitage use colloquial, conversational language in 'Remains'?
cards.answer: To reflect how soldiers actually speak, making the psychological trauma feel authentic and immediate rather than literary or distant.

cards.front: How does the repeated word 'bloody' in 'his bloody life in my bloody hands' capture the soldier's guilt?
cards.answer: It works as both literal description of blood on his hands and colloquial swearing, expressing guilt and anger simultaneously.

cards.front: Name the four stages the novella moves through as the story gets closer to the truth about Jekyll and Hyde.
cards.answer: street-level rumour / professional lawyer / scientific eyewitness / the subject's own pen

cards.front: Name the three examples of Victorian 'doubles' Stevenson uses to explain the story's obsession with hidden vice.
cards.answer: the respectable husband who kept a mistress / the clergyman with a secret life / the civilised man who was also an animal
items: the respectable husband who kept a mistress
the clergyman with a secret life
the civilised man who was also an animal

cards.front: Why does Jekyll lose the ability to control his transformations into Hyde?
cards.answer: He believed he could separate his good and evil selves, but the evil self, given its own body, grew stronger while the good weakened.

cards.front: Why is the ending of the novella tragic rather than triumphant?
cards.answer: There is no cure or moral redemption, only a confession — Jekyll and Hyde die but the double remains as a lesson.

title: Fusions: What Fusion Music Means — Afro Celt Sound System and Esperanza Spalding
subject: music-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four checklist areas the lesson says to work through when answering a fusion listening question.
cards.answer: Instruments and their cultural origin / Scale or harmonic style / Rhythmic pattern / Texture or production

cards.front: Name the three Celtic instruments the lesson says to listen for in Release.
cards.answer: Tin whistle / Fiddle / Uilleann pipes

cards.front: Why does Release create a dense, multi-layered texture compared to a purely acoustic folk recording?
cards.answer: Studio techniques like sampling and looping repeat programmed fragments continuously, with live Celtic and African instrumental lines added on top.

cards.front: How does the texture in Samba Em Preludio differ from Release's texture?
cards.answer: It stays transparent and acoustic, letting the walking bass, guitar rhythm and vocal improvisation be heard as separate interlocking strands rather than layered under studio effects.

cards.front: Name the five possible identities the lesson suggests for Inspector Goole.
cards.answer: A ghost / A time traveller / The voice of God / The embodiment of collective conscience / A man who knew too much
items: A man who knew too much

cards.front: Name the three things the Inspector controls during his interrogation of the Birlings.
cards.answer: Who speaks when / What information is revealed / How the story unfolds

cards.front: Why does Priestley give the Inspector no dramatic exit after his final speech?
cards.answer: So he doesn't force change; he offers a moral choice, leaving the family to decide for themselves whether to accept or reject his message.

cards.front: How does the Inspector's language change as the play progresses?
cards.answer: It moves from the factual tone of a police investigation to the elevated, prophetic register of a sermon or political speech.

cards.front: Name the three things Shylock is stripped of by the end of the trial.
cards.answer: His bond / His wealth / His faith

cards.front: How does Shylock's understatement in his exit lines make his defeat more powerful?
cards.answer: He does not rage, weep or curse but simply submits, so his quiet despair contrasts starkly with the Christians' triumph.

cards.front: How does Gratiano's taunt after the trial undercut Portia's mercy speech?
cards.answer: His wish that Shylock had ten more godfathers to send him to the gallows shows casual viciousness the mercy speech hasn't cured.

title: The First and Second New Deals
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Name the five key agencies created during the Hundred Days (1933).
cards.answer: AAA / CCC / FERA / NRA / TVA

cards.front: Name three New Deal figures (other than Roosevelt or Frances Perkins) described as its architects.
cards.answer: Harry Hopkins / Senator Robert Wagner / Eleanor Roosevelt

cards.front: Why did the Glass-Steagall Act (1933) stop the bank-run panics of 1930-33?
cards.answer: It separated commercial and investment banking and created the FDIC, guaranteeing bank deposits so savers no longer feared losing their money.

cards.front: Why did Roosevelt shift emphasis to workers' rights and social security in the Second New Deal of 1935?
cards.answer: Because the Supreme Court had struck down the NRA and AAA, so he responded with new legislation on labour rights and social security instead.

cards.front: What three purposes does the lesson give for marriage according to most Christians?
cards.answer: Mutual companionship and support / Sexual union within a committed relationship / Procreation and upbringing of children
items: Sexual union within a committed relationship

cards.front: What four things does the lesson say an Islamic nikah ceremony requires?
cards.answer: Consent of both parties / Presence of witnesses / Setting of the mahr / Offer and acceptance (ijab and qubul)

cards.front: Why does traditional Christian teaching hold that sexual relationships should only take place within marriage?
cards.answer: The body is described as the temple of the Holy Spirit, so sexual union is reserved for the marriage covenant.

cards.front: Why is polygyny only permitted in Islam under strict conditions?
cards.answer: Because Islamic teaching requires that a husband treats all his wives with justice and equal treatment.

cards.front: Name the five land-use categories recorded in an urban land-use survey.
cards.answer: Comparison retail / Convenience retail / Services / Leisure / Vacant

cards.front: Name the three fixes for reducing bias in an environmental quality survey.
cards.answer: Calibration / Triple sampling / Photo logging

cards.front: Why is careful sampling especially important in human fieldwork?
cards.answer: People are far less uniform than rocks, so how they are selected strongly affects whether the sample represents the population.

cards.front: How does photo logging help improve the reliability of an environmental quality survey?
cards.answer: Each score is paired with a photograph so the judgement can be re-checked later for accuracy.

title: Ethics, the Environment and Pressure Groups
subject: business-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four common ethical issues the lesson gives that businesses must consider.
cards.answer: Paying fair wages throughout the supply chain / Avoiding misleading advertising / Refusing to use child labour / Treating employees equally regardless of background
items: Paying fair wages throughout the supply chain
Treating employees equally regardless of background

cards.front: Name the four elements of the marketing mix that pressure group activity can force a business to change.
cards.answer: Product / Price / Place / Promotion

cards.front: Why have ethical considerations become more commercially significant for businesses?
cards.answer: Consumers and investors increasingly choose businesses that align with their values, making unethical behaviour risk boycotts and reputational damage.

cards.front: Why might a business that delays investing in sustainability suffer later on?
cards.answer: As consumer preferences and regulation shift towards sustainability, delaying may leave it with stranded assets and regulatory penalties.

title: Gender Equality and the Roles of Women and Men
subject: religious-studies-eduqas

cards.front: The lesson gives four traditional roles in the Theravada Buddhist four-fold hierarchy. What are they?
cards.answer: Monks (bhikkhus) / Nuns (bhikkhunis) / Laymen / Laywomen

cards.front: Why do women not lead Friday prayers over mixed congregations in mainstream Sunni and Shia tradition?
cards.answer: Qur'an 2:228 says men have a degree over women, interpreted in traditional jurisprudence to reserve Friday prayer leadership to men.

cards.front: Why has the bhikkhuni sangha not been fully reinstated in some Theravada countries like Thailand and Sri Lanka?
cards.answer: Some authorities resist full reinstatement because they believe the unbroken ordination lineage for nuns has been lost.

cards.front: Why can women serve as rabbis in Reform Judaism but not in Orthodox Judaism?
cards.answer: Reform grounds this in the Torah's ethical core of full human equality, seeing old restrictions as historically conditioned, unlike Orthodox halakha.

title: Crowd Behaviour and Zimbardo's Prison Study
subject: psychology-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four evaluation points the lesson gives for Zimbardo's prison study.
cards.answer: Strength: control from random allocation to roles / Weakness: ethics – participants suffered real distress / Weakness: limited generalisability – small male American student sample / Weakness: validity – guards may have exaggerated knowing they were observed
items: Strength: control from random allocation to roles
Weakness: ethics – participants suffered real distress
Weakness: limited generalisability – small male American student sample
Weakness: validity – guards may have exaggerated knowing they were observed

cards.front: Why can deindividuation lead to prosocial behaviour instead of antisocial behaviour?
cards.answer: Reduced personal accountability lets the crowd's prevailing norm take over, so a generous crowd mood produces more giving, not harm.

cards.front: How does culture affect how readily a person joins in with crowd behaviour?
cards.answer: Cultural norms about respect for authority, personal space and group solidarity affect how much an individual conforms to the crowd.

cards.front: Name the five common mistakes in Period Essays given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Storytelling / Shopping list conclusion / Undated evidence / Ignoring the question's concept / Abandoning the thesis at the end
items: Abandoning the thesis at the end

cards.front: Why is writing a 'storytelling' essay a mistake in a Period Essay?
cards.answer: It narrates events in order without analysis, so evidence isn't grouped by argument.

cards.front: Why must you address the question's concept, such as 'how far' or 'change', in every paragraph?
cards.answer: Ignoring the concept means only listing events instead of addressing extent, pace or limits as asked.

title: CPU Architecture and the Fetch-Execute Cycle
subject: computer-science-aqa

cards.front: Name the five main components inside the CPU.
cards.answer: ALU / Control unit / Clock / Registers / Bus

cards.front: Name the three factors that have the greatest effect on CPU performance.
cards.answer: Clock speed / Number of cores / Cache size

cards.front: Why is a cache hit faster than fetching data from RAM?
cards.answer: Cache sits close to the CPU, so if the data is already there it can be retrieved much faster than going to main memory.

cards.front: Why can registers be accessed faster than main memory?
cards.answer: Registers are tiny storage areas built directly onto the CPU chip itself, so access is much quicker than reaching main memory.

cards.front: Name the three reasons the lesson gives for the taiga's low productivity.
cards.answer: Short growing season / Cold soils slow microbial activity / Low-light angle for much of the year
items: Low-light angle for much of the year

cards.front: Name the four types of commercial threat to the taiga the lesson identifies.
cards.answer: Softwood logging / Fossil fuel extraction / Mining / HEP dams

cards.front: Why do taiga needles cut water loss and resist frost?
cards.answer: They have a waxy coating instead of broad leaves, which reduces water loss and resists frost.

cards.front: Why does the taiga risk switching from a carbon sink to a carbon source?
cards.answer: As permafrost thaws and fires release stored carbon, the taiga's huge carbon store starts entering the atmosphere instead.

title: Acts 2-3: Hath Not a Jew Eyes?
subject: english-literature-ocr

cards.front: Why does Shylock's 'Hath not a Jew eyes?' speech end by justifying revenge rather than pleading for peace?
cards.answer: Shylock argues Christians preach mercy but practise revenge, so he has learned cruelty from their example and will follow it.

cards.front: How does Antonio's lost ships change Shylock's situation with the bond?
cards.answer: Antonio cannot repay the loan, so the pound of flesh bond becomes enforceable and Shylock can pursue it.

title: Exam Practice: Performer, Director and Designer
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: In the row scene in Act Two Scene One, why might a director remove the underscore and use silence instead of sad music?
cards.answer: Music would soften the insults, so silence keeps the cruelty raw and unaccompanied as Delaney's dialogue intends.

cards.front: How does staging the flat on a thrust stage change the audience's experience compared to a proscenium arch?
cards.answer: On a thrust stage side audiences feel part of the cramped room with no fourth wall, making it feel inescapable, unlike the framed, distanced view a proscenium gives.

cards.front: Why does a calm, private smile from Jo in the final moment make her isolation feel more painful to the audience?
cards.answer: The audience knows Geof has left for good while Jo does not, so her calm contentment creates dramatic irony that sharpens her isolation.

cards.front: Name the four specific design choices the lesson gives for the freezing flat at the start of Act One Scene One.
cards.answer: Damp-stained wallpaper and sagging armchair / Unshaded practical bulb hung low / Distant tugboat horn / Low industrial hum fading in

cards.front: Name the four weaknesses of the Weimar 'Golden Age' recovery given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Dependence on American loans / Unemployment stayed above 1 million / Farmers struggled with low prices / Extremist parties still won Reichstag seats
items: Extremist parties still won Reichstag seats

cards.front: Name the four strengths of the Weimar economic recovery given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Industrial output surpassed pre-war levels / Exports rose / New housing was built / Wages increased for many workers

cards.front: Why did Stresemann call off passive resistance in the Ruhr in 1923?
cards.answer: To help end hyperinflation and stabilise the economy, though this angered nationalists as an unpopular decision.

cards.front: Why did right-wing nationalists like Hitler attack the Young Plan of 1929?
cards.answer: They argued Germany should not be paying reparations at all, even though the plan reduced the burden.

title: Characters: The Inspector and Mr Birling
subject: english-literature-aqa

cards.front: Why does the Inspector show the photograph to only one character at a time?
cards.answer: To stop the characters comparing stories, forcing each to face their guilt individually.

cards.front: Why does the Inspector use graphic language like 'burnt her inside out'?
cards.answer: To shock the characters and audience out of complacency and confront the real human cost of their actions.

title: The Endocrine System and Blood Glucose Control
subject: science-aqa

cards.front: Name the five hormones the lesson says the pituitary gland produces.
cards.answer: Growth hormone / FSH / LH / ADH / TSH

cards.front: Name the three treatments the lesson gives for Type 2 diabetes.
cards.answer: Carbohydrate-controlled diet / Increased exercise / Sometimes medication

cards.front: Why is Type 2 diabetes becoming more common worldwide?
cards.answer: Because rising obesity levels are increasing the number of people with insulin resistance.

cards.front: Why do hormonal responses act on a wider area of the body than nervous responses?
cards.answer: Because hormones are carried in the blood, which reaches target organs throughout the whole body.

cards.front: Why does Cassius's collaborative language ('ourselves', 'we') work so effectively on Brutus?
cards.answer: Brutus would never take orders, but responds to an appeal framed as between honourable equals.

cards.front: Why does Caesar dismiss the soothsayer's warning in Act 1, Scene 2?
cards.answer: His dismissal shows his arrogance and belief that he is above mortal danger.

cards.front: How does Shakespeare use Portia's self-wounding to challenge Elizabethan gender expectations?
cards.answer: It shows her willingness to endure pain and refusal to be dismissed as a weak woman, demanding equal treatment.

cards.front: Name the six types of music (Musikrichtungen) given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Popmusik / Rockmusik / klassische Musik / Rap/Hip-Hop / elektronische Musik / Jazz

cards.front: Name the six types of TV programme (Fernsehsendungen) given in the lesson.
cards.answer: die Seifenoper / die Nachrichtensendung / die Sportsendung / die Quizsendung / die Realityshow / die Serie

cards.front: Why does the adjective in 'Der Film ist gut' have no ending?
cards.answer: Because the adjective comes after the verb (predicative position), so it never takes an ending.

cards.front: How does the adjective ending change for a masculine noun after 'der' when it moves from nominative to accusative?
cards.answer: It changes from -e in the nominative (der neue Film) to -en in the accusative (den neuen Film).

cards.front: Name the three parts of the hypocaust heating system used in Roman baths.
cards.answer: Praefurnium (furnace) / Pilae (brick pillars under floor) / Tubuli (hollow wall tiles)

cards.front: Why did bathers often wear wooden-soled sandals in the caldarium?
cards.answer: The hypocaust heated the floor so much that sandals protected bathers' feet from the heat.

cards.front: Why were admission prices for the baths sometimes free?
cards.answer: Local politicians sponsored free bathing days as a form of public generosity, called euergetism, to win popularity.

cards.front: Why is combining literary and material sources the strongest way to study Roman baths?
cards.answer: Literary sources give personal accounts but only from upper-class men, while material remains show layout and heating but not experience or frequency.

cards.front: Name the three character contrasts (foils) the lesson gives as Delaney's dramatic method.
cards.answer: The Boy's tenderness exposes Peter's cruelty / Geof's devoted care exposes Helen's neglect / Jo's directness exposes Helen's evasion
items: The Boy's tenderness exposes Peter's cruelty
Geof's devoted care exposes Helen's neglect

cards.front: Why does Peter's departure at the end of his relationship with Helen confirm the audience's suspicions about him?
cards.answer: He leaves Helen for another woman, proving he was never interested in her as a person, only as a convenience.

cards.front: Why does Geof's departure from the play happen quietly rather than dramatically?
cards.answer: Helen destroys his relationship with Jo through homophobic bullying and Jo does not fight hard enough to keep him, so he leaves without drama.

title: Quantitative Chemistry: Mass, Moles and Concentrations
subject: science-aqa

cards.front: Name the five steps given for calculating the mass of a substance in a reaction.
cards.answer: Write the balanced chemical equation / Identify the molar ratio from the equation / Calculate moles of the known substance / Use the molar ratio to find moles of unknown substance / Convert moles back to mass using molar mass
items: Identify the molar ratio from the equation
Calculate moles of the known substance
Use the molar ratio to find moles of unknown substance
Convert moles back to mass using molar mass

cards.front: How do you work out the molar mass of a compound like CO₂?
cards.answer: Add up the relative atomic masses of all the atoms present in the compound.

title: Jerusalem Lost, Ransom Paid: Richard's Return and Capture
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name three routes home Richard could not use in October 1192, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Western Mediterranean (Philip controlled southern France) / Through Spain (coasts closed by treaties) / Through Italy (unsafe due to quarrel with Henry VI)
items: Through Italy (unsafe due to quarrel with Henry VI)

cards.front: Name four sources the lesson gives for raising Richard's ransom in England.
cards.answer: Quarter tax on income and moveables / Wool clip of Cistercian and Gilbertine monasteries / Church plate seized from cathedrals / Tallages on the Jewish community
items: Quarter tax on income and moveables
Wool clip of Cistercian and Gilbertine monasteries

cards.front: Why was Philip II's departure from the crusade a strategic disaster for Richard?
cards.answer: It removed part of the army, let Philip plot against Richard's French lands, and destroyed the legitimacy of a joint royal crusade.

cards.front: How did the ransom England paid for Richard shape problems John later inherited?
cards.answer: It exhausted the Treasury, hardened scutage as a substitute for knight service, and taught barons royal demands could escalate without limit.

title: Act 3: Hath Not a Jew Eyes?
subject: english-literature-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three Christian characters/parties and what each takes from Shylock.
cards.answer: Antonio takes his dignity / Jessica takes his family / The court takes his faith

cards.front: Why does Shylock justify his desire for revenge in the 'Hath not a Jew eyes?' speech?
cards.answer: He argues Christians taught him revenge by their own example, so his vengeance is learned imitation, not inherent villainy.

cards.front: How does Portia help Bassanio choose the correct casket without breaking her oath?
cards.answer: She has a song sung before his choice whose rhymes all end in '-ed', hinting at 'lead' without directly telling him.

title: Sources and interpretations of empire and war
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: The lesson names three key debates about the 1890-1918 period. What are they?
cards.answer: Was the First World War necessary? / Were the generals competent? / Did militancy or constitutional pressure win women the vote?
items: Was the First World War necessary?
Did militancy or constitutional pressure win women the vote?

cards.front: The lesson gives four reasons why historians' interpretations of the same events differ. What are they?
cards.answer: They write at different times / They ask different questions / They use different sources / They are influenced by their era's values
items: They are influenced by their era's values

cards.front: Why did Niall Ferguson's interpretation of WWI in The Pity of War differ from earlier historians'?
cards.answer: He wrote post-Cold War when empire and sacrifice were less unquestioned, had access to new archives, and asked a counterfactual question.

cards.front: How did the 'lions led by donkeys' interpretation of WWI become embedded in popular culture?
cards.answer: It was shaped by anti-war literature from Sassoon, Owen and Graves, then spread through plays like Oh, What a Lovely War! (1963).

cards.front: Name the five processes inside schools that the lesson says affect achievement.
cards.answer: Streaming / Setting / Labelling / Self-fulfilling prophecy / Development of anti-school subcultures

cards.front: Name the five things the lesson says pupils learn through the hidden curriculum.
cards.answer: Queue / Sit in silence / Accept the authority of the teacher / Observe punctuality / Behave in gender-appropriate ways
items: Accept the authority of the teacher

cards.front: How did Bowles and Gintis link the hidden curriculum to the correspondence principle?
cards.answer: They argued it prepares working-class pupils for factory discipline and routine employment rather than critical independent thinking.

cards.front: Why did Willis argue the lads' resistance still ended up reproducing class inequality?
cards.answer: Their resistance, though experienced as freedom, prepared them for working-class factory jobs just as effectively as conformity would have.

cards.front: Name the four features the lesson says the UK and USA democratic systems share.
cards.answer: Regular free elections / Independent judiciaries / Protection of civil liberties / Bicameral legislatures

cards.front: Name the four types of elections the lesson says US citizens can vote in.
cards.answer: Presidential elections / Congressional elections / Senate elections / State and local elections

cards.front: Why can the Electoral College produce a President who got fewer total votes than their opponent?
cards.answer: Because winning requires a majority of state electoral votes, not the national popular vote total.

cards.front: Why can citizens in China not vote to remove their national government?
cards.answer: Because China does not allow multi-party elections at national level, so political authority flows from the CCP rather than elected representatives.

title: Sound: Diegetic, Non-Diegetic, Score and Sound Bridges
subject: film-studies-eduqas

cards.front: According to the lesson, what three things does film sound tell the spectator?
cards.answer: How to feel / Where to look / What the world of the film means
items: What the world of the film means

cards.front: In the city-at-night sound design example, what three techniques build the spectator's dread?
cards.answer: Diegetic ambient sound establishing place / Silence creating tension / Non-diegetic leitmotif delivering threat information

cards.front: Why is a voice from an unseen character in the next room still classed as diegetic sound?
cards.answer: It exists inside the film's world, we just can't see the source at that moment.

cards.front: How does the way dialogue is mixed reveal a power relationship between two characters?
cards.answer: When one character's voice fills the whole soundscape while another's seems muffled or distant, the mix signals power.

cards.front: Why does Heaney structure the poem into sixteen lines then eight lines?
cards.answer: The unequal stanzas mirror how briefly the pleasure of picking lasts compared to how long the disappointment of rot stays.

cards.front: Why does Heaney compare the children's hands to Bluebeard's?
cards.answer: It hints that even a childhood pleasure like picking berries carries a shadow of guilt, since Bluebeard's hands were stained with blood.

cards.front: How does Heaney link the children's hunger to the fungus that ruins the fruit?
cards.answer: The fungus is shown 'glutting' on the store, suggesting desire itself can spoil what it seeks, just as the children were greedy.

title: Modern recruitment: conscription, women and the professional army
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four possible outcomes a WW1 or WW2 conscientious objector tribunal could give.
cards.answer: Absolute exemption / Conditional exemption / Non-combatant service in uniform / Refusal leading to court-martial

cards.front: Name the three older forms of compelled military service in Britain mentioned before 1916.
cards.answer: Medieval feudal duty / Eighteenth-century Militia Act ballots / Royal Navy impressment (press gangs)

cards.front: Why did the government introduce the Military Service Act in January 1916?
cards.answer: Casualties on the Western Front, especially at the Somme, outpaced volunteer recruitment, narrowing the government's political room for manoeuvre.

cards.front: Why did public attitudes towards conscientious objectors differ between 1914-18 and 1939-45?
cards.answer: In WW1 the white-feather campaign shamed objectors as cowards, but by WW2 opposition was tolerated more since fighting Nazi Germany was widely seen as morally justified.

cards.front: Name the three Gothic novels the lesson mentions, in order of publication, alongside Jekyll and Hyde.
cards.answer: Frankenstein (1818) / The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde (1886) / Dracula (1897)
items: The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde (1886)

cards.front: Why does Jekyll create Hyde, according to the lesson's reading of the novella?
cards.answer: Not because he is unusually evil, but because the pressure to appear respectable at all times is unbearable.

cards.front: How does Jekyll's loss of control over Hyde show Stevenson's warning about repression?
cards.answer: It shows repression doesn't remove desires but only makes their eventual release more violent and destructive.

title: Family Life: Birth, Bar and Bat Mitzvah, Marriage and Mourning
subject: religious-studies-aqa

cards.front: Name the four key Jewish life-cycle ceremonies the lesson describes.
cards.answer: Brit Milah / Bar/Bat Mitzvah / Wedding / Shiva and Kaddish

cards.front: Why do mourners cover mirrors and sit on low chairs during shiva?
cards.answer: The focus during shiva is entirely on honouring the deceased and supporting the grieving family, not on normal life or appearance.

cards.front: Why is a minyan needed for saying kaddish?
cards.answer: It draws mourners into the synagogue community and ensures they are surrounded by others while grieving.

cards.front: Why does Judaism hold a baby-naming ceremony (simchat bat) for girls instead of a physical rite?
cards.answer: No equivalent physical rite exists for girls, so communities instead welcome and name the girl before the congregation.

cards.front: Name the three people who plan to smuggle Magwitch down the Thames onto a foreign steamer.
cards.answer: Pip / Herbert / Startop

cards.front: Name the three things Pip has lost by the end of the novel.
cards.answer: His fortune / His status / His illusions

cards.front: Why does Dickens describe sunlight streaming through the courtroom windows as Magwitch is sentenced?
cards.answer: To create a cruel, ironic contrast between the beauty of the natural world and the brutality of human justice.

cards.front: Why is the revelation that Estella is Magwitch's daughter significant to the novel's ideas about class?
cards.answer: It shows Estella's supposed superiority was manufactured, not inherited, demolishing the idea that class is inherent.

title: The King's Great Matter and the Reformation Parliament
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Name the four key Acts that completed the legislative break from Rome, 1532-1534.
cards.answer: Submission of the Clergy (1532) / Act in Restraint of Appeals (1533) / Act of Supremacy (1534) / Treason Act (1534)

cards.front: How did the Submission of the Clergy (1532) weaken the Church's independence?
cards.answer: It made the Church accept it could not make new canon law without royal permission, ending its legislative independence.

cards.front: Why did Thomas Cranmer's appointment as Archbishop allow Henry to marry Anne Boleyn?
cards.answer: Cranmer held an ecclesiastical court that declared Henry's marriage to Catherine void, then confirmed his marriage to Anne valid.

cards.front: Why did Cardinal Wolsey lose his position in 1529?
cards.answer: He failed to secure the Pope's annulment of Henry's marriage to Catherine of Aragon, the 'Great Matter'.

cards.front: The lesson gives six distinct tasks that happen during post-production. Name them.
cards.answer: audio mixing and sound design / music licensing and composition / visual effects and colour grading / motion graphics or animated titles / quality assurance review / final export or delivery

cards.front: Why is it a mistake to say post-production just means 'editing the video'?
cards.answer: Because post-production covers many processes beyond editing, including audio mixing, VFX, colour grading, motion graphics and quality review.

cards.front: Name the three medical uses of radioactive materials described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Medical tracers / PET scans / Radiotherapy

cards.front: Name the three risks of nuclear power stations given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Possibility of accidents / Generation of long-lived radioactive waste / Security concerns around nuclear materials

cards.front: Why does alpha radiation become highly dangerous if the source is inside the body (contamination)?
cards.answer: Because alpha particles ionise tissue directly when the source is inside the body, even though alpha radiation is weakly penetrating from outside.

cards.front: Why are longer half-life beta emitters used for industrial thickness gauging rather than short half-life isotopes?
cards.answer: Because the source needs to last months or years in service without needing frequent replacement.

cards.front: Name the four questions the lesson gives for reading a poem's structure.
cards.answer: Where does it begin and end emotionally / Where is the turn / What repeats / How do the final lines land
items: Where does it begin and end emotionally
How do the final lines land

cards.front: Name the terminology the lesson lists as always safe to use on an unseen poem.
cards.answer: Stanza, quatrain, couplet / Refrain, rhyme scheme, half-rhyme / Enjambment, caesura, volta / Free verse, first person, present tense
items: Free verse, first person, present tense

cards.front: Why does a tight, regular rhyme scheme suit a poem making an argument feel proved?
cards.answer: It makes the poem sound settled and inevitable, so the argument feels resolved and certain.

cards.front: Why does a sudden break in a regular rhyme scheme deserve its own sentence in an analysis?
cards.answer: Because the break is a structural event, signalling a shift that needs separate explanation.

cards.front: Why does goal setting help motivate performers?
cards.answer: Goals give emotional fuel and a reference point to measure effort, so seeing the gap close between current and target ability makes each session feel worthwhile.

cards.front: Why does goal setting improve performance?
cards.answer: A goal gives the benchmark and endpoint for training so coaches can plan progressive overload; without it, improvement tends to plateau.

title: Your Fieldwork Approach for 2028: Transects and Place
subject: geography-eduqas

cards.front: Name the five kinds of transect enquiry listed in the specification.
cards.answer: Quality of life or environmental quality across an urban area / Micro-climate across a town or up a slope / Patterns of flow and deposition across a river channel / Vegetation patterns across a sand dune or woodland / Slope profiles and sediment sorting up a beach
items: Quality of life or environmental quality across an urban area
Micro-climate across a town or up a slope
Patterns of flow and deposition across a river channel
Vegetation patterns across a sand dune or woodland
Slope profiles and sediment sorting up a beach

cards.front: Name the five kinds of place enquiry listed in the specification.
cards.answer: Coastal features in two locations / River features in two locations / An ecosystem in two locations / Two villages or two urban environments / Quality of life in two neighbourhoods
items: Two villages or two urban environments
Quality of life in two neighbourhoods

cards.front: Why does choosing a wider sampling interval along a transect risk missing important data?
cards.answer: It covers more distance but may miss the point where the biggest change actually happens.

cards.front: Why must a place enquiry collect the same kind of evidence at both locations?
cards.answer: So the comparison between the two contrasting locations is fair.

cards.front: Name the five major themes the lesson says every Pride and Prejudice essay should connect to.
cards.answer: Pride and prejudice (self-knowledge) / Marriage and money / Class and social hierarchy / Appearance versus reality / Women and independence

cards.front: What do AO1, AO2 and AO3 require in an essay on Pride and Prejudice?
cards.answer: AO1: sustained critical response with references from extract and novel / AO2: analyse Austen's methods like irony and free indirect discourse / AO3: embed context such as Regency marriage and women's roles
items: AO1: sustained critical response with references from extract and novel
AO2: analyse Austen's methods like irony and free indirect discourse
AO3: embed context such as Regency marriage and women's roles

cards.front: Why does Austen's use of passive voice in the opening line matter?
cards.answer: It makes the marriage obsession sound like natural law rather than social pressure created by families.

cards.front: Why is the word 'must' significant in the novel's opening line?
cards.answer: It implies obligation, making it seem as though wealthy men have no choice but to marry.

cards.front: What are the three purposes of Zakah, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Purifies the giver from greed and selfishness / Supports those in genuine need / Reduces inequality within the ummah
items: Purifies the giver from greed and selfishness

cards.front: Name the six key ritual stages of Hajj described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Tawaf - circling the Ka'aba / Sa'i - walking between Safa and Marwa / Standing at Arafat / Muzdalifah - resting and collecting pebbles / Stoning the pillars at Mina / Animal sacrifice
items: Sa'i - walking between Safa and Marwa

cards.front: Why do pilgrims stop at Muzdalifah during Hajj?
cards.answer: They pray, rest under the open sky, and collect pebbles needed for stoning the pillars at Mina the next day.

cards.front: How does giving Zakah benefit the person who gives it?
cards.answer: It purifies wealth by removing attachment to possessions, develops generosity and compassion, and brings spiritual reward on the Day of Judgement.

title: SQL: Modifying Data with INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE
subject: computer-science-aqa

cards.front: Name the three SQL commands used to modify data in a database.
cards.answer: INSERT INTO / UPDATE / DELETE FROM

cards.front: Why should you run a SELECT query with the same WHERE condition before running an UPDATE or DELETE?
cards.answer: To confirm the condition targets exactly the intended rows, preventing accidental changes or data loss.

cards.front: Why must the student_id used in an INSERT into Enrolments already exist in the Students table?
cards.answer: Because the student_id is a foreign key, so you cannot enrol a student who doesn't exist.

cards.front: Name the three men who condemn Hero based only on what they saw from a distance at night.
cards.answer: Claudio / Don Pedro / Leonato

cards.front: Why is Don Pedro's support of Claudio's accusation significant?
cards.answer: It shows the accusation is not just one man's jealousy but an institutional assault, reinforced by pack mentality.

cards.front: Why does the Friar's plan use deception to fix a problem caused by deception?
cards.answer: Because observation proved unreliable, so only carefully managed lies can manipulate Claudio's emotions and reveal the truth.

cards.front: Name the three problems the lesson gives as the fundamental barriers to better medieval public health.
cards.answer: Poverty / Lack of central authority / No scientific understanding of disease spread
items: No scientific understanding of disease spread

cards.front: What three conditions does the lesson say public health involves managing, alongside clean water?
cards.answer: Waste disposal / Housing standards / Food safety

cards.front: Why did life expectancy fall so low in some industrial districts between 1800 and 1850?
cards.answer: Housing was built quickly with no sanitation, so overflowing cesspits and shared privies contaminated rivers used for water.

cards.front: How did removing the Broad Street pump handle change how disease spread was understood?
cards.answer: It showed cholera spread through contaminated water rather than miasma, a major step toward germ theory.

cards.front: Name the three ecological harms of metal extraction given in the lesson.
cards.answer: habitat and topsoil loss from open-cast mining / heavy metals leaching into waterways from tailings / carbon dioxide and sulphur dioxide from smelting
items: habitat and topsoil loss from open-cast mining
heavy metals leaching into waterways from tailings
carbon dioxide and sulphur dioxide from smelting

cards.front: Name the four non-ferrous metals covered in the lesson.
cards.answer: aluminium / copper / zinc / tin

cards.front: Why is stainless steel used for saucepan handles instead of copper?
cards.answer: Stainless steel is a poorer thermal conductor than copper, so it stays cooler to touch.

cards.front: Why does duralumin suit aircraft frames better than pure aluminium?
cards.answer: Duralumin has tensile strength close to mild steel while keeping aluminium's low density, giving strength without extra weight.

cards.front: Name the three environmental challenges the specification identifies for designers.
cards.answer: Deforestation / Increased CO2 levels leading to global warming / The need for fair trade
items: Increased CO2 levels leading to global warming

cards.front: Name the four ways designers can reduce a product's carbon footprint.
cards.answer: Choosing low-energy manufacturing methods / Sourcing local materials to cut transport emissions / Designing for energy efficiency during use / Making products last longer so replaced less often
items: Sourcing local materials to cut transport emissions
Designing for energy efficiency during use
Making products last longer so replaced less often

cards.front: Why might a designer choose manufactured boards like MDF or plywood instead of solid sustainable timber?
cards.answer: They use smaller offcuts and waste timber more efficiently than solid wood.

cards.front: Why does manufacturing in countries with lower wages create an economic and ethical challenge?
cards.answer: It reduces manufacturing costs but raises ethical concerns about workers' safety and conditions.

cards.front: Name the three things the lesson states about series circuits.
cards.answer: Current is the same at every point / Potential difference is shared between components / Total resistance equals sum of individual resistances
items: Current is the same at every point
Potential difference is shared between components
Total resistance equals sum of individual resistances

cards.front: Name the four things the lesson states about parallel circuits.
cards.answer: Potential difference is the same across each branch / Current splits between branches / Adding resistors decreases total resistance / Household circuits use parallel wiring
items: Potential difference is the same across each branch

cards.front: Why does static charge only build up on insulators and not conductors?
cards.answer: On insulators electrons cannot flow away, but on a conductor any excess charge immediately spreads out or flows to earth.

cards.front: Why does adding resistors in parallel decrease the total resistance of a circuit?
cards.answer: Because there are more paths for current to flow through.

cards.front: Name the three river courses and the dominant process shaping each.
cards.answer: Upper course – vertical erosion / Middle course – lateral erosion / Lower course – deposition

cards.front: Name the three UK estuaries given as examples.
cards.answer: Lower Severn / Thames / Humber

cards.front: Why does the flood plain beyond the levees become fertile farmland?
cards.answer: Floodwater slows as it spreads beyond the levees, dropping fine silt across the wider flood plain.

cards.front: Why does a wide estuary form at a river's mouth?
cards.answer: The river slows further as it meets the sea, and if the tide is strong this creates a wide estuary where fresh and salt water mix.

cards.front: Name the four religious changes England went through in the twenty-five years before Elizabeth's 1559 Settlement.
cards.answer: Henry VIII's break with Rome / Henry VIII as Supreme Head / Edward VI's Protestant reforms / Mary I's return to papal obedience
items: Mary I's return to papal obedience

cards.front: Why did Elizabeth retain traditional features like clerical vestments and the crucifix in the Chapel Royal?
cards.answer: To please moderate traditionalists and keep the settlement broadly acceptable, even though it frustrated committed Protestants who wanted plainer worship.

cards.front: Why did Elizabeth's 1559 Religious Settlement prove more stable than earlier religious changes in England?
