cards.answer: It was a genuine compromise pleasing no one perfectly, giving workable stability that survived her whole reign without civil war.

title: Sources of Wisdom and Forms of Expression in Christianity
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: What are the three ways the lesson describes Christians understanding the Bible's authority?
cards.answer: The literal Word of God / The inspired Word of God / A source of guidance and teaching
items: A source of guidance and teaching

cards.front: What are the traditional symbols of the four evangelists in Christian art?
cards.answer: Matthew - man or angel / Mark - lion / Luke - ox / John - eagle

cards.front: Why did the Filioque clause cause the Great Schism of 1054?
cards.answer: Western churches added 'and the Son' to the Nicene Creed without an Ecumenical Council, which Eastern churches saw as an unauthorised alteration.

cards.front: Why are icons used in Orthodox worship?
cards.answer: Icons act as 'windows into heaven', venerated as aids to prayer rather than worshipped as idols.

cards.front: Name the four groups disqualified from standing as a candidate in a UK general election.
cards.answer: Members of the House of Lords / Sitting judges / Undischarged bankrupts / Holders of certain Crown or civil service offices requiring political neutrality
items: Members of the House of Lords
Holders of certain Crown or civil service offices requiring political neutrality

cards.front: Name the four UK general election turnout figures given in the lesson, with their years.
cards.answer: 1992: around 78% / 2001: around 59% / 2019: around 67% / 2024: around 60%

cards.front: Why are sitting judges disqualified from standing for election as an MP?
cards.answer: To preserve the separation of powers between the judiciary and the legislature.

cards.front: Why do some political scientists argue low voter turnout is not necessarily a democratic crisis?
cards.answer: Non-voting can reflect satisfaction with the status quo, and citizens can engage through petitions, campaigns and pressure groups instead.

cards.front: Name the five marriage models Austen presents in the novel.
cards.answer: Elizabeth and Darcy / Jane and Bingley / Charlotte and Collins / Lydia and Wickham / Mr and Mrs Bennet

cards.front: Why does Elizabeth trust Wickham but distrust Darcy at first?
cards.answer: She judges by surface social performance — charm and openness — rather than evidence, mistaking manners for moral character.

cards.front: Why does Austen give Elizabeth a happy ending but not Charlotte or Lydia?
cards.answer: Austen rewards Elizabeth's combination of merit and luck in marrying up, showing the class system can recognise individual worth but still stands.

title: The First Intifada and Arafat's Turn, 1987–88
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four things the lesson says regulated Palestinian life under Israeli occupation.
cards.answer: Work permits into Israel / Identity cards / Military courts / Curfews

cards.front: Name the four different reactions to Arafat's December 1988 renunciation described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Over eighty states and the European Community welcomed it / Israeli government under Shamir refused to negotiate / Hamas rejected it and kept attacking / A minority on the Israeli left began arguing for talks
items: Over eighty states and the European Community welcomed it
Israeli government under Shamir refused to negotiate
Hamas rejected it and kept attacking
A minority on the Israeli left began arguing for talks

cards.front: Why did Rabin's 'iron fist' response to the Intifada backfire for Israel?
cards.answer: Mass arrests, school closures and orders to 'break the bones' of stone-throwers produced TV footage that turned international opinion against Israel.

cards.front: Why does Arafat's Geneva renunciation matter for later attempts to find a solution?
cards.answer: It unlocked direct US-PLO dialogue, made the PLO a recognised diplomatic partner, and made the Madrid Conference and Oslo Accords possible.

title: Karma, Reincarnation, Varna and Hindu Festivals
subject: religious-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four stages of life (ashramas) in Hinduism, in order.
cards.answer: Brahmacharya (student life) / Grihastha (householder) / Vanaprastha (forest-dweller) / Sannyasa (renunciant)

cards.front: Why do many Hindus in northern and western India light lamps and clean their homes at Diwali?
cards.answer: Lakshmi, goddess of wealth and prosperity, is believed to visit clean, well-lit homes.

cards.front: Why does ahimsa lead some Hindu communities into environmental activism, as shown by the Chipko movement?
cards.answer: Ahimsa teaches non-harm to all living beings, so villagers embraced trees to stop loggers cutting them down.

cards.front: How did Vivekananda's teaching challenge the idea that Dalits were spiritually inferior?
cards.answer: He taught that service to humanity was service to God, calling God present in the poor (daridra narayan).

cards.front: Name the ten factors the lesson gives as influencing food choice.
cards.answer: Physical activity level (PAL) / Food availability / Celebration/occasion / Cost and income / Preferences and enjoyment / Healthy eating and lifestyles / Seasonality / Time of day / Time available to prepare/cook

cards.front: Why might someone with a good understanding of nutrition still eat an unhealthy diet, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Structural barriers like cost, lack of time, poor access to fresh food, limited cooking facilities or caring responsibilities can override knowledge.

cards.front: Why does a food desert lead to poor diets even when people understand nutrition?
cards.answer: There is no affordable fresh-food retailer nearby, so people cannot access or afford vegetables even though they know they are nutritious.

cards.front: Why do taste preferences typically differ between young children and adults?
cards.answer: Young children prefer sweeter, milder flavours, while adults develop tolerance for bitterness like coffee and dark chocolate.

cards.front: Name the three traitors Henry exposes in Act 2, Scene 2 for plotting his assassination.
cards.answer: Cambridge / Scroop / Grey

cards.front: How does Henry trap Cambridge, Scroop and Grey into condemning themselves?
cards.answer: He asks their advice on pardoning a minor offender, and when they argue for severity, he uses their own words to justify executing them.

cards.front: Why does Bardolph's execution show that war is not all heroism in Henry V?
cards.answer: Henry, who once drank with Bardolph, allows his old companion's execution without mercy, revealing war's brutality for ordinary soldiers.

title: Industrial warfare c1700–c1900: weapons, transport and the cavalry’s decline
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three examples the lesson gives of trench-style warfare existing before 1914.
cards.answer: Naseby (1645) / Lines of Torres Vedras (1810) / Siege of Petersburg (1864–65)

cards.front: Name the three changes the lesson says drove the transformation of nineteenth-century warfare.
cards.answer: Rifled bullets gave infantry 600-yard reach / Rifled breech-loading artillery threw shells for miles / Steam railways and ships moved armies faster than horses
items: Rifled breech-loading artillery threw shells for miles
Steam railways and ships moved armies faster than horses

cards.front: Why did infantry abandon shoulder-to-shoulder lines during the nineteenth century?
cards.answer: Rifled weapons let soldiers massacre packed lines at long range, forcing officers to disperse men into open order and use cover.

cards.front: How did the Charge of the Light Brigade at Balaclava (1854) show the danger of old cavalry tactics?
cards.answer: It lost roughly 40 per cent of its men in twenty minutes against Russian guns, showing cavalry charges were becoming suicidal.

cards.front: According to the lesson, what four things do the clones demonstrate their humanity through?
cards.answer: Love (Kathy and Tommy) / Creativity (the Gallery, Tommy's art) / Memory (Kathy's narration) / Suffering (donation and completion)

cards.front: Why does the system in Never Let Me Go refuse to acknowledge the clones' humanity?
cards.answer: Because acknowledging it would make the organ donation programme morally indefensible, so denial is necessary for exploitation to continue.

cards.front: Why did Miss Emily's Gallery campaign to prove the clones' humanity fail?
cards.answer: Society did not want proof clones are human, as acknowledging it would make the organ programme unconscionable.

cards.front: How does Ishiguro show that conformity in the novel does not require force?
cards.answer: Guardians give partial knowledge and Hailsham builds habit and comfort, conditioning the clones to accept their purpose without question.

title: Biological Explanations and Eysenck's Personality Theory
subject: psychology-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three personality dimensions Eysenck identified in his theory of criminality.
cards.answer: Extraversion / Neuroticism / Psychoticism

cards.front: According to Eysenck, what three features work together to raise the risk of offending?
cards.answer: Under-arousal from high extraversion drives need for stimulation / High reactivity from high neuroticism causes impulsive action under stress / Aggression and low empathy from high psychoticism reduce concern for victims
items: Under-arousal from high extraversion drives need for stimulation
High reactivity from high neuroticism causes impulsive action under stress
Aggression and low empathy from high psychoticism reduce concern for victims

cards.front: Why might research testing Eysenck's theory with personality questionnaires lack validity?
cards.answer: Questionnaires rely on self-report, so answers can be distorted by social desirability bias.

cards.front: Why is Eysenck's theory questioned in terms of predicting who will actually offend?
cards.answer: Not every offender scores highly on all three dimensions, and some people with this profile never offend.

cards.front: Name the three things the lesson says Hobson is losing during Act 2.
cards.answer: Losing customers / Losing his daughters / Losing himself to drink

cards.front: What three sources of comedy does the lesson identify in Act 2?
cards.answer: Willie's baffled reactions to Maggie / The sisters' snobbery / Hobson's absurd attempts to assert authority
items: Hobson's absurd attempts to assert authority

cards.front: Why does the audience laugh at Hobson's decline even though he is suffering?
cards.answer: Because his downfall is the direct consequence of his own arrogance in refusing to value his daughters or Willie.

cards.front: Why does Willie struggle with reading and writing at the start of the play?
cards.answer: As a working-class child he was put to work instead of being sent to school, a direct result of his class position.

cards.front: Name the three main techniques the lesson says advertisers use to help people remember products.
cards.answer: Using cues / Using repetition / Avoiding overload

cards.front: Name the three memory functions the lesson says the Wechsler Memory Scale measures separately.
cards.answer: Immediate recall / Delayed recall / Working memory

cards.front: Why can't a customer recall an advert's message if there is no strong retrieval cue?
cards.answer: The information is still stored in memory, but it cannot be accessed because the right trigger is missing.

cards.front: How does reconstructive memory theory explain why autobiographical adverts can create false memories?
cards.answer: Memory is rebuilt using schemas and expectation, so a vivid personal-feeling scene can make a viewer reconstruct a memory including the product.

cards.front: Name the five qualities the lesson says a good friend must have (un bon ami doit être...).
cards.answer: fidèle (loyal) / honnête (honest) / gentil (kind) / patient (patient) / drôle (funny)

cards.front: Give the six present tense forms of aller shown in the lesson.
cards.answer: je vais / tu vas / il/elle/on va / nous allons / vous allez / ils/elles vont

cards.front: How do you form the near future tense (le futur proche) in French?
cards.answer: Use the present tense of aller plus the infinitive of the main verb.

cards.front: Why does the lesson recommend adding the near future tense to your writing or speaking?
cards.answer: Using multiple tenses, like adding a future time frame, helps you access higher marks in the exam.

cards.front: Name the four main effects e-commerce brings for a business, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Wider customer reach / Richer data on customer behaviour / Lower fixed costs per sale / Pressure on prices from easy comparison
items: Pressure on prices from easy comparison

cards.front: Name the four things the lesson gives as examples of after-sales service.
cards.answer: Help lines when something goes wrong / User training for complex products / Servicing like a boiler check or MOT / Easy returns or warranty claims
items: Help lines when something goes wrong
Servicing like a boiler check or MOT

cards.front: Why does free and simple returns work as after-sales service for ASOS?
cards.answer: A confident customer is more likely to order in the first place if returns won't be a hassle.

cards.front: How does good customer service eventually lead to higher profit?
cards.answer: Satisfaction rises, which breeds loyalty, giving repeat business that costs less to win than new customers, raising sales and profit.

title: Viceroys, Encomiendas, Las Casas and the New Laws
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four main provisions of the New Laws of 1542.
cards.answer: Banned outright enslavement of Indigenous peoples / No new encomiendas to be granted / Existing encomiendas to expire on holder's death / Royal officials, judges and clergy forbidden from holding encomiendas
items: Banned outright enslavement of Indigenous peoples
No new encomiendas to be granted
Existing encomiendas to expire on holder's death
Royal officials, judges and clergy forbidden from holding encomiendas

cards.front: Give the four examples of internal Spanish conflict the lesson uses to show Spain was not united in supporting conquest.
cards.answer: Velazquez against Cortes / Pizarro against Almagro / Las Casas against Sepulveda / The crown against the encomenderos

cards.front: Why did population collapse make the encomienda system worse over time?
cards.answer: As Indigenous communities shrank from disease, the same tribute demand fell on fewer people, intensifying the burden on survivors.

cards.front: Why did encomenderos in Peru rebel against the New Laws in 1544–48?
cards.answer: They refused to lose their encomiendas and rose under Gonzalo Pizarro after Nunez Vela arrived to enforce the laws.

cards.front: What three demands did workers make during the June 1953 East German uprising?
cards.answer: End to increased work norms / Lower food prices / Free elections

cards.front: The lesson says the SED's power rested on three things — what were they?
cards.answer: Soviet backing / The Stasi / The planned economy

cards.front: Why was the GDR able to avoid the de-Nazification process that West Germany undertook?
cards.answer: It presented itself as the legitimate successor of the anti-fascist resistance, positioning communists as moral heroes of the Nazi era.

cards.front: How did the Stasi's use of Zersetzung help prevent organised opposition?
cards.answer: It created an atmosphere of mutual suspicion so East Germans distrusted one another, achieving control without needing imprisonment.

cards.front: Name the three benefits of economic growth the lesson gives.
cards.answer: Higher living standards / Improved public services / More business investment and innovation

cards.front: Why does potential growth require more than just using spare resources?
cards.answer: Potential growth needs new investment, better technology or a larger, better-trained workforce to raise the economy's ceiling.

cards.front: Why can GDP per capita rise while the average person is no better off?
cards.answer: If the population grows at the same rate as real GDP, GDP per capita stays flat despite headline growth.

cards.front: Why can a boom lead to overheating in the economic cycle?
cards.answer: Demand outstrips supply so inflation accelerates and debts build up as growth runs above its long-run trend.

title: Physical Properties & Selecting Materials for Engineered Products
subject: engineering-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four products this lesson applies material properties to.
cards.answer: Mobile phone casing and screen / Home security alarm housing and sensor / Bicycle frame / Children's play area equipment
items: Home security alarm housing and sensor

cards.front: What three properties must a bicycle frame material have, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: High tensile strength / Good toughness / Low density

cards.front: Why are steel reinforcing bars embedded in concrete?
cards.answer: Concrete has low tensile strength, so steel bars compensate for this weakness under pulling forces.

cards.front: Why do aluminium alloy bicycle frames use larger-diameter tubes?
cards.answer: Aluminium is lighter but not as strong as steel, so larger tubes compensate for its lower strength while keeping the bike light.

title: Observing the Sun and Planets in Motion
subject: astronomy-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four stages of the observation cycle used when designing a solar or meteor observation.
cards.answer: Design / Make / Analyse / Evaluate

cards.front: Name the four items the lesson says are NOT safe for observing the Sun.
cards.answer: Welding glass below shade 14 / Old CDs / Unexposed film / Unfiltered binoculars or telescopes

cards.front: Why are Venus transits of the Sun so rare?
cards.answer: Venus transits occur in pairs 8 years apart, with the pairs separated by over a century.

cards.front: Why should observers look 45°-90° away from a meteor shower's radiant rather than straight at it?
cards.answer: Looking away from the radiant gives the longest meteor trails to observe.

cards.front: Why does the split chestnut tree still symbolise hope for Jane and Rochester's future?
cards.answer: The two halves stay connected at the roots, showing they are separated by Bertha's revelation but ultimately reconnected.

cards.front: Why does Jane see Rochester's plea to become his mistress as self-serving rather than compassionate?
cards.answer: Staying would make her a dependent mistress with no legal rights, the powerless position she has always fought against.

cards.front: Name the five things a plant can do with glucose made by photosynthesis.
cards.answer: Break it down in respiration for energy / Convert to starch for storage / Convert to cellulose for cell walls / Combine with nitrates to make amino acids/proteins / Convert to lipids for storage in seeds
items: Break it down in respiration for energy
Convert to cellulose for cell walls
Combine with nitrates to make amino acids/proteins
Convert to lipids for storage in seeds

cards.front: Name the four resources producers need for photosynthesis and growth.
cards.answer: Water / Carbon dioxide / Light / Mineral ions (nitrates and phosphates)

cards.front: Why does increasing carbon dioxide concentration increase the rate of photosynthesis?
cards.answer: CO2 is a raw material for the carbon-fixing stage, so more CO2 provides more molecules for the reaction, raising the rate.

cards.front: Why are seeds energy-rich foods?
cards.answer: Glucose from photosynthesis is converted into lipids, which are stored in seeds for energy.

cards.front: Name the three types of Hindu pilgrimage the lesson gives, with an example site for each.
cards.answer: Sacred river - the Ganges / Sacred city - Varanasi / Deity's childhood place - Vrindavana

cards.front: Why do Hindus perform seva (charity work) through organisations like Sewa UK?
cards.answer: Seva is selfless service expressing karma yoga and bhakti, reflecting the Bhagavad Gita's teaching that service to others is service to God.

cards.front: Why is the Ganges considered able to purify a person's karma?
cards.answer: The Ganges is regarded as the goddess Ganga Mata, whose waters purify karma and bless those who bathe in them.

cards.front: Name the twelve king-becoming graces Malcolm lists to Macduff.
cards.answer: Justice / Verity / Temperance / Stableness / Bounty / Perseverance, mercy, lowliness, devotion, patience, courage, fortitude
items: Perseverance, mercy, lowliness, devotion, patience, courage, fortitude

cards.front: Why does Macbeth order the murder of Lady Macduff and her children?
cards.answer: It is his most gratuitous crime, with no political benefit or threat to neutralise, showing pure tyranny.

cards.front: Why does Lady Macbeth speak in prose rather than verse during her sleepwalking scene?
cards.answer: Verse represents order and control, so switching to disordered prose shows her mind has fractured.

cards.front: Why does Malcolm pretend to be worse than Macbeth when he first meets Macduff?
cards.answer: He is testing Macduff's loyalty before trusting him, since a genuine reaction would prove his honesty.

cards.front: Name the three symbolic associations of the colour red in the red room scene.
cards.answer: Anger / Passion / Danger

cards.front: Name the three literary techniques the red room scene combines.
cards.answer: Pathetic fallacy / Gothic terror / Psychological realism

cards.front: Why does the red room scene foreshadow Jane's adult life?
cards.answer: It establishes a pattern she repeats later: choosing between submitting to unjust authority or asserting her own moral independence.

cards.front: Why is Brocklehurst's public humiliation of Jane significant for the novel's themes?
cards.answer: It shows how those with power can control a person's narrative, branding Jane a liar before she can speak for herself.

cards.front: Name the three types of corrective editing done before creative effects are applied to a mix.
cards.answer: Unwanted audio removal / Pitch correction / Rhythmic correction

cards.front: Name the three types of speakers/headphones used for monitoring during mixing.
cards.answer: Headphones / Main speakers / Near-field speakers

cards.front: Why does panning instruments across the stereo field improve a mix?
cards.answer: It creates width and separation between sounds, preventing a cluttered, mono-sounding mix.

cards.front: How does adding reverb make a sound seem further away in a mix?
cards.answer: More reverb versus dry signal increases apparent distance, while a dry, close-miked sound appears right in front of the listener.

cards.front: What are the four line shapes described on a distance-time graph and what motion do they show?
cards.answer: Horizontal line - stationary (speed = 0) / Straight diagonal line - constant speed / Curve getting steeper - accelerating / Curve getting shallower - decelerating

cards.front: What are the five typical speeds given in the lesson, with their approximate values?
cards.answer: Walking ~1.5 m/s / Running ~3 m/s / Cycling ~6 m/s / Car in town ~13 m/s (30 mph) / Speed of sound in air ~340 m/s
items: Speed of sound in air ~340 m/s

cards.front: Why does doubling an object's speed quadruple its kinetic energy?
cards.answer: Because kinetic energy equals 1/2 x mass x speed squared, so squaring a doubled speed gives four times the energy.

cards.front: Why does a car travelling at 40 mph need four times the braking distance of one at 20 mph?
cards.answer: It has four times the kinetic energy at double the speed, so four times as much energy must be removed to stop it.

cards.front: Name the six factors the lesson gives that decided an enslaved person's status within a familia.
cards.answer: Skill / Education / Cost / Length of service / Gender / Urban or rural location

cards.front: What two rewards did Varro recommend giving a trusted overseer to keep him loyal?
cards.answer: A female companion from other enslaved workers / A peculium (personal fund)
items: A female companion from other enslaved workers

cards.front: Why did Varro warn against buying too many enslaved people of the same nationality?
cards.answer: Because it was very often accustomed to cause domestic quarrels.

cards.front: How did Crassus force Spartacus's army into a final battle?
cards.answer: He built a wall across an isthmus to trap Spartacus's army.

title: The Great Famine and Recovery under Liu and Deng, 1959-65
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four causes the lesson gives for the Great Famine, layered over the same harvest.
cards.answer: Structural: communes destroyed peasant incentives / Scientific: quotas set on inflated yield figures / Personal: no one dared challenge Mao after Lushan / External: Soviet advisers withdrawn in 1960
items: Scientific: quotas set on inflated yield figures
Personal: no one dared challenge Mao after Lushan

cards.front: Name the four things sanzi yibao covered in the 1961-62 recovery reforms.
cards.answer: Private plots restored / Free rural markets reopened / Private sideline industries allowed / Household production contracts

cards.front: Why did grain keep being exported and sent to cities while villages starved during the famine?
cards.answer: Local cadres inflated yield figures out of fear of denunciation, so procurement quotas took grain that villages actually needed to survive.

cards.front: Why did Mao see Liu and Deng's recovery measures as a betrayal justifying the Cultural Revolution?
cards.answer: He viewed them as 'capitalist roaders' restoring the old order under a new label, even though their reforms stayed within socialist language.

cards.front: What are the three pillars on which Jack's power is built?
cards.answer: Violence (Roger as enforcer) / Ritual (the hunting chant) / Control of resources (Piggy's glasses/fire)

cards.front: What four things does Jack offer the boys that Ralph cannot?
cards.answer: Excitement / Meat / Certainty / A tribe to belong to

cards.front: Why does Piggy's death symbolise the destruction of both reason and democracy at once?
cards.answer: He is struck by a boulder and killed while holding the conch, so reason and democracy are destroyed together.

cards.front: Why do Sam and Eric end up joining Jack's tribe despite being loyal to Ralph?
cards.answer: After Piggy's death they are forced into the tribe through torture, showing decent people lack the strength to resist tyranny.

cards.front: Name the six major biomes that wrap the planet from the equator to the poles.
cards.answer: Tropical rainforest / Savanna / Hot desert / Temperate forest / Taiga (boreal forest) / Tundra

cards.front: Name the four layers of the tropical rainforest, from top to bottom.
cards.answer: Emergents / Canopy / Understory / Forest floor

cards.front: Why do rainforest trees have shallow roots that grab nutrients quickly?
cards.answer: So they can absorb nutrients from decomposing matter before heavy rainfall washes them through the thin soil.

cards.front: How does decomposition keep the rainforest nutrient cycle working?
cards.answer: Decomposers like bacteria, fungi and termites break down dead leaves and animals within weeks, quickly returning nutrients to living biomass.

cards.front: What are the three key ways to express obligation in Spanish given in this lesson?
cards.answer: Se debe + infinitive / Deber + infinitive / Tener que + infinitive

cards.front: Name the three modal verbs covered for talking about healthy living.
cards.answer: Deber (must, should) / Tener que (have to) / Poder (can, to be able to)

cards.front: Why is 'Debo como' wrong when using a modal verb?
cards.answer: Because after a modal verb the second verb must stay in the infinitive, not be conjugated.

cards.front: Why does the adjective in 'una dieta equilibrada' end in -a?
cards.answer: Because the adjective must agree with dieta, which is a feminine noun.

cards.front: Name the four things the lesson says to write down in your exam plan.
cards.answer: Your chosen comparison poem / 3–4 comparison points / Key quotations from both poems / One AO3 point per poem

cards.front: Name the five angles the lesson says each comparison point should address.
cards.answer: Language / Form / Structure / Imagery / Context

cards.front: Why does Owen's use of half-rhyme in Exposure create an unsettling effect?
cards.answer: It denies the reader a satisfying resolution, creating a dissonant atmosphere that mirrors the soldiers' own denied expectations of heroism.

cards.front: How does Weir's use of enjambment in Poppies convey the mother's grief?
cards.answer: The flowing enjambment creates a breathless, reaching quality, showing her grief overflowing the line just as it overflows her ability to contain it.

cards.front: Name the three forms of mass movement described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Sliding / Slumping / Rock falls

cards.front: Name the four processes of wave erosion at the coast.
cards.answer: Hydraulic power / Abrasion / Attrition / Solution

cards.front: How does solution (corrosion) erode limestone and chalk cliffs?
cards.answer: Slightly acidic seawater dissolves alkaline rock like limestone and chalk, slowly widening joints and helping caves form.

cards.front: Why does the beach profile get lower in winter?
cards.answer: Frequent Atlantic storms bring destructive waves with strong backwash that drag material offshore, exposing the cliff base.

cards.front: The lesson names five consequences of guilt that Macbeth and Lady Macbeth suffer. What are they?
cards.answer: Insomnia and nightmares / Paranoia and fear / Social isolation / Mental breakdown / Spiritual damnation

cards.front: What three reasons does Macbeth give in Act 1 Scene 7 for not killing Duncan?
cards.answer: Duncan is his king / Duncan is his kinsman / Duncan is his guest

cards.front: Why does Macbeth keep committing more murders after killing Duncan?
cards.answer: He commits increasingly brutal murders partly to silence his guilty conscience, but each crime only increases his torment.

cards.front: How does Lady Macbeth's early dismissal of guilt make her later breakdown ironic?
cards.answer: She claims water clears the deed, but later realises no perfume can sweeten her hand, showing guilt cannot be washed away.

cards.front: Name the three certainties the narrator loses over the course of the novel.
cards.answer: Belief in British superiority / Belief in human significance / Belief in the reliability of civilisation
items: Belief in the reliability of civilisation

cards.front: Why does Wells include the brother's alternative viewpoint of the London evacuation?
cards.answer: To show how the invasion affects people differently depending on their circumstances, contrasting with the narrator's experience.

cards.front: How does the curate's response to the invasion contrast with the narrator's?
cards.answer: The curate collapses into hysteria, selfishness and self-pity, while the narrator relies on pragmatic survival instinct.

title: Newspaper Front Pages: The Guardian and The Sun (2025 editions)
subject: media-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three colours The Guardian's house style uses in its front page design, and what each signals.
cards.answer: Deep sapphire blue - newsstand visibility and brand recognition / Red type near masthead - signals a news story / Yellow - used only for emphasis
items: Deep sapphire blue - newsstand visibility and brand recognition
Red type near masthead - signals a news story

cards.front: Why does the caption on The Guardian's balcony photo count as anchorage?
cards.answer: It explains the family are leaning left to see the flypast, turning an off-guard moment into a relatable, unified family scene.

cards.front: Why is the word 'rethink' used in The Guardian's headline instead of a more aggressive word?
cards.answer: It connotes careful reconsideration rather than panic, reflecting The Guardian's left-leaning sympathy with the Labour government.

cards.front: Why are the letters 'Y' and 'S' printed wonky in The Sun's 'Faulty Powers' headline?
cards.answer: They echo the misspelled hotel sign running joke in Fawlty Towers, implying chaos and incompetence in Britain's infrastructure.

title: Social policies, women and education under Mao
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Name the four activities the All-China Women's Federation carried out.
cards.answer: Ran literacy classes for women / Organised participation in cooperatives and communes / Campaigned for enforcement of Marriage Law / Mobilised women into political participation
items: Organised participation in cooperatives and communes
Campaigned for enforcement of Marriage Law

cards.front: Name the three changes made to higher education in China in 1952.
cards.answer: Technical institutes prioritised over humanities / Universities amalgamated and reorganised / Curricula rewritten around Marxist-Leninist ideology

cards.front: Why can the political education of the 1950s be linked to the Cultural Revolution a decade later?
cards.answer: The generation taught loyalty to Mao and class struggle in the 1950s became the deeply indoctrinated Red Guards of the 1960s.

cards.front: Why do historians caution against accepting the CCP's claim that it fully 'liberated' women?
cards.answer: Legal equality existed on paper, but rural social conservatism, inconsistent enforcement and stigma meant emancipation was partial in practice.

title: Immigration, the Red Scare and nativism
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: What three things did Marcus Garvey's UNIA promote, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Black economic self-sufficiency / pride in African heritage / an independent Black nation in Africa
items: an independent Black nation in Africa

cards.front: Why did the Palmer Raids eventually stop?
cards.answer: Legal challenges, cancelled deportation orders on due-process grounds, and Palmer's failed May Day revolution prediction damaged his credibility.

cards.front: How did the 1919 mail bombs affect action against radicals in the US?
cards.answer: Bombs targeting officials, including Palmer, intensified public demands for action, leading to the Palmer Raids.

cards.front: Why were Sacco and Vanzetti's trial and conviction seen as unfair?
cards.answer: Critics argued prosecution was driven by their immigrant background and anarchist beliefs, and the judge showed prejudice against them.

title: Music for Stage, Screen and Games
subject: music-aqa

cards.front: Name the four types of song in musical theatre the lesson describes.
cards.answer: "I want" song / Patter song / Reprise / Ballad

cards.front: Name the four film score techniques the lesson explains.
cards.answer: Leitmotif / Underscore / Mickey-mousing / Ostinato

cards.front: Why does game music need to loop and use layers rather than being written as one fixed recording?
cards.answer: A game has no fixed running time, so the music must loop indefinitely and react to whatever the player is doing right now.

cards.front: How does an ostinato build tension in a film score?
cards.answer: A short pattern repeats unchanged while more instruments are added on top, making the texture thicker and louder over time.

cards.front: Name the four disadvantages the lesson gives for using a programmable system instead of a hard-wired circuit.
cards.answer: requires programming knowledge / relies on power supply stability / software bugs can cause faults / initial setup more complex

cards.front: Why would a PLC be chosen over a microcontroller to control a bottling plant's conveyor and filling machines?
cards.answer: The PLC must run continuously without failure in a noisy factory environment, which a microcontroller isn't built to withstand.

cards.front: Why is a flowchart system a good choice for a teacher planning the logic of a new control system before coding it?
cards.answer: It lets you map out decision trees and loops visually before writing code, acting as a design document.

title: The Arms Race and the Space Race
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the three early Soviet space race achievements that gave the USSR the lead before Apollo 11.
cards.answer: Sputnik 1 (1957) / Gagarin's first crewed flight (1961) / Leonov's spacewalk (1965)

cards.front: According to the lesson, what three things did the Moon landings NOT change about the Cold War?
cards.answer: Thousands of warheads still pointed at each other / The Berlin Wall still stood / The Vietnam War was still raging
items: Thousands of warheads still pointed at each other
The Vietnam War was still raging

cards.front: Why did Kennedy pledge in May 1961 to land a man on the Moon before the decade was out?
cards.answer: To let the West reclaim the symbolism the Soviets had captured with Sputnik and Gagarin, since the Soviets led in spectacular firsts.

cards.front: How did MIRVs, deployed by 1970, make arms control harder?
cards.answer: MIRVs let one rocket carry several warheads, so the count that mattered became cheaper-to-produce warheads rather than rockets.

title: Music for Ensemble 3: Musical Theatre and Chamber Groups
subject: music-eduqas

cards.front: What three techniques let four string players create a texture as full as a small orchestral section?
cards.answer: Spacing chords across the full pitch range / Double-stopping (playing two notes at once) / Interweaving countermelodies so no moment sounds thin
items: Spacing chords across the full pitch range
Interweaving countermelodies so no moment sounds thin

cards.front: What three techniques does a wind quintet use to avoid gaps in the texture?
cards.answer: Horn sustains harmony notes or extends the bass register / Bassoon doubles or reinforces the bass line / Upper woodwind share melodic material through imitation or alternating register
items: Horn sustains harmony notes or extends the bass register
Bassoon doubles or reinforces the bass line
Upper woodwind share melodic material through imitation or alternating register

cards.front: Why does a homophonic duet in musical theatre suggest agreement or romantic unity between two characters?
cards.answer: Both voices move together in the same rhythm, often in thirds or sixths, showing the characters are aligned.

cards.front: Why do wind quintet composers often write dialogue-like passages where instruments answer or interrupt each other?
cards.answer: The five instruments have strikingly different timbres, so composers exploit that contrast instead of blending them into one sound.

cards.front: What three things does choosing the right data type decide?
cards.answer: Which operations are allowed / How much memory is used / Whether invalid data can be caught early
items: Whether invalid data can be caught early

cards.front: Why does adding two numbers typed as input without casting give "23" instead of 5?
cards.answer: Because the inputs are read as strings, and adding strings joins them end-to-end rather than performing arithmetic.

cards.front: Why are arrays and loops so often used together?
cards.answer: Because a single loop can visit each index in turn, so the same few lines work whether there are 30 items or 3000.

title: Engineering Processes — Marking, Cutting, Shaping & Drilling
subject: engineering-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four key marking-out tools listed in the lesson.
cards.answer: Scriber / Centre punch / Try-square / Vernier calipers and steel rule

cards.front: What five shapes can a centre lathe produce from round bar stock, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Face off a flat end / Turn down a diameter / Drill along the axis / Cut threads / Produce tapers

cards.front: Why must drill speed be reduced when drilling harder materials or using larger drill bits?
cards.answer: To avoid overheating and breaking the drill bit.

cards.front: Why is a bandsaw useful for cutting curved shapes compared to a hacksaw?
cards.answer: It uses a continuous toothed blade loop and can cut thicker material much faster, suiting curved cuts.

title: Increasing Food Supply: Strategies & Sustainable Futures
subject: geography-aqa

cards.front: Name the six key strategies the lesson gives for increasing food supply.
cards.answer: Irrigation / Aeroponics and hydroponics / New Green Revolution (biotechnology/GM crops) / Appropriate technology / Organic farming / Urban farming

cards.front: What features make sand dams an example of appropriate technology?
cards.answer: Use simple materials (concrete, rock, labour) / Need no electricity or pumps / Can be maintained by the community without engineers / Last 50 years or more / Fit the landscape by using seasonal sand rivers
items: Can be maintained by the community without engineers
Fit the landscape by using seasonal sand rivers

cards.front: Why did the original 1960s-70s Green Revolution fail to fully solve food insecurity?
cards.answer: It relied on expensive inputs poor smallholders couldn't afford, favoured irrigated lowlands over rain-fed uplands, and damaged soils and water tables through chemical overuse.

cards.front: Why is the Indus Basin Irrigation System vulnerable in the long term?
cards.answer: It partly relies on meltwater from Himalayan glaciers, which are retreating due to climate change, threatening future water availability.

cards.front: Familiaris Consortio names four tasks of the family. What are they?
cards.answer: Forming a community of persons / Serving life / Participating in the development of society / Sharing in the life and mission of the Church
items: Participating in the development of society
Sharing in the life and mission of the Church

cards.front: What five types of family structure does the Church recognise as existing in 21st-century society?
cards.answer: Nuclear / Single-parent / Same-sex parent / Extended / Blended

cards.front: Why does Catholic teaching say artificial contraception violates the full meaning of the sexual act?
cards.answer: Because it deliberately removes the procreative dimension, artificially separating it from the unitive dimension which cannot be split apart.

cards.front: Why is the family called 'the domestic church' in Catholic teaching?
cards.answer: Because it is the first place where faith is lived and passed on to children.

title: Citizens in Action: Two Case Studies
subject: citizenship-aqa

cards.front: Name the four methods disability rights organisations used to campaign for stronger equality protections.
cards.answer: Direct advocacy to MPs and ministers / Evidence submissions to parliamentary committees / Public awareness campaigns / Legal challenges under existing equality legislation
items: Direct advocacy to MPs and ministers
Legal challenges under existing equality legislation

cards.front: Name the three citizenship principles the lesson says the Hillsborough case illustrates.
cards.answer: Ordinary citizens can challenge state institutions and win justice / Legal processes are an important route alongside political pressure / Meaningful change in complex cases takes decades of perseverance
items: Ordinary citizens can challenge state institutions and win justice
Legal processes are an important route alongside political pressure
Meaningful change in complex cases takes decades of perseverance

cards.front: How did the disability rights campaign combine insider and outsider tactics?
cards.answer: They used insider tactics like formal consultations and committee evidence alongside outsider tactics like public campaigns and demonstrations.

cards.front: Why is it a misconception to judge citizenship campaigns as either fully succeeding or fully failing?
cards.answer: Campaigns can partially succeed, such as changing awareness without changing law, so outcomes should be judged in nuanced terms.

title: Conservation of Energy, Efficiency and Energy Resources
subject: science-aqa

cards.front: Name the seven renewable energy resources given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Solar / Wind / Hydroelectric / Tidal / Geothermal / Wave power / Biofuels

cards.front: Name the three types of home insulation the lesson gives that reduce thermal energy loss.
cards.answer: Loft insulation / Cavity wall insulation / Double glazing

cards.front: How does double glazing reduce heat loss from a house?
cards.answer: A layer of gas between two panes of glass reduces energy transfer by conduction and convection.

cards.front: Why is a mix of energy resources needed to ensure a reliable electricity supply?
cards.answer: Because many renewable resources are weather- or location-dependent, so they can't always supply enough energy alone.

cards.front: Name the three personality dimensions in Eysenck's PEN model that he linked to criminality.
cards.answer: High psychoticism / High extraversion / High neuroticism

cards.front: Why does high neuroticism make self-control harder in stressful situations, according to Eysenck?
cards.answer: The ANS reacts too quickly and strongly to stress and the limbic system amplifies fear and anxiety, making self-control harder.

cards.front: Why did Eysenck argue extraverted children take longer to learn moral restraint?
cards.answer: Because they are chronically under-aroused, their anxiety response is weaker, so punishment does not condition them as effectively.

cards.front: Why does Heaven's (1996) study only offer limited support for Eysenck's theory?
cards.answer: Psychoticism predicted delinquency at the same time but was a weak predictor of delinquency two years later.

cards.front: Name the four state symbols used in chemical equations and what they mean.
cards.answer: (s) solid / (l) liquid / (g) gas / (aq) dissolved in water

cards.front: Why does Al2O3 have the formula Al2O3 rather than AlO for aluminium oxide ions Al3+ and O2-?
cards.answer: Two Al3+ ions (total +6) balance three O2- ions (total −6) so the overall charge is zero.

cards.front: Why must a coefficient be added instead of changing a subscript when balancing an equation?
cards.answer: Changing a subscript would change the ratio of atoms and so change the identity of the substance.

cards.front: How do you find the number of moles in 44g of CO2 (Mr = 44)? (Higher)
cards.answer: Divide the mass by the relative formula mass: 44 ÷ 44 = 1 mole.

cards.front: Name the three examples the lesson gives of Newton's Third Law pairs in action.
cards.answer: Pushing a wall (wall pushes back equally) / Gravity pulling you down (you pull Earth up equally) / Swimmer pushing water back (water pushes swimmer forward)
items: Pushing a wall (wall pushes back equally)
Gravity pulling you down (you pull Earth up equally)
Swimmer pushing water back (water pushes swimmer forward)

cards.front: Name the three factors the lesson says air resistance depends on.
cards.answer: Speed / Surface area / Shape

cards.front: Why does a falling skydiver eventually stop accelerating and reach terminal velocity?
cards.answer: As speed increases air resistance increases until it equals weight, making resultant force zero.

cards.front: Why does a skydiver slow down when their parachute opens?
cards.answer: The bigger surface area makes air resistance suddenly much greater than weight, decelerating the skydiver.

cards.front: How does a microwave oven heat food?
cards.answer: Microwaves cause water molecules in the food to vibrate, which heats it.

cards.front: Why can long wave radio signals travel around hills but short wave signals reach distant places via the sky?
cards.answer: Long wave can diffract around hills, while short wave reflects off the ionosphere for long-distance communication.

cards.front: Name the three rules for drawing electric field lines given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Field lines run from positive to negative / Field lines never cross each other / Closer lines together mean a stronger field
items: Field lines run from positive to negative
Field lines never cross each other
Closer lines together mean a stronger field

cards.front: Name the four practical applications of static electricity described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Electrostatic paint spraying / Inkjet printers / Photocopiers and laser printers / Electrostatic precipitators

cards.front: Why does a charged comb attract small, uncharged pieces of paper?
cards.answer: The charge on the comb induces a redistribution of charge in the paper, attracting the opposite charge on the near side.

cards.front: How does lightning form in a thundercloud?
cards.answer: Colliding ice crystals and water droplets transfer charge, making the cloud base negative and the ground below positive; the air ionises and discharges when the potential difference is large enough.

cards.front: What are the five stages of Scrooge's emotional arc, one per stave?
cards.answer: Isolation and cruelty (Stave 1) / Regret and emotional vulnerability (Stave 2) / Guilt and growing compassion (Stave 3) / Terror and repentance (Stave 4) / Joy, generosity, and redemption (Stave 5)

cards.front: Name the five characters the lesson says act as contrasting foils to Scrooge, and the quality each highlights.
cards.answer: Bob in generosity / Fred in warmth / Fezziwig in employer kindness / Belle in emotional openness / Marley as a warning

cards.front: Why does Dickens show us Scrooge's lonely childhood in Stave 2?
cards.answer: To present Scrooge as a product of his experiences rather than simply a villain.

cards.front: Why is it significant that Tiny Tim 'did NOT die' after Scrooge changes?
cards.answer: It shows that individual generosity can save lives, reversing the fatal consequences of neglecting the poor.

cards.front: Name the four metal finishing processes described for protecting metal from corrosion.
cards.answer: Dip coating / Powder coating / Galvanising / Anodising

cards.front: Name the five factors that decide which finish to choose for a product.
cards.answer: Material category / Product's environment (indoor/outdoor, wet/dry) / Desired appearance / Cost / Whether it needs to be food-safe
items: Whether it needs to be food-safe

cards.front: How does galvanising protect steel from rusting?
cards.answer: The zinc coating acts as a sacrificial layer, corroding before the steel underneath can rust.

cards.front: How does anodising increase aluminium's resistance to corrosion?
cards.answer: It is an electrochemical process that thickens the natural oxide layer on aluminium, making it harder and more corrosion resistant.

cards.front: Name the three biographical facts the lesson gives about Dickens that shaped his writing.
cards.answer: His father was imprisoned for debt / He worked in a blacking factory as a child / He used fiction as a weapon for social change
items: His father was imprisoned for debt
He worked in a blacking factory as a child
He used fiction as a weapon for social change

cards.front: Why did the Victorian wealthy believe poverty was a moral failing?
cards.answer: They believed if you were poor it was because you were lazy or immoral, letting them ignore suffering with a clear conscience.

cards.front: Why did Dickens deliberately set A Christmas Carol at Christmas?
cards.answer: Christmas was linked to rising traditions of generosity and family, so it connected his message of social responsibility to readers already thinking about goodwill.

cards.front: How does Marley's chain reflect the Gothic theme in A Christmas Carol?
cards.answer: It shows the Gothic idea that past sins have the power to curse your future.

cards.front: Name the four main printing methods used to apply colour to fabric described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Block printing / Screen printing / Digital (inkjet) printing / Sublimation printing

cards.front: Name the four barriers stopping smart/e-textiles becoming mainstream.
cards.answer: Electronics must survive washing, bending and sweat / Data privacy concerns from biometric monitoring / High costs from small production volumes / Hard to separate electronics from fabric for recycling
items: Electronics must survive washing, bending and sweat
Data privacy concerns from biometric monitoring
High costs from small production volumes
Hard to separate electronics from fabric for recycling

cards.front: Why must disperse dyes be applied under high temperature and pressure for polyester?
cards.answer: The dye molecules have to physically enter the fibre structure, which polyester only allows under heat and pressure.

cards.front: Why does quilting improve the warmth of a fabric?
cards.answer: Two fabric layers are stitched together with wadding in between, and the wadding traps air, providing insulation.

title: Second Civil War, Pride's Purge and regicide
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Name the three regions where Royalist uprisings broke out in the Second Civil War (1648).
cards.answer: Kent / Essex / Wales

cards.front: Why did the Rump Parliament proceed with Charles I's trial without the House of Lords?
cards.answer: The Lords refused to participate in setting up the High Court of Justice, so the Rump went ahead without them.

cards.front: How did Charles I's refusal to plead affect the fairness of his trial?
cards.answer: Because he refused to acknowledge the court, no defence was mounted, making the proceedings one-sided.

cards.front: What four impulsive actions show Romeo's hamartia driving the tragedy?
cards.answer: Falls in love instantly / Marries within 24 hours / Kills Tybalt in rage / Commits suicide without checking Juliet is truly dead
items: Commits suicide without checking Juliet is truly dead

cards.front: What three things should you examine when analysing Romeo and Juliet's characters?
cards.answer: Their language changes / Their interactions with other characters / How they respond to conflict

cards.front: How does dramatic irony affect the audience's experience of Romeo and Juliet's story?
cards.answer: The audience already knows their fate from the Prologue, which adds poignancy to the lovers' hopes and plans.

cards.front: How does Juliet's relationship with her parents change as the play progresses?
cards.answer: She starts respectful and obedient but becomes increasingly defiant as her love for Romeo grows, reflecting generational conflict.

cards.front: Name the three things the lesson says the Fitzgeralds provide Alem with.
cards.answer: Warmth / Stability / A sense of belonging

cards.front: Name the three things Alem learns as he adjusts to life in England.
cards.answer: The rhythms of school / The Fitzgeralds' household routines / The social codes that confused him
items: The social codes that confused him

cards.front: Why do Mustapha and Alem stand together against Sweeney?
cards.answer: Because Mustapha has also been bullied by Sweeney, so the two boys share the experience of hostility and support each other.

cards.front: Why is the Fitzgeralds' relationship with Alem always complicated, despite their love for him?
cards.answer: Because it is temporary — Alem's future depends on the asylum hearing, not on the Fitzgeralds' love for him.

cards.front: Name the six stages of the novel's progressive collapse from order to chaos, in order.
cards.answer: Conch establishing order / Signal fire going out / Jack's tribe splitting / Simon's murder / Piggy's death and conch destruction / The manhunt

cards.front: What are the four parts of the PEAC essay paragraph structure?
cards.answer: Point / Evidence / Analysis / Context

cards.front: Why does Jack's authoritarian leadership prove more effective than Ralph's democratic leadership?
cards.answer: Democratic leadership needs people to consent, whereas Jack offers simple answers, exploits fear, and punishes dissent without needing consent.

cards.front: Why does fear give Jack more power than Ralph and Piggy's reasoning?
cards.answer: Fear is a more powerful motivator than logic, so Jack's promise to hunt the beast attracts followers away from rational reassurance.

title: Vietnamisation, Paris and Why the US Lost, 1969-75
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four overlapping reasons the lesson gives for why the United States lost the Vietnam War.
cards.answer: Strengths of North Vietnam and the Vietcong / Failure of US tactics / Political weakness of South Vietnam / Impact of opposition at home
items: Strengths of North Vietnam and the Vietcong

cards.front: What four terms did the January 1973 Paris Peace Agreement set out?
cards.answer: US forces withdraw within sixty days / American POWs returned / A ceasefire in place / Political talks among the Vietnamese parties
items: US forces withdraw within sixty days
Political talks among the Vietnamese parties

cards.front: Why did Vietnamisation fail to solve South Vietnam's strategic problem despite ARVN growing to around 1.1 million men?
cards.answer: South Vietnam still had no rural legitimacy and the ARVN was riven by corruption, desertion and politically appointed officers who broke in combat.

cards.front: Why did South Vietnam collapse so quickly to the North Vietnamese offensive in 1975?
cards.answer: Watergate forced Nixon's resignation, Congress slashed aid to Saigon, and ARVN units collapsed as officers abandoned their men.

cards.front: What five demands does Hari's notice in Scene Two make for lascar crewmates?
cards.answer: Equal pay with white sailors / Equal food and water rations / No more beatings / Rest periods between heavy labour / Recognition as members of the human race
items: Recognition as members of the human race

cards.front: Why does the royal household force Victoria to retract Abdul's higher honour in 1897?
cards.answer: The Prince of Wales insists the Munshi is not their equal and refuses to travel with him unless she backs down.

cards.front: Why is Dadabhai disillusioned and packing to return to India by 1900?
cards.answer: Years of believing in British fairness were undone by famine and plague in India and the Boer War's concentration camps.

cards.front: Name the five types of constraint the lesson says investigations can face.
cards.answer: Time constraints / Cost constraints / Ethical issues / Confidentiality concerns / Convenience

cards.front: Name the three strategies the lesson gives for reducing non-response.
cards.answer: Keep questionnaires short / Offer an incentive / Follow up with reminders

cards.front: Why might a study on seasonal behaviour give misleading results if data collection is limited to one month?
cards.answer: Behaviour like ice cream sales or flu cases varies across the year, so a short collection window misses the full seasonal picture.

cards.front: Why is convenience a constraint on some investigations?
cards.answer: The ideal population may not be realistically accessible, such as surveying a random sample of all UK secondary school students.

cards.front: Name the three everyday examples of exothermic reactions given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Combustion (e.g. burning methane) / Neutralisation (acid + alkali) / Hand warmers (iron reacting with oxygen)

cards.front: Name the three ways given to reduce error when measuring temperature change in a calorimetry experiment.
cards.answer: Use a lid on the cup / Take readings quickly / Use a digital thermometer
items: Use a lid on the cup

cards.front: Why does even an exothermic reaction need an initial energy input to start?
cards.answer: Because bonds in the reactants must first be broken, which requires energy, before new bonds can form and release energy.

cards.front: How do you calculate the overall energy change of a reaction using bond energies?
cards.answer: Subtract the total energy released making bonds in the products from the total energy needed to break bonds in the reactants.

title: Europe in 1894: Empires, Alliances and the Long Fuse
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: According to the lesson's key fact, what distinct national interest did each of the five Great Powers pursue in 1894?
cards.answer: British empire and naval supremacy / French recovery of Alsace-Lorraine / German industrial expansion / Austro-Hungarian unity of a multi-ethnic empire / Russian access to the Mediterranean
items: Austro-Hungarian unity of a multi-ethnic empire

cards.front: Why did Bismarck deliberately keep Germany's ambitions modest and avoid major colonial expansion?
cards.answer: He feared a 'nightmare of coalitions' where France gained powerful allies and Germany faced a war on two fronts.

cards.front: Why did France and Russia form an alliance in 1894 despite being very different political systems?
cards.answer: A shared interest in containing Germany pulled them together, reinforced by French capital funding Russian railway and industrial projects.

cards.front: Name the three main tools governments have for managing the economy.
cards.answer: Fiscal policy (spending and taxation) / Monetary policy (interest rates) / Supply-side policies

cards.front: What is the five-step chain of reasoning linking education and training investment to higher real GDP?
cards.answer: Better training / Higher productivity / Lower average costs for firms / Lower prices and greater competitiveness / Higher real GDP

cards.front: Why does privatisation tend to improve the efficiency of a business that used to be state-owned?
cards.answer: Private firms are driven by the profit motive, giving them stronger incentives to cut costs, improve efficiency and respond to consumers than government-run enterprises.

cards.front: Why can deregulation increase competition and lower prices in a market?
cards.answer: Removing rules that raise firms' costs lowers barriers to entry, attracting new firms, increasing competition and consumer choice.

cards.front: Why does Priestley place Birling's confident speeches immediately before the Inspector's arrival?
cards.answer: So the audience already sees Birling's views as wrong and are primed to side with the Inspector against him.

cards.front: Why does the Inspector pause and look hard at people before speaking?
cards.answer: It gives him power over the conversation by forcing the Birlings to wait in uncomfortable silence.

cards.front: Why does Sheila's reaction to sacking Eva differ from her father's reaction to sacking Eva?
cards.answer: Sheila feels immediate genuine remorse and accepts responsibility, while Birling tries to justify his actions, showing the generational divide.

cards.front: Why does Priestley keep Eva Smith absent from the stage throughout the play?
cards.answer: So the audience focuses on judging the Birlings' guilt rather than pitying Eva as an individual victim.

title: Ethical, Cultural, Environmental and Privacy Impacts
subject: computer-science-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three ethical issues that appear regularly in extended-response computing questions.
cards.answer: Privacy / AI bias / Automation's impact on employment

cards.front: Name the three contexts in which the lesson says the digital divide exists.
cards.answer: International, between high- and low-income countries / Domestic, between urban and rural areas / Domestic, between older and younger generations
items: International, between high- and low-income countries
Domestic, between urban and rural areas
Domestic, between older and younger generations

cards.front: Why do civil liberties organisations object to mass surveillance by governments?
cards.answer: Because monitoring everyone rather than targeting suspects chills free expression and presumes guilt rather than innocence.

cards.front: How does the energy mix used by a data centre affect its environmental impact?
cards.answer: Data centres powered by renewable sources have a much lower carbon footprint than those powered by coal or gas.

cards.front: Name the four types of barriers to inclusion in care settings given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Physical (no wheelchair access) / Communicative (no BSL interpreter) / Attitudinal (staff assumptions about age/ethnicity) / Systemic (referral pathways excluding those without fixed address)
items: Systemic (referral pathways excluding those without fixed address)

cards.front: Why does exclusion from services harm an individual's well-being, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Excluded individuals experience worse health outcomes, greater isolation and lower levels of well-being.

cards.front: How does being included in the community support a positive self-concept?
cards.answer: Being included in their community makes an individual feel valued, which supports a positive self-concept.

cards.front: Name the five metal ions and the flame colours the lesson gives for flame tests.
cards.answer: Lithium - crimson / Sodium - yellow / Potassium - lilac / Calcium - red-orange / Copper - blue-green

cards.front: Why can flame tests only tell you which metal is present, not how much?
cards.answer: Flame tests are qualitative tests, so they identify the metal ion present but give no information about its quantity.

cards.front: In fractional distillation, why do lower boiling point liquids get collected first?
cards.answer: Liquids with lower boiling points travel further up the fractionating column and are collected first.

cards.front: Name the four ways the lesson says pathogens can be transmitted between organisms.
cards.answer: Air (droplets) / Water (contamination) / Direct contact / Vectors (e.g. mosquitoes)

cards.front: Name the four measures the lesson gives for reducing the spread of communicable diseases.
cards.answer: Hygiene measures / Destroying vectors / Isolation of infected individuals / Vaccination

cards.front: How does vaccination give immunity without causing the disease?
cards.answer: It introduces dead or inactive pathogen, stimulating white blood cells to make antibodies and memory cells without illness.

cards.front: How does overuse and misuse of antibiotics lead to antibiotic-resistant bacteria?
cards.answer: Overuse and misuse of antibiotics drives the evolution of bacteria that survive treatment, creating resistant 'superbugs'.

cards.front: Name the three cephalopod groups used as zone fossils, based on suture-line complexity.
cards.answer: Goniatites / Ceratites / Ammonites

cards.front: Why can biostratigraphy be used to correlate rock outcrops on different continents?
cards.answer: The same zone fossil, with its short time range, appears in rocks worldwide, acting as a time stamp regardless of location.

cards.front: How does using two overlapping zone fossil ranges improve the precision of dating a rock bed?
cards.answer: The bed's age must fall within the overlap of both fossils' ranges, narrowing the estimate more than either fossil alone.

title: Invasion of the Body Snatchers and E.T.: Aliens and Anxiety
subject: film-studies-eduqas

cards.front: The lesson names four filmic techniques Invasion of the Body Snatchers uses to construct the alien as a threat. What are they?
cards.answer: Monochrome photography / Static framing / Silence / Gradual reveal

cards.front: The lesson names four filmic techniques E.T. uses to construct the alien as a source of transcendence. What are they?
cards.answer: Warm colour cinematography / Child's-eye-view camera / Non-diegetic orchestral maximalism / Iconic silhouette

cards.front: Why does Siegel stage the first pod reveal at the Belicec house gradually rather than as a shock cut?
cards.answer: Because the horror lies not in the sight itself but in the implication of what the pod means for everyone the characters know.

cards.front: Why does Carmen Dragon's score drop out entirely at the moment of the pod's discovery?
cards.answer: To replace music with near-silence broken by an unsettling ambient hum, making the internal, invisible threat feel more unnerving.

cards.front: Name the four key twentieth/twenty-first century public health interventions the lesson lists, each tackling a different problem.
cards.answer: Clean Air Act 1956 (air pollution) / Smoking ban 2007 (tobacco disease) / Change4Life 2009 (obesity and inactivity) / Sugar tax 2018 (childhood obesity and diabetes)

cards.front: Why did the government initially respond cautiously to the 1950 evidence linking smoking to lung cancer?
cards.answer: Partly because tobacco generated significant tax revenue for the government.

cards.front: How did new council housing built after the 1919 Addison Act improve living conditions for working-class families?
cards.answer: It gave families homes with gardens, indoor sanitation and proper ventilation, unlike overcrowded Victorian slums.

cards.front: Why was the NHS vaccination programme launched in December 2020 significant?
cards.answer: It was the most rapid mass vaccination programme in British history, with most adults getting a dose by mid-2021.

cards.front: Name the eight pieces of information UK food labels must legally carry.
cards.answer: Product name / Ingredients list by weight / Allergen information in bold / Net quantity / Date mark / Storage conditions / Manufacturer name and address / Country of origin for certain foods

cards.front: Name the four preservation methods the lesson describes for extending shelf life.
cards.answer: Freezing / Jam-making / Pickling / Bottling and vacuum packing

cards.front: Why does chilling a sliced apple slow enzymic browning?
cards.answer: Chilling inhibits the enzyme polyphenol oxidase so it reacts more slowly with oxygen, slowing browning.

cards.front: Why can frozen food be stored safely for weeks or months at −18°C?
cards.answer: Micro-organisms cannot reproduce at this temperature and enzyme activity slows dramatically, though the organisms do not die.

cards.front: Name the four contact forces given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Friction / Tension / Normal contact force / Air resistance

cards.front: Name the three non-contact forces given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Gravity / Magnetism / Electrostatic attraction

cards.front: How do you find the resultant force when two forces act in opposite directions on an object?
cards.answer: Subtract the smaller force from the larger one; the resultant acts in the direction of the larger force.

cards.front: Why does a heavy truck accelerate much less than a bicycle when the same resultant force is applied?
cards.answer: The truck has far greater inertial mass, so the same resultant force produces much less acceleration.

cards.front: In her Act 4 potion soliloquy, what three terrifying possibilities does Juliet consider before drinking?
cards.answer: The potion might not work, forcing marriage to Paris / The Friar might be poisoning her to hide the secret marriage / She might wake too early and go mad in the tomb
items: The potion might not work, forcing marriage to Paris
The Friar might be poisoning her to hide the secret marriage
She might wake too early and go mad in the tomb

cards.front: What four steps make up Friar Lawrence's plan in Act 4, Scene 1?
cards.answer: Juliet drinks a potion faking death for 42 hours / Her family places her in the Capulet tomb / The Friar sends a letter to Romeo in Mantua / Romeo returns to rescue her when she wakes
items: Juliet drinks a potion faking death for 42 hours
Her family places her in the Capulet tomb
The Friar sends a letter to Romeo in Mantua
Romeo returns to rescue her when she wakes

cards.front: How does Capulet's grief over Juliet's apparent death create dramatic irony?
cards.answer: The audience knows Juliet is alive, so his praise of her as a lost flower exposes the hypocrisy of the man who threatened to let her starve.

cards.front: How does the Friar's line 'She's not well married that lives married long' work as dramatic irony?
cards.answer: It seems a general comment on death but secretly describes the truth: Juliet is married to Romeo and will die young, understood only by the audience.

cards.front: What three things happened to a baby left at the Foundling Hospital, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Given a new name / Educated / Trained for employment

cards.front: Why does Gavin include Toby, a Black child, at the Foundling Hospital?
cards.answer: To remind readers that exploiting children was part of a wider culture treating human beings as property, broadening who counted as fully human.

cards.front: How does the Foundling Hospital contrast with what actually happens to the babies Otis Gardiner collects?
cards.answer: The Hospital saves children like Aaron, while Otis and Meshak actually bury most of the babies rather than delivering them there.

cards.front: Why did Gavin choose to set Coram Boy in 18th-century England?
cards.answer: To invite modern readers to see parallels between historical and contemporary attitudes to children, poverty and race.

title: Responding to Sports Injuries: First Aid (SALTAPS & PRICE)
subject: cambridge-nationals-sport-science

cards.front: Name the five steps of DRABC, the emergency first-aid checklist for an unresponsive performer.
cards.answer: Danger / Response / Airway / Breathing / Circulation

cards.front: Why should ice never be applied directly to the skin during PRICE therapy?
cards.answer: Direct contact with ice can cause an ice burn, so it must be wrapped in a damp cloth or ice bag first.

cards.front: How can a first aider tell if a bandage applied during Compression is too tight?
cards.answer: If the performer's fingers or toes become pale, cold or numb, the bandage is too tight and must be loosened.

cards.front: Name the four levels of isolation the lesson identifies in The Woman in Black.
cards.answer: Physical isolation / Social isolation / Psychological isolation / Emotional isolation

cards.front: Name the four stages of the model paragraph structure for extract analysis.
cards.answer: Point / Evidence / Analysis / Effect

cards.front: How does Arthur's rationalism cause his psychological isolation?
cards.answer: His refusal to believe in ghosts isolates him from understanding events and stops him taking the danger seriously until too late.

cards.front: Why does Hill spread guilt across the whole community rather than one person?
cards.answer: The townspeople's silence, Alice Drablow's adoption of Nathaniel, and Sam Daily's unclear warning all contribute, showing collective inaction lets evil persist.

title: Enslavement and the Lives of the Enslaved
subject: latin-eduqas

cards.front: Name the five routes into slavery the lesson gives for the Roman world.
cards.answer: Capture in war / Seizure by pirates / Birth to an enslaved mother / Punishment for crime or debt / Abandonment as an infant

cards.front: Where were Rome's two dedicated slave markets located?
cards.answer: Beside the Temple of Castor in the Forum / In the Campus Martius
items: Beside the Temple of Castor in the Forum

cards.front: Why did emperor Trajan rule that free-born infants raised as slaves should not have to buy their freedom?
cards.answer: Because he decided anyone who could prove free birth should be able to claim it without paying back their upbringing costs.

cards.front: Why did public slaves such as the artisans at New Carthage have a better chance of freedom?
cards.answer: Because officials like Scipio promised freedom to public slaves who worked hard providing equipment for war.

cards.front: Name the three types of prototype designers use, depending on what they need to test.
cards.answer: Appearance models / Functional prototypes / Production prototypes

cards.front: What are the six things a well-developed prototype must do, according to the specification?
cards.answer: Satisfy the requirements of the brief / Respond to client wants and needs / Demonstrate innovation / Be functional / Consider aesthetics / Be potentially marketable
items: Satisfy the requirements of the brief
Respond to client wants and needs

cards.front: How does rapid prototyping speed up the iterative design process?
cards.answer: A designer can turn a CAD model into a physical prototype in hours, test it, modify the digital file, and print an improved version the same day.

cards.front: Why does the testing-and-improvement cycle for a prototype keep repeating?
cards.answer: Because it continues until the product meets all specification requirements or the best possible compromise is reached.

cards.front: Name the three settings multiplied together to work out a sound file's size in bits.
cards.answer: Sample rate / Duration / Bit depth

cards.front: Why does a low-resolution image look blocky when stretched across a large screen?
cards.answer: Each pixel is enlarged until you can see the individual coloured squares.

cards.front: How does a greater bit depth make a sound recording cleaner?
cards.answer: It lets each sample record the amplitude more precisely, giving a wider range of volumes.

cards.front: What three things drive Enid's fierce protectiveness of her daughters, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Her experience of an abusive marriage / Her mother's death and their estrangement / Her experience of racism as a Windrush immigrant
items: Her experience of an abusive marriage
Her mother's death and their estrangement
Her experience of racism as a Windrush immigrant

cards.front: What six dramatic techniques does the lesson say to analyse alongside language in Leave Taking?
cards.answer: Naturalistic dialogue / Code-switching / Dual settings / Obeah scenes / Silence / Stagecraft

cards.front: Why does the title 'Leave Taking' capture the play's theme of belonging?
cards.answer: It refers to Enid's departure from Jamaica, the daughters' departure from her values, and leaving shame behind.

cards.front: Why does Pinnock avoid staging dramatic racist incidents in Leave Taking?
cards.answer: Because racism works as pervasive structural pressure shaping every character's choices, which is more realistic and powerful.

cards.front: Name the five stages of the five-act structure Shakespeare uses in Romeo and Juliet.
cards.answer: Exposition (Act 1: feud, lovers meet) / Rising action (Act 2: balcony, marriage) / Turning point (Act 3: Mercutio and Tybalt die, banishment) / Falling action (Act 4: potion plan) / Catastrophe (Act 5: deaths and reconciliation)
items: Turning point (Act 3: Mercutio and Tybalt die, banishment)

cards.front: Name the four key structural techniques Shakespeare uses in the play.
cards.answer: Prologue as a structural frame / Five-act structure with turning point at centre / Mirrored scenes (ball/tomb, opening/closing) / Compressed four-day timeline
items: Five-act structure with turning point at centre

cards.front: Why does the Prologue's dramatic irony make the play more emotional rather than less suspenseful?
cards.answer: We watch the lovers' joy knowing it cannot last, which makes it both more beautiful and more painful.

cards.front: How does the play's compressed four-day timeline help cause the tragedy?
cards.answer: It creates breathless urgency so the lovers have no time to reflect or reconsider, making the speed that excites us also make tragedy inevitable.

title: Specialist Writing on Film: Reviews, Theory, Cinematography
subject: film-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three types of specialist writing on film described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Film review / Film criticism / Writing on cinematography

cards.front: Which three critics does the lesson name as widely referenced writers of film reviews?
cards.answer: Pauline Kael / Roger Ebert / Mark Kermode

cards.front: Why does simply mentioning a specialist term like 'continuity editing' earn nothing in extended writing?
cards.answer: Because the term only counts if the rest of the sentence explains what that technique does in the specific sequence, making an argument about meaning.

cards.front: How should auteur theory be used to analyse a director's choices in this unit?
