cards.answer: Schweinshaxe (pork knuckle) / Bratwurst (fried sausage) / Currywurst / Döner Kebab / Kartoffelsalat (potato salad) / Schnitzel (breaded cutlet)

cards.front: Why does the lesson say using 'Könnte ich...?' instead of 'Ich möchte...' is useful in the restaurant role-play?
cards.answer: Because 'Könnte ich...?' is a polite conditional form that shows higher-level language than the basic 'I would like' phrases.

cards.front: How does the phrase 'es hat mir (nicht) geschmeckt' differ from 'es hat ... geschmeckt' when describing a meal?
cards.answer: 'Es hat ... geschmeckt' describes how the food tasted, while 'es hat mir (nicht) geschmeckt' says whether you liked or disliked it.

title: Joining & Finishing — Permanent and Temporary Fixings
subject: engineering-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three heat-treatment processes described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Annealing / Hardening / Tempering

cards.front: Name the four finishing methods described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Painting / Plating / Polishing / Chemical treatment (etching)

cards.front: Why is brazing more suitable for steel and copper than for aluminium?
cards.answer: Brazing needs high temperatures, and aluminium has a melting point too low, so it would melt instead of staying solid.

cards.front: How does hardening make steel hard but brittle?
cards.answer: Steel is heated to the correct temperature then rapidly quenched, which traps its structure in a hard but brittle state.

title: London’s response: government, Royals, propaganda and ‘Dig for Victory’
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four things Mass Observation diaries from 1940-41 recorded about how the Blitz actually felt.
cards.answer: Looting in bombed shops / Panic on the worst nights / Shelter trekking by middle-class families to outer suburbs / Class resentment over West End private deep shelters
items: Shelter trekking by middle-class families to outer suburbs
Class resentment over West End private deep shelters

cards.front: Name the six foods that rationing covered by 1942.
cards.answer: Meat / Butter / Sugar / Cheese / Eggs / Tea

cards.front: Why did the government keep cinemas, dancehalls and theatres open during the Blitz instead of closing them for safety?
cards.answer: Home Intelligence reports concluded closing leisure venues for safety would damage morale more than the casualties from occasional bombing.

cards.front: Why was the documentary London Can Take It! widely shown in the United States?
cards.answer: It packaged one night of the Blitz as cheerful resilience to push American sympathy towards the British cause.

cards.front: Name the three methods of good customer service the lesson identifies.
cards.answer: Product knowledge / Customer engagement / Post-sales services

cards.front: Name the three ICT developments the lesson says have transformed customer service.
cards.answer: Websites / E-commerce / Social media

cards.front: Why does strong product knowledge help build customer trust?
cards.answer: Staff who really understand what they sell save the customer time, turning an uncertain shopper into a confident one.

cards.front: Why is customer engagement deliberately kept low at a budget supermarket?
cards.answer: The business competes on price rather than experience, so it keeps staff to a minimum to keep prices low.

title: Family Life, Women and the Marriage Law
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four aspects of pre-1949 family life shaped by Confucian patriarchy that the lesson lists.
cards.answer: Arranged child marriage / Bride prices / Legal concubinage in wealthy households / Female infanticide in poor villages / Foot binding

cards.front: The lesson gives four 'genuine gains' for women under Mao's rule — what are they?
cards.answer: End of foot binding / Legal right to divorce / Mass literacy / Near-universal urban employment by 1976

cards.front: Why did the 1950 Marriage Law provoke violent backlash in rural China?
cards.answer: Husbands, mothers-in-law and clan elders saw it as an attack on the family economy since a divorced wife could take property and remarry.

cards.front: How did the 1958 communes disrupt traditional family life?
cards.answer: They banned family cooking for communal mess halls, made childcare collective and abolished private plots under the slogan 'production over kinship'.

title: Cold War End, the Gulf War and Oslo, 1989–95
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four conditions the lesson gives that together made Oslo possible.
cards.answer: End of Cold War removed Soviet support for rejectionism / Gulf War cost the PLO its funding / Madrid Conference brought all regional states together / Rabin's 1992 election win
items: End of Cold War removed Soviet support for rejectionism
Gulf War cost the PLO its funding
Madrid Conference brought all regional states together

cards.front: Name the three final-status issues the lesson says Oslo deferred and never resolved (plus one more).
cards.answer: Refugees / Jerusalem / Settlements / Borders

cards.front: Why was the thirty-five-state Gulf War coalition of 1990-91 significant for Middle East diplomacy?
cards.answer: It included Arab states like Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Syria and Morocco alongside NATO allies, a line-up impossible during the Cold War.

cards.front: How did Rabin's restraint during the Gulf War Scud attacks benefit Israel afterwards?
cards.answer: Israeli restraint was visibly valuable to the US, creating a debt the next administration could later collect in peace diplomacy.

cards.front: Name the four rhetorical techniques the lesson says Antony uses in his funeral speech.
cards.answer: Ironic repetition of 'honourable men' / Rhetorical questions / Emotional appeals / Physical props

cards.front: What are the four balanced clauses Brutus uses in his funeral speech to justify killing Caesar?
cards.answer: As Caesar loved me, I weep for him / As he was fortunate, I rejoice at it / As he was valiant, I honour him / As he was ambitious, I slew him
items: As Caesar loved me, I weep for him
As he was fortunate, I rejoice at it
As he was valiant, I honour him
As he was ambitious, I slew him

cards.front: How does Cassius's line about 'ages hence' create metatheatre in Act 3, Scene 1?
cards.answer: He imagines future audiences re-enacting the assassination, which mirrors Shakespeare's real audience watching the scene, blurring Rome and the Elizabethan theatre.

cards.front: Why does Antony shake hands with the conspirators after finding Caesar's body?
cards.answer: It is a calculated political act that appears to signal acceptance while he privately views them as butchers, hiding his true intentions.

cards.front: Name the three couples who celebrate together at the close of The Merchant of Venice.
cards.answer: Bassanio and Portia / Gratiano and Nerissa / Lorenzo and Jessica

cards.front: What four things has Jessica done that make her assimilation into Belmont uneasy?
cards.answer: Betrayed her father / Stole his money / Traded her dead mother's ring for a monkey / Converted to Christianity
items: Traded her dead mother's ring for a monkey

cards.front: How does the ring trick reassert Portia's authority over the marriage?
cards.answer: She has saved Antonio, outperformed the male lawyers, and now proves she controls the marriage by testing the rings.

cards.front: Why does Lorenzo's speech on music seem aimed at Shylock?
cards.answer: Shylock earlier complained about music, so the speech marks him as unfit for treasons and excluded from Belmont's harmonious community.

title: Jewish Beliefs about God and Sacred Place
subject: religious-studies-eduqas

cards.front: What four functions does the synagogue serve in Jewish life?
cards.answer: Prayer / Study / Celebration / Assembly

cards.front: What four things does a Jewish family do at home to mark the start of Shabbat?
cards.answer: Light candles / Say kiddush (blessing over wine) / Bless the challah (bread) / Abstain from creative work

cards.front: Why does Judaism forbid artistic representations of G-d?
cards.answer: Because G-d is transcendent, and images or statues would reduce the infinite to something finite, misrepresenting G-d's true nature.

cards.front: Why is the kippah worn by many Jewish men?
cards.answer: It is a visible reminder that G-d is above, watching over the person's actions.

cards.front: Name the four impacts of production technology on a business that the lesson gives.
cards.answer: lower unit costs / higher productivity / more consistent quality / faster product flexibility (smart systems)

cards.front: Why does getting batch size wrong reduce the cost savings of batch production?
cards.answer: Too small a batch means changeover costs dominate, while too large a batch leaves unsold stock.

cards.front: Why can modern 'smart' factories with reprogrammable robots be more flexible than older flow lines?
cards.answer: Reprogrammable robots can be switched to make different products faster than people could, unlike rigid old lines.

title: The Nervous System and Fight or Flight
subject: psychology-aqa

cards.front: Name the four physical changes the lesson gives for when the sympathetic branch activates.
cards.answer: heart beats faster / breathing quickens / pupils dilate / digestion slows / adrenaline released

cards.front: Why can chronic stress harm physical health, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Chronic stress keeps the sympathetic ANS activated, raising blood pressure and suppressing the immune system.

cards.front: Why does the James–Lange theory struggle to explain how we tell fear and excitement apart?
cards.answer: Fear and excitement produce similar bodily states, so interpreting bodily changes alone can't distinguish between them.

cards.front: Name the four types of evidence the lesson gives for reconstructing past climate.
cards.answer: Global temperature records / Ice cores / Tree rings (dendrochronology) / Paintings and diaries

cards.front: Name the three natural causes of climate change given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Variations in solar output / Changes in the Earth's orbit / Volcanic activity

cards.front: How do ice cores preserve a record of past atmospheres?
cards.answer: Snow falls in annual layers and compresses into ice, trapping tiny air bubbles from the year it fell.

cards.front: Why have sea levels risen since 1900?
cards.answer: Warmer water expands in volume and ice sheets are melting, both adding water and raising sea levels.

cards.front: What three types of cause does the lesson give for insomnia?
cards.answer: Psychological cause (nervous system arousal) / Physical cause (sleeping environment) / Biological cause (brain damage)

cards.front: What four sleep hygiene strategies does the lesson list for improving sleep?
cards.answer: Consistent bedtime and wake-up time / Dark, quiet and cool bedroom / Avoiding screens, caffeine and heavy meals before bed / Using the bed only for sleep and rest
items: Avoiding screens, caffeine and heavy meals before bed
Using the bed only for sleep and rest

cards.front: How do sleep diaries help work out which type of insomnia a person has?
cards.answer: By recording sleep and waking times each night, showing whether the problem is falling asleep or staying asleep.

cards.front: Why is it important to match insomnia treatment to its specific cause rather than treating insomnia as one single problem?
cards.answer: Because insomnia can stem from different causes, so a treatment that works for one cause won't fix a different underlying cause.

cards.front: Name the four aims of punishment described in Muslim thought.
cards.answer: Protection / Retribution / Deterrence / Reformation

cards.front: Name the three reasons non-religious thinkers give for opposing capital punishment.
cards.answer: Violates the right to life / Risks executing an innocent person / Lacks reliable evidence it deters crime
items: Lacks reliable evidence it deters crime

cards.front: Why do many Muslims see crime as a distraction from focusing on Allah?
cards.answer: Because a person absorbed in wrongdoing has stopped directing their life towards worship and obedience.

cards.front: Why do Muslims see punishment as a form of justice?
cards.answer: Because it restores balance after a wrong and is needed to protect people and deter future crime.

cards.front: Name the four independent lines of evidence the lesson gives for climate change.
cards.answer: Ice cores / Temperature records / Sea level measurements / Satellite data (sea ice/glaciers)

cards.front: Name the three sources of methane emissions the lesson gives.
cards.answer: Livestock digestion (enteric fermentation) / Rice paddies / Landfill sites

cards.front: Why does methane have a stronger warming effect per molecule than CO2, despite being present in lower concentrations?
cards.answer: Each molecule of methane traps substantially more heat than a molecule of CO2.

cards.front: Why can reducing methane emissions produce quicker effects on warming than reducing CO2 emissions?
cards.answer: Methane breaks down in the atmosphere in about a decade, whereas CO2 persists for centuries.

cards.front: Name the five types of force and stress covered in this lesson.
cards.answer: Tension / Compression / Bending / Torsion / Shear

cards.front: Name the four reinforcement methods given for strengthening materials.
cards.answer: Lamination / Folding / Webbing / Fabric interfacing

cards.front: Why is corrugated card strong in compression?
cards.answer: Its fluted inner layer acts as a series of small arches that resist compression.

cards.front: Why is a triangulated frame, like a roof truss, efficient at distributing loads?
cards.answer: Triangles cannot be deformed without changing the length of a side.

cards.front: Name the four sources of support for McCarthy that the lesson identifies.
cards.answer: Republican politicians attacking Democrats / business conservatives resenting the New Deal / ordinary Americans frightened by events / religious groups fearing Communism as atheist threat
items: business conservatives resenting the New Deal
religious groups fearing Communism as atheist threat

cards.front: Name the three types of workplace the blacklist operated in.
cards.answer: Hollywood / the civil service / universities

cards.front: Why did McCarthy's accusation at Wheeling in 1950 land so powerfully with the public?
cards.answer: It came right after Alger Hiss's conviction, the Soviet atomic bomb test, and China 'falling' to Communism, fuelling existing fear.

cards.front: How did McCarthy silence people who criticised his methods?
cards.answer: He called his critics Communist sympathisers, making it dangerous for anyone to publicly oppose him.

cards.front: What three broad historical periods do sociologists use to study how family relationships have changed?
cards.answer: Pre-industrial / Industrial / Contemporary

cards.front: Name the four contemporary family issues studied by sociologists mentioned in the lesson.
cards.answer: Quality of parenting / Relationships between teenagers and adults / Care of disabled and elderly family members / Arranged marriage
items: Care of disabled and elderly family members

cards.front: How did industrialisation change the family's economic role?
cards.answer: Paid work moved into factories and offices, separating public and private spheres and shifting the family from a unit of production to a unit of consumption.

cards.front: How does the functionalist view explain historical changes in family relationships?
cards.answer: The family adapted by shedding functions it could no longer perform efficiently to schools, hospitals and the state, keeping primary socialisation and personality stabilisation.

title: Magnets, Electromagnetism and the Motor Effect
subject: science-aqa

cards.front: Name the four magnetic materials given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Iron / Steel / Cobalt / Nickel

cards.front: Name the three ways given to increase the speed of a d.c. motor.
cards.answer: Increasing the current / Using a stronger magnet / Adding more turns to the coil
items: Adding more turns to the coil

cards.front: Why are permanent magnets made from steel rather than soft iron?
cards.answer: Soft iron loses its magnetism as soon as it leaves a magnetic field, unlike steel.

cards.front: Why does a d.c. motor coil rotate continuously instead of stopping after 180°?
cards.answer: The split-ring commutator reverses the current every half turn, keeping the force acting in the right direction.

cards.front: Name the four things the lesson says the pre-frontal cortex is heavily involved in.
cards.answer: Decision-making / Planning ahead / Controlling impulses / Regulating personality and social behaviour

cards.front: According to Damasio et al.'s reconstruction, which four areas of Gage's brain were left untouched by the rod?
cards.answer: Movement / Sensation / Speech / General intelligence

cards.front: Why does visual agnosia show that seeing and recognising an object are separate brain processes?
cards.answer: A person can see an object clearly but not name it, yet recognise it instantly by touch, showing recognition needs separate processing areas.

cards.front: Why does prosopagnosia suggest the brain has a dedicated area for face processing?
cards.answer: The deficit only affects recognising faces, while other objects are still recognised normally, suggesting face processing is separate from general object recognition.

cards.front: The lesson names three types of bullying. What are they?
cards.answer: Physical (hitting, pushing) / Verbal (name-calling, threats) / Cyber (online harassment)

cards.front: Name the five cultural factors covered in the lesson that can affect health and wellbeing.
cards.answer: Religion / Gender roles and expectations / Gender identity / Sexual orientation / Community participation

cards.front: Why might some religious beliefs negatively affect a person's healthcare?
cards.answer: Some religious practices may restrict access to certain treatments, like blood transfusions, or create conflict with family or community beliefs.

cards.front: How does workplace discrimination affect a person economically?
cards.answer: It can limit career progression and reduce a person's income.

title: Mechanical Calculations: Stress, Strain, Young's Modulus and Factors of Safety
subject: engineering-aqa

cards.front: Why does a thin cable snap before a thick cable under the same load?
cards.answer: A thinner cable has a smaller cross-sectional area, so the same force produces higher stress.

cards.front: Why are brittle materials used for bricks in walls but avoided where tensile impact loads occur?
cards.answer: Brittle materials cope well with compressive loads but fracture suddenly with no warning under tensile impact.

cards.front: Why might choosing a higher factor of safety make a component less desirable?
cards.answer: Higher factor of safety values can mean heavier and more expensive components.

title: Deep Time and the Age of the Earth
subject: geology-eduqas

cards.front: Why was John Joly's ocean salinity estimate for Earth's age too low?
cards.answer: It assumed salt only accumulated, ignoring that salt is removed by evaporite formation and subduction into the mantle.

cards.front: Why did geologists conclude Ussher's 6,000-year estimate was wrong?
cards.answer: Processes like sedimentation, erosion and uplift observed in rock strata could not have produced the geological record in only 6,000 years.

cards.front: In the toilet-roll analogy, what does the lesson say each part represents?
cards.answer: Each sheet = one million years / Whole roll (500 sheets) = 500 million years / Full Earth history = about nine rolls / Human history = thinner than the printed ink
items: Full Earth history = about nine rolls
Human history = thinner than the printed ink

cards.front: Name the four earldoms held by the Godwin family and who held each one, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Harold – Wessex / Tostig – Northumbria / Gyrth – East Anglia / Leofwine – south-east

cards.front: Name the four rival claimants to the English throne in January 1066.
cards.answer: Harold Godwinson / William of Normandy / Harald Hardrada / Edgar the Aethling

cards.front: Why was Harold's alleged oath to William on holy relics so damaging to his reputation?
cards.answer: Swearing on holy relics was sacred and binding, so breaking the oath was a sin against God, giving William moral as well as political authority.

cards.front: Why did Harold's decision during the 1065 Northumbrian revolt weaken his family's power?
cards.answer: Harold refused to support his brother Tostig and accepted Morcar as earl instead, losing Godwin control of Northumbria though securing Mercian loyalty.

cards.front: Name the four other anthology poems the lesson pairs with 'A Song' for comparison.
cards.answer: Looking at Your Hands (Martin Carter) / Poem for My Love (June Jordan) / Flirtation (Rita Dove) / The Perseverance (Raymond Antrobus)

cards.front: Name the three stages the six stanzas of 'A Song' move through.
cards.answer: Stanzas I–II: past contentment with the trade / Stanza III: present tense, lover's departure / Stanzas IV–VI: distress once he is gone
items: Stanzas I–II: past contentment with the trade
Stanza III: present tense, lover's departure
Stanzas IV–VI: distress once he is gone

cards.front: How does Williams make the storm metaphor in the final stanza of 'A Song' feel powerful?
cards.answer: The sea stays calm with only a soft breeze, so the storm existing nowhere but her soul shows her turmoil is entirely internal.

cards.front: Why does Williams withhold pathetic fallacy when describing the waves in 'A Song'?
cards.answer: The waves stay calm and 'faithless', offering no pity, so nature refuses to mirror her feelings, emphasising her isolation.

cards.front: Name the four factors the lesson says drive change in the fight against lung cancer.
cards.answer: Science and technology / Government and institutions / Attitudes in society / Individuals

cards.front: Name the four modern treatment methods for lung cancer given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Surgery / Chemotherapy / Radiotherapy / Immunotherapy

cards.front: Why does chemotherapy often cause severe side effects?
cards.answer: Because the powerful drugs used to kill cancer cells also damage healthy cells.

cards.front: Why is early detection of lung cancer so important for survival?
cards.answer: Early detection significantly improves survival rates, and lung cancer is often diagnosed late, lowering overall survival.

title: Characters: Rani, Hari, Abdul and the Queen
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: Name the three betrayals in Rani's arc that the lesson describes as repeated betrayal.
cards.answer: Susan Matthews abandons her at Tilbury with no contract / Lord Oakham seduces her then denies the child / She leaves her newborn on the docks from desperation
items: Susan Matthews abandons her at Tilbury with no contract
Lord Oakham seduces her then denies the child
She leaves her newborn on the docks from desperation

cards.front: Name the four stages of Hari's journey a designer could show through costume changes.
cards.answer: barefoot undernourished lascar in rough cotton / beaten bloodied figure thrown ashore at the Cape / man digging in a diamond mine / well-fitted brown suit in the final Tilbury scene
items: barefoot undernourished lascar in rough cotton
beaten bloodied figure thrown ashore at the Cape
man digging in a diamond mine
well-fitted brown suit in the final Tilbury scene

cards.front: Why does Victoria retract the honour she wanted to give Abdul?
cards.answer: Her household threatens to declare her insane if she continues to honour him, so she keeps him as Munshi but withdraws the honour.

cards.front: Why does Abdul's promotion to munshi fail to protect him after Victoria's death?
cards.answer: The wider royal household, especially Lady Sarah, never accepts the promotion, and this lasting hostility destroys him once Victoria dies.

cards.front: Name the five main jobs of an operating system, as given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Providing a user interface / Managing memory and multitasking / Managing peripherals through drivers / Managing users and their access rights / Managing files
items: Managing users and their access rights

cards.front: Name the three examples of utility software given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Encryption software / Defragmentation / Data compression

cards.front: How does an operating system make it seem like several programs run at the same time?
cards.answer: It gives each running program a tiny slice of processor time in turn, switching between them so quickly they appear simultaneous.

cards.front: Why does data compression count as utility software rather than a job the operating system does by default?
cards.answer: It performs a task—shrinking files by encoding them to use fewer bits—that the operating system does not handle on its own.

cards.front: Name the four stages of the information processing model, in order.
cards.answer: Input / Decision Making / Output / Feedback

cards.front: What three sources of sensory information does the lesson give for the input stage?
cards.answer: Eyes tracking ball and defenders / Ears picking up teammate shouts / Proprioceptors sensing body position and balance
items: Proprioceptors sensing body position and balance

cards.front: Why does Hick's Law say a player with more shot options takes longer to decide?
cards.answer: Reaction time increases with the number of possible responses available, so more choices slow down decision making.

cards.front: Why is a beginner's output slower than an expert's when performing the same skill?
cards.answer: The beginner must consciously direct each element of the movement, while the expert's motor programme runs automatically.

cards.front: Name the five common validation checks the lesson gives.
cards.answer: Presence check / Range check / Type check / Length check / Format check

cards.front: Name the five examples of misuse the lesson gives that a program must anticipate.
cards.answer: Leaving a required field empty / Typing letters where a number is expected / Entering an impossible value like -5 / Giving a date that does not exist / Pasting in an enormous amount of text
items: Typing letters where a number is expected
Giving a date that does not exist
Pasting in an enormous amount of text

cards.front: Why does a range check fail to catch a wrong year of birth like 1999 instead of 2000?
cards.answer: Because a range check only confirms the year is a sensible four-digit number, not that it is actually correct.

cards.front: Why does consistent indentation help make code maintainable?
cards.answer: It shows the shape of the code so readers can see which lines sit inside a loop or condition.

cards.front: Name the eight Boolean algebra laws covered in the lesson.
cards.answer: Identity / Annulment (Null) / Idempotent / Complement / Commutative / Associative / Distributive / Absorption

cards.front: What three symbols does standard Boolean notation use for AND, OR and NOT?
cards.answer: dot (·) for AND / plus sign (+) for OR / overbar for NOT

cards.front: Why does the Absorption law let A + A·B simplify straight to A?
cards.answer: Because A is already in the expression, any term multiplying A by something else adds no new information and is redundant.

cards.front: Why does it matter when a Boolean expression simplifies down to a constant like 1?
cards.answer: It means the output never changes, so the circuit can be replaced with a simple connection to logic HIGH or LOW instead of gates.

title: Your Fieldwork Approach for 2027: Change Over Time and Sphere of Influence
subject: geography-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four change-over-time enquiries listed in the specification.
cards.answer: Retail patterns vs historical data / Weather vs same period in an earlier year / River or coastal landforms vs historical maps/photos / Land use today vs earlier date
items: Weather vs same period in an earlier year
River or coastal landforms vs historical maps/photos
Land use today vs earlier date

cards.front: Name the five sphere-of-influence enquiries listed in the specification.
cards.answer: Urban area's reach over rural hinterland / Externalities of a major event or venue / Visitor pressure at a honeypot site / Impact of a distinctive landscape feature / Impact of a river catchment on flood risk
items: Urban area's reach over rural hinterland
Externalities of a major event or venue
Visitor pressure at a honeypot site
Impact of a distinctive landscape feature
Impact of a river catchment on flood risk

cards.front: Why must the historical evidence in a change-over-time enquiry cover the same location as your fieldwork site?
cards.answer: Because the comparison only works if the 'then' evidence describes the same place, otherwise differences may not show real change.

cards.front: How do you judge the impact side of a sphere-of-influence enquiry?
cards.answer: By identifying the effects found and sorting them into positive impacts (like extra income) and negative impacts (like erosion or litter).

cards.front: Why can deflation lead to a damaging downward spiral in the economy?
cards.answer: Consumers delay spending expecting further price falls, demand drops, so firms cut output and jobs, worsening the economy.

cards.front: Why does the Bank of England Governor sometimes have to write a letter to the Chancellor?
cards.answer: Because CPI inflation has moved more than 1 percentage point above or below the 2% target.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Robotics
subject: computer-science-edexcel

cards.front: The lesson names four possible parties who could be liable when an AI system causes harm. What are they?
cards.answer: The company that developed the AI software / The organisation that deployed the system / The engineer who designed the training process / The dataset provider
items: The company that developed the AI software
The organisation that deployed the system
The engineer who designed the training process

cards.front: What three benefits of AI, machine learning and robotics does the lesson give?
cards.answer: AI diagnosing diseases from scan images / Machine learning detecting banking fraud in milliseconds / Robots doing dangerous or repetitive tasks
items: AI diagnosing diseases from scan images
Machine learning detecting banking fraud in milliseconds
Robots doing dangerous or repetitive tasks

cards.front: How can an adversarial attack cause an AI safety failure?
cards.answer: Small, imperceptible changes to an input can make a well-trained image classifier confidently produce a completely wrong output.

cards.front: Why can developers of deep learning systems not explain a specific prediction for a specific individual?
cards.answer: Predictions come from thousands of weighted calculations that cannot be easily summarised into human-readable rules.

cards.front: In the required practical on acceleration, name the two pieces of apparatus used to measure motion of the trolley.
cards.answer: Light gate / Ticker tape timer

cards.front: Why do two cars travelling at 30 m/s in opposite directions have different velocities but the same speed?
cards.answer: Speed only measures how fast they move, but velocity includes direction, and their directions are opposite.

cards.front: How can you show that F = ma using the required practical results?
cards.answer: Plotting force against acceleration gives a straight line through the origin, showing they are directly proportional.

cards.front: What does a downward sloping line on a velocity-time graph show about the object's motion?
cards.answer: The object is decelerating, meaning its velocity is decreasing over time.

title: Yalta, Potsdam and the changing order 1945-1948
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Why did the atmosphere at Potsdam become much cooler than at Yalta?
cards.answer: Truman had replaced Roosevelt, the USA had tested the atomic bomb, and Stalin's Soviet-dominated buffer in Eastern Europe was already visible.

cards.front: Why did the February 1948 Czech coup shock Western opinion and push towards NATO?
cards.answer: Czechoslovakia had kept a coalition government and free press longer than others, so its forcible takeover alarmed the West into discussing a defence pact.

cards.front: Name the four countries where salami tactics dismantled coalition governments between 1945-1948.
cards.answer: Poland / Hungary / Romania / Bulgaria

cards.front: Give the six deaths or losses caused by the Agra treasure that Doyle uses to show greed's consequences.
cards.answer: The merchant is murdered / The four conspirators are imprisoned / Sholto dies tormented by guilt / Morstan dies in an argument over it / Bartholomew is murdered for it / Small loses the treasure and his freedom
items: Morstan dies in an argument over it
Small loses the treasure and his freedom

cards.front: Why does Jonathan Small throw the Agra treasure into the Thames rather than let it be captured?
cards.answer: He realises he cannot escape and would rather destroy the treasure than let anyone else have it.

cards.front: How does the contrast between Watson and Holmes's endings reflect the novel's dual structure?
cards.answer: Watson moves forward into marriage and emotional fulfilment while Holmes stays trapped in a cycle of cases and cocaine, showing emotion versus intellect.

cards.front: Why is journalism a meaningful choice of career for Dante within the novel's structure?
cards.answer: Journalism means telling the truth and giving people a voice, ironic since Dante is now silenced by his circumstances.

cards.front: How does Blackman use Tyler to present single fatherhood in the novel?
cards.answer: Tyler shows single fatherhood is not extraordinary but simply what men in this family do.

title: Pre-production Documents: Mood Boards, Mind Maps & Visualisation Diagrams
subject: cambridge-nationals-creative-imedia

cards.front: Name the five things a visualisation diagram should include, as stated in the lesson.
cards.answer: Overall dimensions and orientation / Placeholder boxes for images / Positions and sizes of text elements / The planned colour scheme / Annotations explaining design choices
items: Positions and sizes of text elements

cards.front: Why are mind maps described as non-linear thinking tools?
cards.answer: Because they let a creator jump between ideas and notice unexpected connections instead of thinking in a straight line.

title: The Red Guards and the Red Terror, 1966-68
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: The lesson gives three reasons why young people responded so completely to Mao's call. What are they?
cards.answer: Lin Biao's PLA cult of Mao already in schools / education reform offering loyalty over exam merit / 'Bombard the Headquarters' poster naming enemies inside CCP
items: Lin Biao's PLA cult of Mao already in schools
education reform offering loyalty over exam merit
'Bombard the Headquarters' poster naming enemies inside CCP

cards.front: Why did the reform of education make peasant and worker children keen to join the Red Guards?
cards.answer: It told them academic exams favoured the bourgeoisie, so joining offered a different ladder of merit based on revolutionary loyalty.

cards.front: Why did Mao turn to Lin Biao and the PLA to demobilise the Red Guards from late 1967?
cards.answer: Red Guards had split into rival factions, seized PLA weapons and fought each other, threatening to topple the regime itself.

cards.front: Name the four reasons the lesson gives for why young children are at particular risk of accidents.
cards.answer: Naturally curious / Lack awareness of danger / Developing motor control / Cannot assess risk independently

cards.front: Name four ways the lesson gives to prevent falls in young children.
cards.answer: Fit stair gates top and bottom / Fit window restrictors (max 6.5cm opening) / Use non-slip mats / Keep furniture away from windows
items: Fit stair gates top and bottom

cards.front: Why should a rear-facing car seat never be placed in the front passenger seat with an active airbag?
cards.answer: Because the airbag could injure the child in a collision, so rear-facing seats must not be used there.

cards.front: Why does a spilt mug of tea still pose a scald risk 15 minutes after being made?
cards.answer: Because the liquid stays hot enough for long enough to still scald a child even after standing for 15 minutes.

title: Uneven Global Development & Strategies to Address It
subject: geography-edexcel-a

cards.front: Name the three broad categories of causes of uneven development given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Physical (climate, hazards, landlockedness, resources) / Historic (colonialism, conflict) / Economic (trade, debt, technology)

cards.front: Name the three types of international aid described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Bilateral (government to government) / Multilateral (through organisations like the World Bank or UN) / Non-governmental (charities such as Oxfam)
items: Multilateral (through organisations like the World Bank or UN)

cards.front: How did colonialism cause lasting uneven development in former colonies?
cards.answer: Colonialism reshaped economies to serve imperial powers, leaving newly independent countries with infrastructure built for export rather than internal development.

cards.front: Why do rich-country tariffs on processed cocoa or cotton keep poorer countries poor?
cards.answer: The tariffs make processed exports less profitable, encouraging poorer countries to sell raw materials instead at lower prices.

title: Hernán Cortés and the road to Tenochtitlán
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: What did Cortés's expedition consist of when he set out from Cuba in February 1519?
cards.answer: Around 11 ships / About 500-600 soldiers / 16 horses / A handful of artillery pieces

cards.front: What three different ways have historians interpreted La Malinche's role in the conquest?
cards.answer: Spanish chroniclers praised her as essential to Cortés's success / Mexican nationalists condemned her as a traitor / Modern historians see her as enslaved, making strategic choices to survive
items: Spanish chroniclers praised her as essential to Cortés's success
Mexican nationalists condemned her as a traitor
Modern historians see her as enslaved, making strategic choices to survive

cards.front: Why did Moctezuma II likely receive Cortés peacefully at Tenochtitlán in November 1519?
cards.answer: He was probably applying a diplomatic strategy, welcoming a potentially powerful ally while assessing the threat he posed.

cards.front: How did the Cholula massacre affect other cities on the road to Tenochtitlán?
cards.answer: It sent a clear message that resistance would be met with overwhelming violence, showing Cortés's willingness to use terror politically.

title: Atomic Structure and the Development of the Atom
subject: separate-sciences-ocr

cards.front: Name the five scientists/models in order in the development of the atomic model, from Dalton to Chadwick.
cards.answer: Dalton's solid sphere model / Thomson's plum pudding model / Rutherford's nuclear model / Bohr's model with fixed shells / Chadwick's neutron

cards.front: Why did the large-angle deflections in the alpha scattering experiment disprove the plum pudding model?
cards.answer: Large deflections needed a concentrated positive charge, but plum pudding spread charge out so wouldn't deflect particles much.

cards.front: How did Bohr's model improve on Rutherford's nuclear model?
cards.answer: Bohr placed electrons in specific fixed energy levels at set distances, explaining why atoms emit light at particular wavelengths.

title: Ancient Astronomy: Eratosthenes, Aristarchus and Precession
subject: astronomy-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three things Aristarchus tried to measure or estimate about the Moon and Sun using geometry.
cards.answer: Diameter of the Moon / Distance to the Moon / Distance to the Sun and diameter of the Sun
items: Distance to the Sun and diameter of the Sun

cards.front: Why does Stonehenge's Heel Stone still align with the summer solstice sunrise today?
cards.answer: Because the alignment depends on Earth's axial tilt, which has changed very little since Stonehenge was built, not on precession.

cards.front: How did Aristarchus use a lunar eclipse to estimate the Moon's diameter?
cards.answer: He timed the Moon crossing Earth's shadow versus crossing its own diameter, giving the ratio of Earth's shadow width to the Moon's diameter.

cards.front: How did Aristarchus work out that the Sun's diameter is about 400 times the Moon's?
cards.answer: Since the Sun and Moon have almost the same angular diameter, being 400 times further away means the Sun must be 400 times larger.

cards.front: Name the three stages of Pip's Bildungsroman journey in Great Expectations.
cards.answer: Childhood at the forge (Chs 1-19) / Gentleman in London (Chs 20-39) / Disillusionment and moral recovery (Chs 40-59)

cards.front: Why did Dickens use first-person narration in Great Expectations?
cards.answer: To force the reader to share Pip's shame, ambition, and painful realisation directly.

title: Windrush, Commonwealth Migration & the Legacy of Empire
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the three sectors/employers the lesson gives for Caribbean migrants who came to Britain 1948-1962.
cards.answer: National Health Service / London Transport / British Rail and textile mills

cards.front: Which four immigration-related Acts/events does the lesson give for the narrowing of Commonwealth citizenship rights (1948-1971)?
cards.answer: 1948 British Nationality Act / 1962 Commonwealth Immigrants Act / 1968 restriction / 1971 Immigration Act

cards.front: Why did the Home Office cause the 2018 Windrush Scandal even though the Windrush generation had lived legally in Britain for decades?
cards.answer: It had destroyed its archive of landing cards in 2010, leaving people unable to prove their legal status.

cards.front: Why did Claudia Jones organise the January 1959 indoor Caribbean Carnival?
cards.answer: It was organised in response to the August 1958 Notting Hill attacks on Caribbean residents.

cards.front: Name the five types of intermarket relationship the lesson says you must identify when tracing a ripple effect between markets.
cards.answer: Substitute goods / Complementary goods / Joint supply / Competitive supply / Derived demand

cards.front: Name the three uses of farmland given as the example of composite demand for land.
cards.answer: Growing crops / Building houses / Renewable energy projects (solar farms)

cards.front: Why did car manufacturers have to pause production lines during the global semiconductor shortage?
cards.answer: Cars need chips to be built, so demand for chips is derived from demand for cars; fewer chips meant fewer cars could be made.

cards.front: Why does a sharp rise in demand for cheese push up the price of drinking milk?
cards.answer: Milk is in composite demand; more milk is diverted to cheese production, leaving less available for drinking, raising its price.

title: Domino Theory: Eisenhower and Kennedy in Vietnam
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: According to Eisenhower's April 1954 domino warning, which five countries could fall to communism next if South Vietnam fell?
cards.answer: Laos / Cambodia / Thailand / Burma / Indonesia

cards.front: What three factors does the lesson give for why US involvement in Vietnam deepened despite Diem's failures?
cards.answer: Domino Theory framed setbacks as regional collapse / Kennedy feared another perceived defeat / Advisers' combat-like role made escalation feel gradual
items: Domino Theory framed setbacks as regional collapse
Advisers' combat-like role made escalation feel gradual

cards.front: How was the Strategic Hamlets programme meant to defeat the Vietcong?
cards.answer: By moving peasants into fortified compounds, physically separating them from the Vietcong to cut off insurgents' food, intelligence and recruits.

cards.front: How did Thich Quang Duc's self-immolation affect American opinion of Diem?
cards.answer: A press photograph of his self-immolation spread worldwide and turned American opinion sharply against Diem's government.

cards.front: Why does eye contact often reveal a person's true feelings even when they try to hide them?
cards.answer: Because the eyes are hard to consciously control, so they leak genuine emotion despite attempts to mask it.

cards.front: Why did Yuki et al.'s findings challenge a purely innate view of reading facial emotion?
cards.answer: If reading emotion were entirely innate, culture should not change which facial feature people rely on, but it did.

cards.front: Name the two groups of evidence Darwin's theory draws on to show facial expressions are innate.
cards.answer: Neonate (newborn) evidence / Sensory-deprived (blind and deaf) evidence

title: The Sanctity of Life, Abortion and Euthanasia
subject: religious-studies-eduqas

cards.front: What are the three Jewish movements the lesson describes as having different views on abortion?
cards.answer: Orthodox Judaism / Conservative Judaism / Reform Judaism

cards.front: Under the Abortion Act 1967, what two grounds allow abortion after 24 weeks in exceptional circumstances?
cards.answer: Continuing pregnancy would endanger the woman's life / Serious foetal abnormality
items: Continuing pregnancy would endanger the woman's life

cards.front: Why did the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Act 1990 set the abortion time limit at 24 weeks?
cards.answer: Because 24 weeks roughly corresponds with the point of foetal viability outside the womb.

cards.front: Why might the Dalai Lama see euthanasia as an act of compassion despite the first Precept?
cards.answer: Because karuna (compassion) means working with suffering rather than simply prolonging it in some circumstances.

cards.front: Name the four groups the lesson gives as opponents of Jenner's vaccination.
cards.answer: Inoculators / Sceptical doctors / Religious groups / Anti-vaccinators

cards.front: Name the four areas of continuity in 18th-century medicine given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Treatments (bloodletting, purging, herbs) / Training / Hospitals / Disease causes (miasma theory)

cards.front: Why did inoculators oppose Jenner's vaccination?
cards.answer: Vaccination threatened their profitable inoculation businesses and they stood to lose customers.

cards.front: Why did religious groups object to vaccination?
cards.answer: They argued it was wrong to interfere with God's will by preventing a disease He had sent.

title: Human Computer Interface (HCI) in Everyday Life
subject: it-ocr

cards.front: Name the four hardware considerations the lesson says shape HCI design.
cards.answer: Display type / Display size / Memory (RAM) / Processing power

cards.front: Name the three things a banking HCI must be, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Secure (two-factor authentication) / Accessible to customers of all ages / Able to handle sensitive transactions reliably
items: Accessible to customers of all ages
Able to handle sensitive transactions reliably

cards.front: Why is the HCI on an embedded system like a washing machine often minimal?
cards.answer: Because the device has a single dedicated purpose, so only a few buttons and an LED display are needed.

cards.front: Why must HCI in entertainment devices like games consoles respond instantly?
cards.answer: Because users expect a smooth, enjoyable experience from entertainment technology.

cards.front: The lesson names four features that Gothic novels typically have. What are they?
cards.answer: Dark and isolated settings / Transgressive acts violating boundaries / Supernatural or monstrous elements / Intense psychological states

cards.front: Why does the Creature seem more 'Romantic' than Victor in the novel?
cards.answer: Denied access to human society, the Creature finds his only comfort in the natural world, unlike Victor who tries to conquer nature.

cards.front: How did the Industrial Revolution shape the anxieties explored in Frankenstein?
cards.answer: It raised fears that unchecked scientific and technological progress, pursued without ethical reflection, would lead to catastrophe.

cards.front: Why did Shelley transform the traditional Gothic 'monster' in Frankenstein?
cards.answer: She made the monster a scientifically created being rather than a supernatural demon, so horror comes from Victor's creation and abandonment, not the Creature itself.

title: Principles of Training: SPORT and FITT
subject: physical-education-aqa

cards.front: Name the four ways the lesson suggests introducing variety to avoid tedium in training.
cards.answer: Different training methods / Different environments / Different partners / Mixed session structures

cards.front: Name the three training types the lesson matches to specific sports.
cards.answer: Continuous training for a long-distance runner / Circuit training with punching drills and HIIT for a boxer / Static stretching sessions for a gymnast
items: Continuous training for a long-distance runner
Circuit training with punching drills and HIIT for a boxer
Static stretching sessions for a gymnast

cards.front: How does the duration (Time) of a session affect which energy system is stressed?
cards.answer: A 30-minute continuous run mainly stresses the aerobic system, while 10-second interval sprints stress the anaerobic system.

cards.front: Why is consistent, year-round training more effective than intense bursts followed by long rest periods?
cards.answer: Because reversibility means fitness losses occur once training stops, so maintaining a training stimulus prevents cardiovascular adaptations being lost.

title: The Atlantic Economy: Trade, Tobacco and Piracy
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: What three things did the Navigation Acts require or protect, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Trade shipped through England first / Trade carried in English ships / Only certain valuable goods listed (tobacco, sugar, indigo, rice)
items: Only certain valuable goods listed (tobacco, sugar, indigo, rice)

cards.front: In the triangular trade described in the lesson, what did each region send: New England, the Middle colonies, and the South send to the West Indies?
cards.answer: New England sent fish, livestock and barrel staves / Middle colonies sent flour and grain / South sent rice and timber
items: New England sent fish, livestock and barrel staves
Middle colonies sent flour and grain

cards.front: Why did colonial merchants regularly smuggle French sugar and molasses despite the Navigation Acts?
cards.answer: French sugar and molasses were cheaper, and cheap smuggled molasses often meant the difference between profit and loss for distilleries.

cards.front: Why did King George I issue a Proclamation offering pardons to pirates in 1717?
cards.answer: It aimed to thin pirate numbers by encouraging surrender before a fixed date, without needing military force.

cards.front: Name the three ways the lesson says high unemployment is costly.
cards.answer: Individuals lose income and purpose / Government pays more benefits and collects less tax / The economy wastes productive capacity
items: Government pays more benefits and collects less tax

cards.front: Name the five conflicts between economic objectives described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Growth vs inflation / Growth vs balance of payments / Unemployment vs inflation / Growth vs environmental sustainability / Growth vs income equality

cards.front: Why can economic growth conflict with environmental sustainability?
cards.answer: More output generally means more energy use, transport and waste, increasing carbon emissions and resource use.

cards.front: Why can economic growth conflict with income equality?
cards.answer: During strong growth, profits and returns to capital often rise faster than wages for low-income workers, widening the gap between rich and poor.

cards.front: Name the four primary research methods named in the lesson.
cards.answer: Questionnaires / Interviews / Trialling / Focus groups

cards.front: Name the four secondary research sources named in the lesson.
cards.answer: Newspapers and magazines / The census / Websites / Internal data

cards.front: Why can a focus group give a biased result?
cards.answer: A small group of 6–10 people is used, and one loud voice can dominate and skew the reactions captured.

cards.front: Why do businesses like Tesco and Netflix use both qualitative and quantitative data?
cards.answer: Quantitative data shows what customers do, while qualitative data explains why, so together they answer the full question.

cards.front: Why does Shelley present Victor's guilt over Justine's death as a moral crime equal to the Creature's violence?
cards.answer: Victor feels the 'never-dying worm' of guilt but only weeps and agonises, doing nothing to save the innocent Justine from execution.

cards.front: How does the framing of Justine show a change in the Creature's behaviour?
cards.answer: It shows the Creature has learned from human society how to manipulate justice, mirroring the cruelty it has received.

cards.front: Name the six long-term sources of finance given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Personal savings / Venture capital / Share capital / Loans / Retained profit / Crowd funding

cards.front: What three factors determine the best source of finance for a business?
cards.answer: The amount needed / How quickly it must be repaid / The implications for ownership and control
items: How quickly it must be repaid
The implications for ownership and control

cards.front: Why does a bank loan make cash-flow planning easier than an overdraft?
cards.answer: A loan has a fixed sum and a predictable repayment schedule, unlike an overdraft which can be withdrawn at short notice.

cards.front: Why might a brand-new start-up struggle to get an overdraft or trade credit?
cards.answer: It has no trading history, so banks are cautious about lending and suppliers may demand upfront payment until trust is established.

cards.front: Name the four logical operators covered in this lesson.
cards.answer: AND / OR / NOT / XOR

cards.front: What are the three common mistakes to avoid in truth table questions, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Confusing XOR with OR / Filling in only the output column for combined gates / Mixing up Boolean notation with arithmetic
items: Filling in only the output column for combined gates
Mixing up Boolean notation with arithmetic

cards.front: Why must you add an intermediate column when building a truth table for the expression NOT A AND B?
cards.answer: Because NOT A must be worked out first before it can be combined with B in the AND stage, so each stage needs its own column.

cards.front: Why are universal gates like NAND practically important for hardware manufacturers?
cards.answer: They let manufacturers produce one gate type in bulk and use it to build every other gate, simplifying chip design and cutting costs.

title: The Catholic Church, the Pope and Veneration of Mary
subject: religious-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Why does the Catholic Church see divisions among Christians as a problem?
cards.answer: Because the Church is meant to be 'one', so division wounds that unity, which Catholics pray and work to heal through ecumenical dialogue.

cards.front: How does the Catechism explain 'outside the Church there is no salvation' in a nuanced way?
cards.answer: Those who know the Church is necessary but refuse to enter cannot be saved, but those without the chance to know the Gospel may still be saved through God's mercy.

cards.front: What did the Second Vatican Council achieve, according to the lesson (name the four effects listed)?
cards.answer: Transformed Catholic worship / Strengthened the role of the laity / Launched new ecumenical dialogue / Launched new inter-faith dialogue
items: Strengthened the role of the laity

title: Modern tactics: trenches, guerrilla and beyond
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four conflicts the lesson gives where British forces faced guerrilla campaigns.
cards.answer: Boer War (1899-1902) / Mau Mau in Kenya (1952-1960) / The Troubles in Northern Ireland (1969-1998) / Falklands (1982)

cards.front: Name the three types of trench in a typical British trench system.
cards.answer: Front-line trench / Support trench / Reserve trench

cards.front: Why was crossing No Man's Land so dangerous for attacking infantry?
cards.answer: It exposed men to machine gun fire across torn ground, barbed wire and shell craters with almost no cover.

cards.front: How did British forces overcome well-defended Argentine positions in the Falklands War?
cards.answer: They used night assaults with superior training, night-vision equipment and fire support to overcome defenders in difficult terrain.

title: Key Sociological Concepts and the Sociological Approach
subject: sociology-eduqas

cards.front: Name the eight core concepts of GCSE Sociology given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Culture / Norms / Values / Roles / Status / Identity / Sanctions / Cultural diversity

cards.front: What three social processes does the lesson give as examples of how society reproduces itself?
cards.answer: Socialisation / Social control / Social stratification

cards.front: Why do sociologists say a social role exists independently of the individual who fills it?
cards.answer: Because the bundle of norms attached to a role, like teacher, existed before that person took it and remains after they leave.

cards.front: How do interactionists explain where social structures come from?
cards.answer: They argue structures are produced by the countless daily face-to-face interactions in which individuals negotiate meaning.

cards.front: Name the three categories of test data the lesson describes for testing input ranges.
cards.answer: Normal test data / Boundary test data / Erroneous test data

cards.front: Name the four good uses for procedures given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Printing a menu / Displaying a result / Writing a line to a file / Sending a notification
items: Writing a line to a file

cards.front: Why does using local variables instead of global variables reduce the risk of bugs?
cards.answer: Only the function itself can change a local variable, so if a value gets corrupted the problem is isolated immediately instead of hidden across many functions.

cards.front: Since this Python subset has no global keyword, how does a subprogram update a value that needs to change outside it?
cards.answer: The subprogram takes the value in as a parameter and returns the new value, which the caller then assigns back to the variable.

title: Diodes, Half-Wave Rectification and Zener Voltage Regulation
subject: electronics-eduqas

cards.front: How does a zener diode keep the output voltage constant when the input voltage rises?
cards.answer: It automatically increases its conduction current so the extra voltage is absorbed by the series resistor, keeping Vout equal to Vz.

cards.front: Why does a lamp not need a flyback protection diode?
cards.answer: A lamp is a resistive load that dissipates energy immediately and produces no voltage spike when switched off.

cards.front: List the seven standard zener diode voltage values the lesson gives.

title: Properties of Media & Preparing Products for Distribution
subject: cambridge-nationals-creative-imedia

cards.front: Name the three visible artefacts that appear after several cycles of JPEG re-saving.
cards.answer: Blocky patterns around edges / Smearing in areas of fine detail / Washed-out colours
items: Smearing in areas of fine detail

cards.front: Name the three lossless file formats mentioned in the lesson.
cards.answer: PNG / GIF / WAV

cards.front: Why do GIF images look flat or banded when used for photographs?
cards.answer: GIF is limited to an 8-bit palette of 256 colours, too few to represent the millions of subtle tones in a photo.

cards.front: Why should image dimensions be reduced before uploading to a web platform rather than letting the platform resize it?
cards.answer: Resizing to the exact dimensions needed reduces file size without needing aggressive compression.

cards.front: What three contrasting character pairs does the lesson suggest using for an Animal Farm character question?
cards.answer: Napoleon vs Snowball / Boxer vs Benjamin / Squealer vs Old Major

cards.front: What four techniques does Squealer use to control the animals?
cards.answer: False statistics / Emotional manipulation / Appeals to fear / Systematic revision of history

cards.front: Why does Orwell present Napoleon as fundamentally 'parasitic'?
cards.answer: He never builds the windmill, fights in battles, or produces anything, surviving only by exploiting the labour and loyalty of others.

cards.front: Why can Clover only sense something is wrong but never challenge the pigs' rule?
cards.answer: She cannot read well enough to check the commandments, so she must rely on what the pigs tell her.

title: Heat Transfer & Why We Cook Food
subject: food-preparation-and-nutrition-eduqas

cards.front: Why can boiling never brown food, while frying, roasting and grilling can?
cards.answer: The Maillard reaction needs about 140°C but water limits boiling to 100°C, so browning can't happen.

cards.front: Why does gelatinisation of starch improve palatability, e.g. in a bechamel sauce?
cards.answer: Starch swells and thickens on heating, turning a thin liquid into a smooth, coating consistency.

cards.front: Why does yeast fermentation make bread dough rise?
cards.answer: Yeast ferments sugars in the dough to produce carbon dioxide, creating gas pockets that cause the loaf to rise.

cards.front: Name the three poems explored in this lesson on nature, place and belonging.
cards.answer: Lines Written in Early Spring (Wordsworth) / Shall Earth no More Inspire Thee (Brontë) / Homing (Liz Berry)
items: Shall Earth no More Inspire Thee (Brontë)

cards.front: Name the three key techniques the lesson identifies in Liz Berry's 'Homing'.
cards.answer: Sensory imagery / Dialect words such as 'bibble' and 'fittle' / Enjambment

cards.front: How does Brontë reverse the typical Romantic relationship between poet and nature in her poem?
cards.answer: Instead of the poet celebrating nature, the Earth itself addresses the poet directly, mixing tenderness with reproach.

cards.front: Why does Berry use the extended metaphor of the accent kept 'in a box beneath the bed'?
cards.answer: It makes the relative's hidden voice and lost dialect feel concrete, showing the longing to recover it as specific rather than abstract.

title: Propaganda, the Cult of Stalin and the 1936 Constitution
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: According to the lesson, what three functions did the Cult of Stalin perform?
cards.answer: Concentrated authority in Stalin alone / Stabilised society during violent upheaval / Served foreign policy by projecting a paternal image
items: Served foreign policy by projecting a paternal image

cards.front: What three features of the existing Lenin cult did the Cult of Stalin build on?
cards.answer: Lenin's embalmed body in the Mausoleum / Renaming Petrograd to Leningrad / Speeches opening with a Lenin quotation
items: Lenin's embalmed body in the Mausoleum
Speeches opening with a Lenin quotation

cards.front: Why was the 1936 Soviet Constitution called a 'paper democracy'?
cards.answer: Although it promised free elections and rights, only Party-approved candidates could be nominated, so elections used a single-name ballot.

cards.front: Why did the regime need the Cult of Stalin after the Show Trials had killed Zinoviev, Kamenev and Bukharin?
cards.answer: With the other Old Bolsheviks dead, the cult presented Stalin as the only legitimate heir of October, since no rivals remained.

title: The Prologue, the Brawl & the Ball
subject: english-literature-edexcel

cards.front: Why does Shakespeare have the Prologue reveal the ending before the play begins?
cards.answer: So the audience focuses on how the tragedy unfolds rather than what happens, darkening every happy moment with dramatic irony.

cards.front: Why does Prince Escalus's decision to banish Romeo instead of executing him still lead to tragedy?
cards.answer: His mercy of banishment over death indirectly causes Romeo's absence, leading to the failed plan and the deaths in the tomb.

cards.front: Name the four stages of genetic engineering described in the lesson, in order.
cards.answer: Cut gene out with restriction enzymes / Cut vector with same enzyme / Insert gene as sticky ends pair up / Seal with ligase and transfer to target organism
items: Cut gene out with restriction enzymes
Insert gene as sticky ends pair up
Seal with ligase and transfer to target organism

cards.front: Name the five kingdoms used in the traditional classification system.
cards.answer: Animals / Plants / Fungi / Protists / Prokaryotes

cards.front: Why can genetic analysis give a more accurate picture of evolutionary relationships than looking at physical features?
cards.answer: Physical similarity can be caused by convergent evolution, but DNA similarity directly shows how recently species shared a common ancestor.

cards.front: Why is genetically engineered bacterial insulin considered more reliable and ethical than insulin from animal pancreases?
cards.answer: Bacteria with the inserted human insulin gene can produce large quantities of insulin without needing to extract it from pig or cow pancreases.

title: Context: Gupta, Empire and the World of the Play
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: Why were lascars often given jobs like stoking boilers on ships?
cards.answer: Because of the mistaken assumption that men from hotter countries could withstand the heat better.

cards.front: Why could an ayah's arrival in Britain still be dangerous for her?
cards.answer: Because the family could dismiss her the moment they no longer needed her once on land.

cards.front: Name the two parallel love stories that structure The Empress.
cards.answer: Rani and Hari / Victoria and Abdul Karim

cards.front: Why is the serang who bullies Hari not a straightforward 'British villain'?
cards.answer: He is himself Indian, enforcing the Clan Line's contract on behalf of a system built by British shipping companies, not acting as a British officer.

cards.front: Name the four forms of deception Shakespeare presents in Much Ado, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Benign (gulling scenes, faked death) / Malicious (Don John's window plot) / Performative (the masked ball) / Self-deception (Benedick and Beatrice denying feelings)

cards.front: What three elements does the lesson say each extract-question analytical point should follow?
cards.answer: Identify a technique / Quote it from the extract / Explain its effect on the audience
items: Explain its effect on the audience

cards.front: Why is Beatrice's demand 'Kill Claudio' both inside and against the honour code?
cards.answer: It requests a duel to avenge Hero within the code, yet exposes that women need men to act for them.

cards.front: How does the play's ending relate to Beatrice's gender critique?
cards.answer: The play ends in marriage restoring patriarchal order, even though Shakespeare has spent five acts exposing its flaws.

cards.front: The lesson pairs characters into four relationships to show contrast — name all four pairings given.
cards.answer: Holmes and Watson as complementary opposites / Small and Sholto mirroring men corrupted by treasure / Mary and Holmes representing emotion versus intellect / Tonga and the Irregulars as marginalised figures used by others
items: Holmes and Watson as complementary opposites
Small and Sholto mirroring men corrupted by treasure
Mary and Holmes representing emotion versus intellect
Tonga and the Irregulars as marginalised figures used by others

cards.front: Why does Thaddeus Sholto's wrongful arrest by Jones create dramatic irony?
cards.answer: Because the most morally honest of the Sholtos, who felt guilt and sent Mary the pearls, is the one punished.

cards.front: Name the three legal changes the lesson gives that progressively restricted cruel sports.
cards.answer: Cruelty to Animals Act 1835 (banned baiting) / Marquess of Queensberry rules 1867 (reformed boxing) / Hunting Act 2004 (banned fox hunting with dogs)
items: Hunting Act 2004 (banned fox hunting with dogs)

cards.front: Why was fox hunting not banned during the Victorian reforms that ended bull-baiting?
cards.answer: Its practitioners were politically powerful and argued it was pest control as well as sport.

cards.front: How did the RSPCA's founding reflect a shift in Victorian attitudes to animal cruelty?
cards.answer: It reflected the view that animals could suffer morally, so causing unnecessary suffering was wrong even if entertaining.

cards.front: Why did the crowd take part in public executions at Tyburn rather than just watch?
cards.answer: Executions were designed as spectacles to deter crime and show royal justice, so crowds cheered, jeered and sometimes rescued the condemned.

title: Crude Oil and the Hydrocarbon Industry
subject: science-ocr-b

cards.front: Name the six main fractions produced by fractional distillation of crude oil, from top to bottom of the column.
cards.answer: Refinery gases / Petrol/gasoline / Kerosene / Diesel / Fuel oil / Bitumen

cards.front: Why is cracking needed after crude oil has been fractionally distilled?
cards.answer: Distillation produces too much heavy fuel oil and not enough light fractions like petrol, so cracking converts excess long chains into more useful shorter molecules.

cards.front: How does catalytic cracking break down long hydrocarbon chains?
cards.answer: Hydrocarbon vapour is passed over a hot zeolite catalyst, which breaks the C–C bonds into shorter molecules.

title: Establishing communist rule and early purges
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Name the four categories the CCP's village committees used to classify inhabitants during land reform.
cards.answer: Poor peasants / Middle peasants / Rich peasants / Landlords

cards.front: Name the four types of targets of the Suppression of Counter-Revolutionaries Campaign.
cards.answer: Former Nationalist officials / Triad gang members / Religious leaders suspected of foreign ties / Anyone labelled an enemy of the state
items: Religious leaders suspected of foreign ties
Anyone labelled an enemy of the state

cards.front: How did the Korean War (1950–53) serve domestic purposes for the CCP?
cards.answer: It generated nationalist solidarity and justified continued mobilisation of Chinese society under wartime discipline.

cards.front: Why was the reception of land reform mixed across different regions of China?
cards.answer: Violence varied by locality; some villages carried out peaceful transfers while others used campaigns for private score-settling.

cards.front: Name the four reasons the lesson gives for doing sport (the um...zu phrases).
cards.answer: um fit zu bleiben (to stay fit) / um gesünder zu werden (to become healthier) / um sich zu entspannen (to relax) / um Spaß zu haben (to have fun)
items: um fit zu bleiben (to stay fit)
um gesünder zu werden (to become healthier)
um Spaß zu haben (to have fun)

cards.front: Name the seven key irregular past participles for sport verbs given in the lesson.
cards.answer: schwimmen – geschwommen / laufen – gelaufen / fahren – gefahren / reiten – geritten / treiben – getrieben / trinken – getrunken / essen – gegessen

cards.front: Why do sport verbs like schwimmen and laufen use sein rather than haben in the perfect tense?
cards.answer: They are verbs of movement or change of state, involving moving from one place to another.

cards.front: How does the um...zu construction work when giving a reason for doing sport in German?
cards.answer: It means 'in order to', with the infinitive verb placed at the end of the phrase, e.g. um in Form zu bleiben.

title: The role of women in war
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four support roles the lesson gives for women in the ATS, WRNS and WAAF in the Second World War.
cards.answer: Operating radar and anti-aircraft batteries / Working as drivers and mechanics / Coding and communications work / Intelligence analysis

cards.front: Name the three ways the lesson says medieval women more commonly contributed to the war effort (besides exceptional cases like Nicolaa de la Haye).
cards.answer: Managing estates while husbands were on campaign / Providing supplies and labour / Facing siege conditions alongside garrison troops
items: Managing estates while husbands were on campaign
Facing siege conditions alongside garrison troops

cards.front: How did Florence Nightingale reduce the death rate among wounded soldiers at Scutari?
cards.answer: She introduced rigorous sanitation and supply management, which the lesson says cut the death rate from around 40% to around 2%.

cards.front: Why does Dorothy Lawrence's case show a social barrier preventing women serving in combat roles?
cards.answer: Her commanding officers were more concerned about the risk of embarrassment than about her demonstrated ability to serve.

cards.front: Name the three city-states that made up the Aztec Triple Alliance.
cards.answer: Tenochtitlan / Texcoco / Tlacopan

cards.front: List the four levels of Aztec society from top to bottom.
cards.answer: Huey tlatoani (emperor) / Nobles, priests, warriors and merchants / Commoners / Slaves

cards.front: How could an Aztec commoner rise into the warrior nobility?
cards.answer: By showing military success, such as capturing several enemy warriors in battle.

cards.front: Why do most modern historians doubt that Moctezuma believed Cortés was the returning Quetzalcoatl?
cards.answer: The claim appears mainly in post-conquest sources written decades later, possibly reflecting the interests of groups who collaborated with the Spanish.

cards.front: In the night-light circuit, why is the LDR placed as R2 (bottom resistor) instead of R1?
cards.answer: So that in darkness, rising LDR resistance increases voltage across it, making V(+) HIGH in darkness.

cards.front: How does a comparator's HIGH output turn on the npn transistor in the night-light circuit?
cards.answer: The HIGH output forward-biases the transistor's base-emitter junction through a base resistor, saturating it.

cards.front: Name the five types of malware covered in this lesson.
cards.answer: Virus / Worm / Trojan / Ransomware / Key logger

cards.front: Name the three common forms of social engineering described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Phishing / Pretexting / Shouldering

cards.front: Why is it important to apply software patches promptly?
cards.answer: Unpatched systems remain exposed to known vulnerabilities that attackers can find and write code to exploit.

cards.front: How does encryption protect data even if an attacker intercepts or steals it?
cards.answer: Encryption scrambles the data so it can only be read by someone with the correct key.

title: Music for Stage and Screen: Showstoppers and Symphonic Scores
subject: music-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three typical musical features of a musical theatre showstopper, as described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Rising vocal line / Driving accompaniment that keeps energy up / Key change before the final climax
items: Driving accompaniment that keeps energy up
Key change before the final climax

cards.front: Why does the key change just before the final phrase of Defying Gravity matter dramatically?
cards.answer: It lifts the whole texture higher, giving the singer's belted top note an extra sense of triumph.

cards.front: How does John Williams's Star Wars Main Title immediately establish the story's heroic scale?
cards.answer: It opens with a bold ascending brass fanfare in a confident major key, played in unison by the full orchestra.

title: Causes of crime across the eras
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three factors the lesson says combined to produce witch panics in the seventeenth century.
cards.answer: Economic hardship / Religious anxiety / Superstition

cards.front: Name the three crimes the lesson says were made easier by nineteenth-century urban conditions.
cards.answer: Pick-pocketing / Prostitution / Street robbery

cards.front: How did warfare increase crime in the medieval era?
cards.answer: Armies marching through the countryside looted supplies and left devastated villages, pushing more people into desperate criminality.

cards.front: Why did Tudor Poor Laws end up criminalising poor people?
cards.answer: Vagrancy legislation made being unemployed and without work in the wrong place itself a crime.

cards.front: Name the four short-term precursors to earthquakes that scientists monitor, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Changes in rate of small foreshocks / Fluctuations in groundwater levels / Changes in radon gas concentrations / Anomalous animal behaviour
items: Changes in rate of small foreshocks

cards.front: What four things does the lesson say effective evacuation requires beyond just a siren?
cards.answer: Clearly marked escape routes / Regular drills so residents know where to go / Accessible transport for elderly or disabled people / A communication network that works when power/phone lines are down
items: Regular drills so residents know where to go
Accessible transport for elderly or disabled people
A communication network that works when power/phone lines are down

cards.front: How does Japan's earthquake early warning system give coastal residents time to react before a damaging earthquake hits?
cards.answer: It detects fast P-waves at coastal seismometers and broadcasts alerts before the slower, more destructive S-waves and tsunamis arrive.

cards.front: Why were scientists prosecuted after the 2009 L'Aquila earthquake?
cards.answer: A commission had declared low risk days before, based on misinterpreted tremor data, and the quake killed 309 people, so scientists were blamed for misleading reassurance.

title: Restoring Order: PLA, Lin Biao and the End of the Cultural Revolution, 1968-76
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four turning points that ended the Cultural Revolution, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: PLA restoration of order 1967-68 / Lin Biao affair September 1971 / Zhou Enlai's Four Modernisations 1975 / Arrest of the Gang of Four October 1976
items: Arrest of the Gang of Four October 1976

cards.front: Why did Mao send the PLA into factories, schools and government offices from late 1967?
cards.answer: Red Guard factions had splintered, looted PLA armouries and turned cities into battlegrounds, so the army was needed to restore order.

cards.front: How did the Lin Biao affair damage Mao's plans for succession?
cards.answer: Lin, Mao's named successor, died fleeing after an alleged failed coup, destroying Mao's succession plan and worsening his health.

cards.front: Why did the radicals block public mourning for Zhou Enlai in early 1976?
cards.answer: They feared mourning would turn into a political demonstration against them, but it triggered the Tiananmen Incident instead.

title: Health, Fitness and Components of Fitness
subject: physical-education-edexcel

cards.front: Name the six skill-related components of fitness listed in this lesson.
cards.answer: Agility / Balance / Coordination / Power / Reaction time / Speed

cards.front: The lesson gives four key definitions describing physical activity and its outcomes. Name all four terms.
