cards.answer: Lactic acid builds up in muscles, lowering pH and interfering with enzyme function, causing burning and fatigue.

cards.front: Why do cells with high energy demands, like muscle, liver and sperm cells, contain large numbers of mitochondria?
cards.answer: Mitochondria are where aerobic respiration happens, and it produces the largest yield of ATP to meet high energy demand.

cards.front: Name the three phases the lessons group Leon's dated chapters into.
cards.answer: Domestic / Institutional / Political

cards.front: Why does De Waal write the whole novel in the present tense?
cards.answer: So events feel as though they are happening now, beside Leon, rather than being recounted afterwards.

cards.front: What four practical issues does the lesson identify in researching families?
cards.answer: Access to private family homes / Time and cost of longitudinal studies / Representativeness of participating families / Changing composition of families over time
items: Time and cost of longitudinal studies
Changing composition of families over time

cards.front: What three approaches does the lesson suggest for addressing ethical issues when researching children in families?
cards.answer: Briefing participants on limits of confidentiality / Using independent child welfare advisers / Letting children speak to researchers separately from parents
items: Briefing participants on limits of confidentiality
Letting children speak to researchers separately from parents

cards.front: Why did Ann Oakley criticise Willmott and Young's survey findings on the domestic division of labour?
cards.answer: Their survey used a low threshold for counting male participation, so respondents may have overstated how much housework men did.

cards.front: Why might trends in divorce and marriage statistics not reflect real changes in family behaviour?
cards.answer: These statistics can shift because of legal reforms, such as the Divorce Reform Act 1969, rather than actual changes in how families live.

title: China in 1945: A Country at the Crossroads
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four strengths the Guomindang had on paper in 1945.
cards.answer: Around 4.3 million soldiers / Control of major cities / A UN Security Council seat / Steady American aid

cards.front: Name the four weaknesses hidden beneath the Guomindang's strong surface in 1945.
cards.answer: Hyperinflation / Widespread corruption / Brutal conscription / A hollowed-out countryside

cards.front: Why did Soviet forces in Manchuria hand captured Japanese weapons to the CCP instead of the Guomindang?
cards.answer: Soviet forces controlled Manchuria after Japan's surrender and chose to arm the CCP's Eighth Route Army there rather than the GMD.

cards.front: Why did the Marshall Mediation of 1945-46 ultimately fail to prevent civil war?
cards.answer: Zhou Enlai played for time, Chiang doubted Marshall's promises and used the lull to position troops, so fighting never really stopped.

cards.front: What three pieces of metadata does the lesson say are stored for a bitmap image?
cards.answer: Width / Height / Colour depth

cards.front: Name the three colour depths and their colour counts given in the lesson's key fact.
cards.answer: 4-bit = 16 colours / 8-bit = 256 colours / 24-bit = 16,777,216 colours

cards.front: Why does zooming into a low-resolution image reveal visible pixel squares?
cards.answer: Because fewer pixels are packed into the same display area, making each one visible.

cards.front: Why does CD-quality audio typically need compression, such as MP3, for streaming?
cards.answer: Because CD-quality audio produces very large file sizes, making it impractical to stream uncompressed.

title: Silver, the Slave Trade and the Government of Empire
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four levels of colonial administration below the Council of the Indies, from top to bottom.
cards.answer: Viceroys / Audiencias / Governors and corregidores / Encomenderos, missions and mita rotas

cards.front: Name the five American crops the lesson says slowly transformed European agriculture and cuisine.
cards.answer: Maize / The potato / The tomato / The chilli pepper / Cocoa

cards.front: Why did mercury use in silver refining kill Indigenous mine workers?
cards.answer: Workers used mercury to refine the silver ore, and repeated exposure to it poisoned them slowly.

cards.front: How could the Spanish empire be powerful and economically weak at the same time?
cards.answer: Silver made the crown a great-power military machine, but inflation and reliance on extraction, forced labour and foreign bankers hollowed out Spanish manufacturing and left it dependent.

cards.front: Name the three parts of Leon's character development traced in the lesson.
cards.answer: Part 1: protector, capable and adult / Part 2: identity struggle and deterioration / Part 3: defiant, purposeful, matured by riots
items: Part 3: defiant, purposeful, matured by riots

cards.front: How does the riots experience mature Leon's understanding in Part 3?
cards.answer: He experiences a fusion of personal and political anger, which gives his quest for Jake direction and matures him.

cards.front: Why does De Waal show Carol through Leon's loving memories rather than an objective view?
cards.answer: It prevents the reader from writing Carol off as simply a bad parent, since Leon remembers good times and affection.

cards.front: Why is Salma's bureaucratic language, like 'permanency planning', significant?
cards.answer: It obscures what is really happening, showing how institutional language can be a form of violence that denies children clarity.

title: The Urban-Rural Continuum in the UK
subject: geography-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four main flows that link rural and urban areas in the UK.
cards.answer: Commuting (people travelling to work) / Shopping (people travelling to retail) / Services (healthcare, education, leisure) / Communications (digital and transport networks)

cards.front: Name the four things rural areas supply to UK cities.
cards.answer: Food / Water / Energy / Recreation

cards.front: Why are accessible rural areas growing while remote rural areas are losing services?
cards.answer: Accessible rural areas are within easy commuting reach of a city so gain population and new houses, while remote areas thin out and lose services.

cards.front: Why is fuel poverty higher in rural households than the urban average?
cards.answer: Partly because off-grid rural homes rely on expensive heating oil instead of mains gas.

cards.front: Name the five core reasons the lesson gives for engineering companies implementing quality systems.
cards.answer: Early intercept of production problems / Reducing waste and its costs / Ensuring consistency of finished products / Meeting conformity requirements of standards/regulations / Reducing customer issues (returns, warranty, reputation)

cards.front: Why must the tolerances of two mating parts, like a shaft and a bearing housing, be compatible?
cards.answer: If the shaft's maximum diameter exceeds the housing's minimum bore, the parts will not assemble at all.

cards.front: Why would an engineer choose a micrometer over a go/no-go gauge for inspecting a part?
cards.answer: A micrometer records the actual dimension, allowing tool wear to be tracked so maintenance happens before parts go out of tolerance.

cards.front: The lesson says a news editor makes three choices when selecting stories for a front page. What are they?
cards.answer: Which stories run / What order they appear in / How much space each receives

cards.front: In the lesson's example of a constructed TV report on local flooding, what four elements are shown in sequence?
cards.answer: Aerial drone footage of submerged streets / Close-up of a tearful resident / Statement from a local councillor / Graphic showing predicted rainfall
items: Aerial drone footage of submerged streets

cards.front: Why can two media outlets covering the same event produce meanings that feel almost unrecognisable to each other?
cards.answer: Because mediation filters the event through different backgrounds, cultural contexts, employer expectations and commercial pressures, even though the event itself hasn't changed.

cards.front: Why does high verisimilitude make it easier for a product to communicate an ideology to its audience?
cards.answer: Because the more real a product feels, the less audiences question it, so it can position them more powerfully.

title: We Lived Happily during the War
subject: english-literature-ocr

cards.front: Name the three other anthology poems this poem is compared with on the theme of guilt or blindness to conflict.
cards.answer: Vergissmeinnicht by Keith Douglas / Flag by John Agard / What Were They Like? by Denise Levertov
items: What Were They Like? by Denise Levertov

cards.front: Why does the poem's use of 'we' from the very first line implicate the reader?
cards.answer: The title runs straight into the opening line, so the collective pronoun 'we' draws the reader in before any context is given.

cards.front: How does the poem's central idea of complicity differ from the guilt shown in Douglas's Vergissmeinnicht?
cards.answer: Kaminsky's speaker feels wider civilian guilt for doing nothing while war happened elsewhere, unlike Douglas's soldier's specific guilt over a dead enemy.

cards.front: Name the four converging crises the lesson says drive Scenes 5–8.
cards.answer: Del at Mai's / Enid searching for her / Brod's revelation / the final reconciliation

cards.front: Name the five deliberate choices the lesson says shape the play's meaning.
cards.answer: the eight-scene structure / the two physical settings / domestic realism / the hybrid incorporation of Obeah / the technique of gradual revelation

cards.front: Why does gradual revelation of Enid's backstory create dramatic tension?
cards.answer: It engages the audience as active interpreters, since in Scene 1 we sense something is wrong before we know what.

cards.front: What is the effect of the play opening and closing at Mai's bedsit?
cards.answer: The Caribbean spiritual world frames the entire action, since it is both where the story begins and where it resolves.

cards.front: Name the four factors the lesson says affect energy supply.
cards.answer: Physical factors like climate and geology / Cost of exploitation / Technology / Political factors
items: Physical factors like climate and geology

cards.front: Name the five consequences of energy insecurity listed in the lesson.
cards.answer: Exploration of difficult areas / Economic costs / Environmental costs / Food production impacts / Industrial output falls

cards.front: Why did European gas prices rise sharply in 2022?
cards.answer: Russia cut gas supplies after invading Ukraine, while sanctions and pipeline sabotage cut flow further, pushing wholesale prices over fivefold.

cards.front: How did fracking change the US energy supply?
cards.answer: Hydraulic fracturing technology unlocked shale gas reserves that were previously inaccessible, boosting US gas production.

title: Divorce and the Roles of Men and Women
subject: religious-studies-ocr

cards.front: Name the three ways the Catholic Church's position on divorce and remarriage plays out, as given in the lesson's comparison of Christian denominations?
cards.answer: Divorce not recognised for valid sacramental marriage / Annulment is possible instead / Remarriage without annulment bars a person from Communion
items: Divorce not recognised for valid sacramental marriage
Remarriage without annulment bars a person from Communion

cards.front: Why can the Catholic Church not recognise divorce as ending a marriage?
cards.answer: Because it teaches that valid sacramental marriages are indissoluble, so divorce cannot end one.

cards.front: Why do many theologians reject 1 Timothy 2:11-14 as a rule restricting women's leadership today?
cards.answer: They argue it addresses a specific local situation in Ephesus rather than being a universal rule.

cards.front: Why do non-religious perspectives see divorce as sometimes necessary despite the pain it causes?
cards.answer: Because the harm principle means remaining in a damaging or abusive marriage can cause greater harm than ending it.

title: Case Studies, Correlations and Types of Data
subject: psychology-ocr

cards.front: Name the three dot patterns scatter diagrams show for the three types of correlation.
cards.answer: Positive correlation: dots trend bottom-left to top-right / Negative correlation: dots trend top-left to bottom-right / Zero correlation: scattered cloud with no clear pattern
items: Positive correlation: dots trend bottom-left to top-right
Negative correlation: dots trend top-left to bottom-right
Zero correlation: scattered cloud with no clear pattern

cards.front: Name the four benefits the lesson gives for quantitative, qualitative, primary and secondary data.
cards.answer: Quantitative data allows comparison / Qualitative data allows depth / Primary data is tailored to the study / Secondary data saves time and resources
items: Primary data is tailored to the study
Secondary data saves time and resources

cards.front: Why might a case study researcher's interpretation of their findings be biased?
cards.answer: The researcher may grow close to the person being studied over time, risking a subjective or biased interpretation.

cards.front: Why does the correlation between ice cream sales and drowning rates not mean ice cream causes drowning?
cards.answer: Hot weather is a third variable that affects both ice cream sales and drowning rates, causing the correlation.

cards.front: Name six services that local councils provide, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Rubbish collection / Roads and parks / Planning permission / Social care for elderly/vulnerable / Housing / Libraries and leisure facilities

cards.front: Why does central government retain significant influence over what councils can afford to do?
cards.answer: Because most council funding comes as grants from central government, not from council tax alone.

cards.front: Why do critics argue English Votes for English Laws (EVEL) is problematic?
cards.answer: It creates a two-tier Parliament, complicates voting on the same bill, and risks deepening divisions between UK nations.

title: Practitioner Application: Naturalism vs Heightened Style
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: What three key questions does Stanislavski's system ask for every moment on stage?
cards.answer: What does my character want? (objective) / What is stopping them? (obstacle) / What action do they take?

cards.front: The lesson says a director's choice between naturalism and heightened style affects which six departments?
cards.answer: performer training / voice work / blocking / set design / lighting / costume

cards.front: Why does the prologue of Romeo and Juliet work as a Brechtian framing device?
cards.answer: It tells the audience the ending before it begins, so they cannot be surprised and must think about why the tragedy happens, not whether it will.

cards.front: How does Frantic Assembly's physical theatre style externalise Romeo and Juliet's desire?
cards.answer: It makes emotional force literal and spatial through the physics of the performers' bodies, weight, momentum and proximity, such as a run ending in a catch.

title: The End of the Mandate and the Creation of Israel, 1945–48
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three armed Jewish underground groups active in Palestine by 1945.
cards.answer: Haganah / Irgun / Lehi (Stern Gang)

cards.front: What were the two plans contained in the September 1947 UNSCOP report?
cards.answer: Majority plan: partition into Jewish and Arab states / Minority plan: single federal state
items: Majority plan: partition into Jewish and Arab states

cards.front: Why did the King David Hotel bombing push Britain towards withdrawal from Palestine?
cards.answer: It showed insurgents could strike British rule's heart, meaning holding the Mandate meant endless costly counter-insurgency Britain no longer wanted to fund.

cards.front: Why did the Deir Yassin attack accelerate the Palestinian exodus in 1948?
cards.answer: News of the killing of around 100 villagers spread rapidly, causing Palestinian civilians near the fighting to flee in fear.

cards.front: Name the seven types of EM wave in order of decreasing wavelength.
cards.answer: Radio waves / Microwaves / Infrared / Visible light / Ultraviolet / X-rays / Gamma rays

cards.front: Why can long wave radio signals travel around hills but short wave signals reach distant places differently?
cards.answer: Long wave diffracts around hills, while short wave reflects off the ionosphere for long-distance communication.

cards.front: How does the danger of EM radiation change as frequency increases?
cards.answer: Danger generally increases with frequency, from low-risk radio waves and microwaves to cell-damaging X-rays and gamma rays.

title: The Nature of God and the Trinity
subject: religious-studies-ocr

cards.front: Name the three persons of the Trinity and their roles, as given in the lesson's Key Fact.
cards.answer: God the Father - creator and sustainer / God the Son - Jesus, incarnate redeemer / God the Holy Spirit - counsellor and guide
items: God the Father - creator and sustainer
God the Son - Jesus, incarnate redeemer
God the Holy Spirit - counsellor and guide

cards.front: Why do Evangelical and Pentecostal Christians often emphasise God's immanence?
cards.answer: They stress his closeness, availability and power to act in daily life.

cards.front: Why does the Trinity matter for how Christians understand love?
cards.answer: Because God is three persons in relationship within himself, love is not added later but is what he eternally is.

cards.front: Why do Unitarian Christians like the Christadelphians reject the doctrine of the Trinity?
cards.answer: They believe God is strictly one person, the Father alone, and argue the Trinity was a later addition not found in scripture.

title: Believers, Creation and Humanity as Khalifah
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: The lesson gives three groups of people described at the start of Surah al-Baqarah. What are they?
cards.answer: Believers / Disbelievers / Hypocrites

cards.front: Why does the Qur'an treat hypocrisy as more dangerous than open disbelief?
cards.answer: Because hypocrites claim to believe but do not, and this corrupts the community from within.

cards.front: How does the khalifah concept lead to Islamic environmental ethics?
cards.answer: As Allah's steward on earth, humanity is a trustee not an owner, so environmental destruction is a betrayal of that trust.

title: End of the war and its international legacy
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Name the three legacies the lesson gives for the USA of the Vietnam War (besides the death toll)
cards.answer: Exposed the limits of American military power / Damaged public trust in government / Produced a generation of veterans with physical and psychological injuries
items: Exposed the limits of American military power
Produced a generation of veterans with physical and psychological injuries

cards.front: Name the three schools of interpretation of appeasement given in the lesson
cards.answer: Guilty Men / A.J.P. Taylor's revisionist reading / R.A.C. Parker's reply

cards.front: Why did Congress pass the War Powers Act in 1973?
cards.answer: It was a direct response to the way the President had bypassed congressional approval throughout the Vietnam War.

cards.front: How did A.J.P. Taylor's revisionist reading of appeasement differ from the Guilty Men view?
cards.answer: Taylor argued appeasement reflected a genuine popular desire to avoid another catastrophic war, rather than culpable naivety.

title: Health, Non-Communicable Diseases and Plant Tissues
subject: separate-sciences

cards.front: Name the four environmental factors that affect the rate of transpiration.
cards.answer: Temperature / Humidity / Air movement / Light intensity

cards.front: Name the five main plant tissues described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Epidermal tissue / Palisade mesophyll / Spongy mesophyll / Xylem / Phloem

cards.front: How does spongy mesophyll tissue help gas exchange in a leaf?
cards.answer: It has air spaces that let carbon dioxide and oxygen diffuse easily through the leaf.

cards.front: How does transpiration cause water to move up through the xylem?
cards.answer: Water evaporates and diffuses from the leaf surface, creating a transpiration stream that pulls water up through the xylem.

title: Popular entertainment in the Jazz Age
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four Hollywood stars the lesson names as household names in the 1920s.
cards.answer: Charlie Chaplin / Mary Pickford / Douglas Fairbanks / Rudolph Valentino

cards.front: Name the four ways the lesson describes flappers defying social convention.
cards.answer: Wore short skirts / cut their hair short / wore make-up / drank and smoked publicly

cards.front: Why did talkies give Hollywood a special commercial advantage in Britain and other English-speaking markets?
cards.answer: Because talkies used English-language dialogue, making American films especially influential and popular in English-speaking countries.

cards.front: Why was jazz controversial among conservatives in 1920s America?
cards.answer: Many conservatives condemned jazz as immoral and associated it with Black culture.

cards.front: Name the five narrative techniques the lesson says Syal uses in Anita and Me.
cards.answer: Child narrator / Humour / Code-switching / Episodic structure / Foreshadowing

cards.front: What three events make up the 'crisis' phase of Meena's bildungsroman arc?
cards.answer: Sam's racism / the attack / the riding accident

cards.front: Why does Meena's narration wander, circle back and sometimes contradict itself?
cards.answer: It mimics the way memory actually works, reflecting the instability of childhood identity.

cards.front: How does the split between Punjabi and English mirror Meena's identity?
cards.answer: Punjabi dominates at home while English is required outside, mirroring the tension between her two identities.

title: Valor Ecclesiasticus and Visitation of the Monasteries
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Name the four types of misconduct the Comperta alleged monasteries were guilty of.
cards.answer: Sodomy / Keeping of concubines / Superstitious relics / Financial corruption

cards.front: Name the four obligations the Valor Ecclesiasticus recorded monasteries owed in return for holding their lands.
cards.answer: Charitable distributions / Almsgiving / Hospitality / Maintenance of bridges and roads

cards.front: Why did the Valor and Comperta together give Parliament a strong case for the 1536 Suppression Act?
cards.answer: The Valor showed monasteries were wealthy, giving an economic reason, while the Comperta alleged corruption, giving a moral reason to dissolve them.

cards.front: Why did some monks and nuns, like Abbot Whiting, risk execution during the dissolution?
cards.answer: Those who surrendered voluntarily typically received a pension, but those who refused to accept dissolution risked execution instead.

title: Ways of Living: The Four Margas
subject: religious-studies-ocr

cards.front: Name the four margas (paths to liberation) in Hinduism.
cards.answer: Jnana yoga (knowledge) / Bhakti yoga (devotion) / Karma yoga (selfless action) / Raja yoga (meditation)

cards.front: Name the eight stages of raja yoga outlined in Patanjali's Yoga Sutras.
cards.answer: Yama (ethical restraint) / Niyama (personal observance) / Asana (posture) / Pranayama (breath control) / Pratyahara (withdrawal of senses) / Dharana (concentration) / Dhyana (meditation) / Samadhi (absorption)

cards.front: Why do actions performed through karma yoga not tie a person to samsara?
cards.answer: Because they are performed without craving reward or fearing failure, so they do not generate karmic residue.

cards.front: Why is jnana considered the highest path within Advaita Vedanta?
cards.answer: Because it directly confronts and dissolves the ignorance (avidya) that perpetuates samsara.

cards.front: Name the four features that always describe a Newton's third law force pair.
cards.answer: Act on two different objects / Equal in size / Opposite in direction / Same type of force

cards.front: According to F = ma, what three things does the equation tell us about force, mass and acceleration?
cards.answer: A larger force produces a greater acceleration / A larger mass needs a greater force for the same acceleration / If resultant force is zero, there is no acceleration
items: A larger force produces a greater acceleration
A larger mass needs a greater force for the same acceleration
If resultant force is zero, there is no acceleration

cards.front: Why can a rocket still accelerate even though the force it exerts on the gas equals the force the gas exerts on it?
cards.answer: The two equal and opposite forces act on different objects (rocket and gas), so they don't cancel out for either object.

cards.front: Why does a skydiver's acceleration decrease as they fall, before reaching terminal velocity?
cards.answer: Air resistance increases with speed while weight stays constant, so the resultant force and acceleration get smaller.

title: From Hastings to Coronation: William Takes the Throne
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the five places William's army moved through as it circled London during the March of Submissions (mid-October to December 1066).
cards.answer: Romney / Dover / Canterbury / Wallingford / Berkhamsted

cards.front: Name the five towns where motte-and-bailey castles were built within months of Hastings.
cards.answer: London / Dover / Canterbury / Winchester / Wallingford

cards.front: Why did William adopt moderate, conciliatory policies in the early months after his coronation?
cards.answer: Conciliation was a tool of conquest that bought time while William consolidated power, built castles and brought over Norman lords.

cards.front: Why couldn't the Witan's chosen king, Edgar Atheling, stop William taking the throne?
cards.answer: Edgar had no army, the northern earls Edwin and Morcar had returned home, and the archbishops could not raise London to fight.

title: Electronic Systems: Sensors, Logic and Components
subject: engineering-aqa

cards.front: Name the three passive/component symbols the lesson says students commonly confuse, and their correct identity.
cards.answer: Resistor = box or zigzag / Transistor = three connections with arrow on emitter / Diode = triangle pointing to a bar
items: Transistor = three connections with arrow on emitter
Diode = triangle pointing to a bar

cards.front: Why does an analogue sensor need an ADC to work with a microcontroller?
cards.answer: Because most sensors produce continuous analogue voltages, but a microcontroller can only read digital binary numbers, so an ADC converts between them.

cards.front: How does an LDR's resistance change between bright light and darkness, and what effect does this have on current?
cards.answer: In bright light resistance is low giving high current; in the dark resistance is high giving low current.

cards.front: Name the four non-ferrous metals the lesson gives as examples.
cards.answer: Aluminium / Copper / Lead / Zinc

cards.front: Name the four ferrous metals the lesson gives as examples.
cards.answer: Cast iron / Low carbon steel / High carbon steel / Stainless steel

cards.front: How does alloying make a metal harder and stronger than the pure metal alone?
cards.answer: The extra atoms disrupt the regular crystal lattice, making it harder for dislocations to move.

cards.front: Why does reducing grain size increase a metal's strength?
cards.answer: Finer grains create more grain boundaries, which impede the movement of dislocations.

cards.front: Name the three poems studied as 'dark places' poems in this lesson, with their poets.
cards.answer: London - Blake / Nothing's Changed - Afrika / In Romney Marsh - Davidson

cards.front: Name the three institutions Blake's 'London' attacks for allowing suffering.
cards.answer: The Church / The monarchy / The marriage laws

cards.front: Why does Afrika write 'Nothing's Changed' in short, clipped stanzas with no regular rhyme?
cards.answer: The fragmented form mirrors the speaker's controlled anger at continuing racial injustice.

cards.front: Why does Davidson use regular quatrains and an ABAB rhyme scheme in 'In Romney Marsh'?
cards.answer: The regular form creates a hymn-like quality, as if the speaker is worshipping the overwhelming landscape.

cards.front: What three things does the lesson say the total supply of labour in an economy depends on?
cards.answer: Size of the working-age population / Participation rate (proportion willing to work) / Number of hours worked

cards.front: How does capital increase the productive capacity of labour?
cards.answer: Capital equipment, like a mechanical mixer or combine harvester, lets workers produce far more output per hour than working by hand.

cards.front: Why does low occupational mobility cause structural unemployment?
cards.answer: When an industry declines, workers whose skills don't transfer easily to other jobs are left behind and unable to find new work.

title: Treating disease: medieval medicine to anaesthetics
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three main types of treatment used in medieval medicine.
cards.answer: Bloodletting / Herbal medicines / Surgery by barber surgeons

cards.front: Why was speed the most valued skill for a surgeon before 1847?
cards.answer: Surgery was performed on conscious patients, so a fast surgeon reduced the pain and shock the patient suffered.

cards.front: Why did the medical establishment initially resist Simpson's use of chloroform in childbirth?
cards.answer: Some believed pain in childbirth was natural and biblically ordained, so easing it was seen as wrong.

cards.front: Name the four models of faith the lesson identifies across the novel.
cards.answer: Brocklehurst's hypocrisy / Helen's patience / St John's rigour / Jane's marriage as affectionate honesty

cards.front: Name the four earlier settings the lesson says Jane must walk through before the happy ending is possible.
cards.answer: Gateshead / Lowood / Thornfield / Moor House

cards.front: Why does the lesson say Rochester's blindness and injury are a 'humbling' rather than a punishment?
cards.answer: His new dependence on Jane rebalances their relationship, lowering his once-dominant status to create moral equality between them.

cards.front: How does Brontë's use of the Gothic setting at Ferndean differ from its earlier use at Thornfield?
cards.answer: At Ferndean the wilderness marks Rochester's humility and reduced state, whereas at Thornfield the Gothic setting had hidden Bertha's secret.

cards.front: Name the four Gothic conventions the lesson identifies in the novella.
cards.answer: The doppelgänger / The mad scientist / The discovered manuscript / Atmosphere of dread

cards.front: How does the discovered manuscript convention work in the novella?
cards.answer: The truth is revealed through found documents like Lanyon's letter and Jekyll's statement, creating a sense of authenticity.

cards.front: Why does Stevenson make Hyde animalistic rather than simply morally bad?
cards.answer: It suggests evil is a biological reality lurking inside everyone, not just a moral failing.

cards.front: Name the seven spectral types in order from hottest to coolest.
cards.answer: O / B / A / F / G / K / M

cards.front: Why does a star's spectral type reveal its surface temperature?
cards.answer: The dominant absorption lines depend on which elements are ionised or excited, which is determined by surface temperature.

cards.front: How does Wien's displacement law explain why hotter stars look blue and cooler stars look red?
cards.answer: Hotter stars peak in the ultraviolet and appear blue, while cooler stars peak in the infrared and appear red.

title: The Peasants' Revolt: events of May-June 1381
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: What three additional demands did Wat Tyler present at Smithfield on 15 June 1381?
cards.answer: Distribution of Church wealth / Abolition of all lordship except the king's / Equality before the law
items: Abolition of all lordship except the king's

cards.front: Why did the rebels burn John of Gaunt's Savoy Palace instead of looting it?
cards.answer: Rebels forbade looting, turning the act into a symbolic political statement about who they blamed for their condition, rather than theft.

cards.front: Why did the rebel army disperse after Wat Tyler was killed at Smithfield?
cards.answer: With Tyler dead and no leader, and after Richard II claimed authority over them, the rebels lost cohesion and the revolt collapsed.

cards.front: What four things did Cortés lose during La Noche Triste?
cards.answer: About half his Spanish soldiers / Most of his horses / Virtually all his artillery / Virtually all his gold

cards.front: What three things combined to defeat Tenochtitlán in 1521?
cards.answer: Naval blockade with thirteen brigantines / Systematic demolition of the city / A vast allied indigenous army (mainly Tlaxcalan)
items: A vast allied indigenous army (mainly Tlaxcalan)

cards.front: Why was Moctezuma's death in June 1520 so damaging to the Spanish position?
cards.answer: It removed the last possibility of negotiating through the emperor, and the Aztecs elected Cuitláhuac, who organised an assault on the Spanish.

cards.front: Why did Cortés have Mexico City built directly on top of the ruins of Tenochtitlán?
cards.answer: It was a deliberate act of symbolic erasure, physically overwriting the Aztec city as a statement about the permanence of Spanish power.

title: Astronomy: Solar System, Stars and the Big Bang
subject: separate-sciences-edexcel

cards.front: Name the six types of bodies that make up the Solar System.
cards.answer: The Sun / Eight planets / Moons (natural satellites) / Dwarf planets / Asteroids / Comets

cards.front: Give the six stages in the life cycle of a star much more massive than the Sun, in order.
cards.answer: Nebula / Protostar / Main sequence star / Red supergiant / Supernova / Neutron star or black hole

cards.front: Why do communication satellites in high geostationary orbit move more slowly than the International Space Station in low orbit?
cards.answer: A stable circular orbit needs a specific radius for each speed; a lower orbital speed requires a larger orbital radius, so high satellites move slower.

cards.front: Why does an 80 kg astronaut weigh less on the Moon than on Earth?
cards.answer: Weight depends on gravitational field strength, which is lower on the Moon (about 1.6 N/kg) than on Earth (about 10 N/kg), even though mass stays the same.

title: Scenes 1–3: Enid, Del & the Obeah Woman
subject: english-literature-aqa

cards.front: Why does Enid's rejection of her Caribbean heritage create a gap between her and her daughters in Leave Taking?
cards.answer: Because her assimilation strategy means she rarely speaks about Jamaica, so her daughters sense a heritage they cannot name.

cards.front: Why is Mai significant to Del in Leave Taking?
cards.answer: Mai represents Jamaica and the old ways Enid rejected, and recognises Del's potential as her spiritual successor.

cards.front: How does Brod's experience in England contrast with Enid's in Leave Taking?
cards.answer: Brod embodies disillusionment and gave up everything for England, showing a Windrush experience Enid has refused to allow herself.

cards.front: Why was the killing at Glencoe seen as especially shocking, beyond the number of dead?
cards.answer: Soldiers had been billeted with the MacDonalds under Highland hospitality customs before killing their own hosts.

cards.front: How did the failure of the Darien Scheme push Scotland towards union with England?
cards.answer: It left Scotland economically desperate and proved it could not trade independently while England blocked it, driving both sides towards union.

title: The Respiratory System and Gas Exchange
subject: physical-education-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four features that maximise diffusion at the alveoli.
cards.answer: Large surface area / Thin membrane / Rich blood supply / Steep concentration gradients

cards.front: During inhalation, what two muscle actions increase the volume of the thoracic cavity?
cards.answer: Diaphragm contracts and flattens / External intercostals contract and lift ribcage
items: External intercostals contract and lift ribcage

cards.front: Why does air rush into the lungs during inhalation?
cards.answer: Thoracic volume increases, lowering pressure inside the lungs below atmospheric pressure, so air moves down the pressure gradient into the lungs.

cards.front: Why does breathing rate stay high after a 100m sprint even though the race has finished?
cards.answer: Elevated breathing continues to repay the oxygen debt, supplying extra oxygen needed to remove lactic acid and restore the body's pre-exercise state.

title: Gorbachev & the Collapse of the Soviet Union
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: What four problems did Gorbachev recognise were facing the Soviet Union when he became leader?
cards.answer: Stagnating economy / War in Afghanistan draining resources / Cripplingly expensive arms race / Shortages of basic goods

cards.front: Name the three Cold War summit meetings between Gorbachev and Reagan mentioned in the lesson.
cards.answer: Geneva Summit, November 1985 / Reykjavik Summit, October 1986 / INF Treaty signing, December 1987

cards.front: Why did the 1986 Reykjavik Summit talks collapse?
cards.answer: Reagan refused to abandon his proposed space-based missile defence system, SDI.

cards.front: How did Gorbachev's reforms end up destroying the Soviet system he wanted to save?
cards.answer: Glasnost let people criticise the government and demand independence, while perestroika failed to improve the economy, fuelling frustration and nationalist movements.

title: Divorce: Causes, Consequences and Theoretical Perspectives
subject: sociology-eduqas

cards.front: What four main reasons does the lesson give for the rise in divorce since 1945?
cards.answer: Legal change (1969 Divorce Reform Act) / 2022 no-fault divorce reform / Secularisation reducing religious stigma / Changing social attitudes and status of women
items: Changing social attitudes and status of women

cards.front: What are the main consequences of divorce listed in the lesson?
cards.answer: Financial hardship, particularly for women / Social isolation, particularly for men / Varied impacts on children's wellbeing / Disruption of extended family relationships / Significant increase in lone parent families
items: Significant increase in lone parent families

cards.front: Why do men tend to experience greater social isolation after divorce than women?
cards.answer: Men are less likely to have primary care of children and may have weaker social networks outside the family.

cards.front: How do Marxists explain the causes of marital breakdown?
cards.answer: They argue it stems from capitalism's economic conditions, including poverty, financial stress, work alienation and housing insecurity.

cards.front: Name the two elements of asthma treatment during sport given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Reassurance / Inhalers or nebulisers

cards.front: Why does wearing a scarf or sports buff over the mouth help an asthmatic performer in cold weather?
cards.answer: It warms and humidifies the inhaled air, reducing the exercise-induced asthma trigger.

cards.front: Why should a coach make sure a Type 1 diabetic's reliever items, like glucose tablets, are kept immediately accessible during sport?
cards.answer: Exercise significantly increases the risk of a hypo, so fast-acting carbohydrates must be to hand during activity.

cards.front: Why does the body produce symptoms like increased thirst and frequent urination in diabetes?
cards.answer: The body tries to dilute excess blood sugar by drawing water from cells and kidneys filter the excess glucose through urine.

cards.front: Name the three reasons the lesson gives for why reported incidence of mental health problems has risen.
cards.answer: Increased challenges of modern living / Increased recognition of mental health problems / Lessening of social stigma
items: Increased recognition of mental health problems

cards.front: How can updates to the ICD classification system make it look like mental illness has risen, even if it hasn't?
cards.answer: As the system is updated, conditions can be redefined, merged or added, changing how many cases are officially recorded.

cards.front: Why does research suggest higher rates of mental health difficulty among LGBTQ+ groups?
cards.answer: It is often linked to discrimination and minority stress.

title: Bush's War on Terror and Operation Enduring Freedom
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: What three aims did Bush state for launching Operation Enduring Freedom?
cards.answer: Destroy al-Qaeda's leadership and training camps / Capture or kill Osama bin Laden / Remove the regime that protected him
items: Destroy al-Qaeda's leadership and training camps
Capture or kill Osama bin Laden
Remove the regime that protected him

cards.front: What three factors explain why the Taliban regime collapsed so quickly in 2001?
cards.answer: Air force and air defences destroyed within ten days / US paid local commanders huge sums to switch sides / Northern Alliance had prepared for five years
items: Air force and air defences destroyed within ten days
US paid local commanders huge sums to switch sides
Northern Alliance had prepared for five years

cards.front: Why did NATO's invocation of Article 5 in September 2001 matter symbolically?
cards.answer: An alliance built to deter the Soviet Union was now mobilised against a stateless network of religious radicals.

cards.front: Why couldn't the quick US-led military victory in Afghanistan be turned into lasting political stability?
cards.answer: Because the Western ground footprint was deliberately kept small, giving a fast military win but little control on the ground.

cards.front: Name the four risks the lesson gives of starting a business.
cards.answer: Losing savings invested / Giving up a guaranteed salary / Mortgaging a home to raise finance / Long hours replacing evenings and weekends
items: Mortgaging a home to raise finance
Long hours replacing evenings and weekends

cards.front: Name the three common causes the lesson gives for start-ups failing in the first three years.
cards.answer: Under-estimating time to win customers / Over-estimating profit margins / Taking on unaffordable personal debt

cards.front: Why did Pasta Evangelists trial its subscription in London before going nationwide?
cards.answer: Starting small before scaling reduces risk while keeping the potential reward intact if the idea works.

cards.front: How did Sir James Dyson's vacuum story show both risk and reward?
cards.answer: He remortgaged his house and was rejected by five retailers, risking everything, before Japan's stocking led to a billion-pound company.

cards.front: Name the three wartime resisters against Nazi Germany given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Hans and Sophie Scholl (White Rose) / Claus von Stauffenberg (July Plot) / Dietrich Bonhoeffer (anti-Nazi theologian)

cards.front: Name the six countries Germany overran in rapid succession in the first two years of the war.
cards.answer: Poland / Denmark / Norway / France / the Low Countries / Yugoslavia

cards.front: Why did the German advance into the Soviet Union stall before reaching Moscow?
cards.answer: Soviet resistance stiffened, German supply lines became over-extended, and the Russian winter halted the advance.

cards.front: Why did Germany surrender unconditionally on 8 May 1945?
cards.answer: Soviet forces had encircled Berlin and Hitler killed himself on 30 April 1945, leading to Germany's collapse.

cards.front: Name the four sub-problems given for decomposing an online GP appointment booking system.
cards.answer: Patient login / Show available slots / Book a slot / Send confirmation

cards.front: How does breaking a program into subprograms reduce complexity for a developer reading the code?
cards.answer: It shows short, clearly-named blocks instead of one huge sequence, hiding detail inside each subprogram.

cards.front: Why does decomposing the GP appointment system into four sub-problems cut development time?
cards.answer: Each sub-problem is small enough to be designed, coded and tested independently, so a team can work on them simultaneously.

cards.front: Name the four things standardisation keeps identical for every participant except for the IV condition.
cards.answer: Procedure / Instructions / Materials / Environment

cards.front: Name the six planning decisions the lesson says you need to work through when designing an investigation.
cards.answer: Hypothesis / Independent variable / Dependent variable / Extraneous variables / Standardisation / Design

cards.front: How does counterbalancing reduce the effect of practice or fatigue in a repeated measures design?
cards.answer: Half the participants complete condition A first and half complete condition B first, so the practice or fatigue effect balances out across the sample.

cards.front: In the flashcard revision study, why must a difference in participants' baseline memory be controlled as an extraneous variable?
cards.answer: Because better baseline memory in one group could explain the recall difference instead of the revision method used.

title: The Battle of the Cowshed & Snowball's Leadership
subject: english-literature-aqa

cards.front: Why does Napoleon oppose Snowball's windmill plan?
cards.answer: Not because it's a bad idea, but because he opposes Snowball having the credit for it.

cards.front: What did Snowball's windmill plan promise to do for the animals?
cards.answer: It would bring electricity and reduce the animals' workload to three days a week.

cards.front: Name the three brain areas the lesson says brain imaging has shown volume/activity differences in for schizophrenia.
cards.answer: Frontal lobes / Hippocampus / Temporal lobes

cards.front: Why is psychotherapy for schizophrenia usually given alongside anti-psychotic medication rather than instead of it?
cards.answer: Symptoms often need to be biologically stabilised first before a patient can engage fully with talking therapy.

cards.front: Why can psychotherapy for clinical depression sometimes be used alone, unlike for schizophrenia?
cards.answer: It can be used alone for milder cases, only combined with anti-depressants for severe or treatment-resistant depression.

cards.front: Why might symptoms return after a person stops taking biological treatment for a mental health problem?
cards.answer: Because biological treatments change brain chemistry rather than the underlying thoughts or life circumstances causing symptoms.

cards.front: Name the four steps for preparing a light microscope slide, given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Place a thin sample on a clean slide / Add a drop of stain / Lower a coverslip at 45° / Focus on lowest magnification first, then increase
items: Place a thin sample on a clean slide
Focus on lowest magnification first, then increase

cards.front: Why is the cell wall able to stop a plant cell bursting when water enters by osmosis?
cards.answer: It is made of cellulose which strengthens and supports the cell, preventing it from bursting as water enters.

cards.front: Why are mitochondria so efficient at transferring energy?
cards.answer: Their inner membranes are folded into cristae, which increase the surface area for respiration enzymes.

cards.front: Why does iodine stain make plant cell structures easier to see under a light microscope?
cards.answer: Iodine stains plant cell walls and nuclei yellow-brown, making otherwise colourless structures visible.

cards.front: How can PIES impacts of a lack of safeguarding link together in one service user?
cards.answer: Emotional distress can cause social withdrawal, which reduces intellectual stimulation and leads to physical decline through loss of appetite.

cards.front: Why might a person with a sensory impairment struggle to get help if they are being harmed?
cards.answer: Limited access to information and reduced ability to raise the alarm makes it harder for them to seek support.

cards.front: Name the four things safeguarding training ensures all staff can do.
cards.answer: Recognise possible signs of harm or abuse / Know the setting's reporting procedures / Understand their personal duty to report / Know who the DSL is and how to contact them
items: Recognise possible signs of harm or abuse
Understand their personal duty to report
Know who the DSL is and how to contact them

title: The Designers' Toolkit: Set, Lighting, Sound, Costume
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: Name the four design fundamentals that apply to every theatre design discipline.
cards.answer: Scale / Shape / Colour / Texture

cards.front: Name the four core design disciplines in theatre.
cards.answer: Set design / Lighting design / Sound design / Costume design

cards.front: Why does light from directly above (top light) make a face look gaunt or threatening?
cards.answer: Top light creates hard shadows under the eyes, distorting the face to look gaunt or threatening.

cards.front: Why does a design answer naming only 'dark lighting to show sadness' score poorly?
cards.answer: It is vague: it doesn't name the specific element, effect, or connect the choice to a named moment.

cards.front: Name the four nutrients UK law requires bread flour to be fortified with.
cards.answer: Calcium / Iron / Thiamin (B1) / Niacin (B3)

cards.front: Name the five main categories of food additives the lesson covers.
cards.answer: Preservatives / Colourings / Flavour enhancers / Emulsifiers / Stabilisers

cards.front: Why does steaming vegetables preserve more vitamins than boiling them?
cards.answer: The food does not sit in water, so water-soluble vitamin C and B vitamins do not leach out into the cooking water.

cards.front: How does adding nitrates to cured meat like bacon extend its shelf life?
cards.answer: Nitrates inhibit the growth of Clostridium botulinum and other spoilage bacteria, dramatically extending shelf life.

title: Origins of the Universe & Human Life
subject: religious-studies-aqa

cards.front: Name the six things the Bible says God created in order in Genesis 1.
cards.answer: Light / Sky / Land / Plants / Animals / Humans

cards.front: Why do many non-literal Christians see no conflict between Genesis and the Big Bang theory?
cards.answer: Because the Genesis order of light, sky, land, plants, animals and humans broadly matches the scientific order of events.

cards.front: Why do creationists reject the Big Bang theory?
cards.answer: It contradicts a literal reading of Genesis, and cannot explain what existed before or caused the explosion, suggesting a creator.

cards.front: Why do most Muslims reject the idea that humans evolved from apes?
cards.answer: Because the Qur'an describes Adam's special creation from clay, so most believe Allah directly created Adam as the first human.

cards.front: Name the four techniques the lesson gives for how Squealer uses propaganda.
cards.answer: Emotional manipulation / Statistics that contradict lived experience / The 'Jones would come back' threat / Gradual rewriting of the commandments

cards.front: Name the four elements of Napoleon's rise to power that mirror Stalin's, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Eliminating a charismatic rival / Using secret police / Rewriting history / Building a cult of personality

cards.front: Why does Orwell deliberately make Napoleon less charismatic than Snowball?
cards.answer: Because Stalin was not a great orator but a ruthless operator, so Napoleon's power comes from fear and manipulation, not inspiration.

cards.front: How do Boxer's blind loyalty and Benjamin's cynical inaction both enable tyranny?
cards.answer: Boxer's trust is exploited by the pigs while Benjamin sees the truth but stays silent, so neither awareness nor action alone stops the pigs' power.

title: Sources and interpretations of Elizabeth's reign
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three main historical interpretations of Elizabeth I given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Whig/traditional Golden Age view / Revisionist troubled reign view / Feminist view of negotiating power

cards.front: Why do feminist historians say Elizabeth used the Gloriana myth?
cards.answer: It was a clever adaptation to the real limitations placed on women in power in a male-dominated political culture.

cards.front: Why does the lesson say royal portraits are not reliable evidence of Elizabeth's real appearance?
cards.answer: They were official propaganda constructed to project power, purity and authority rather than painted from life.

cards.front: Name the three costs of out-of-town retail parks given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Higher CO2 emissions and air pollution from car use / Independent high-street shops lose footfall and close / Farmland or scrub permanently sealed under tarmac
items: Higher CO2 emissions and air pollution from car use
Independent high-street shops lose footfall and close
Farmland or scrub permanently sealed under tarmac

cards.front: Name three types of shop the lesson says are filling gaps left on UK high streets.
cards.answer: Charity shops / Vape shops / Chain coffee outlets

cards.front: Why did rising car ownership help out-of-town retail parks grow?
cards.answer: Around 80% of households own a car, making parking the most important convenience out-of-town parks offer over the high street.

cards.front: How did technology allow out-of-town retail parks to stock more products than high-street shops?
cards.answer: Large warehouses with refrigeration and stock-control software let one site hold far more product lines than a small high-street shop.

cards.front: Name the seven stock forms the lesson gives for metals.
cards.answer: Bar / Sheet / Plate / Pipe/tube / Castings / Wire / Powder

cards.front: Name the four stock forms the lesson gives for natural and manufactured timbers.
cards.answer: Regular sections / Mouldings / Dowels / Sheets

cards.front: Why can extrusion only be used to make certain stock forms?
cards.answer: Because extrusion needs a shaped die to push or pull material through, creating a length of constant cross-section.

cards.front: Why is it important to choose a stock size close to what a design actually needs?
cards.answer: It reduces waste and expense, and cuts the amount of scrap material sent to landfill, making the process more sustainable.

title: Food as a Display of Wealth and Power
subject: latin-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four Roman writers this lesson discusses in relation to food, wealth and power.
cards.answer: Petronius / Martial / Pliny / Seneca

cards.front: According to the lesson, what three things could a host's food reveal about their guests' status?
cards.answer: Boast about wealth / Humiliate guests / Sort guests into ranks

cards.front: Why does Trimalchio tell his guests that yesterday he served worse wine to more respectable men?
cards.answer: He is deliberately reminding this evening's guests that they rank below the guests he entertained yesterday.

cards.front: Why does Seneca include the story of Vedius Pollio in his treatise?
cards.answer: The treatise urges Nero to show clementia, and Pollio is held up as the extreme opposite, a man who abused power to commit cruelty.

cards.front: Name the four processes that transport sediment along the coast.
cards.answer: Traction / Saltation / Suspension / Solution

cards.front: Give the five-stage sequence in which erosional landforms evolve on a headland.
cards.answer: Crack / Cave / Arch / Stack / Stump

cards.front: Why do constructive waves build up a beach?
cards.answer: Their swash is strong and pushes sediment up the beach, while their backwash is weak so little is dragged back.

cards.front: Why does the Holderness coast erode much faster than the Cornish coast?
cards.answer: Holderness is made of soft boulder clay that erodes easily, while Cornwall's coast is hard rock that resists erosion.

cards.front: Name the three effector responses the body uses when it is too hot.
cards.answer: Vasodilation / Sweating / Body hairs lying flat

cards.front: Name the three effector responses the body uses when it is too cold.
cards.answer: Vasoconstriction / Shivering / Body hairs standing on end

cards.front: How does shivering warm the body when it is cold?
cards.answer: Skeletal muscles contract rapidly and repeatedly, and the increased metabolic activity generates heat.

cards.front: Why is Type 2 diabetes often preventable while Type 1 is not?
cards.answer: Type 2 is linked to obesity and lifestyle so it can be managed by diet and exercise, but Type 1 is autoimmune destruction of beta cells.

cards.front: Name the three types of solar eclipse the lesson describes.
cards.answer: Total solar eclipse / Annular solar eclipse / Partial solar eclipse

cards.front: Name the five key distances/sizes the lesson gives for the Sun, Earth and Moon system.
cards.answer: Sun diameter ~1.4 million km / Earth diameter ~13 000 km / Moon diameter ~3 500 km / Earth-Moon distance ~384 000 km / Earth-Sun distance ~150 million km (1 AU)

cards.front: Why does a total solar eclipse only occur when the Moon is closer to Earth in its orbit?
cards.answer: Being closer makes the Moon's angular size large enough to completely cover the Sun's photosphere, unlike near apogee.

cards.front: Why does the Sun affect Earth's tides only about 46% as strongly as the Moon, despite being far more massive?
cards.answer: The Sun's much greater distance reduces its differential gravitational effect, outweighing its greater mass.

cards.front: Name the three causes of diseconomies of scale given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Poor communication / Coordination issues / Reduced staff motivation

cards.front: Name the six typical sections a business plan includes, as listed in the lesson.
cards.answer: Business idea and aims / Target market / Marketing plan / Operations plan / Management and staff details / Financial forecasts

cards.front: Why does spreading fixed costs over more units lower the average cost per loaf?
cards.answer: Fixed costs stay the same as output rises, so dividing the same fixed cost across more loaves reduces the cost per loaf.

cards.front: How can a business use the extra profit margin gained from economies of scale?
cards.answer: It can cut prices, raise profit margins, or invest the difference back into the business.

cards.front: What four consequences does the lesson say flow from Romeo killing Tybalt?
cards.answer: Triggers his banishment / Separates him from Juliet / Sets the Friar's desperate plan in motion / Leads directly to the deaths in the tomb
items: Sets the Friar's desperate plan in motion
Leads directly to the deaths in the tomb

cards.front: What four events does the lesson say flow from the Act 3 Scene 1 turning point?
cards.answer: The forced marriage to Paris / The sleeping potion / The missed letter / The double suicide

cards.front: How does Romeo's attempt to make peace directly cause Mercutio's death?
cards.answer: Romeo tries to intervene between the fighting Mercutio and Tybalt, and in that moment Tybalt stabs Mercutio under Romeo's arm.

cards.front: Why does Mercutio's death show the feud destroys more than just the two families?
cards.answer: Mercutio belongs to neither the Montagues nor Capulets yet is killed by their feud, proving it consumes participants and bystanders alike.

cards.front: Name the three common mistakes to avoid, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Plot retelling / Bolted-on context / Missing AO2 (no named techniques)

cards.front: Name the two question type choices for the Pride and Prejudice exam question.
cards.answer: Extract-based question linked to whole novel / Discursive question
items: Extract-based question linked to whole novel

cards.front: Why should context be embedded within analysis rather than given its own paragraph?
cards.answer: Bolting on context as a separate paragraph is a common mistake; context should be woven into analysis, not separated out.

cards.front: Why should a student memorise short embedded quotations rather than long passages?
cards.answer: Short embedded quotations are more effective than long passages, so 2-3 per theme should be memorised and woven into analytical sentences.

cards.front: Name the three phrases the lesson gives describing Scrooge's coldness in Stave 1.
cards.answer: His own low temperature always about with him / Iced his office in the dog-days / No warmth could warm him
items: His own low temperature always about with him
Iced his office in the dog-days

cards.front: Why does Dickens insist so firmly at the start that Marley is dead?
cards.answer: So that when Marley's ghost later appears, the supernatural event carries its full shocking weight.

cards.front: How do Bob Cratchit and Fred together establish the novella's moral standard in Stave 1?
cards.answer: They show happiness doesn't need wealth, since Bob has nothing but is content and Fred is joyful, unlike miserable, wealthy Scrooge.

cards.front: How does the cold imagery in Stave 1 link to Scrooge's isolation?
cards.answer: The cold symbolises how Scrooge has frozen out all human connection, cutting himself off from other people.

cards.front: Name the three ways of changing a repeated cell described in this lesson.
cards.answer: Additive process / Phasing / Layering

cards.front: Name the three textural features that build the sound of Reich's Music for 18 Musicians.
cards.answer: Pulsing chords / Tuned percussion interlocking in hocket / Very slow harmonic rhythm

cards.front: How does the texture in Short Ride in a Fast Machine grow from a few instruments to a full orchestra?
cards.answer: Layer after layer is added on top of the pulse, thickening the sound gradually until it reaches a full ensemble.

cards.front: How can you tell from an unfamiliar extract whether it is sonata form or minimalism?
cards.answer: If a clear tune returns transformed, it's sonata form; if a short pattern repeats and mutates with little melody, it's minimalism.

cards.front: What are Darwin's five observations that make up the theory of natural selection?
cards.answer: Individuals show variation in characteristics / Organisms produce more offspring than the environment can support / Best-adapted individuals more likely to survive and reproduce / These individuals pass on advantageous alleles to offspring / Advantageous allele becomes more common over generations
items: Organisms produce more offspring than the environment can support
Best-adapted individuals more likely to survive and reproduce
These individuals pass on advantageous alleles to offspring
Advantageous allele becomes more common over generations

cards.front: What are the two processes that create genetic variation within a population?
cards.answer: Mutations / Sexual reproduction

cards.front: Why does sexual reproduction increase genetic variation?
cards.answer: Fusion of gametes from two parents, plus random allele mixing in meiosis and random fertilisation, gives each offspring a unique allele combination.

cards.front: How can speciation occur when populations become geographically isolated?
cards.answer: Separated groups face different environments, so different characteristics are favoured, and over time they change too much to interbreed.

title: Opposition, persecution and the racial state
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Name the four groups the lesson identifies as persecuted by the racial state.
cards.answer: Jews / Disabled people / Homosexuals / Jehovah's Witnesses

cards.front: What three things did Jehovah's Witnesses refuse to do, leading to their persecution?
cards.answer: Give the Hitler salute / Swear loyalty oaths / Serve in the military

cards.front: Why couldn't left-wing parties organise effective opposition to the Nazis after 1933?
cards.answer: They had been destroyed by mid-1933, and remaining underground Communist and Social Democrat networks were continually disrupted by Gestapo raids.

cards.front: How does eugenics ideology link the persecution of Jews and disabled people?
cards.answer: Both drew on eugenics, which defined the German nation biologically and sought to remove 'undesirable' hereditary and racial traits.

title: The UK in the Wider World
subject: geography-ocr

cards.front: Name the five international organisations the lesson says the UK is a member of.
cards.answer: United Nations / NATO / G7 / G20 / Commonwealth

cards.front: What four factors does the lesson give for why London is a primary node in the global financial network?
cards.answer: Time-zone overlap with Asian and American markets / English language / Common-law legal system / Concentration of professional services
items: Time-zone overlap with Asian and American markets

cards.front: Why did the 2021 container shipping crisis cause goods to stockpile at the Port of Felixstowe?
cards.answer: Imports keep British shelves stocked, but supply chains can be disrupted by events thousands of miles away.

cards.front: Why does soft power matter for the UK's trade and diplomacy?
cards.answer: Soft power underpins trade and diplomacy because countries are more willing to do business with a place they admire.

cards.front: Name the three wires in a UK three-pin plug and their colours.
cards.answer: Live wire (brown) / Neutral wire (blue) / Earth wire (green and yellow stripes)

cards.front: Why must fuses and circuit breakers be wired into the live wire, not the neutral wire?
cards.answer: The live wire carries the alternating potential difference, so breaking it stops voltage reaching the appliance and makes it safe.

cards.front: Why does stepping up the voltage with a transformer force the current to decrease?
cards.answer: Because power in equals power out in an ideal transformer (VpIp = VsIs), so increasing voltage must proportionally decrease current.

title: Arguments For the Existence of God
subject: religious-studies-aqa

cards.front: Name the three main arguments for God's existence covered in the lesson.
cards.answer: Design argument / First Cause argument / Argument from miracles

cards.front: What three objections did Hume raise against Paley's watchmaker analogy?
cards.answer: An analogy is not proof / The universe might have many designers, not one / Poor design suggests an imperfect or uncaring designer
items: The universe might have many designers, not one
Poor design (disease, disasters) suggests an imperfect or uncaring designer

cards.front: Why did Aquinas argue there must be an uncaused First Cause?
cards.answer: Because an infinite chain of causes could never have got started, so something must have begun it without itself being caused.

cards.front: Why do humanists reject miracles as evidence for God's existence?
cards.answer: They explain seemingly miraculous events through natural causes like misdiagnosis or spontaneous remission, believing the world is governed entirely by natural laws.

cards.front: Name the six stages of linear design, in order, as given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Analyse the brief / Research / Write a specification / Generate ideas / Make a prototype / Evaluate

cards.front: What four steps make up one cycle of iterative design?
cards.answer: Produce an idea / Test or evaluate it / Identify weaknesses / Redesign and test again

cards.front: Why does user-centred design reduce the risk of a product failing in the market?
cards.answer: Designers gather detailed user research and continually involve users, so the final product is highly likely to meet real user needs.

cards.front: Why is ergonomic design essential for tools and equipment used repeatedly over long periods?
cards.answer: Poor fit between the product and the human body leads to injury or error, so ergonomic design improves safety and comfort.

cards.front: Name the three March zones used to administer each side of the Anglo-Scottish border.
cards.answer: West March / Middle March / East March

cards.front: Name the five reiver families given in the lesson as raiding across the Anglo-Scottish border.
cards.answer: Armstrongs / Elliots / Grahams / Nixons / Scotts

cards.front: Why did the English victory at the Battle of Pinkie (1547) fail to produce a political settlement with Scotland?
cards.answer: The Scots gained French support and sent Mary to France, frustrating English plans for a marriage union.

cards.front: Why did the Union of Crowns in 1603 end border reiving?
cards.answer: It removed the frontier between two rival states that had let reivers operate, allowing one Crown to suppress the clans.

cards.front: Name the three strict conditions that must be met for lesser jihad to be permitted in Islam.
cards.answer: Declared by a legitimate authority / Proportionate / A last resort

cards.front: Name the three names given for Allah linked to peace, mercy and forgiveness.
cards.answer: As-Salaam (source of peace) / Ar-Rahman (the most merciful) / Al-Ghaffar (the most forgiving)

cards.front: Why do some Christians accept violence despite Jesus's teaching of non-violence?
cards.answer: Some Christians believe violence may sometimes be justified as a last resort when all peaceful options have failed.

cards.front: What is the key contrast between Christian and Muslim views on violence?
cards.answer: Christianity has a stronger tradition of absolute pacifism (e.g. Quakers), while Islam more explicitly permits defensive violence under strict conditions.

cards.front: How does Mercutio's Queen Mab speech make his death more tragic?
cards.answer: He is a rationalist who rejects fate and dreams, so dying cursing both families is especially senseless.

cards.front: Why does the Friar call Romeo's threat of suicide 'womanish'?
cards.answer: Elizabethan society expected men to bear suffering stoically, so Romeo's emotional intensity showed a lack of self-control.

cards.front: How does Juliet resolve her conflict between loving Romeo and mourning Tybalt?
cards.answer: She reasons logically that her husband lives while Tybalt would have killed him, so she chooses Romeo.

title: Black America in 1954: Segregation, Voting and the NAACP
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four deliberate barriers the lesson gives that stopped Black Southerners voting by 1954.
cards.answer: Literacy tests / Poll taxes / White-only primaries / Grandfather clauses

cards.front: Name the three pressures the lesson says were converging on Jim Crow by the early 1950s.
cards.answer: Returning Black soldiers refusing segregation / Northern migration giving Black voters political weight / Cold War making segregation a propaganda gift to the USSR
items: Northern migration giving Black voters political weight
Cold War making segregation a propaganda gift to the USSR

cards.front: Why was 'separate but equal' in reality unequal for Black Americans in the South?
cards.answer: Black schools, teachers, hospitals and buses received far less funding and worse treatment than white equivalents despite the law's promise of equality.

cards.front: Why was the NAACP harassed and banned in some Southern states by 1956?
cards.answer: White supremacists saw its legal strategy as a real threat, so states demanded membership records and banned it, like in Alabama.

cards.front: Name the three ways bootleggers supplied speakeasies with alcohol during Prohibition.
cards.answer: Domestic illegal distillation / Smuggling from Canada and the Caribbean / Diversion of industrial alcohol
items: Smuggling from Canada and the Caribbean

cards.front: Name the three signs that Prohibition succeeded in its early years.
cards.answer: Cirrhosis death rates dropped / Arrests for public drunkenness declined / Reduced domestic violence in some areas
items: Reduced domestic violence in some areas

cards.front: Why was Prohibition so difficult to enforce across the USA?
cards.answer: The federal Prohibition Bureau was chronically underfunded, had only about 1,500 agents nationwide, and agents were often bribed.

cards.front: How did Prohibition cause organised crime to grow in American cities?
cards.answer: Criminal networks expanded massively into the alcohol trade, using violence to control territory and corruption to neutralise law enforcement.

cards.front: Name the six indirect object pronouns used with doler, as given in the lesson.
cards.answer: me (to me) / te (to you) / le (to him/her/you formal) / nos (to us) / os (to you all) / les (to them/you all formal)

cards.front: Why does 'me duele' change to 'me duelen' in some sentences?
cards.answer: Doler works like gustar, so it agrees with the body part: singular body part uses duele, plural uses duelen.

cards.front: Why does Spanish say 'tengo fiebre' instead of using a verb like 'to be' as English does?
cards.answer: Spanish uses tener (to have) for many conditions where English uses 'to be', so tengo fiebre literally means 'I have a fever'.

cards.front: Name the four steps of Kennedy's non-military response to the Berlin Wall going up.
cards.answer: Sent Johnson and Clay to West Berlin / Sent a US battle group up the autobahn / Deployed US tanks at Checkpoint Charlie / Gave the 'Ich bin ein Berliner' speech in 1963
items: Sent Johnson and Clay to West Berlin
Sent a US battle group up the autobahn
Deployed US tanks at Checkpoint Charlie
Gave the 'Ich bin ein Berliner' speech in 1963

cards.front: Why did Khrushchev order the Berlin Wall to be built rather than issue another ultimatum?
cards.answer: The Vienna ultimatum had not moved the West, so Khrushchev needed a way to stop refugees fleeing without starting a war.

cards.front: Why did Kennedy accept the Berlin Wall instead of trying to tear it down?
cards.answer: He had no good military options, since removing the wire would mean troops firing on East German conscripts and risking nuclear escalation.

cards.front: How did the Berlin Wall help stabilise the Cold War in the short term?
cards.answer: It removed Berlin as an immediate flashpoint, letting both leaders turn their attention to other issues.

title: Context: 1981 Britain, Race & the Care System
subject: english-literature-aqa

cards.front: What three things caused the Handsworth riots to break out, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Racial discrimination / Aggressive policing / Mass unemployment in Black communities

cards.front: What immediate event triggered the violence in Handsworth on 10 July 1981?
cards.answer: A well-known police superintendent was attacked / He was trying to calm rumours of a National Front march
items: A well-known police superintendent was attacked
He was trying to calm rumours of a National Front march

cards.front: Why does de Waal's 2016 retrospective viewpoint help show structural racism in the novel?
cards.answer: It lets readers see, through Leon's child perspective, things that were invisible to many white people at the time.

cards.front: How did underfunding affect children's experience of the 1980s care system?
cards.answer: Overworked social workers managed enormous caseloads, so children's emotional needs were often secondary to bureaucratic processes.

title: US involvement in Iran, Iraq and the Gulf War
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: What two reasons did Saddam Hussein give for invading Kuwait in 1990?
cards.answer: Claimed Kuwait was historically part of Iraq / Resented Kuwait's oil overproduction depressing prices
items: Claimed Kuwait was historically part of Iraq
Resented Kuwait's oil overproduction depressing prices

cards.front: Why did the US support for Iraq during the Iran-Iraq War later prove embarrassing?
cards.answer: The USA had armed and supported Saddam Hussein, who then invaded Kuwait less than two years later, forcing the USA to mobilise against him.

cards.front: How did the USA's response to the USS Stark incident in 1987 show its priorities in the Iran-Iraq War?
cards.answer: It treated the Iraqi attack that killed 37 sailors with restraint, showing it prioritised containing Iran over confronting Iraq.

cards.front: Name the three core ideas in the Peelian Principles drafted by Rowan and Mayne.
cards.answer: Police power comes from public approval, not force / The goal is prevention of crime, not punishment after the fact / The police officer is a citizen in uniform, not a separate class
items: Police power comes from public approval, not force
The goal is prevention of crime, not punishment after the fact
The police officer is a citizen in uniform, not a separate class

cards.front: Name the three continuities that persisted in policing despite the changes after 1829.
cards.answer: Policing remained locally administered / Policing by public consent linked back to community tradition / Poverty remained the underlying driver of crime
items: Policing by public consent linked back to community tradition
Poverty remained the underlying driver of crime

cards.front: Why did reform of London's policing get blocked for decades before 1829?
cards.answer: Vested interests defended the old system and there was deep suspicion of a standing police resembling continental state spies and arbitrary arrest.

cards.front: What were Robert Peel's two main arguments for setting up a professional police force?
cards.answer: Urban crime was too large for amateur enforcement, and a disciplined uniformed force would be less threatening to liberty than the existing chaotic mix of watchmen and thief-takers.

cards.front: Name four factors the lesson says have shaped how cuisines evolve over time.
cards.answer: Climate / Trade routes / Migration and cultural exchange / Industrialisation, food technology and globalisation

cards.front: Name the four regional British cuisines the lesson describes.
cards.answer: Scottish cuisine / Welsh cuisine / Northern English cuisine / West Country cooking

cards.front: Why are many traditional British dishes cooked as one-pot or slow-cooked meals?
cards.answer: To make the most of cheaper cuts of meat, which become tender through long, moist cooking.

cards.front: Why is fusion cuisine wrongly seen as less authentic, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Because no cuisine is static — ingredients like tomatoes and chillies only reached Italy and India in the 16th century, showing authenticity means internal consistency, not pure origins.

cards.front: Name the eight energy stores given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Kinetic / Thermal / Chemical / Elastic potential / Gravitational potential / Electrostatic / Magnetic / Nuclear

cards.front: Name the four energy transfer pathways given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Mechanically (by forces) / Electrically (by currents) / By heating / By radiation

cards.front: Why does a ball thrown upwards momentarily stop at the top of its flight?
cards.answer: All of its kinetic energy has transferred into the gravitational potential store, leaving none for movement.

title: Bombs over London: Black Saturday, the East End and the V-weapons
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four types of bombs used by Germany against London during the war.
cards.answer: Incendiary bombs (magnesium sticks) / High-explosive bombs (50–1,800kg) / V1 doodlebugs (jet-powered) / V2 rockets (supersonic ballistic missiles)
