cards.answer: All soldiers manned the fire step with bayonets fixed, ready for a possible enemy attack.

cards.front: Why can't newborn babies walk straight after birth?
cards.answer: The cerebellum, which coordinates movement and balance, continues developing into early childhood.

cards.front: Why does the brain develop in a bottom-up order, with survival structures first?
cards.answer: This reflects evolution prioritising survival over sophisticated cognition, so life-sustaining structures form before thinking structures.

cards.front: Name the three stages of Othello's language arc from Acts 1-2 to Act 4.
cards.answer: Eloquent iambic pentameter (Acts 1-2) / Fragmented, broken prose (Act 4 Scene 1) / Epileptic collapse

cards.front: What three ideas has Othello adopted from Iago's worldview by Act 4?
cards.answer: Women are dishonest / Appearance hides corruption / Love is a facade

cards.front: Why is Iago's word 'medicine' ironic when he watches Othello's fit?
cards.answer: Iago claims to be healing Othello, but he is actually the disease destroying him, not the cure.

cards.front: How does Othello's collapsing language mirror his loss of identity?
cards.answer: As his once eloquent, dignified rhetoric fractures into broken prose and incoherence, the destruction of his speech mirrors the destruction of the self it once defined.

cards.front: Why does a skilful movement in a chain like a javelin throw break down if one body part fires too early?
cards.answer: Different body parts must work together in the correct timed sequence, so an early or late link disrupts the co-ordination.

cards.front: Why is a gymnastics floor routine classed as a closed skill even though it is very complex?
cards.answer: Closed depends on the environment being predictable and controlled, not on how difficult or complex the skill's movements are.

cards.front: Name the four characters and their different responses to duality that the lesson identifies.
cards.answer: Jekyll — attempts to separate good and evil / Hyde — evil without conscience / Utterson — refuses to look too closely / Lanyon — destroyed by the truth he cannot accept
items: Jekyll — attempts to separate good and evil
Utterson — refuses to look too closely
Lanyon — destroyed by the truth he cannot accept

cards.front: Why does Utterson fail to investigate Jekyll even though he suspects something is wrong for months?
cards.answer: Victorian propriety forbids intrusion into another gentleman's private affairs, so he never asks the right questions.

cards.front: Why does witnessing Jekyll's transformation kill Lanyon?
cards.answer: It exposes a truth his conventional Victorian worldview could only survive while hidden, so it shatters once revealed.

cards.front: Name the three main functions Kenilworth Castle served across its history, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Military fortress and defence / Aristocratic/royal residence / Administrative and political centre

cards.front: What four things did Colonel Joseph Hawkesworth's 1649-50 slighting of Kenilworth involve?
cards.answer: Breaching part of the Norman keep / Stripping lead from roofs / Cutting the causeway dam / Draining the Great Mere permanently
items: Breaching part of the Norman keep

cards.front: How did John of Gaunt change Kenilworth's function after inheriting it in 1361?
cards.answer: He transformed it from a military fortress into a palatial residence with state apartments, a great hall and an administrative centre for his estates.

cards.front: Why did Robert Dudley spend so lavishly on the 1575 royal entertainment at Kenilworth?
cards.answer: It was political theatre designed to show Dudley's fitness as a royal consort and persuade Elizabeth I to marry him.

cards.front: Name the three key techniques Berry uses in 'On an Afternoon Train from Purley to Victoria, 1955'.
cards.answer: Documentary precision / Free verse and everyday language / Four stanzas marking conversation stages

cards.front: Name the three key techniques Dharker uses in 'A Century Later'.
cards.answer: War imagery in a peaceful setting / Enjambment across a stanza break / Free verse with no fixed stanza pattern
items: War imagery in a peaceful setting
Free verse with no fixed stanza pattern

cards.front: How does Berry's plain, unmetaphorical tone make the woman's racism in the poem more disturbing?
cards.answer: It shows the casual racism as ordinary and unremarkable, built into everyday life rather than exceptional.

cards.front: How does Robinson's use of imperatives like 'trace', 'smell' and 'hum' support the poem's idea of home?
cards.answer: They ask the reader to use their senses, showing cultural memory is embodied in the body, not just the mind.

title: Glaciated Uplands: Land Use, Tourism & Management
subject: geography-edexcel-a

cards.front: Name the five main economic activities that occupy UK glaciated uplands.
cards.answer: Upland farming / Commercial forestry / Quarrying / Water storage / Tourism

cards.front: Name the three traditional methods Fix the Fells uses to repair eroded upland paths.
cards.answer: Stone pitching / Drainage channels / Helicopter-lifts of stone

cards.front: Why do deep U-shaped glacial troughs make good sites for reservoirs?
cards.answer: They form natural deep basins in the valley that can be dammed or raised to store water for public supply.

cards.front: Why did UNESCO World Heritage status in 2017 partly worsen the tourism problem it aimed to help manage?
cards.answer: It raised the landscape's international profile, which increased international visitor numbers and added to visitor pressure.

cards.front: Name the three qualities the lesson says Anita Rutter values (contrasted with Meena's parents' values).
cards.answer: Toughness / Streetwise savvy / Social dominance

cards.front: Name the three factors the lesson says can turn ordinary people into agents of hatred, as shown through Sam Lowbridge.
cards.answer: Economic deprivation / Poor education / Political manipulation through figures like Powell
items: Political manipulation through figures like Powell

cards.front: Why does Meena keep tolerating Anita's cruelty and put-downs in their friendship?
cards.answer: Because being Anita's follower feels better to Meena than being left alone.

cards.front: How do Anita and Sam differ in the way they respond to their shared deprivation, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Anita manipulates individuals for personal control, while Sam targets entire communities through racism.

cards.front: Name the four key rights the Data Protection Act 2018 / UK GDPR gives individuals.
cards.answer: Right of access (Subject Access Request) / Right to erasure (right to be forgotten) / Right to rectification / Right to data portability
items: Right to erasure (right to be forgotten)

cards.front: Name the four things the BCS Code of Conduct requires members to do.
cards.answer: Act in the public interest / Maintain professional competence / Act with integrity / Respect the organisation and individuals

cards.front: Why was the Computer Misuse Act 1990 introduced?
cards.answer: Because two high-profile hacking cases showed UK law had no way to prosecute unauthorised access to computer systems.

cards.front: Why must a programmer report a serious security flaw in their employer's software, even if it's commercially damaging?
cards.answer: The BCS Code of Conduct requires acting with integrity and reporting concerns about unethical or dangerous software in the public interest.

title: McCarthyism and the Red Scare of the 1950s
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the four events that triggered the second Red Scare.
cards.answer: Soviet atomic bomb (Aug 1949) / Communist victory in China (Oct 1949) / Conviction of Alger Hiss (Jan 1950) / Outbreak of the Korean War (June 1950)

cards.front: Name four groups of people affected by McCarthyism beyond the entertainment industry, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Marxist academics sacked by universities / Books removed from public libraries / Left-wing officers purged from trade unions / China experts lost from the State Department
items: Left-wing officers purged from trade unions
China experts lost from the State Department

cards.front: Why did Hollywood studios issue the Waldorf Statement in November 1947?
cards.answer: Studios were terrified of losing audiences, so they announced they would not employ Communists.

cards.front: Why did Eisenhower drop his planned defence of General Marshall during his 1952 campaign in Wisconsin?
cards.answer: McCarthy had become electorally dangerous, so Eisenhower avoided confronting him rather than defend his friend Marshall.

title: CPU, Main Memory and the Fetch-Decode-Execute Cycle
subject: computer-science-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three key components of the CPU itself.
cards.answer: Control unit / Arithmetic logic unit (ALU) / Registers

cards.front: Name the three buses that connect the CPU to main memory.
cards.answer: Address bus / Data bus / Control bus

cards.front: Why did the stored-program concept mean a computer no longer had to be physically rewired to run a different program?
cards.answer: Because instructions and data are stored together in memory, so changing the data in memory changed the program, letting the same hardware run any program.

cards.front: Why is there no bus activity during the decode stage of the fetch-decode-execute cycle?
cards.answer: Because decode happens entirely inside the CPU, where the control unit interprets the instruction without needing to transfer data.

title: Lenin in Power: Brest-Litovsk, Cheka and Civil War
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the four reasons the lesson gives for why the Reds won the Civil War.
cards.answer: Geography: held the central core with railways and people / Leadership: Trotsky built a disciplined five-million-strong Red Army / Unity: single command and clear cause / Propaganda: cast Whites as agents of foreign capital
items: Geography: held the central core with railways and people
Leadership: Trotsky built a disciplined five-million-strong Red Army
Unity: single command and clear cause
Propaganda: cast Whites as agents of foreign capital

cards.front: Name the four White generals mentioned in the lesson and where they operated.
cards.answer: Denikin in the south / Kolchak in Siberia / Yudenich near Petrograd / Wrangel in Crimea

cards.front: Why was the Bolshevik government forced to accept the harsh Treaty of Brest-Litovsk in March 1918?
cards.answer: Trotsky tried delaying tactics but a renewed German advance forced Russia to accept the treaty to honour the Decree on Peace.

cards.front: Why did the Bolsheviks order the murder of the Romanov family in July 1918?
cards.answer: As White forces approached Ekaterinburg, killing the family closed off any restoration of the dynasty and removed a rallying point.

cards.front: How does Shakespeare show that mercy is not a neutral virtue in the play?
cards.answer: Mercy is a form of power, as the person with authority gets to define what mercy means.

cards.front: Why might Shylock's cruelty be seen as the product of his treatment rather than his nature?
cards.answer: Christian prejudice despised and abused him for so long that it created the 'monster' they feared.

cards.front: For whole-play Shakespeare tasks, how widely should quotations be drawn?
cards.answer: Quotations should be drawn from at least three different scenes.

cards.front: Why does Shylock agree to lend Antonio money despite Antonio's abuse of him?
cards.answer: Lending gives Shylock power over Antonio for the first time, making it strategy rather than generosity.

cards.front: How does Antonio's use of 'the devil' against Shylock reveal his own hypocrisy?
cards.answer: Antonio uses religious language to justify himself while denying Shylock the right to do the same.

cards.front: What four reasons does the lesson give for why Mao launched the Cultural Revolution?
cards.answer: Great Leap Forward damaged his authority / Pragmatic recovery undermined Maoist ideology / Feared revisionist bureaucratic elite betraying revolution / Soviet de-Stalinisation showed the revolution decaying
items: Great Leap Forward damaged his authority
Feared revisionist bureaucratic elite betraying revolution
Soviet de-Stalinisation showed the revolution decaying

cards.front: What three things had Mao achieved by 1968, marking the end of the first phase of the Cultural Revolution?
cards.answer: Liu Shaoqi and Deng purged / Old Party apparatus broken / Army restored order in provinces

cards.front: Why did Mao send Red Guards to the countryside from 1968?
cards.answer: To remove them from the cities before their factional violence became a direct political threat to Mao himself.

cards.front: Why did factional violence break out among Red Guard groups?
cards.answer: Different Red Guard groups competed against each other, each claiming greater revolutionary purity than the others.

title: Africans, Asians and other migrants in early modern England
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Name the three routes the lesson gives for how Africans arrived in early Tudor England.
cards.answer: Members of Spanish and Portuguese diplomatic parties / Servants brought by merchants / Skilled professionals in their own right
items: Members of Spanish and Portuguese diplomatic parties
Skilled professionals in their own right

cards.front: Name the three restrictions the lesson gives that alien residents faced in medieval England.
cards.answer: Paid the alien subsidy tax / Faced restrictions on trading independently / Sometimes required to live with English hosts
items: Sometimes required to live with English hosts

cards.front: Why did John Lok bring five Africans to London in 1555?
cards.answer: He intended to teach them English so they could serve as interpreters for future trading voyages to West Africa.

cards.front: Why did tensions arise between alien merchants and English merchants in medieval England?
cards.answer: English merchants complained that alien traders undercut local prices and took trade away from English guilds.

cards.front: Name the three Pilgrim Festivals.
cards.answer: Pesach / Shavuot / Sukkot

cards.front: Name the five symbolic foods eaten at the Passover Seder meal.
cards.answer: Matzah / Bitter herbs / Salt water / Lamb shank bone / Charoset

cards.front: Why do Reform Jews observe Shabbat more liberally than Orthodox Jews, e.g. driving to synagogue?
cards.answer: They see the spirit of rest, rather than the specific technical prohibitions, as most important.

cards.front: Why is the hanukkiah lit in windows during Hanukkah?
cards.answer: So that passersby can see and the miracle of the oil is publicised.

cards.front: Name the three sources of evidence the lesson gives for what Earth's early atmosphere was like.
cards.answer: Chemical composition of ancient rocks / Volcanic emissions today / Comparison with other planets like Mars and Venus
items: Comparison with other planets like Mars and Venus

cards.front: Why does the absence of oxidised iron minerals in very ancient rocks suggest little free oxygen existed then?
cards.answer: Ancient rocks show what gases were present when they formed, so no rust-like oxidised iron suggests there was little or no free oxygen.

cards.front: Why can't ice cores tell us about Earth's very early atmosphere?
cards.answer: Ice cores only preserve trapped air from up to around 800,000 years ago, far too recent to sample the early atmosphere.

cards.front: Why have carbon dioxide levels risen significantly since industrialisation?
cards.answer: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon that had been locked away for millions of years back into the atmosphere.

cards.front: Name the three unities of drama that An Inspector Calls observes.
cards.answer: Unity of time / Unity of place / Unity of action

cards.front: How does the Inspector's plain, direct language give him moral authority over the Birlings?
cards.answer: His short, simple sentences cut through the Birlings' evasions, unlike their more elaborate, self-serving speech.

cards.front: How does dramatic irony give the 1945 audience moral superiority over the Birlings?
cards.answer: The audience knows Birling's confident predictions about the Titanic and war are wrong, so they reject his worldview.

cards.front: How does Sheila's changing language across the play show her moral growth?
cards.answer: She moves from shallow exclamations like “Oh — how horrible!” to measured, thoughtful sentences showing real understanding.

cards.front: Name the six key structures found inside a synovial joint.
cards.answer: Joint capsule / Synovial membrane / Synovial fluid / Articular cartilage / Ligaments / Bursae/menisci

cards.front: Name the three types of blood vessel in the cardiovascular system.
cards.answer: Arteries / Veins / Capillaries

cards.front: Why does the left ventricle have much thicker walls than the right ventricle?
cards.answer: Because it must generate higher pressure to pump blood around the entire body, not just to the lungs.

cards.front: How does the structure of capillaries allow efficient gas and nutrient exchange?
cards.answer: They are only one cell thick with a tiny diameter, so red blood cells pass in single file, maximising contact time for exchange.

cards.front: What four features must be true of a Newton's Third Law pair of forces?
cards.answer: Equal in size / Opposite in direction / Same type of force / Act on different objects

cards.front: Why does a spacecraft drifting in deep space keep moving at the same velocity forever?
cards.answer: There is no friction or air resistance, so there is no resultant force to change its motion.

cards.front: Why does doubling a car's speed quadruple its braking distance?
cards.answer: Braking distance is proportional to speed squared, so doubling speed multiplies braking distance by four.

cards.front: Why does a book resting on a table stay stationary?
cards.answer: The normal contact force from the table exactly balances the book's weight, giving zero resultant force.

cards.front: Name the three main ways the lesson says consumer law impacts businesses.
cards.answer: Damage to reputation / Cost of returns and refunds / Cost of product recalls

cards.front: Name the four things the lesson says businesses do to stay ahead of consumer law.
cards.answer: Build quality assurance into production / Train staff to handle returns politely / Use clear labelling and honest advertising / Track customer feedback to spot problems early
items: Train staff to handle returns politely
Use clear labelling and honest advertising
Track customer feedback to spot problems early

cards.front: Why did the 2013 Tesco horsemeat scandal wipe £300 million off its stock market value?
cards.answer: Customers switched to rivals after Tesco was exposed selling beef with horse DNA, breaching the 'as described' test.

cards.front: How did the Volkswagen 2015 emissions scandal breach consumer law principles?
cards.answer: Its diesel cars' official emissions data did not match their real performance, so they were not 'as described'.

title: Paris, Saigon and the Price of Conflict
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the four terms the Paris Peace Accords required.
cards.answer: A ceasefire in place / US withdrawal of all military forces within sixty days / Return of US prisoners of war / A vague commitment to political settlement between North and South
items: US withdrawal of all military forces within sixty days
Return of US prisoners of war
A vague commitment to political settlement between North and South

cards.front: Name the three key cities that fell, in order, during North Vietnam's 1975 Spring Offensive.
cards.answer: Buon Ma Thuot (10 March) / Hue (25 March) / Da Nang (30 March)

cards.front: Why did the December 1972 Linebacker II bombings target both Hanoi and Saigon?
cards.answer: They showed Hanoi the cost of breaking talks, and showed Thieu that Nixon would still use force to defend the South.

cards.front: Why did President Ford lack the power to help South Vietnam during its final 1975 offensive?
cards.answer: Watergate had forced Nixon's resignation, while Congress had banned renewed military action and slashed aid, leaving Ford no authority or funds to intervene.

cards.front: Name the three main types of cost in a hospitality or catering business.
cards.answer: Labour costs / Material costs / Overheads

cards.front: Name the four types of media that can impact a hospitality business.
cards.answer: Printed media / Broadcast media / Internet and social media / Competition from other establishments

cards.front: How does a strong pound affect UK hotels?
cards.answer: A strong pound makes foreign holidays cheaper, so fewer people holiday in the UK, which hurts UK hotels.

cards.front: How do online booking systems improve efficiency for a hospitality business?
cards.answer: They let customers book tables or rooms 24/7, increasing bookings and reducing the need for reception staff to answer calls.

cards.front: Name the three ways forces can change an object's shape.
cards.answer: Stretched / Bent / Compressed

cards.front: Name the three things done in the springs practical to improve accuracy and reliability.
cards.answer: Read ruler at eye level / Wait for spring to stop oscillating / Repeat readings and calculate a mean
items: Wait for spring to stop oscillating
Repeat readings and calculate a mean

cards.front: Why should you read the ruler at eye level in the springs practical?
cards.answer: To avoid parallax error.

cards.front: Why does a rubber band's force-extension graph curve from the start instead of being a straight line?
cards.answer: It does not obey Hooke's law, so its force-extension relationship is non-linear even though it still returns to its original shape.

cards.front: Name the three effects acid rain has, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Corrodes limestone/marble buildings / Kills trees / Acidifies lakes

cards.front: Name the four alternative approaches the lesson gives for reducing pollution.
cards.answer: Switch to renewable energy sources / Use electric or hydrogen-powered vehicles / Improve fuel efficiency / Develop carbon capture and storage technologies
items: Develop carbon capture and storage technologies

cards.front: How does flue gas desulfurisation remove sulfur dioxide from power station emissions?
cards.answer: It reacts SO2 with calcium oxide or calcium carbonate, producing calcium sulfate.

cards.front: Why do soot particles cause global dimming?
cards.answer: Soot particles block sunlight from reaching the Earth's surface.

title: Matthew Hopkins and the witch-hunts of 1645–47
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three conditions that overlapped to cause the 1645–47 witch-hunts in East Anglia.
cards.answer: Civil War chaos weakened court oversight / Strong Puritan belief in the region / Hopkins willing to travel for payment
items: Civil War chaos weakened court oversight
Strong Puritan belief in the region
Hopkins willing to travel for payment

cards.front: Name the three reasons the witch-hunts collapsed by 1647.
cards.answer: Cost of paying Hopkins's fees / Growing scepticism, e.g. John Gaule's sermons / Hopkins's own death in 1647
items: Growing scepticism, e.g. John Gaule's sermons

cards.front: Why were most people accused of witchcraft in 1645–47 poor, older women?
cards.answer: Puritan ministers saw women as prone to the Devil's temptation, and villagers blamed poor women refused charity for later misfortunes.

cards.front: How did the printing press help fuel witchcraft accusations in this period?
cards.answer: Cheap pamphlets spread sensational stories of witches soon after trials, giving villagers a ready-made template for accusations.

cards.front: Why did the AIDS crisis intensify prejudice against homosexuality in 1980s Britain?
cards.answer: Tabloid newspapers labelled AIDS a 'gay plague', deepening stigma against homosexuality from 1981 onwards.

cards.front: How does Winterson's setting show class intersecting with religion in the novel?
cards.answer: In a working-class northern community lacking material wealth, the church provides structure, meaning and social connection instead.

cards.front: Why does the church give Jeanette's mother power she wouldn't have elsewhere?
cards.answer: The church gives women like the mother a platform for authority they would not have in secular society.

cards.front: How should context like Section 28 be used when answering the prose exam question?
cards.answer: It must be embedded naturally within analysis of language and evidence, not written as a standalone bolt-on paragraph.

cards.front: What three sounds of war does the lesson say are heard offstage but never seen in Act 1?
cards.answer: Distant shelling / Rifle fire / The rumble of artillery

cards.front: What three ordinary topics do the officers talk about instead of grand themes in Act 1?
cards.answer: Food / Earwig races / Bed arrangements

cards.front: How does keeping the sounds of war offstage but never shown affect the audience in Act 1?
cards.answer: It keeps the violence out of sight, making it more menacing, so the audience can only listen and wait like the characters.

cards.front: How does Stanhope's plan to censor Raleigh's letters create dramatic irony in Act 1?
cards.answer: The audience knows Raleigh's letter will be full of admiration, not criticism, so Stanhope's fear is unfounded.

cards.front: Name the four areas of Jeanette's life the mother controls.
cards.answer: Education / Friendships / Diet / Beliefs

cards.front: Name the six characters and the structural purpose each serves, as given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Mother - control/love contradiction / Elsie - alternative love / Pastor Finch - institutional authority / Melanie - submission as foil / Katy - catalyst for final break / Miss Jewsbury - hypocrisy exposed

cards.front: Why does Jeanette's dual role as narrator and protagonist create dramatic irony?
cards.answer: As a child she accepts her world uncritically, but the adult narrator lets the reader see the control, absurdity and cruelty the child cannot.

cards.front: Why must the local pastor crush Jeanette's difference publicly by denouncing her and ordering the exorcism?
cards.answer: His authority depends on the congregation's obedience, so any visible deviation from the norm must be crushed publicly.

cards.front: Name the four murders/framings committed by the Creature in the novel.
cards.answer: Murders William / Frames Justine for William's murder / Kills Henry Clerval / Strangles Elizabeth

cards.front: Name the three acts that show the Creature's capacity for empathy and connection.
cards.answer: Secretly helps the De Laceys / Restrains itself when attacked by Felix / Approaches the blind father with eloquent humility
items: Restrains itself when attacked by Felix
Approaches the blind father with eloquent humility

cards.front: Why does Justine falsely confess to William's murder?
cards.answer: She confesses under pressure from her confessor, showing how institutional power like the Church can override truth.

cards.front: Why is the De Laceys' rejection of the Creature especially significant?
cards.answer: They are themselves victims of injustice, exiled for helping a wrongly accused man, showing prejudice is universal even among virtuous people.

title: The Problem of Suffering in Islam
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: The lesson gives three atheist/humanist challenges to the 'life as test' response — name them.
cards.answer: Scale of suffering is disproportionate / Some predestined to fail the test by birth / Future paradise makes injustice ethically irrelevant
items: Some predestined to fail the test by birth
Future paradise makes injustice ethically irrelevant

cards.front: How do Muslims respond to the atheist challenge that the scale of suffering is too disproportionate for a fair test?
cards.answer: They argue the Day of Judgement is the ultimate measure of justice, and Allah's mercy and wisdom extend beyond human perception of any case.

cards.front: Why does prayer (du'a) help Muslims cope with suffering, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: It lets Muslims bring their pain and needs directly to Allah, trusting he hears and may respond in ways serving their ultimate good.

cards.front: Why is charity considered a practical response to suffering rather than just accepting it?
cards.answer: Charity redistributes wealth, addressing the conditions that produce poverty and inequality rather than merely accepting the suffering they cause.

title: The Work of Past & Present Designers
subject: design-technology-edexcel

cards.front: Name the ten specification criteria used to analyse a product.
cards.answer: Form / Function / Client and user requirements / Performance requirements / Materials and components/systems / Scale of production and cost / Sustainability / Aesthetics / Marketability / Consideration of innovation

cards.front: What three things did the Arts and Crafts movement promote in reaction to mass-produced Victorian goods?
cards.answer: Hand-craftsmanship / Natural materials / Decorative pattern design

cards.front: Why should analysis of an existing product be linked to the ten criteria rather than just personal opinion?
cards.answer: The criteria give the analysis structure so every point is linked to evidence from the product and the needs of its users.

cards.front: How should product and designer analysis be used within your own NEA project?
cards.answer: It should feed directly into the design brief and specification, and be revisited throughout the project as you test and refine your prototype.

title: Détente, SALT 1 and the Nixon-Brezhnev Era
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the three sources of tension the lesson says détente did not solve.
cards.answer: Ideology: both systems still saw each other as hostile / Third World: Soviet support for revolutionary movements / Human rights: Soviet treatment of dissidents
items: Ideology: both systems still saw each other as hostile
Third World: Soviet support for revolutionary movements
Human rights: Soviet treatment of dissidents

cards.front: Name the three things the lesson says had genuinely changed by 1972.
cards.answer: Arms control became institutionalised / Both sides accepted the other's European sphere / Language of confrontation gave way to negotiation
items: Both sides accepted the other's European sphere
Language of confrontation gave way to negotiation

cards.front: Why did Nixon's February 1972 visit to China strengthen his hand before the Moscow summit?
cards.answer: It split the communist world, so Moscow had to worry the Americans might play China against the USSR.

cards.front: Why did the Soviet treatment of dissidents like Sakharov and Solzhenitsyn damage détente?
cards.answer: It convinced American conservatives that the Soviet human rights record meant they should oppose further concessions.

title: Profit Margins & Average Rate of Return
subject: business-ocr

cards.front: Name the two strengths of the ARR method the lesson gives.
cards.answer: Simple to calculate and explain / Uses the full life of a project
items: Uses the full life of a project

cards.front: Name the two weaknesses of the ARR method the lesson gives.
cards.answer: Ignores timing of returns / Ignores risk and relies on forecasts
items: Ignores risk and relies on forecasts

cards.front: Why does ARR treat a project paying profits in year 1 the same as one paying them in year 5?
cards.answer: Because ARR averages profit over the whole project, ignoring when the returns actually arrive.

cards.front: Why might a small high-street shop have a large gap between gross and net margin?
cards.answer: Because expensive shop rents and many staff create high overheads that eat into gross profit.

title: Form and Methods: Direct Address, Music and Comedy
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: How should an actor physically play one of Helen's asides to the audience?
cards.answer: With a clear turn towards the audience, a shift in eye-line away from other characters, and a conspiratorial, dry vocal tone.

cards.front: Why does calling A Taste of Honey 'straightforwardly naturalistic' miss half the picture?
cards.answer: Because its content feels realistic but it is staged through openly theatrical devices like songs, live music and direct address.

cards.front: Why did Delaney give her characters Standard English instead of phonetic dialect?
cards.answer: To challenge the stereotype that working-class characters must sound uneducated, letting sharp wit and pace carry the comedy.

cards.front: Why does a director stage the Act Two Scene One time-jump with dance rather than dialogue?
cards.answer: Because the stage directions mark the passing weeks through movement, letting the audience read time passing and domestic routine without words.

title: Evaluating Good and Evil and Exam Skills
subject: religious-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three parts of a strong evaluation answer's structure.
cards.answer: Agree paragraph with a named source / Disagree paragraph with a named source and non-religious view / Conclusion with a justified personal position
items: Agree paragraph with a named source
Disagree paragraph with a named source and non-religious view
Conclusion with a justified personal position

cards.front: What are the three levels of using a source of authority, from weakest to strongest?
cards.answer: Emerging - mention / Secure - reference / Mastering - interpret

cards.front: Why do Humanists oppose capital punishment?
cards.answer: Because execution is irreversible and the evidence that it deters crime is weak.

cards.front: Why does Catholic teaching hold that the death penalty is inadmissible?
cards.answer: Because it violates human dignity, grounded in the belief that all humans are made in the image of God.

cards.front: Why does Meena reshape reality as a narrator instead of telling events straight?
cards.answer: She copes with the gap between who she is and who she wants to be by turning to mythology when she lacks history.

cards.front: Why does Syal present Anita as more than just a villain?
cards.answer: Anita's neglect, poverty, and dysfunctional family have shaped her into a survivor who uses toughness and manipulation as defence mechanisms.

cards.front: Why is Sam Lowbridge dangerous beyond just holding racist views?
cards.answer: He has charismatic authority among Tollington's young people, meaning he can mobilise others to act on his views.

cards.front: How does Mama Kumar typically respond to racism?
cards.answer: She responds with quiet dignity rather than confrontation, modelling a resilience Meena eventually learns to admire.

cards.front: Name the three inputs/outputs a D-type flip-flop has (2 outputs, 1 data input, plus clock).
cards.answer: D (data) input / CLK (clock) input / Q output / Q-bar output

cards.front: Why does Q1 toggle on the falling edge of Q0 in a 2-bit counter, not on Q0's rising edge?
cards.answer: Q1 is clocked by Q0's Q-bar output, and Q-bar rises (triggering Q1) exactly when Q0 falls.

cards.front: How does connecting Q-bar back to D make a D-type flip-flop toggle every clock cycle?
cards.answer: At each rising edge Q copies D, which is the opposite of Q, so Q flips to the opposite value every cycle.

cards.front: Why is a sensor's brief pulse better captured using a D-type flip-flop as a data latch?
cards.answer: The flip-flop latches onto D's value at the rising clock edge and holds it, so the brief pulse isn't lost before it can be read.

cards.front: Name the five links in Priestley's chain of responsibility that led to Eva Smith's death.
cards.answer: Birling sacked her / Sheila got her sacked again / Gerald used and abandoned her / Eric got her pregnant / Mrs Birling turned her away from the charity
items: Mrs Birling turned her away from the charity

cards.front: Name the three stages of class-based injustice Eva Smith faces in the play.
cards.answer: Asked for a pay rise and was sacked / Found new work and was sacked again / Sought help from a charity and was refused
items: Asked for a pay rise and was sacked
Found new work and was sacked again
Sought help from a charity and was refused

cards.front: Why does Priestley present responsibility as a chain rather than blaming one Birling alone?
cards.answer: Each Birling contributed one selfish act, and their cumulative effect was fatal, showing no action is isolated in a connected society.

cards.front: Why were the 1945 audience receptive to Priestley's argument against the rigid class system of 1912?
cards.answer: Shared wartime suffering and effort had weakened class barriers, creating solidarity that made audiences reject a return to the old class system.

title: Stamford Bridge and Hastings: the Battles of 1066
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: According to the lesson, what three factors turned the Battle of Hastings, rather than Norman tactical superiority alone?
cards.answer: Feigned (or genuine) retreats / Wearing-down of the housecarls / The death of Harold

cards.front: Why were Hardrada's men caught off guard at Stamford Bridge?
cards.answer: They had left their mail behind at Riccall, expecting only a ceremonial hostage meeting, so Harold's fast march surprised them.

cards.front: Why did William's cavalry charges fail to break the English line for most of the Battle of Hastings?
cards.answer: The English held the high ground on Senlac ridge, which negated William's cavalry advantage for most of the day.

cards.front: What three things does the lesson say define Pip's life in London?
cards.answer: The Finches of the Grove dining club / Mounting debts he cannot pay / Idleness
items: The Finches of the Grove dining club

cards.front: Why does Jaggers wash his hands after every client meeting?
cards.answer: To symbolise his attempt to separate himself from the moral contamination of his work.

cards.front: How does Dickens use Wemmick's double life to comment on Victorian London?
cards.answer: It shows how Victorian London forces people to split identities: public hardness for survival, private warmth for humanity.

title: The Plains Nations: Beliefs and Way of Life
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name six distinct Plains nations mentioned in the lesson.
cards.answer: Lakota Sioux / Cheyenne / Arapaho / Comanche / Crow / Pawnee

cards.front: Give four things Plains nations made from parts of the buffalo.
cards.answer: Meat for food / Sinew for bowstrings / Bone for tools / Bladder turned into water-skin

cards.front: Why did the spread of the horse in the 1700s transform Plains life?
cards.answer: It let nations that had once walked ride hundreds of miles, follow buffalo herds far more effectively and outrun rivals.

cards.front: Why did the Plains belief that land was shared clash with American settlers?
cards.answer: Settlers saw land as a fenced, owned rectangle to be claimed and inherited, while Plains nations used territory in common with no ownership.

cards.front: Name the four methods the lesson gives for how Napoleon consolidates power after expelling Snowball.
cards.answer: Military force (the dogs) / Propaganda (Squealer) / Scapegoating Snowball / Controlling information

cards.front: How does Napoleon control information on the farm after the coup?
cards.answer: With Snowball gone and Sunday debates abolished, animals get information only through Squealer and cannot verify it independently.

cards.front: Why does using Squealer as an intermediary protect Napoleon from accountability?
cards.answer: Because orders come through Squealer, Napoleon can deny anything Squealer says if it later proves unpopular.

cards.front: Name the four main sources of primary data described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Experimental / Simulation / Questionnaire / Observation

cards.front: Name the three types of experiment listed under primary data.
cards.answer: Laboratory experiment / Field experiment / Natural experiment

cards.front: Why can secondary data cover much larger populations than most researchers could achieve with primary data?
cards.answer: Bodies like ONS, NHS Digital and the Met Office publish huge datasets built over years that no individual could replicate.

cards.front: Why does high control in a laboratory experiment make it easier to claim causation but reduce real-world realism?
cards.answer: Holding other variables constant isolates the cause clearly, but the artificial setting may not transfer well to real-world settings.

cards.front: Name the six comparison operators SQL can use in a WHERE condition.
cards.answer: equal to = / not equal to <> / less than / less than or equal to =

cards.front: Name the five common mistakes the lesson lists when writing a query.
cards.answer: forgetting quotes around text / putting quotes around a number / writing clauses out of order / naming a field that doesn't exist / using > instead of >= for 'at least'
items: naming a field that doesn't exist

cards.front: Why does WHERE genre = Drama (without quotes) cause an error?
cards.answer: Without quotes the database reads Drama as a field name rather than a text value, so it can't compare it properly.

cards.front: Why does an OR condition always return the same number of records or more than an AND condition on the same two tests?
cards.answer: OR keeps a record if at least one condition is true, while AND needs both true, so OR is easier to satisfy.

cards.front: Name the stages a rock fragment goes through, in order, from weathering of an igneous rock to becoming sedimentary rock.
cards.answer: Weathering / Erosion / Transport / Deposition / Compaction and cementation (lithification)

cards.front: What four effects did the end-Cretaceous meteorite impact cause?
cards.answer: Wildfires / Tsunamis / Impact winter from dust blocking sunlight / Mass extinction including non-avian dinosaurs
items: Impact winter from dust blocking sunlight

cards.front: Why is it wrong to think of the rock cycle as a single fixed one-way pathway?
cards.answer: Any rock type can be eroded to sediment, metamorphosed, or melted into new magma, so many different routes exist.

cards.front: Why can river erosion cut a gorge in a human lifetime while subduction of oceanic crust takes tens of millions of years?
cards.answer: Different rock cycle processes, like surface erosion and plate-tectonic subduction, operate at vastly different rates.

cards.front: Name the four manufacturing processes that thermoforming polymers can be processed by.
cards.answer: Injection moulding / Vacuum forming / Blow moulding / Extrusion

cards.front: Name the four thermosetting polymers covered in the lesson.
cards.answer: Urea formaldehyde (UF) / Melamine formaldehyde (MF) / Polyester resin (PR) / Epoxy resin (ER)

cards.front: Why does PVC raise environmental concerns at the end of its life?
cards.answer: Its chlorine-based additives can form toxic compounds when PVC is incinerated.

cards.front: Why does polypropylene float in water?
cards.answer: Its density (approximately 0.9 g/cm3) is lower than that of water.

title: Hosting a Major Event — During & After (Legacy)
subject: cambridge-nationals-sport-studies

cards.front: Name the five negative impacts the lesson gives for during a major sporting event.
cards.answer: Transport congestion / Noise and litter / Security costs / Terrorism risk / Displacement of local residents

cards.front: Why did grassroots cycling participation gains from London 2012 not last in the long term?
cards.answer: Funding cuts to grassroots sport in subsequent years undermined the participation gains inspired by Team GB's medal success.

cards.front: Why did most Athens 2004 venues become white elephants within a decade?
cards.answer: Greece's financial crisis made maintaining the expensive facilities impossible, so they fell into disrepair or sat empty.

title: Storage Units, File Sizes and Compression
subject: computer-science-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three lossless file formats the lesson gives as examples.
cards.answer: ZIP / PNG / FLAC

cards.front: Name the three lossy file formats the lesson gives as examples.
cards.answer: JPEG / MP3 / AAC

cards.front: Why are binary multiples like the kibibyte based on 1024 rather than 1000?
cards.answer: Computer memory circuits operate in powers of 2, so a chip with 10 address lines accesses 2^10 = 1,024 locations, not 1,000.

cards.front: Why must a hospital use lossless compression for patient scan images rather than lossy?
cards.answer: A lossy compression artefact could look like a clinical finding and lead to misdiagnosis, so data integrity is essential.

cards.front: Why did Ed keep lying rather than admit he killed Wellington?
cards.answer: Admitting it would force him to explain why, and that explanation would destroy his version of reality.

cards.front: How does the play's staging show that Swindon feels safe for Christopher?
cards.answer: Through contained ensemble movement, familiar domestic projections, and Christopher moving with confidence.

title: Act 3: Hath Not a Jew Eyes?
subject: english-literature-aqa

cards.front: Why does Shylock say he will be cruel to the Christians?
cards.answer: He argues Christians taught him cruelty, so he will copy and even improve on their example.

cards.front: Why is the 'Hath not a Jew eyes?' speech considered ambiguous?
cards.answer: It can be read as a plea for human sympathy or as a villain justifying revenge, and Shakespeare leaves both open.

cards.front: Why does hearing Shylock's grief through Solanio complicate our sympathy for him?
cards.answer: Solanio openly mocks Shylock, so his pain is filtered through the contempt of someone enjoying his suffering.

cards.front: How does the ring Portia gives Bassanio set up later events in the play?
cards.answer: She warns that parting with it will ruin their love, and Bassanio's vow never to remove it sets up Act 5's ring subplot.

title: The End of Appeasement: Prague and the Polish Guarantee
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: The lesson says the end of appeasement happened in four stages over less than a month in 1939. Name them in order.
cards.answer: German troops enter Prague (15 March) / Chamberlain's Birmingham speech (17 March) / Polish guarantee announced (31 March) / Mussolini invades Albania (7 April)

cards.front: Why was the Polish guarantee not militarily credible?
cards.answer: Britain and France had no direct way to defend Poland, since their only real hope was a Western Front offensive neither was ready to launch.

cards.front: Why did Britain introduce peacetime conscription in April 1939?
cards.answer: To signal to Berlin that Britain's rearmament had entered a new phase, committing men as well as money to the coming confrontation.

cards.front: Name the three main tasks of the Presentation layer.
cards.answer: Data translation / Data compression / Encryption

cards.front: Name the three types of hardware that operate at the Physical layer.
cards.answer: Cables / Repeaters / Hubs

cards.front: How does TCP guarantee reliable delivery of data?
cards.answer: It establishes a connection using a three-way handshake and acknowledges every segment sent.

cards.front: Why is checkpointing at the Session layer useful for large file transfers?
cards.answer: If a transfer fails midway, it can resume from the last checkpoint instead of restarting from scratch.

cards.front: Why did Prospero lose his dukedom to Antonio?
cards.answer: Prospero neglected his ducal duties to study 'the liberal arts' and magic, giving Antonio the chance to seize power.

cards.front: How does Miranda function as an audience surrogate in Act 1 Scene 2?
cards.answer: She asks Prospero questions so he can explain the play's backstory to the audience.

cards.front: Name the five parts of the PECLC paragraph structure for comparison essays.
cards.answer: Point / Evidence (Poem 1) / Comment on method / Link to Poem 2 / Context

cards.front: Why should you pick a comparison poem with a contrasting approach rather than a very similar one?
cards.answer: Similarities give connection points but differences give analytical depth, so greater contrast makes the comparison richer.

cards.front: Why must AO2 be discussed alongside AO1 in the comparison essay?
cards.answer: AO2 (methods) is equally weighted with AO1 (ideas), so discussing methods is needed to access the top band.

cards.front: Name the four scientists (in order) whose models developed our understanding of atomic structure.
cards.answer: Dalton (solid sphere) / Thomson (plum pudding) / Rutherford (nuclear model) / Bohr (electron shells)

cards.front: Name the four natural sources of background radiation given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Radon gas from the ground / Cosmic rays / Food and drink / Building materials

cards.front: Why did Rutherford conclude the atom has a dense positive nucleus from the gold foil experiment?
cards.answer: A very few alpha particles bounced straight back, showing they hit something small, dense and positively charged.

cards.front: How did Bohr's model explain why atoms emit and absorb specific frequencies of radiation?
cards.answer: Electrons orbit only in fixed, specific energy levels, so energy changes occur in set amounts producing set frequencies.

cards.front: Name the five other significant coral reefs mentioned in the lesson besides the Great Barrier Reef.
cards.answer: Mesoamerican Barrier Reef (Mexico to Honduras) / Red Sea Reef (Africa to Arabia) / New Caledonia Barrier Reef (Pacific) / Florida Reef / Andros Coral Reef (Bahamas)

cards.front: Name the five strategies in Australia's Reef 2050 Plan for managing the Great Barrier Reef.
cards.answer: Marine Protected Areas / Water quality improvements / Crown-of-thorns starfish culls / Coral gardening / International climate action

cards.front: Why does the reef nutrient cycle stay a closed loop even though surrounding tropical seas are nutrient-poor?
cards.answer: Decomposer bacteria quickly release nutrients from dead organisms back into the water, where other reef organisms absorb them before they escape.

cards.front: Why does bleached coral eventually die if warm temperatures don't ease?
cards.answer: Without zooxanthellae, coral gets no sugars from photosynthesis, so it starves and dies if the heat persists.

title: Cnut, Emma & the North Sea Empire
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the four rival claimants to the English throne after Edward the Confessor died childless in 1066.
cards.answer: Harold Godwinson / Edgar Aetheling / Harald Hardrada of Norway / William of Normandy

cards.front: Why did Aethelred's Danegeld payments fail to buy lasting peace from Viking raiders?
cards.answer: Each payment showed the Danes that raiding worked, encouraging a fresh fleet to come back for more.

cards.front: Why did Cnut govern England through Anglo-Saxon laws and English earls rather than as a foreign conqueror?
cards.answer: He cultivated the public image of a Christian English king, confirming Edgar's laws and endowing monasteries, while keeping Danish housecarls as his guard.

cards.front: Why was a personal union like Cnut's North Sea Empire fragile?
cards.answer: It depended on one life, so when Cnut died his sons squabbled and the empire fell apart within seven years.

title: The Role of the Finance Function
subject: business-ocr

cards.front: Name the six core jobs of the finance team given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Recording transactions / Paying bills / Producing financial statements / Budgeting / Managing cash flow / Supporting decisions

cards.front: Name the three financial statements built from raw transaction data.
cards.answer: Income statement / Cash flow forecast / Statement of financial position

cards.front: Why must a business pay its bills on time?
cards.answer: Paying suppliers late means they stop delivering, and paying HMRC late means the business faces penalties.

cards.front: How does operations rely on the finance function?
cards.answer: Finance adds up the cost of raw materials, bottling, transport and labour to calculate cost per unit and flag unprofitable products.

title: Conflict with Spain and the Spanish Armada (1588)
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: What were the three long-running pressures pushing England and Spain towards war before 1588?
cards.answer: Religious conflict between Catholic Spain and Protestant England / Elizabeth's support for the Dutch Revolt against Spain / English Sea Dogs raiding Spanish treasure ships
items: Religious conflict between Catholic Spain and Protestant England
Elizabeth's support for the Dutch Revolt against Spain
English Sea Dogs raiding Spanish treasure ships

cards.front: What four factors combined to defeat the Spanish Armada, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: English race-built ships and long-range cannon / Stand-off broadside tactics / The fireship attack and failed Parma rendezvous / Storms off Scotland and Ireland
items: English race-built ships and long-range cannon
The fireship attack and failed Parma rendezvous

cards.front: Why did Philip's invasion plan depend on capturing a deep-water port in the Netherlands?
cards.answer: Parma's flat-bottomed barges needed a safe deep-water port to meet the Armada, otherwise the risky rendezvous had to happen at sea.

cards.front: Why is it a misconception to say the 'Protestant Wind' alone defeated the Armada?
cards.answer: The Armada had already lost its strategic purpose at Calais before the worst storms, due to fireships and the failed Parma rendezvous.

cards.front: Name the seven consumer music formats covered in the lesson.
cards.answer: Vinyl / Cassette / CD / Minidisc / MP3 / Music video / Streaming

cards.front: How do analogue synthesisers generate waveforms differently from digital synthesisers?
cards.answer: Analogue synthesisers use voltage-controlled oscillators, while digital synthesisers use mathematical algorithms to create waveforms.

cards.front: How did tape delay create an echo effect in hardware studios?
cards.answer: It used a tape loop to record audio and replay it after a short time gap, producing an echo.

cards.front: Name the four types of protein the lesson gives as examples controlled by DNA.
cards.answer: Enzymes (biological catalysts) / Structural proteins e.g. collagen / Hormones e.g. insulin / Antibodies (immune system)

cards.front: Name the four stages of the cell cycle, in order.
cards.answer: Cell grows and increases in size / DNA replicates so there are two copies of every chromosome / Cell grows a little more / Cell divides by mitosis
items: Cell grows and increases in size
DNA replicates so there are two copies of every chromosome

cards.front: How does raising temperature increase enzyme reaction rate, up to the optimum?
cards.answer: Molecules move faster and collide more frequently with the enzyme, increasing the rate of reaction.

cards.front: How does DNA replication produce two identical copies of the DNA molecule?
cards.answer: The double helix unzips and each strand acts as a template, with new complementary nucleotides added to form two identical DNA molecules.

cards.front: Name the four main actions Ariel performs for Prospero, as listed in the lesson.
cards.answer: Creates the storm / Leads Ferdinand to Miranda with a song / Appears as a harpy to terrify the nobles / Stages the wedding masque
items: Leads Ferdinand to Miranda with a song
Appears as a harpy to terrify the nobles

cards.front: Name the three character foil pairs the lesson identifies.
cards.answer: Ferdinand vs Caliban / Gonzalo vs Antonio / Ariel vs Caliban

cards.front: Why does Ariel's line about becoming 'tender' shame Prospero into showing mercy?
cards.answer: A non-human spirit shows more compassion than Prospero, reminding him what humanity should mean and pushing him to choose virtue over vengeance.

cards.front: Why does Caliban's line 'my profit on't is I know how to curse' encapsulate the colonial dynamic?
cards.answer: The coloniser's 'gift' of language becomes the weapon the colonised person turns back against them.

title: Antagonistic Pairs and Muscle Fibre Types
subject: physical-education-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four antagonistic muscle pairs the lesson identifies, with their joints.
cards.answer: Biceps and triceps (elbow) / Quadriceps and hamstrings (knee) / Hip flexors and gluteus maximus (hip) / Gastrocnemius and tibialis anterior (ankle)

cards.front: Name the four activities the lesson gives as examples relying on Type IIx fibres.
cards.answer: 100 m sprinting / Shot put / Olympic weightlifting / Plyometric jumping

cards.front: Why are the hamstrings particularly prone to strain during sprinting?
cards.answer: They contract rapidly as the agonist in the late swing phase to decelerate the extending knee, causing high stress.

cards.front: Why is the tibialis anterior the agonist during ankle dorsi-flexion even though it's smaller than the gastrocnemius?
cards.answer: The agonist is whichever muscle is producing the current movement, not the bigger or stronger muscle.

title: Correlation, Causation and the Vocabulary of Association
subject: statistics-aqa

cards.front: The lesson gives three directions a correlation can have. What are they?
cards.answer: Positive correlation: both variables increase together / Negative correlation: one increases as the other decreases / Zero correlation: no consistent pattern between the variables
items: Positive correlation: both variables increase together
Negative correlation: one increases as the other decreases
Zero correlation: no consistent pattern between the variables

cards.front: In the worked example, what three steps are used to classify a correlation coefficient?
cards.answer: Direction - is it positive or negative / Strength - strong, weak or no correlation / Causation caution - consider other factors that might explain it
items: Direction - is it positive or negative
Strength - strong, weak or no correlation
Causation caution - consider other factors that might explain it

cards.front: Why do ice cream sales and drowning incidents show a strong positive correlation even though neither causes the other?
cards.answer: Both are caused by a lurking variable, hot weather, which increases ice cream sales and swimming (and so drowning) separately.

cards.front: Why should you say two variables are 'associated' rather than say one 'causes' the other?
cards.answer: A strong correlation does not prove causation, so 'associated' shows understanding while 'causes' claims something the data can't prove.

cards.front: Name the four environmental impacts of business activity given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Traffic congestion / Noise and air pollution / Waste sent to landfill / Use of scarce resources

cards.front: Why did the Volkswagen dieselgate scandal cost the firm so much long-term?
cards.answer: It cost over thirty billion dollars in fines and lost sales and damaged its brand for years.

title: The Cardiovascular System and Pathway of Blood
subject: physical-education-ocr

cards.front: Name the four chambers of the heart, in the order blood flows through them starting from the right side.
cards.answer: Right atrium / Right ventricle / Left atrium / Left ventricle

cards.front: Name the three types of blood vessel described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Arteries / Veins / Capillaries

cards.front: Why are capillary walls only one cell thick?
cards.answer: To allow oxygen and nutrients to diffuse into muscle cells and carbon dioxide/waste to diffuse back into the blood.

cards.front: Why can exercising vigorously straight after a large meal cause discomfort?
cards.answer: The digestive system competes with the working muscles for blood supply when the muscles' demand for blood is greatly elevated.

cards.front: What three tasks did wealthy Athenian women oversee as household managers?
cards.answer: Oversaw household budgets / Supervised slaves / Made practical decisions to keep the household running
items: Made practical decisions to keep the household running

cards.front: What three freedoms did Roman aristocratic women have that respectable Athenian women lacked?
cards.answer: Attended dinner parties with husbands / Visited temples and public spaces / Were visible in the life of the city
items: Were visible in the life of the city

cards.front: Why did Athenian democratic ideology exclude women from full citizenship and political participation?
cards.answer: Political participation was linked to the qualities of a citizen warrior, and since women did not fight, they were not considered full citizens.

cards.front: Why is Aristophanes' Assemblywomen valuable evidence for Athenian attitudes towards women in politics?
cards.answer: The comedy only works because the audience automatically assumes women running the city is ridiculous, revealing real cultural attitudes.

cards.front: Name the five frame joints the lesson lists for building frames such as chairs and tables.
cards.answer: Mitre joint / Dowel joint / Mortise and tenon joint / Halving joint / Bridle joint

cards.front: Name the five box (carcass) joints the lesson lists for building boxes and cabinets.
cards.answer: Butt joint / Lap joint / Housing joint / Dovetail joint / Comb joint

cards.front: Why is a butt joint very weak unless reinforced with nails, screws or brackets?
cards.answer: Because end-grain glue bonds poorly, so the joint has little strength without mechanical reinforcement.

cards.front: Why is an oval wire nail used in furniture instead of a round wire nail?
cards.answer: Its oval shank is driven with its long axis along the grain, which reduces splitting.

title: The Nature of God and the Mool Mantra
subject: religious-studies-aqa

cards.front: Name the eight attributes of God given in the Mool Mantra.
cards.answer: One (Ik Onkar) / The Truth (Sat Nam) / The Creator (Karta Purakh) / Without fear (Nirbhau) / Without enmity (Nirvair) / Beyond time and death (Akal Murat) / Self-existent (Ajooni Saibhang) / Known through the Guru's grace (Gur Prasad)

cards.front: Name the four names for God given in the Guru Granth Sahib.
cards.answer: Waheguru / Hari / Ram / Allah

cards.front: How can Sikh teaching hold that God is both immanent and transcendent at the same time?
cards.answer: God's light (jot) is present within every being, yet God is also beyond all names, forms and descriptions, so both are true at once.

cards.front: How does the oneness of God (Ik Onkar) lead to the oneness of humanity in Sikh teaching?
cards.answer: Because there is one God, all people share the same divine light within them, so divisions of religion, caste and status do not exist before God.

cards.front: Name the two biblical texts most frequently cited by Christians opposing same-sex relationships.
cards.answer: Leviticus 20:13 / 1 Timothy 1:8-10

cards.front: Why do critics argue Leviticus 20:13 should not be simply applied to same-sex relationships today?
cards.answer: The same Holiness Code forbids things like eating shellfish, so consistency requires reading it in its ancient context.

cards.front: Why do some Hindus see same-sex relationships as conflicting with dharma?
cards.answer: Traditional teaching links the householder ashrama to sexual activity aimed at procreation and continuing family lineage, part of one's dharma.

cards.front: Why does Reform Judaism affirm same-sex relationships despite Leviticus prohibitions?
cards.answer: It grounds its position in human dignity (kavod ha-beriyot) and the commandment to love one's neighbour, reinterpreting tradition accordingly.

cards.front: Name the five colours used in Mycenaean frescoes.
cards.answer: Ochre red / Blue / Black / Yellow / White

cards.front: Name the five groups below the wanax in the Mycenaean palace hierarchy.
cards.answer: Military commanders / Landowners / Craftsmen / Traders / Agricultural labourers

cards.front: How did smoke from the megaron's central hearth escape the building?
cards.answer: It escaped through a hole or clerestory in the roof above the hearth.

cards.front: Why did Mycenaean palaces choose hunting, warfare and elite figures as fresco subjects?
cards.answer: The palace walls proclaimed the values and status of the ruling class to everyone who entered.

title: Health, Fitness and the Components of Fitness
subject: physical-education-aqa

cards.front: Name the ten components of fitness identified in the lesson.
cards.answer: Agility / Balance / Cardiovascular endurance / Coordination / Flexibility / Muscular endurance / Power / Reaction time / Strength / Speed

cards.front: Name the four types of strength described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Maximal strength / Static strength / Dynamic strength / Explosive strength

cards.front: Why is cardiovascular endurance less important for a 100m sprinter than for a marathon runner?
cards.answer: The 100m race is too short for the aerobic system to be the limiting factor on performance.

cards.front: Why does a footballer recovering from a knee injury lose fitness even though they are otherwise healthy?
cards.answer: They cannot train at full intensity, so their cardiovascular fitness and muscular strength decline despite being healthy.

cards.front: Name the five main objectives businesses set, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Profit / Survival / Growth / Providing a service / Market share

cards.front: Name the six benefits the lesson gives for why businesses set objectives.
cards.answer: Give direction / Motivate workers / Provide a yardstick for success / Support planning / Help secure finance / Help prioritise under pressure

cards.front: How can a growth objective end up harming a business's service quality?
cards.answer: Growth can damage service quality if expansion runs ahead of staff training.

cards.front: Why does a multinational like Unilever focus on growth and market share rather than survival?
cards.answer: It has already survived the early stages and operates in dozens of countries, so it targets growth, market share and shareholder returns.

cards.front: Name the four prepositions used before countries or cities in French, based on gender/number.
cards.answer: en + feminine country (en France) / au + masculine country (au Canada) / aux + plural country (aux États-Unis) / à + city (à Paris)

cards.front: Name the five types of transport that use 'en' in French.
cards.answer: en avion (by plane) / en voiture (by car) / en train (by train) / en bateau (by boat) / en bus/autocar (by bus/coach)

cards.front: Why do bike, foot and horse use 'à' instead of 'en' when talking about transport in French?
cards.answer: Because à is used for open or human-powered transport, while en is used for enclosed transport like cars or planes.

cards.front: Why is 'le Mexique' an exception to the usual rule about country gender and prepositions?
cards.answer: It ends in -e like feminine countries, but it is actually masculine, so it takes 'au' rather than 'en'.

cards.front: Name the four techniques of persuasive communication the lesson gives.
cards.answer: Appealing to emotion / Appealing to authority / Creating aspiration or fear / Propaganda

cards.front: Name the four choices in print media that position audiences, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Choice of photograph / Headline wording / Font size / Page position

cards.front: Why is spin harder for audiences to identify and challenge than propaganda?
cards.answer: Spin frames information to seem favourable without obviously misrepresenting facts, unlike propaganda's open, one-sided presentation.

cards.front: Why does tokenism fail to solve the problem of under-representation?
cards.answer: It creates the impression of inclusion by including one representative while leaving the overall pattern of representation unchanged.

title: Akhirah: Life After Death and the Day of Judgement
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four features of the Day of Judgement described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Deeds recorded by Kiraman Katibin / Mizan weighs good and bad deeds / Record given in right or left hand / Sirat bridge crossed over hell
items: Mizan weighs good and bad deeds
Record given in right or left hand

cards.front: How does entry to Jannah work according to Islamic teaching?
cards.answer: Entry to Jannah is by Allah's mercy, not deeds alone — deeds only indicate faith, but Allah makes the final decision.

cards.front: Why do Sunni scholars generally believe Jahannam is not eternal for all its inhabitants?
cards.answer: Non-believers remain permanently, but sinning believers may be punished temporarily before entering Jannah by Allah's mercy.

title: Selma and the Voting Rights Act, 1965
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four devices the lesson gives that kept Black Americans off the electoral roll in the Deep South.
cards.answer: Arbitrary literacy tests / Poll taxes / Requirement to bring a registered voter to vouch for you / Threat of being sacked, evicted or beaten
items: Requirement to bring a registered voter to vouch for you
Threat of being sacked, evicted or beaten

cards.front: Why did the killing of Jimmie Lee Jackson lead to the Selma to Montgomery march?
cards.answer: Out of grief and anger at Jackson's death, the SCLC announced a march from Selma to Montgomery to deliver a petition to Governor Wallace.

cards.front: Why did the deaths of Jimmie Lee Jackson and James Reeb generate such different reactions?
cards.answer: Reeb's death, unlike Jackson's, produced national headlines and presidential condolences, a contrast King spoke about with honesty.

cards.front: Why did the third Selma to Montgomery march in March 1965 go ahead successfully?
cards.answer: Federal Judge Frank Johnson lifted the restraining order and the march was legally protected by federalised National Guard and US Army troops.

cards.front: Name the four occupation zones Germany was divided into in 1945.
cards.answer: American zone / British zone / French zone / Soviet zone

cards.front: Why did Stalin impose the Berlin Blockade in June 1948?
cards.answer: He saw the West's new Deutschmark currency in West Berlin as a threat and wanted to force the West to abandon Berlin or accept Soviet terms.

cards.front: Why was the mass emigration of East Germans in the 1950s a serious problem for the GDR?
cards.answer: It drained skilled workers and professionals, threatening the economy and stability, which led to the decision to build the Berlin Wall.

cards.front: Name the four natural methods of pain relief the lesson gives that carry no medical risk.
cards.answer: Water (birthing pool) / Breathing and relaxation techniques / Massage / Hypnobirthing

cards.front: Why might a caesarean section be planned in advance rather than done as an emergency?
cards.answer: It is planned when there is a known risk, such as placenta praevia or a breech presentation.

cards.front: Why can forceps rotate a baby's head but ventouse cannot be used in some positions?
cards.answer: Forceps are metal instruments that cup the head and can rotate it, while ventouse relies on suction so cannot be used for very premature babies or certain positions.

cards.front: Name the four types of personal service given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Tray or trolley service / Vending / Home delivery / Takeaway

cards.front: Name the five room types offered by residential providers.
cards.answer: Single / Double / King / Family / Suite

cards.front: Why is plate service the most widely used type of table service?
cards.answer: It requires less skill from waiting staff and is cost-effective, making it the most common method.

cards.front: Why is counter service popular with catering providers?
cards.answer: It reduces labour costs since customers serve themselves or collect food, and it increases speed of service.

title: Contexts of Film: Social, Cultural, Historical, Political, Institutional
subject: film-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Name the six contexts the lesson identifies for analysing a film.
cards.answer: Social / Cultural / Historical / Political / Institutional / Technological

cards.front: What four characteristics did the lesson say the French New Wave shared?
cards.answer: Rejection of polished studio aesthetics / Embrace of location shooting / Jump cuts / Self-referential storytelling

cards.front: How did digital cinematography from the early 2000s change filmmaking economics?
cards.answer: It enabled low-cost production at a quality previously only available to well-funded studio productions.

cards.front: How does state censorship shape what appears in a film's content?
cards.answer: It leaves marks through what filmmakers could not say as clearly as through what they could say.

title: The Stresemann era — recovery and Weimar culture
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the three pillars that Stresemann's recovery rested on.
cards.answer: A stable currency / US loans through the Dawes Plan / Diplomatic reintegration through Locarno and the League
items: US loans through the Dawes Plan
Diplomatic reintegration through Locarno and the League

cards.front: Name the four areas of Weimar Germany's cultural flowering described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Bauhaus design school / Brecht's theatre / Berlin cabaret / German film industry

cards.front: Why did Stresemann call off passive resistance in the Ruhr in September 1923?
cards.answer: He accepted that the strike against the French occupation could not be won.

cards.front: Why did the 1929 Wall Street Crash hit Germany harder than any other major economy?
cards.answer: Germany's recovery depended on US loans that could be recalled at short notice, a factor beyond German control.

title: Rates of Reaction and Collision Theory
subject: separate-sciences-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four main factors that affect rate of reaction.
cards.answer: Temperature / Concentration (or gas pressure) / Surface area of solids / Presence of a catalyst

cards.front: Name the three ways rate of reaction can be measured, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Collecting gas produced / Monitoring mass loss / Timing a colour change

cards.front: Why does increasing concentration (or pressure for gases) increase reaction rate?
cards.answer: More particles occupy the same volume, so they are closer together and collide more frequently.

cards.front: Why do catalysts and higher temperatures give steeper rate graphs without changing the final volume of product formed?
cards.answer: They speed up the reaction but the same amount of reactant is consumed either way, giving the same final total.

title: Material Costs, Supply and Stock Forms
subject: engineering-aqa

cards.front: What three factors does the lesson give as driving raw material cost?
cards.answer: Rarity or abundance of the ore/feedstock / Degree of processing (e.g. pre-machined or treated) / Economies of scale (bulk pricing)
items: Rarity or abundance of the ore/feedstock
Degree of processing (e.g. pre-machined or treated)

cards.front: What are the four steps for calculating the material cost per part when cutting parts from a sheet?
cards.answer: Divide sheet length by part length, round down / Divide sheet width by part width, round down / Multiply the two whole numbers for total parts / Divide sheet cost by number of parts
items: Divide sheet length by part length, round down
Divide sheet width by part width, round down
Multiply the two whole numbers for total parts
Divide sheet cost by number of parts

cards.front: Why is aluminium more expensive per kilogram than mild steel even though it is abundant?
cards.answer: Because although the ore is abundant, aluminium is very energy-intensive to refine, raising its cost.

cards.front: Why might machined aluminium housing be cheaper than injection-moulded plastic housing for small production quantities?
cards.answer: Because expensive injection-mould tooling costs cannot be spread (amortised) over enough units to make it worthwhile.

title: Particles, Heating and the Particle Model
subject: science-ocr-b

cards.front: Name the five changes of state described in the lesson, with the state change each involves.
cards.answer: Melting (solid to liquid) / Freezing (liquid to solid) / Evaporation/boiling (liquid to gas) / Condensation (gas to liquid) / Sublimation (solid directly to gas)

cards.front: Describe the particle arrangement and movement in each of the three states of matter.
cards.answer: Solid: closely packed, regular, vibrating in place / Liquid: close together, particles move past each other / Gas: widely spaced, moving rapidly and randomly
items: Solid: closely packed, regular, vibrating in place
Liquid: close together, particles move past each other
Gas: widely spaced, moving rapidly and randomly

cards.front: Why does evaporation cause cooling of a liquid?
cards.answer: The fastest-moving particles escape from the surface, which lowers the average kinetic energy (and temperature) of the remaining particles.

cards.front: Why is water used in central heating systems?
cards.answer: Water has a high specific heat capacity, so it can carry a large amount of thermal energy for its mass.

cards.front: Name the five OCR activity settings where hazards must be identified for injury prevention.
cards.answer: Sports hall / Fitness centre / Playing field / Artificial outdoor areas / Swimming pool

cards.front: Why does bending at the waist with a rounded back increase the risk of lower-back injury when lifting equipment?
cards.answer: It transfers compressive force directly to the intervertebral discs and lumbar vertebrae, increasing the risk of disc herniation.

cards.front: Why is a spotter needed when performing a heavy lift like the bench press in a fitness centre?
cards.answer: Without a spotter there is no one to assist if the lifter fails, increasing the risk of injury from an uncontrolled heavy weight.

cards.front: Name the three reasons Mr Collins gives, in order, for wanting to marry.
cards.answer: A clergyman should set an example / It will make him happy / Lady Catherine advised it
items: A clergyman should set an example

cards.front: Name the three things Elizabeth accuses Darcy of when she refuses his first proposal.
cards.answer: Separating Jane from Bingley / Ruining Wickham's prospects / Proposing with a design of insulting her
items: Proposing with a design of insulting her

cards.front: Why does Darcy say, in his letter, that he separated Jane and Bingley?
cards.answer: He genuinely believed that Jane did not return Bingley's feelings.

cards.front: Why does Austen present Charlotte's acceptance of Collins as reasonable rather than condemning her?
cards.answer: Her choice was rational within a system that offered women so few other options.

title: Functionalist and Subcultural Theories of Crime
subject: sociology-eduqas

cards.front: Name Merton's five modes of adaptation to strain.
cards.answer: Conformity / Innovation / Ritualism / Retreatism / Rebellion

cards.front: Why did Merton say working-class people face greater strain than others?
cards.answer: They are socialised into the same success goals as everyone else but face greater structural barriers to legitimate means of achieving them.

cards.front: How does Cohen explain why working-class boys form delinquent sub-cultures?
cards.answer: Cultural deprivation and poor educational prospects cause status frustration, so boys collectively invert mainstream values to gain status instead.

cards.front: Why is Cohen's theory seen as adding something Merton's theory lacks?
cards.answer: It explains non-instrumental crime committed for status, thrill or group belonging rather than for economic gain.
