items: Degree of customisation required by customers
Level of flexibility the market demands

cards.front: Name the four variables the lesson says are traded off when a business invests in production technology.
cards.answer: Cost / Productivity / Quality / Flexibility

cards.front: Why can 3D printing help small businesses compete with traditional job production?
cards.answer: It lets them produce customised items at a lower cost than traditional job production methods.

cards.front: Why do businesses in competitive markets tend to move from job to batch to flow production as they grow?
cards.answer: Lower costs per unit enable lower prices, which help the business win greater market share.

cards.front: Name the four different ways the lesson says the same logic circuit can be described.
cards.answer: A written description in plain English / A Boolean expression / A logic diagram of gates / A completed truth table
items: A written description in plain English

cards.front: In a Boolean expression, what symbol is used for each of the three basic operations: AND, OR and NOT?
cards.answer: A dot for AND / A plus sign for OR / A bar over a letter for NOT
items: A bar over a letter for NOT

cards.front: For the circuit Q = (A AND B) OR C, how do you work out the value of Q for each row of the truth table?
cards.answer: Work out A AND B first as a helper column, then apply OR between that helper column and C.

cards.front: Why is a bubble drawn on the tip of a NOT gate's symbol?
cards.answer: The bubble shows the signal is being inverted, telling you the gate flips its input from 0 to 1 or 1 to 0.

cards.front: Name the four ways the lesson gives for controlling extraneous variables.
cards.answer: Standardised procedures / Counterbalancing / Randomisation / Single/double-blind techniques

cards.front: Why does counterbalancing help control order effects in a study with two conditions?
cards.answer: Half complete Condition A then B, and half complete B then A, spreading practice or fatigue effects evenly across both conditions.

cards.front: How does a double-blind technique reduce bias compared to a single-blind one?
cards.answer: Neither participants nor the researcher running the session know which condition is being tested, removing the researcher's own expectations from influencing treatment.

cards.front: The lesson groups Lagos's growth-related challenges into four big areas. Name them.
cards.answer: Housing / Services / Jobs and crime / Environment

cards.front: Name the three types of environmental pressure the lesson describes in Lagos.
cards.answer: Waste piling up in dumps and the lagoon / Water pollution from sewage, industrial waste and oil / Air pollution from generators, traffic and burning rubbish
items: Waste piling up in dumps and the lagoon
Water pollution from sewage, industrial waste and oil
Air pollution from generators, traffic and burning rubbish

cards.front: Why were Makoko residents left with no protection when the government demolished parts of the slum in 2012?
cards.answer: Houses were built without planning permission and residents had no formal land title, so they had no legal protection from demolition.

cards.front: Why does Lagos's traffic 'go-slow' hit informal workers hardest financially?
cards.answer: Workers in the informal economy are paid by the day, so hours lost sitting in gridlock directly cut their earnings.

title: Describing Systems: Block Diagrams, Schematics and Flowcharts
subject: engineering-aqa

cards.front: Name the three main tools engineers use to describe systems, from the lesson.
cards.answer: Block diagrams / Schematic drawings / Flowcharts

cards.front: Name the six sub-systems of a car given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Engine management / Braking / Steering / Lighting / Infotainment / Climate control

cards.front: Why are most industrial control systems, like cruise-control or furnace controllers, closed-loop?
cards.answer: Because small disturbances, such as draughts or varying load, would cause the output to drift without feedback correction.

cards.front: Why would a circuit diagram not be accepted in place of a block diagram?
cards.answer: Because it shows how components are wired, not the system stages the block diagram question asks for.

cards.front: Name the four inner (rocky) planets of the solar system.
cards.answer: Mercury / Venus / Earth / Mars

cards.front: What three challenges of space exploration does the lesson give?
cards.answer: Extreme distances involved / Hostile environment (radiation, vacuum, microgravity) / Enormous cost

cards.front: Why do the inner planets orbit the Sun faster than the outer planets?
cards.answer: They are closer to the Sun, so they experience stronger gravitational attraction, making them orbit faster.

cards.front: What happens to a satellite if its speed is too low or too high for its orbit?
cards.answer: Too low a speed makes it spiral inward; too high a speed makes it move to a higher orbit or escape entirely.

title: The Destruction of Sennacherib — Lord Byron
subject: english-literature-ocr

cards.front: Why does Byron's use of similes before the destruction make the army's defeat more shocking?
cards.answer: Each simile builds the army up as beautiful, vast and unstoppable, so its sudden destruction contrasts sharply.

cards.front: How does the poem's rhythm create a strong contrast after the army is destroyed?
cards.answer: The same insistent galloping rhythm continues but now describes stillness and silence instead of movement, sharpening the contrast.

cards.front: Name the three physical or emotional details Byron gives after the Angel of Death passes, moving from one body to a nation.
cards.answer: Horse's foam turning cold / Rider lying distorted and pale / Widows of Ashur wailing / Idols broken in temple of Baal
items: Idols broken in temple of Baal

cards.front: What were the three constitutional experiments Cromwell tried between 1653 and 1658?
cards.answer: Barebone's Parliament / Instrument of Government / Rule of the Major-Generals / Humble Petition and Advice

cards.front: What three areas were the Major-Generals responsible for in their districts?
cards.answer: Security (suppressing Royalism) / Taxation (10% tax on Royalist incomes) / Moral reform (alehouses, bear-baiting, Sunday observance)

cards.front: Why did Cromwell refuse the crown offered by the Humble Petition and Advice in 1657?
cards.answer: He believed God had visibly 'blasted' the title of king by executing Charles I, so he could not accept what providence had condemned.

cards.front: Why could the Protectorate never find a stable civilian settlement?
cards.answer: Its legitimacy rested on military power, but Cromwell's godly minority lacked enough electoral support to govern without the army.

title: Woven, Non-Woven and Knitted Textile Construction
subject: design-technology-eduqas

cards.front: What are the three fundamental weave structures described in the lesson?
cards.answer: Plain weave / Twill weave / Satin weave

cards.front: What are the three methods used to bond fibres into non-woven fabrics?
cards.answer: Mechanical entanglement (needle-punching or hydroentangling) / Thermal bonding (melting synthetic fibres to fuse the web) / Chemical bonding (applying an adhesive binder)
items: Thermal bonding (melting synthetic fibres to fuse the web)

cards.front: Why does twill weave drape better than plain weave?
cards.answer: Twill has fewer interlacement points than plain weave, allowing the yarns to move more freely.

cards.front: Why is warp knit fabric more dimensionally stable than weft knit?
cards.answer: Multiple yarns run lengthways and interlock sideways on each course, so it does not ladder or distort easily.

cards.front: Name the four historical events between 1912 and 1945 that the 1945 audience already knew had shattered the Birlings' world.
cards.answer: First World War (1914–1918) / General Strike (1926) / Great Depression (1929–1939) / Second World War (1939–1945)

cards.front: Name the three post-war creations Priestley's campaigning helped bring about after the 1945 Labour landslide.
cards.answer: The NHS / Free education / Social security

cards.front: Why did Birling sack Eva Smith?
cards.answer: She took part in a strike demanding a pay rise from 22s6d to 25s a week, and Birling saw no moral problem in firing strikers.

cards.front: Why did An Inspector Calls premiere in Moscow before London?
cards.answer: Partly because Soviet socialist values aligned with Priestley's message, and partly because London theatres were fully booked.

cards.front: Name the three major Catholic plots against Elizabeth between 1571 and 1586.
cards.answer: Ridolfi Plot (1571) / Throckmorton Plot (1583) / Babington Plot (1586)

cards.front: What multiple causes does the lesson give for Mary's execution in 1587?
cards.answer: Babington letter gave written proof / 1585 Act for Queen's Surety allowed it / Parliament and Privy Council pushed for years / Spanish invasion fleet preparations were visible
items: 1585 Act for Queen's Surety allowed it
Parliament and Privy Council pushed for years
Spanish invasion fleet preparations were visible

cards.front: Why did Walsingham let Mary's letters keep flowing through the beer barrel channel at Chartley?
cards.answer: So Mary would commit herself in writing approving Elizabeth's assassination, giving legal proof to convict her.

cards.front: How did Phelippes use the Babington letter to expose the other plotters?
cards.answer: He forged a postscript asking Babington to name his fellow conspirators, resealed it, and let it through.

title: Reversible Reactions, Equilibrium and the Haber Process
subject: separate-sciences-edexcel

cards.front: Why does increasing pressure shift the Haber process equilibrium to the right?
cards.answer: High pressure shifts equilibrium towards the side with fewer moles of gas, and ammonia has fewer moles.

cards.front: Why is 200 atmospheres used in the Haber process rather than a much higher pressure?
cards.answer: Very high pressures give better yields but are too expensive and dangerous to maintain, so 200 atm is a practical compromise.

cards.front: Why are unreacted nitrogen and hydrogen recycled in the Haber process?
cards.answer: Because the yield per pass is only around 15–25%, so unreacted gases are separated and pumped back into the reactor.

cards.front: What three factors does the lesson say can shift a system at equilibrium?
cards.answer: Temperature / Concentration / Pressure (for gases)

cards.front: Name the three main Mycenaean-world sites the lesson identifies (besides Troy) as key sites.
cards.answer: Mycenae / Tiryns / Pylos

cards.front: What four things happened across Greece during the Mycenaean collapse, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Palaces were burned / Linear B writing disappeared / Population levels fell sharply / Trade networks broke down

cards.front: Why do most scholars now see the Mycenaean collapse as a 'systems collapse' rather than one single event?
cards.answer: Because interconnected palace economies broke down together, with each site falling for locally specific reasons within a wider regional crisis.

cards.front: Why do scholars think Homer's epics are a 'layered blend' rather than a pure record of Mycenaean life?
cards.answer: Because some details match Bronze Age archaeology, but the Odyssey also shows later Iron Age features like iron tools.

cards.front: Name the three factors the lesson gives for variation in UK climate across the country.
cards.answer: Latitude / Altitude / Distance from the sea

cards.front: Name the three factors the lesson gives as producing the UK's mild, wet climate.
cards.answer: Latitude in the mid 50s °N / The Gulf Stream warming Atlantic air / Prevailing south-westerly winds bringing moisture
items: The Gulf Stream warming Atlantic air

cards.front: Why does the equator receive roughly twice as much solar energy per square metre as the poles?
cards.answer: The Sun's rays strike the equator almost vertically but hit the poles at a glancing angle.

cards.front: How do depressions form along the polar front?
cards.answer: Warm subtropical air meets cold polar air, and the temperature and density contrast forces air upwards, creating cloud and rain.

cards.front: Name the six strategies in the 6Rs framework for metal sustainability.
cards.answer: Reduce / Reuse / Recycle / Refuse / Repair / Rethink

cards.front: Name the four applications of shape memory alloys given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Medical stents / Orthodontic arch wires / Actuators in engineering / Eyeglass frames

cards.front: Why can the aluminium drink can have such a thin wall despite holding a carbonated drink?
cards.answer: The internal pressure of the contents stiffens the can, so the thin wall is strong enough (the pressurised vessel effect).

cards.front: Why does declining copper ore grade increase the energy used in extraction?
cards.answer: Lower-concentration deposits mean more rock must be processed per tonne of copper recovered, raising energy use and waste rock volume.

title: The Romantic Concerto: The Age of the Virtuoso Soloist
subject: music-ocr

cards.front: Name the three virtuoso techniques the lesson says Paganini used to astonish audiences.
cards.answer: Rapid double-stopping / Harmonics / Left-hand pizzicato

cards.front: Name four extra instruments the lesson says were added to the Romantic orchestra beyond the Classical orchestra.
cards.answer: Piccolo / Cor anglais / Bass clarinet / Contrabassoon / Trombones / Tuba

cards.front: Why did composers write thicker orchestration and wider dynamic contrasts for Romantic concertos?
cards.answer: Because concerts moved to bigger purpose-built concert halls, and a bigger room demanded a bigger, louder sound.

cards.front: How did the role of the cadenza change from the Classical to the Romantic era?
cards.answer: It changed from being often improvised by the performer to being fully composed by the composer and integrated into the structure.

title: Rivonia Trial and the long silence
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Why did Mandela argue that the ANC's use of sabotage was justified?
cards.answer: Because the apartheid government's violence against its own citizens had made peaceful protest impossible, leaving sabotage as a last resort.

cards.front: How did the Rivonia Trial backfire on the apartheid government?
cards.answer: Mandela's smuggled dock statement spread internationally, turning the accused into martyrs and boosting the ANC's reputation abroad, prompting UN resolutions for their release.

cards.front: Name the three control variables in the pH and enzyme activity investigation.
cards.answer: Temperature / Concentration of enzyme and starch / Volume of solutions

cards.front: What are the four things needed to calculate energy content using calorimetry (Q = mcΔT)?
cards.answer: Mass of water / Specific heat capacity of water / Temperature rise / Heat from burning food sample

cards.front: Why does raising temperature towards the optimum increase enzyme reaction rate?
cards.answer: Molecules have more kinetic energy, collide more frequently, and form enzyme-substrate complexes faster.

cards.front: Why does extreme pH stop an enzyme working?
cards.answer: It alters the bonds holding the enzyme's 3D shape, changing the active site so the substrate can't bind.

cards.front: Name the four advantages (Vorteile) of social media given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Stay in contact with friends/family far away / Useful for school - find info and work with classmates / Meet new people and discover different cultures / It's fun and entertaining
items: Stay in contact with friends/family far away
Useful for school - find info and work with classmates
Meet new people and discover different cultures

cards.front: Name the four disadvantages (Nachteile) of social media given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Cyberbullying is a big problem / Too much screen time causes sleep problems / Data protection problems - info not always safe / Social media can be addictive
items: Too much screen time causes sleep problems
Data protection problems - info not always safe

cards.front: Why is 'das Handy' called a false friend in German technology vocabulary?
cards.answer: It looks like the English word 'handy' but actually means 'mobile phone', not something useful.

cards.front: How does using 'einerseits ... andererseits' help you present a balanced opinion on social media?
cards.answer: It lets you state one advantage (staying in contact with friends) then contrast it with a disadvantage (too much screen time being unhealthy).

title: Enterprise and the Dynamic Business Environment
subject: business-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four reasons the lesson gives for why businesses fail even with a good idea.
cards.answer: Poor financial management / Underestimating competition / Failing to understand what customers want / Bad timing
items: Failing to understand what customers want

cards.front: Why did the rise of smartphones create whole new industries?
cards.answer: New technology opened new possibilities, creating demand for apps, cases, chargers and repair services that barely existed before.

cards.front: Why do smartphone manufacturers release updated versions on a regular cycle?
cards.answer: This is planned obsolescence, a deliberate strategy to encourage customers to keep upgrading to newer versions.

cards.front: How did an ageing UK population create new business opportunities?
cards.answer: Demographic change increased demand for mobility aids, retirement financial services and age-appropriate leisure activities.

cards.front: Name the three specific ways the lesson says a business benefits from motivated employees.
cards.answer: Attracting employees / Retaining employees / Productivity

cards.front: Why can a bonus create problems even though it rewards achievement?
cards.answer: Bonuses can create pressure and may cause employees to cut corners to hit targets quickly.

cards.front: Why is promotion considered one of the most powerful motivators?
cards.answer: It gives a long-term incentive for consistent performance and also brings status and new challenges, not just money.

cards.front: Why can micromanaging demotivate skilled employees?
cards.answer: It removes their autonomy, making them feel their expertise is not respected.

cards.front: Name the five areas of life the lesson says social class determines outcomes in, according to Russell's play.
cards.answer: Education / Employment / Health / Housing / Survival

cards.front: How does Russell use the Johnstones' move to Skelmersdale to show class cannot be escaped by relocation?
cards.answer: Moving to a new estate doesn't change the family's class; the same poverty, unemployment and lack of opportunity follow them.

cards.front: Why does Russell argue that education reinforces class division rather than breaking it down?
cards.answer: Eddie's private school encourages and supports him toward university, while Mickey's comprehensive has low expectations and scarce resources, leading him to unemployment.

cards.front: Why does the Moon appear to go through phases as seen from Earth?
cards.answer: The Sun always lights half the Moon, but as the Moon orbits Earth we see different fractions of that lit half.

cards.front: Why did the late nineteenth century see the world divided into time zones?
cards.answer: Because if every location kept its own Local Mean Time, clocks would differ town to town, making travel and communication chaotic.

title: Rivers: Long Profile, Cross Profile & Processes
subject: geography-aqa

cards.front: Name the four processes the lesson gives for how a river transports its load.
cards.answer: Traction / Saltation / Suspension / Solution

cards.front: Name the four features the lesson lists as forming in a river's cross profile across the three courses.
cards.answer: Interlocking spurs / Meanders / Flood plains / Levees

cards.front: Why does the long profile of a river flatten out from a steep source to a gentle gradient near the mouth?
cards.answer: Near the source energy fights friction on the rough bed so goes into vertical erosion, but downstream the smoother channel needs less energy for friction, letting the river carry more load with a gentler slope.

cards.front: Why does a river drop larger material first while the finest particles travel furthest downstream?
cards.answer: Larger material needs more energy to carry, so it is deposited as soon as the river slows, while fine particles stay carried until energy drops further.

cards.front: Name the six staging configurations the lesson identifies.
cards.answer: Proscenium arch / Thrust stage / Theatre in the round / Traverse / End-on staging / Promenade

cards.front: Why can a proscenium arch theatre support illusionistic staging with hidden machinery?
cards.answer: The audience sees only one face of the stage, so the wings to either side stay invisible, hiding backdrops and machinery.

cards.front: Why does traverse staging create a sense of surveillance or voyeurism?
cards.answer: The two audience banks face each other across the action, so each group can see the other watching the performance.

cards.front: Name the four separation techniques described in the lesson for different mixtures.
cards.answer: Filtration / Crystallisation / Simple distillation / Fractional distillation

cards.front: Name the three steps used in the UK to produce potable water from fresh water sources.
cards.answer: Sedimentation / Filtration / Chlorination

cards.front: Why is a pencil line (not pen) used for the baseline in paper chromatography?
cards.answer: Pencil is insoluble and will not dissolve in the solvent, unlike pen ink.

cards.front: Why must water used for chemical analysis not contain dissolved salts?
cards.answer: Dissolved ions could interfere with test results, giving false positives or inaccurate measurements.

cards.front: Name the four purposes of marketing set out in the specification.
cards.answer: Identifying customers / Understanding customers / Informing customers / Increasing sales

cards.front: Name the three businesses given as examples of identifying a specific target customer group, and their target group.
cards.answer: LEGO – children aged 4-11 and parents / Saga – over-50s / Aldi – price-conscious shoppers

cards.front: Why did Ben Francis spend time in gyms and on Instagram before advertising Gymshark?
cards.answer: To understand what young gym-goers actually wanted before informing them about the product.

cards.front: Why can a brilliant product still fail even with good marketing?
cards.answer: Because a brilliant product no customers know about will fail, so marketing must inform them for sales to happen.

title: Time Series, Index Numbers and Rates of Change
subject: statistics-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three named index numbers the lesson identifies.
cards.answer: RPI (Retail Price Index) / CPI (Consumer Price Index) / GDP (Gross Domestic Product)

cards.front: How do you choose how many points to use in a moving average? (Higher)
cards.answer: Match the number of points to the cycle length in the data, e.g. 4-point for quarterly, 7-point for weekly, 3-point for a 3-period cycle.

cards.front: Why do RPI and CPI give housing a bigger weight than entertainment? (Higher)
cards.answer: Because households spend far more of their income on housing, so it should have more influence on the overall index.

cards.front: How do you predict a future value using a trend line and seasonal effect?
cards.answer: Take the trend line's value at that point in time, then adjust it using the average seasonal effect for that period.

title: Chapters 1–3: The Door, the Will and Dr Jekyll
subject: english-literature-aqa

cards.front: Name the three key structural and language methods established in Chapters 1–3.
cards.answer: Mystery and withholding / Setting as symbolism / Fog and darkness

cards.front: Why do Enfield and Utterson agree never to speak of the trampling incident again?
cards.answer: It reflects a very Victorian response, prioritising discretion over truth.

cards.front: How does the fog in London link to the story's themes?
cards.answer: The fog symbolises the obscured truth and moral confusion at the heart of the story.

cards.front: Why does Utterson's rational perspective limit what the reader can understand?
cards.answer: He cannot understand Jekyll's experiment because it is beyond rational explanation.

title: Regulation, Digital Disruption and the BBFC, OFCOM, IPSO, ASA and PEGI
subject: media-studies-aqa

cards.front: Name the six UK media regulatory bodies given in the lesson.
cards.answer: OFCOM / IPSO / BBFC / ASA / PEGI / Video Standards Council (VSC)

cards.front: Name the five PEGI age rating categories for video games.
Why does digital disruption challenge the existing media regulation framework?
cards.answer: Social media lets billions publish unscreened content, anonymous speech enables harassment, and deepfakes/disinformation spread faster than regulators can respond.

cards.front: Why do critics see a risk in OFCOM's statutory status?
cards.answer: A government-backed regulator always risks political influence over the media it oversees.

cards.front: According to the lesson, what four parts should each main essay paragraph make when analysing Anita and Me?
cards.answer: A specific claim / A supporting quotation / Analysis of Syal's language and methods / Embedded relevant context
items: Analysis of Syal's language and methods

cards.front: Why does Meena tolerate Anita's cruelty for so long in their friendship?
cards.answer: Her willingness to tolerate it reveals the depth of her desire to belong, since the friendship is never between equals.

cards.front: Why is the eventual breakdown of the Meena-Anita friendship presented as a positive step?
cards.answer: It shows Meena learning that real friendship cannot be built on inequality and the suppression of identity.

cards.front: How should context (AO3) be used across an essay on Anita and Me, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: It must be woven into every analytical paragraph and always linked to Syal's purpose, not bolted on separately.

cards.front: What three reasons does Mrs Birling give for rejecting Eva's charity appeal?
cards.answer: Eva used the name 'Mrs Birling' / Sybil disliked her manner / Eva refused stolen money from the father
items: Eva refused stolen money from the father

cards.front: How does Gerald's behaviour in Act 3 undermine his moment of genuine feeling for Daisy in Act 2?
cards.answer: He recovers quickly and leads efforts to prove the Inspector was a hoax, restoring the status quo instead of changing.

cards.front: Why is Mrs Birling's demand that the father be publicly shamed an example of dramatic irony?
cards.answer: She unknowingly demands her own son Eric be publicly humiliated, since he is the father of Eva's child.

title: The Four Aims of Life and Dharma
subject: religious-studies-aqa

cards.front: Name the four stages of life (ashramas) described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Student stage (brahmacharya) / Householder stage (grihastha) / Retirement stage (vanaprastha) / Renunciation stage (sannyasa)

cards.front: How does dharma act as a guardrail for the pursuit of artha and kama?
cards.answer: Wealth and pleasure are only wrong when pursued through greed, deception, lust or exploitation, which transgress dharma.

cards.front: Why do many Hindus prefer the term sanatana dharma over the word 'Hinduism'?
cards.answer: Because sanatana dharma stresses that its principles are universal and eternal, not tied to one culture, unlike the colonial-era term 'Hinduism'.

cards.front: Name the four types of work the lesson gives as examples of Lagos's informal economy.
cards.answer: Street selling / Motorbike taxis (okadas) / Small workshops repairing phones and TVs / Casual building work
items: Small workshops repairing phones and TVs

cards.front: Name the five formal services or resources the lesson says Lagos provides that rural villages cannot.
cards.answer: Specialist hospital care / University-level education / Piped water system / National grid electricity / Waste collection in planned districts

cards.front: Why would Lagos keep growing even if migration into the city stopped completely?
cards.answer: Migrants are mostly young adults who have children, birth rates stay high, and the death rate has fallen due to better healthcare and clean water.

cards.front: Why do sociologists describe Lagos's informal economy as the city's 'real economy'?
cards.answer: Because for most new arrivals it is the first, and often only, way to earn enough to put food on the table.

cards.front: Name the three dramatists of the Manchester School mentioned in the lesson.
cards.answer: Harold Brighouse / Stanley Houghton / Allan Monkhouse

cards.front: According to the lesson, what four things does AO3 context for Hobson's Choice require understanding of?
cards.answer: Victorian Salford / the rigid class system / attitudes to women / why Brighouse set the play in 1880 but wrote it decades later
items: why Brighouse set the play in 1880 but wrote it decades later

cards.front: Why does Willie Mossop work in the cellar while Maggie, Alice and Vickey work on the shop floor?
cards.answer: It creates a spatial hierarchy showing the most skilled worker has the lowest position, critiquing a system that rewards ownership over ability.

cards.front: Why did Hobson initially prefer Albert Prosser and Fred Beenstock over Willie Mossop as sons-in-law?
cards.answer: Because as a solicitor's son and a corn merchant's son they carried social status, which Hobson valued over Willie's practical skill.

cards.front: Name the four common metal stock forms described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Sheet and plate / Bar and rod / Tube / Angle section

cards.front: Name the four types of force that metals experience in service.
cards.answer: Tension / Compression / Shear / Torsion

cards.front: Why does quenching during hardening produce a hard but brittle steel structure?
cards.answer: Rapid cooling prevents carbon atoms migrating, locking a hard but brittle martensite crystal structure in place.

cards.front: Why is tube a more efficient stock form than solid rod for making a handrail?
cards.answer: Starting from tube eliminates the need to bore out the centre, saving time and material waste.

cards.front: Name the three colour worlds Deakins uses to structure Skyfall's visual journey.
cards.answer: Shanghai / Macau / Scottish Highlands

cards.front: Name the three named sequences given as micro-analysis worked examples in the lesson.
cards.answer: Macau-casino lizard-pit confrontation / Whitehall public-inquiry attack / Skyfall-house chapel finale

cards.front: Why does Deakins shift the palette from Shanghai's neon darkness to the Scottish Highlands' desaturated tones?
cards.answer: The shift strips Bond of his urban slickness, placing him in a bleaker, more exposed setting as narrative punctuation.

cards.front: Why does the colour change from gold to cold blue in the Macau lizard-pit confrontation matter?
cards.answer: It signals a sudden change in power dynamic, marking the transition from spectacle to threat.

cards.front: Name the three concessions Nicholas II made in the October Manifesto.
cards.answer: Civil rights (speech, assembly, conscience) / Legal political parties / An elected parliament (the Duma)

cards.front: Name the three things that saved the Tsarist regime after the 1905 Revolution.
cards.answer: The October Manifesto split the opposition / The war with Japan ended, freeing troops / The army stayed loyal
items: The October Manifesto split the opposition
The war with Japan ended, freeing troops

cards.front: Why did the October Manifesto split the opposition to the Tsar?
cards.answer: Liberals and Octobrists welcomed its concessions while revolutionaries dismissed them, so moderates now had something to lose by joining further uprisings.

cards.front: How did ending the Russo-Japanese War help the Tsar crush the Moscow Uprising?
cards.answer: The Treaty of Portsmouth brought the field army home from Manchuria, freeing reliable troops to crush the uprising with artillery.

cards.front: Name the three factors the lesson gives for why Viking raids on England began.
cards.answer: Population pressure in Scandinavia pushed younger sons abroad / Advances in longship technology allowed raids far inland / Anglo-Saxon England was divided and rich in monasteries
items: Population pressure in Scandinavia pushed younger sons abroad
Advances in longship technology allowed raids far inland
Anglo-Saxon England was divided and rich in monasteries

cards.front: Name the three military reforms Alfred introduced to defend Wessex after Edington.
cards.answer: Divided the fyrd into two rotating halves / Built or strengthened thirty burhs across Wessex / Invested in a small fleet for naval defence
items: Divided the fyrd into two rotating halves
Built or strengthened thirty burhs across Wessex
Invested in a small fleet for naval defence

cards.front: Why did dividing the fyrd into two halves help Alfred's defence of Wessex?
cards.answer: One half could always be on campaign while the other worked the fields, ending armies dispersing at harvest.

cards.front: Why did Æthelred's St Brice's Day massacre in 1002 lead to full-scale invasion?
cards.answer: The massacre of Danish settlers provoked the Danish king Sweyn Forkbeard to launch a full invasion of England.

cards.front: Name the three ways media ownership can change, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Merger / Takeover / Demerger

cards.front: Name the three supply-chain stages a vertically integrated film conglomerate might own.
cards.answer: Production (studio creating content) / Distribution (gets content to retailers/broadcasters) / Exhibition (streaming service or cinema chain)

cards.front: How does diversification reduce financial risk for a media conglomerate?
cards.answer: If one division performs poorly in a given year, profits from another division can compensate.

cards.front: Why are independent (indie) producers not entirely free from conglomerate power structures?
cards.answer: They often rely on conglomerate-owned distributors to get their work to audiences.

cards.front: Name the four men who kill the suitors together in Book 22.
cards.answer: Odysseus / Telemachus / Eumaeus / Philoetius

cards.front: Name the two loyal servants who help Odysseus and are contrasted with the disloyal ones in the homecoming books.
cards.answer: Eumaeus the swineherd / Philoetius the cowherd

cards.front: Why must Odysseus stay disguised as a beggar when he first returns to Ithaca?
cards.answer: Over a hundred suitors have taken his palace, so he would be killed if recognised before he could prepare.

cards.front: How does the moral case built across the poem justify Odysseus killing the suitors in Book 22?
cards.answer: They were repeatedly warned, violated xenia, dishonoured his household, and the gods disapproved and sanctioned the punishment.

cards.front: Name the four things the lesson says the kyria managed within the Athenian household.
cards.answer: Supervised domestic slaves / Managed food stores and finances / Organised weaving and cloth production / Raised and cared for children

cards.front: Name the four occasions the lesson gives when Athenian women could leave the house.
cards.answer: Attend religious festivals / Visit other women / Attend funerals / Collect water

cards.front: Why was the gynaikon usually placed at the back or upper floor of an Athenian house?
cards.answer: To stop women being seen by men arriving at or leaving the house, keeping them separate from male visitors.

cards.front: Why did weaving matter as a symbol of Athenian female virtue?
cards.answer: It was practically useful for producing household cloth, but also symbolically showed a woman's domestic virtue and loyalty, as with Penelope.

cards.front: What three quotations should you learn for each poem in your cluster?
cards.answer: One for the central idea / One for the strongest image / One from the ending

cards.front: How does a shift from 'you' to 'they' in a poem's pronouns reveal attitude?
cards.answer: It shows the speaker stepping back from the subject, distancing themselves from it.

cards.front: How does using the present tense affect how an old wound feels in a poem?
cards.answer: It makes the old wound feel current, whereas a sudden shift to past tense pushes the feeling safely out of reach.

cards.front: Why is misquotation costly in part (b) answers?
cards.answer: It stops responses reaching the higher bands, especially for analysis of method.

title: Changes in tactics and strategy: medieval to early modern
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: The lesson lists four dominant weapon/arm types across British warfare, in order. What are they?
cards.answer: Infantry (shield wall) / Cavalry (Norman knight) / Missile (longbow) / Firearm (musket and rifle)

cards.front: Why was Viking raiding hard for Saxon England to defend against?
cards.answer: Longships let Vikings strike coastal and river targets fast, plunder, and withdraw before a defensive force could be gathered.

cards.front: Why could cavalry charges by armoured knights fail against disciplined infantry?
cards.answer: Cavalry struggled against disciplined pikemen, prepared defensive terrain, and especially the English longbow.

cards.front: What single factor does the lesson say stayed constant from the shield wall to the musket line?
cards.answer: Discipline: disciplined soldiers consistently outperformed undisciplined ones whatever formation or weapon they used.

title: Investigating the Work of Designers and Companies
subject: design-technology-eduqas

cards.front: Name the five designers/companies you need to know for the exam.
cards.answer: Airbus / Apple / James Dyson / Philippe Starck / Matthew Williamson

cards.front: Name the three linked ideas to focus on when writing about Apple in an extended answer.
cards.answer: Minimalism / Material precision / Integration

cards.front: Why did Apple remove the headphone jack from the iPhone?
cards.answer: To reduce the number of components and waterproofing failure points, reflecting Apple's philosophy of simplification despite short-term controversy.

cards.front: Why does Airbus's design philosophy prioritise engineering precision over aesthetics?
cards.answer: Because decisions like using composite materials are driven by measurable performance data and safety regulations, not visual style.

title: The Babadook: Narrative and Grief as Monster
subject: film-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four production companies/organisations that produced or backed The Babadook.
cards.answer: Causeway Films / Smoking Gun Productions / Screen Australia / South Australian Film Corporation

cards.front: Name the three diegetic domestic sounds mixed louder than naturalism requires in The Babadook.
cards.answer: Clocks / Creaking floorboards / Samuel's night-terrors

cards.front: How does the film's desaturated palette make the Babadook's appearance more disturbing?
cards.answer: Because the world is already drained of colour, the Babadook's high-contrast black-and-white shapes feel like a graphic intrusion rather than darkness entering a bright space.

cards.front: Why is sudden silence used in the police-station sequence?
cards.answer: The ambient domestic sound drops completely on the cut, and this contrast is more unsettling than a jump scare.

cards.front: Name the three events the lesson gives that cause Elizabeth's growth.
cards.answer: Darcy's letter reveals her errors / Pemberley shows Darcy's true character / the Lydia crisis proves Darcy's love
items: the Lydia crisis proves Darcy's love

cards.front: Name the four qualities the lesson says Darcy's pride conceals.
cards.answer: loyal / generous / honest / responsible

cards.front: How does the pun on 'prided' in Elizabeth's self-recognition quotation work?
cards.answer: It shows her realising that her prejudice was actually a form of pride in her own judgement.

cards.front: Why is the Wickham/Darcy pairing described as the most important foil in the novel?
cards.answer: Wickham looks like a gentleman but isn't, while Darcy looks unfriendly but truly is one, showing appearance and reality rarely align.

cards.front: Name the four areas the USSR expanded into after signing the Nazi-Soviet Pact.
cards.answer: Eastern Poland / The Baltic states / Finland / Romania

cards.front: Why did Stalin sign the Nazi-Soviet Pact in August 1939?
cards.answer: To buy time and keep the USSR out of the coming war while gaining territory in Eastern Europe.

cards.front: Why is the Battle of Stalingrad seen as the turning point of the war on the Eastern Front?
cards.answer: It was Germany's first major defeat there, shifting the strategic initiative to the Soviet Union for the rest of the war.

title: Reading Data — Graphs, Histograms & Pie Charts
subject: engineering-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four graph types the lesson describes and their main use.
cards.answer: Bar chart — discrete categories / Histogram — continuous data intervals / Line graph — trends over time / Pie chart — proportions of a whole
items: Pie chart — proportions of a whole

cards.front: In the component diameter histogram, why does the tall central bar (120 out of 200 within tolerance) suggest good process control?
cards.answer: Most components cluster near the target diameter with only a few significantly over- or under-size, showing a roughly symmetrical distribution.

cards.front: How should you decide whether a histogram's bar height shows frequency or frequency density?
cards.answer: Check the vertical-axis label, since area (not always height) represents frequency unless class widths are equal.

cards.front: Name the four levels of colonial society's social hierarchy, from top to bottom.
cards.answer: Colonial gentry / Middling sort / Tenant farmers, labourers, indentured servants / Enslaved people

cards.front: Name the three sources of tension between groups in colonial society described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Tidewater elites vs backcountry farmers / Religious dissent between Puritans, Quakers and Anglicans / Urban tradesmen vs merchants over prices
items: Religious dissent between Puritans, Quakers and Anglicans
Urban tradesmen vs merchants over prices

cards.front: Why did backcountry farmers resent the tidewater-dominated colonial assemblies?
cards.answer: Assemblies ignored their petitions for protection from frontier raids and gave the backcountry too few seats.

cards.front: Why were the Middle colonies more ethnically and religiously diverse than New England or the South?
cards.answer: Religious toleration, fertile soil and the busy port of Philadelphia attracted a wider mix of nationalities and faiths.

cards.front: The lesson names five common everyday sources of free sugars that people often overlook. What are they?
cards.answer: Ketchup / Low-fat yoghurt / Ready-made pasta sauces / Flavoured drinks / Breakfast cereals

cards.front: What are the three common scenarios given for using nutritional data to make targeted recipe changes?
cards.answer: Increasing dietary fibre (NSP) / Reducing saturated fat / Meeting free sugar recommendations

cards.front: Why does swapping 50 g butter for 50 g olive oil greatly reduce saturated fat even though total fat barely changes?
cards.answer: Butter is about 52% saturated fat while olive oil is only about 15% saturated, so total fat stays similar but saturated fat drops sharply.

cards.front: How can you check whether a recipe's stated kcal-per-serving figure is plausible?
cards.answer: Multiply the grams of fat, carbohydrate and protein by their energy yields (9, 3.75, 4 kcal/g) and add the results to compare with the stated figure.

cards.front: What three social layers make up the class hierarchy in Raveloe?
cards.answer: Squire Cass and his sons / respectable villagers like farmers and tradespeople / labourers and outsiders like Silas
items: respectable villagers like farmers and tradespeople

cards.front: Why did Eliot set Silas Marner in an earlier period than when she published it?
cards.answer: To capture a pre-industrial rural world that her readers were losing to factories, railways and migration.

cards.front: How does Eppie's final choice show female agency in the novel?
cards.answer: She chooses to stay with Silas rather than accept Godfrey's wealth, acting on her own will despite limited women's rights.

title: Social & Emotional Development — Bowlby, Ainsworth & Burke
subject: health-social-care-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three attachment types Ainsworth identified in the Strange Situation.
cards.answer: Secure attachment / Insecure-avoidant attachment / Insecure-resistant (ambivalent) attachment

cards.front: What social and emotional changes does the lesson say later adulthood brings?
cards.answer: Retirement changing identity and purpose / More frequent bereavement of partners/friends / Shrinking social networks / Increased physical dependency affecting self-esteem / Loneliness risk

cards.front: Why does Bowlby's internal working model shape a person's future relationships?
cards.answer: The primary attachment figure gives the infant a mental template of what relationships are like, which shapes expectations of all later relationships.

cards.front: Why might a teenager copy a behaviour they see a peer being praised for, according to Bandura?
cards.answer: Through vicarious reinforcement, seeing someone else rewarded for a behaviour makes the teenager more likely to imitate it themselves.

cards.front: Name the four additions Leicester made to Kenilworth for Elizabeth's visits in the 1570s.
cards.answer: Leicester's Building (state apartments) / a grand new gatehouse / great windows cut into the Norman keep / a privy garden
items: great windows cut into the Norman keep

cards.front: Name the six entertainments the lesson describes at the 1575 visit.
cards.answer: fireworks / hunting / masques / bear-baiting / an Italian tumbler / a swimming pageant with Arion

cards.front: Why do historians think the 1575 visit was Leicester's last bid to marry Elizabeth?
cards.answer: The pageants staged masques of marriage and a lady freed from an enchanted lake, and a planned marriage-themed entertainment was never performed, likely because the queen declined it.

cards.front: How did Leicester turn the mere, an old medieval defence, into part of his entertainment for Elizabeth?
cards.answer: The mere, which had once made Kenilworth almost siege-proof, was used as a stage for water pageants, including the swimming performance of Arion on a mechanical dolphin.

title: Charles II: The King and His Court
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the three items the East India cities/territories part of Catherine of Braganza's dowry included alongside cash and trading rights.
cards.answer: City of Bombay / City of Tangier / Trading rights in Brazil and East Indies
items: Trading rights in Brazil and East Indies

cards.front: Why did who got near Charles II's mistresses matter politically?
cards.answer: Court mistresses were channels of patronage, so being close to them could win jobs, contracts and titles.

cards.front: Why was reaching Charles II's bedchamber the surest sign of political favour?
cards.answer: Access to the king moved by stages from public rooms to the bedchamber, admitting only a handful of trusted courtiers.

cards.front: How did the Earl of Danby use court patronage to manage Parliament?
cards.answer: As Lord Treasurer he distributed Crown money and offices, with an estimated 200 MPs receiving payments in some form.

title: Electric Circuits, Ohm's Law and I-V Characteristics
subject: separate-sciences-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three rules that apply to a series circuit.
cards.answer: Same current everywhere / Voltages add up / Resistances add up

cards.front: In the core practical for I-V characteristics, name three things you must do to get a reliable graph.
cards.answer: Record at least six evenly spaced values / Repeat readings to check anomalies / Allow cooling time between filament lamp readings
items: Record at least six evenly spaced values
Allow cooling time between filament lamp readings

cards.front: Why does an LDR's resistance fall as light intensity increases?
cards.answer: A light-dependent resistor's resistance falls as light intensity increases, giving low resistance in bright conditions and high resistance in darkness.

cards.front: Why does adding more branches to a parallel circuit decrease the total resistance?
cards.answer: Each extra branch gives current another path to flow through, so adding more branches decreases the total resistance.

title: Information Processing, Forgetting and the Brain
subject: psychology-ocr

cards.front: Why can retrieval failure make a memory feel completely lost even though it still exists?
cards.answer: Without the correct retrieval cue, stored information cannot be accessed, even though it has not decayed or been displaced.

cards.front: Why does shallow, surface-level encoding tend to produce weaker memories?
cards.answer: Repeating information without thinking about its meaning fades quickly, unlike linking it to something already known.

cards.front: Name the three ways encoding can happen, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Visually (as an image) / Acoustically (as a sound) / Semantically (by meaning)

title: The Great Society, Feminism and Roe v Wade
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the three programmes created by the 1964 Economic Opportunity Act.
cards.answer: Job Corps / Head Start / Volunteers in Service to America (VISTA)

cards.front: What four things did Phyllis Schlafly's STOP ERA campaign claim the amendment would cause?
cards.answer: Force women into the military draft / End alimony / Abolish single-sex bathrooms / Undermine the family
items: Force women into the military draft

cards.front: Why did the Vietnam War undermine the Great Society?
cards.answer: Military spending rose from $100 million to $20 billion a year, diverting money that could have funded anti-poverty programmes.

cards.front: Why did many married women oppose the Equal Rights Amendment in the 1970s?
cards.answer: They benefited from alimony, presumed custody and draft exemption, and feared losing those legal protections.

title: The Trinity, the Incarnation and Jesus as Moral Authority
subject: religious-studies-eduqas

cards.front: In the Sermon on the Mount, what three examples does Jesus give showing that interior disposition matters, not just external acts?
cards.answer: Anger is the root of murder / Lust is the root of adultery / Generosity must be given freely without public display
items: Anger is the root of murder
Lust is the root of adultery
Generosity must be given freely without public display

cards.front: Why does the Incarnation give Catholic theology a deep respect for material and bodily existence?
cards.answer: Because if God became truly human, human nature — including bodily existence, suffering and death — has been taken into the life of God.

cards.front: Why is it significant that it is the incarnate Son of God, not just a human being, who suffers on the Cross?
cards.answer: Because Jesus is fully God and fully human, so his suffering shows God himself entering the darkest human experience.

cards.front: Name the six relational operators in Python.
cards.answer: == (equal to) / != (not equal to) / (greater than) / = (greater than or equal to)

cards.front: Name the three logical operators in Python.
cards.answer: and / or / not

cards.front: Why does adding a string and an integer together in Python cause a TypeError?
cards.answer: Because Python's + operator can only concatenate strings, so a number must first be converted to a string with str().

cards.front: Why is len(s) - 1 used to get the last character of a string instead of a negative index?
cards.answer: Because Python does not include negative indexes, so len() is used to calculate the position of the last character.

cards.front: Name the three types of technical textile used in buildings, homes and sport, as described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Construction textiles / Domestic textiles / Sports textiles

cards.front: Name the six modern/smart materials the lesson says react to a stimulus rather than staying fixed.
cards.answer: Shape-memory alloys / Nanomaterials / Reactive glass / Piezoelectric materials / Temperature-responsive polymers / Conductive inks

cards.front: Why is plywood strong in more than one direction and less likely to split?
cards.answer: It is made of glued wood veneer layers with the grain of each layer rotated, spreading strength in multiple directions.

cards.front: Why are shape-memory alloys useful in self-adjusting fittings without motors or switches?
cards.answer: They snap back to their original shape when heated past a set temperature, changing shape automatically without electronics.

cards.front: Name the three most useful structural terms the lesson says you should learn to identify.
cards.answer: Enjambment / Caesura / Volta

cards.front: Why might a stanza break in a poem about a relationship represent a change in mood?
cards.answer: The gap between stanzas can mark a shift in time, perspective or mood, like a moment of emotional change.

cards.front: How does regular rhyme breaking down across a poem mirror emotional change?
cards.answer: Full rhyme breaking down in the final stanza structurally mirrors a shift from happiness to loss.

cards.front: Why do short lines create a sense of control or tension in a poem?
cards.answer: Short lines feel abrupt and controlled, while long lines suggest expansiveness or overwhelming emotion.

title: Rehabilitation & Reducing the Risk of Injury
subject: cambridge-nationals-sport-science

cards.front: Name the four group characteristics a risk assessment considers when deciding on supervision and precautions.
cards.answer: Age / Experience / Medical conditions / Group size

cards.front: Name the three methods used in medical screening before contact sport.
cards.answer: Health questionnaires / Physical examinations / Electrocardiograms (ECGs)

cards.front: How does electrotherapy help an injured performer during rehabilitation?
cards.answer: It uses electrical stimulation, such as TENS, to reduce pain and stimulate contractions in weakened muscles.

cards.front: Why is PNF stretching particularly useful in the later stages of rehabilitation?
cards.answer: Contracting then stretching the muscle in PNF stretching helps the athlete regain full flexibility at the injured joint.

title: Data Structures: Arrays, Records and File Design
subject: computer-science-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three data structures the lesson says you need to understand for GCSE.
cards.answer: One-dimensional array / Two-dimensional array / Record

cards.front: The lesson lists four fields in the example student file design. What are they?
cards.answer: StudentID / Surname / Forename / YearGroup

cards.front: Why are arrays efficient for storing data?
cards.answer: All elements are the same type and size, so the computer can jump directly to any index in one step.

cards.front: Why is a file needed instead of just a single record when storing data on thousands of patients?
cards.answer: A file stores many related records together permanently on secondary storage, whereas a record only represents one entity.

cards.front: Name four ways the lesson says religious believers work for justice and reconciliation.
cards.answer: Interfaith dialogue between conflicting communities / Organisations like the Corrymeela Community / Prison chaplaincy and restorative justice programmes / Charitable work addressing causes of conflict / Prayer for those affected by violence
items: Prison chaplaincy and restorative justice programmes
Charitable work addressing causes of conflict
Prayer for those affected by violence

cards.front: Name three arguments the lesson gives for why forgiveness is not always desirable.
cards.answer: Quick forgiveness minimises the wrong done / True forgiveness needs genuine repentance / Premature forgiveness can silence victims
items: Quick forgiveness minimises the wrong done

cards.front: Why might reconciliation built on injustice be considered a 'false peace'?
cards.answer: Because true peace is said to be impossible without justice, so peace without justice will eventually break down.

cards.front: Why did Martin Luther King Jr say Christians were obligated to oppose racial segregation?
cards.answer: Because he argued segregation was a form of social injustice that Christians had a duty to challenge.

cards.front: Name the three wires in a UK three-pin plug, with their colours.
cards.answer: Live - brown / Neutral - blue / Earth - green and yellow striped

cards.front: Why is the live wire always dangerous even when an appliance is switched off?
cards.answer: Because it remains connected to the mains supply at about 230 V.

cards.front: How do the earth wire and fuse work together to protect against a fault?
cards.answer: If live touches the casing, a surge of current flows through the earth wire, blowing the fuse and cutting the supply.

cards.front: Why don't double-insulated appliances need an earth wire?
cards.answer: The plastic casing is an insulator so it can't become live, so there's no shock risk even with a wiring fault.

cards.front: Name the four reasons the lesson gives for counter-urbanisation in the UK.
cards.answer: Better roads (M25, M6, M62) / Electronic working, especially since 2020 / Perceived crime in cities / Rising house prices pushing families out
items: Rising house prices pushing families out

cards.front: The lesson names four historical factors that determined where UK Industrial Revolution cities grew. What are they?
cards.answer: Access to coal / Access to iron ore / Fast water for early mills / Port access for trade

cards.front: Why do cities in emerging and developing countries often develop informal settlements like favelas?
cards.answer: Because cities grow faster than housing supply, leaving migrants without enough affordable homes.

cards.front: Why do birth rates spike within rapidly urbanising cities, beyond migration itself?
cards.answer: Because young migrants moving to cities are typically of childbearing age, causing natural increase.

title: From Page to Stage: The Rehearsal Process
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: Name the seven main stages of a professional rehearsal process, in order.
cards.answer: Read-through / Blocking rehearsals / Character and scene work / Production meetings / Technical rehearsal / Dress rehearsal / Previews

cards.front: Name the three reasons the lesson gives for why a short scene might take an hour to tech.
cards.answer: A lighting state may need refocusing / A sound cue may arrive at the wrong moment / A scene change may need to be refined
items: A lighting state may need refocusing
A sound cue may arrive at the wrong moment
A scene change may need to be refined

cards.front: Why might a director ask a performer to try a scene both in stillness and with continuous movement during early rehearsals?
cards.answer: To find out which choice communicates more clearly to the audience at the back of the house, testing whether the director's concept works.

cards.front: How does a production meeting turn a director's technical request into a working solution?
cards.answer: The director states a specific need, the designer proposes a solution, and the stage manager records it in production notes.

cards.front: Name the three network topologies covered in the lesson.
cards.answer: Bus (single shared cable) / Star (central hub) / Ring (loop of devices)

cards.front: Name the six hardware devices the lesson describes as making a network function.
cards.answer: Router / Switch / Hub / Modem / Network interface card (NIC) / Wireless Access Point (WAP)

cards.front: Why does performance get worse in a bus topology as more devices are added?
cards.answer: Because all devices share the same single backbone cable to send and receive data.

cards.front: How does encryption protect data from packet sniffing?
cards.answer: It scrambles data using a key so intercepted packets appear as meaningless ciphertext without the decryption key.

cards.front: According to the lesson, what three qualities does Orwell use to build reader sympathy for Boxer before his death?
cards.answer: His loyalty / His gentleness / His simple decency

cards.front: How does Squealer explain away the horse slaughterer's writing on the side of the van?
cards.answer: He claims the van used to belong to a knacker but was now owned by a vet who hadn't repainted it.

cards.front: Why does Orwell suggest Benjamin is complicit in the pigs' crimes even though he never actively helps them?
cards.answer: He has the intelligence and literacy to prove the commandments are being changed but does nothing, letting the pigs act unchallenged.

cards.front: Why does Boxer's broken retirement promise represent Orwell's most damning criticism of the Soviet system?
cards.answer: It symbolises the social contract between workers and the state — work hard and you'll be looked after — which Napoleon betrays completely.

title: Lenses, Visible Light and Black Body Radiation
subject: science-aqa

cards.front: Name the three standard rays used to draw a ray diagram for a convex lens.
cards.answer: Ray parallel to the axis, refracts through the principal focus / Ray through the centre of the lens, passes straight through unbent / Ray through the near focus, refracts to become parallel to the axis
items: Ray parallel to the axis, refracts through the principal focus
Ray through the centre of the lens, passes straight through unbent
Ray through the near focus, refracts to become parallel to the axis

cards.front: Name the three secondary colours formed by mixing two primary colours of light.
cards.answer: Red + green = yellow / Red + blue = magenta / Green + blue = cyan

cards.front: How do a cyan filter and a yellow filter together produce only green light?
cards.answer: The cyan filter absorbs red and the yellow filter absorbs blue, so together they absorb both, transmitting only green.

cards.front: How does the greenhouse effect increase the Earth's surface temperature?
cards.answer: Greenhouse gases absorb outgoing infrared radiation and re-emit some of it back towards the Earth, raising the surface temperature.

title: The League of Nations: Structure and Membership
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the four specialist agencies or commissions of the League described in the lesson (besides its main political bodies).
cards.answer: International Labour Organization / Health Committee / High Commission for Refugees / Slavery Commission / Mandate Commissions

cards.front: Why did the US Senate's refusal to ratify the Treaty of Versailles matter for the League?
cards.answer: It meant the USA, despite Wilson designing the League, never joined it.

cards.front: How did Eric Drummond shape the League's Secretariat?
cards.answer: He built it into a genuinely international civil service, recruiting staff loyal to the League rather than their home states.

cards.front: Why could the League do little when a great power was the aggressor and willing to accept sanctions?
cards.answer: It had no army of its own and members had no obligation to send troops, leaving only economic threats.

cards.front: How does Walby say 'the state' structure of patriarchy restricts women's power?
cards.answer: The state does little to protect women from patriarchal power — women are under-represented in office and equal pay laws are weakly enforced.

cards.front: How does patriarchal culture, according to Walby, control women's behaviour?
cards.answer: Cultural norms and media impose double standards on men's and women's behaviour, so women who challenge them face ridicule or stigma.

cards.front: According to the lesson, why does the social model of disability say disabled people have limited power in society?
cards.answer: Because of social barriers like inaccessible buildings, discriminatory attitudes and lack of support, not the impairment itself.

cards.front: Name the six factors, besides gender, the lesson identifies as producing unequal power relationships.
cards.answer: Social class / Sexuality / Race and ethnicity / Age / Disability / Religion and beliefs

cards.front: Name the four types of daily offerings made to the Lares.
cards.answer: Incense / Wine / Cakes / Garlands

cards.front: Name the three deities honoured in the Capitolium temple at Pompeii's forum.
cards.answer: Jupiter / Juno / Minerva

cards.front: Why was the Genius of the paterfamilias worshipped at the household shrine?
cards.answer: Worshipping his divine life-force reinforced the authority of the male head of household within the family's religious and social life.

cards.front: Why is it significant that Horace mentions Roman religious practice only in passing?
cards.answer: The incidental, unexplained nature of his references suggests religious practice was so ordinary it needed no explanation.

title: The Five Life Stages & Their Developmental Milestones
subject: health-social-care-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four PIES milestones a nursery key-worker would expect to see in a 5-year-old, one from each domain.
cards.answer: Can dress themselves and use scissors accurately / Vocabulary growing rapidly with theory of mind developing / Comparing self to peers, sensitive to praise or criticism / Play becoming cooperative with friendships based on shared interests
items: Can dress themselves and use scissors accurately
Vocabulary growing rapidly with theory of mind developing
Comparing self to peers, sensitive to praise or criticism
Play becoming cooperative with friendships based on shared interests

cards.front: Why is forming an attachment bond so significant during infancy?
cards.answer: It is an infant's most significant emotional development and forms the foundation for emotional security later in life.

cards.front: Why do many older adults face a higher risk of loneliness in later adulthood?
cards.answer: Social networks may shrink because mobility reduces and peers die, increasing the risk of isolation.

cards.front: Why does Austen use Mrs Reynolds's praise of Darcy to change Elizabeth's view of him?
cards.answer: As a servant with nothing to gain, her praise is more credible than anything Darcy could say about himself.

cards.front: How does Darcy's behaviour at Pemberley show he has changed since his first proposal?
cards.answer: He shows change through actions like asking permission to introduce Georgiana and treating the Gardiners with warmth, rather than declaring it.

cards.front: How does Georgiana Darcy's near-elopement with Wickham parallel Lydia's situation?
cards.answer: Both were targeted by Wickham, but Georgiana was rescued by Darcy's wealth and protection while Lydia's family cannot save her.

cards.front: How was Mr Bennet partly responsible for Lydia's elopement?
cards.answer: He let Lydia go to Brighton despite Elizabeth's warnings and retreated into his books instead of confronting the problem.

cards.front: Name the five types of love Shakespeare presents in Romeo and Juliet.
cards.answer: Petrarchan love / True romantic love / Physical love / Parental love / Friendship love

cards.front: Name the four moments the lesson uses to show violence escalating through the play.
cards.answer: The servants' brawl (Act 1, Scene 1) / Tybalt's fury at the ball / Mercutio's death and Tybalt's killing (Act 3, Scene 1) / The double suicide in the tomb (Act 5, Scene 3)
items: Mercutio's death and Tybalt's killing (Act 3, Scene 1)
The double suicide in the tomb (Act 5, Scene 3)

cards.front: Why does the lesson argue that love and violence are connected rather than opposites in Romeo and Juliet?
cards.answer: Romeo kills Tybalt out of love for Mercutio, Juliet kills herself for love of Romeo, and the feud only ends because the parents love their dead children enough to stop fighting.

cards.front: How does honour culture create an endless cycle of violence in the play?
cards.answer: Honour culture demands every insult be answered with a sword, so even Romeo, who tries to refuse fighting Tybalt, gets dragged back into the cycle.

title: Native Americans, Chicanos and other civil rights movements
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Name the four problems the lesson says Native Americans faced before the civil rights movements.
cards.answer: Extreme poverty / High unemployment / Poor health outcomes / Broken treaty promises

cards.front: Name the four directions the Chicano movement developed in beyond the UFW.
cards.answer: Alianza Federal de Mercedes (Tijerina) / Crusade for Justice (Gonzales) / LA school walkouts (1968) / La Raza Unida Party (1970)

cards.front: Why were many charges against AIM leaders after Wounded Knee eventually dismissed?
cards.answer: They were dismissed due to government misconduct, later linked to FBI surveillance of AIM documented by the Church Committee.

cards.front: Why did Native American activists argue the Indian Civil Rights Act 1968 was a limited gain?
cards.answer: It gave legal rights but did not restore treaty lands, so conditions on reservations remained dire without an economic base.

cards.front: What four reforms did Dubcek's Action Programme introduce in April 1968?
cards.answer: Abolished censorship and let independent newspapers flourish / Released political prisoners / Began to decentralise economic planning / Allowed open debate of past Stalinist abuses
items: Abolished censorship and let independent newspapers flourish
Allowed open debate of past Stalinist abuses

cards.front: What three responses did younger reformers turn to after concluding change inside the system was impossible post-1968?
cards.answer: Silent emigration / Dissident protest / Simple cynicism

cards.front: Why was Brezhnev alarmed by the success of the Prague Spring reforms?
cards.answer: He feared that if the Czech experiment succeeded, reformers in Poland, East Germany and elsewhere would press for similar reforms.

cards.front: Why were East German troops held back at the border during the August 1968 invasion?
cards.answer: To avoid awakening memories of the German occupation of Czechoslovakia in 1938-39.

title: Closing the Gap: Aid, Trade & Tourism in The Gambia
subject: geography-aqa

cards.front: Name the seven main strategies geographers identify for reducing the global development gap.
cards.answer: Investment / Industrial development / Tourism / International aid / Intermediate technology / Fair trade / Microfinance loans / debt relief

cards.front: Give the three examples of intermediate technology used in the lesson, with their countries.
cards.answer: Hand-drilled wells in Malawi / Treadle pumps in Bangladesh / Clay pot fridges in Sudan

cards.front: How does the multiplier effect help a poorer country's economy through tourism?
cards.answer: Money tourists spend gets re-spent locally on food, building materials and education, circulating through the economy.

cards.front: Why do charities like Oxfam favour aid that builds local capacity rather than giving handouts?
cards.answer: Because aid can create dependency or be misused if governments are corrupt, so capacity-building aid avoids these problems.

title: Runnymede 1215: Magna Carta and the First Barons' War
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the six broad areas covered by Magna Carta's provisions.
cards.answer: Feudal incidents / Taxation / Justice / The Church / Royal forests, weights and measures / Treatment of foreign mercenaries

cards.front: What three different things did the rebel barons at Runnymede want, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Customary law of Henry I over feudal incidents / Personal redress for royal extortion / A constitutional principle that the king is under the law
items: Customary law of Henry I over feudal incidents
A constitutional principle that the king is under the law

cards.front: Why did John destroy the south-east tower of Rochester Castle during the siege?
cards.answer: His miners undermined the tower and set the timbers alight by burning forty fat pigs in the mine, collapsing the foundation.

cards.front: Why did the rebel barons offer the English throne to Prince Louis of France in 1216?
cards.answer: They had run out of moderate options once the Pope became their enemy, so needed an alternative ruler with continental resources to match John's mercenaries.

title: Questionnaires, Pilot Studies and Cleaning Data
subject: statistics-aqa

cards.front: Name the five key features to consider when designing a good questionnaire.
cards.answer: Leading questions / Avoiding biased sources / Choice of open or closed questions / Interview technique / Time factors
items: Choice of open or closed questions

cards.front: What four purposes does a pilot study serve before the main data collection?
cards.answer: Identifying ambiguous or unclear questions / Checking response categories are exhaustive and mutually exclusive / Estimating how long the questionnaire takes / Revealing leading or loaded language
items: Checking response categories are exhaustive and mutually exclusive
Estimating how long the questionnaire takes

cards.front: Why might asking about sleep habits on a Monday give misleading results?
cards.answer: Answers on a Monday reflect weekend sleep patterns, so they differ from typical mid-week sleep, biasing the data.

cards.front: Why does excluding non-respondents from analysis risk biasing the results?
cards.answer: If the people who didn't respond share a characteristic, excluding them makes the remaining data unrepresentative.

cards.front: Name the five central themes of The Empress covered in this lesson.
cards.answer: Empire and exploitation / Identity and belonging / Belonging and exclusion (then and now) / Racism / Gender / Resistance and agency

cards.front: Name the three gendered vulnerabilities the lesson gives for the ayahs.
cards.answer: Employed as carers, traditionally female work / More economically dependent on employers / Danger of being women alone in a foreign country
items: Employed as carers, traditionally female work
Danger of being women alone in a foreign country

cards.front: Why does Gupta present the ayahs as sources of strength, not just victims?
cards.answer: Their solidarity, mutual care, and cultural practices represent a specifically female form of resistance to oppression.

cards.front: Why do strong essay answers on The Empress need to range across the whole play?
cards.answer: Because the most common mistake is writing about only one part, so answers should cover different acts and characters to show breadth.

cards.front: Name the remaining animal-to-real-world mappings in Animal Farm (not counting Old Major, Napoleon, Snowball, Squealer, Boxer or Moses)
cards.answer: Benjamin = cynical intellectuals / Mollie = the bourgeoisie / the dogs = secret police (NKVD) / the sheep = citizens who repeat propaganda / Mr Jones = Tsar Nicholas II / Frederick = Hitler, Pilkington = Western powers
items: The sheep = citizens who repeat propaganda

cards.front: Why does Napoleon ban the song 'Beasts of England' once he consolidates power?
cards.answer: Because the song represented the original revolutionary dream, and keeping it alive would expose how far the new reality had fallen from that promise.

cards.front: Why does Napoleon let Moses stay and give him a daily ration of beer?
cards.answer: It parallels Stalin rehabilitating the Russian Orthodox Church in WWII, showing totalitarian regimes co-opt any institution that helps maintain control.

cards.front: How does the repeated destruction and rebuilding of the windmill support Orwell's message about promises of a better future?
cards.answer: Each cycle costs the animals more suffering while delivering less benefit, showing the promised future never actually arrives for ordinary citizens.

title: Ethics in Daily Life: Precepts and Perfections
subject: religious-studies-aqa

cards.front: Name the six qualities that make up the Mahayana Six Perfections.
cards.answer: Generosity (dana) / Morality / Patience (khanti) / Energy/Diligence (viriya) / Meditation (dhyana) / Wisdom (prajna)

cards.front: Why do most Theravada Buddhists extend the first Precept beyond just not killing humans?
cards.answer: Because all beings experience suffering (dukkha), so harming any sentient being contradicts the Buddhist path, linking the Precept to karuna.

cards.front: Why is kamma not the same as fate, according to Buddhist teaching?
cards.answer: Intentional actions create conditions for the future, but the practitioner retains free will to choose wisely in each moment.

cards.front: Name the four poems in the Conflict anthology that explore social conflict and identity.
cards.answer: Half-caste (Agard) / No Problem (Zephaniah) / The Class Game (Casey) / Belfast Confetti (Carson)

cards.front: Why does Agard write Half-caste without punctuation or standard capitalisation?
cards.answer: The rejection of conventional English grammar mirrors his rejection of the social conventions that label him "half."

cards.front: How does the form of Belfast Confetti reflect the effect of the violence on the speaker?
cards.answer: The poem's fragmented form, with interrupting dashes, mirrors the fragmentation of the speaker's mind and city caused by the violence.

cards.front: Why does Agard use colloquial Caribbean dialect instead of standard English in Half-caste?
cards.answer: Using standard English would mean accepting the hierarchy that labels him as inferior, so his dialect becomes an act of resistance.

cards.front: Why did the USA fear South Vietnam's collapse under the domino theory?
cards.answer: Because if South Vietnam fell to communism, neighbouring states like Laos, Cambodia and Thailand might follow.

cards.front: Why did Diem's anti-Buddhist policies weaken his government in 1963?
cards.answer: They triggered large-scale protests, adding to unpopularity from his authoritarian, corrupt rule in rural areas.

cards.front: Why did the USA feel unable to abandon South Vietnam by the mid-1960s?
cards.answer: Having pledged to defend South Korea, abandoning South Vietnam would signal US security guarantees could not be trusted.

cards.front: Name the four methods the lesson gives for preventing rusting.
cards.answer: Galvanising (zinc coating) / Painting / Oiling / Using a sacrificial metal

cards.front: Name the four common alloys the lesson describes and what metals each contains.
cards.answer: Steel: iron + carbon / Bronze: copper + tin / Brass: copper + zinc / Gold alloys: gold + silver or copper
items: Gold alloys: gold + silver or copper

cards.front: Why does the solution turn from blue to pale green when iron is added to copper sulfate solution?
cards.answer: Iron displaces copper, forming pale green iron(II) sulfate solution while copper metal is deposited on the iron.

cards.front: Why is limestone added to a blast furnace during iron extraction?
cards.answer: Limestone removes acidic silicon dioxide impurities by reacting with them to form calcium silicate slag, which is tapped off separately.

cards.front: Name the four rules the lesson gives about magnetic field lines.
cards.answer: Run from north to south outside the magnet / Closer lines mean a stronger field / Strongest at the poles, weakens with distance / Field lines never cross
