cards.answer: Her cruelty to Tracey mirrors how she herself has been treated by her own parents.

cards.front: Name the three drawbacks of cloud computing given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Depends on a reliable internet connection / Charges an ongoing subscription / Raises concerns about data security
items: Depends on a reliable internet connection

cards.front: Name the three benefits of organising protocols into layers.
cards.answer: Different teams can develop different layers / A layer can be improved or replaced without breaking others / Faults are easier to track down
items: Different teams can develop different layers
A layer can be improved or replaced without breaking others
Faults are easier to track down

cards.front: Why does a network slow down as more devices connect to it at once?
cards.answer: All the connected devices must share the same fixed bandwidth, so each one gets a smaller share and runs slower.

cards.front: Why is a wired connection generally more secure than a wireless one?
cards.answer: An intruder needs physical access to the cable to intercept a wired connection, whereas wireless signals are easier to intercept.

cards.front: Name the five advantages of social media given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Good way to stay in touch / Can share photos and experiences / Useful for studying / Allows you to meet people from other countries / Entertaining and fun
items: Good way to stay in touch
Allows you to meet people from other countries

cards.front: Name the six disadvantages of social media given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Can be addictive / Cyberbullying is a serious problem / Wastes a lot of time / Can affect mental health / There are privacy risks / People share an unrealistic image of their life
items: People share an unrealistic image of their life

cards.front: Why is the conjunction 'aunque' useful when discussing social media for higher marks?
cards.answer: It lets you show contrast in one complex sentence, e.g. social media is useful for staying in touch although it can be addictive.

cards.front: Why does the verb 'seguir' catch students out in the exam?
cards.answer: It is irregular in the present tense, changing to sigo, sigues, sigue instead of following the regular pattern.

title: Ethical and Legal Issues in Digital Technology
subject: computer-science-aqa

cards.front: Name the six technologies explicitly named in this topic on ethical and privacy issues.
cards.answer: Mobile technologies / Wireless networking / Cloud storage / Wearable technologies / Computer-based implants / Autonomous vehicles

cards.front: Name the three categories of offence covered by the Computer Misuse Act 1990.
cards.answer: Unauthorised access to computer material / Unauthorised access with intent to commit further offences / Unauthorised acts that damage or disrupt a computer
items: Unauthorised access with intent to commit further offences
Unauthorised acts that damage or disrupt a computer

cards.front: Why is it illegal for a 'white hat' security researcher to probe a system without permission?
cards.answer: Probing a system without permission is illegal regardless of intent, since only defined legal agreements make such access authorised.

cards.front: How can wireless networking put your personal data at risk?
cards.answer: Public Wi-Fi can be monitored, poorly secured home routers expose devices, and unencrypted data transmitted over networks can be intercepted.

cards.front: Name the three sections the Amidah prayer is divided into.
cards.answer: Praise of God (three opening blessings) / Petitions (thirteen blessings) / Thanksgiving (three closing blessings)

cards.front: Name the two most significant differences between Orthodox and Reform synagogues.
cards.answer: The role of women / The language of prayer

cards.front: Why is the Amidah shortened on Shabbat and festivals?
cards.answer: The thirteen petitions are replaced with a single blessing for the special holiness of the day, shortening the service.

cards.front: Why are musical instruments not used in Orthodox services on Shabbat?
cards.answer: Playing instruments is not permitted on the day of rest, so Orthodox services use unaccompanied cantorial singing (chazanut).

title: The arrival and immediate impact of the Black Death
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the six factors the lesson gives for why the Black Death spread so fast in England.
cards.answer: Population density in towns / Poor sanitation / Trade routes and pilgrim roads / Monasteries and hospitals concentrating the sick / Malnutrition among poorer peasants / No understanding of how disease spread
items: Monasteries and hospitals concentrating the sick
No understanding of how disease spread

cards.front: Why did monasteries and hospitals, meant to help the sick, actually speed up the spread of plague?
cards.answer: They concentrated infected people together in one place, which inadvertently accelerated transmission of the disease.

cards.front: Why did the combination of bubonic and pneumonic plague make the epidemic so hard to stop?
cards.answer: Bubonic spread via fleas and rats while pneumonic spread through the air without needing them, so the epidemic had virtually no natural brake.

cards.front: Why did religious responses to the Black Death, such as mass prayer gatherings and pilgrimages, often make things worse?
cards.answer: They brought large numbers of people together, which may have actively spread the disease further.

cards.front: Why does Benedick's opening soliloquy in Act 2, Scene 3 create dramatic irony?
cards.answer: He mocks men who become fools for love, just before he himself falls for the same trick and is tricked into loving Beatrice.

cards.front: How does Shakespeare reveal that Benedick's hostility to love was really a defence mechanism?
cards.answer: His instant switch to accepting love once told Beatrice loves him shows the feelings were already there, hidden behind his mockery.

cards.front: Name the four character pairs (foils) Dickens sets up in the novel.
cards.answer: Joe vs Magwitch / Estella vs Biddy / Miss Havisham vs Magwitch / Compeyson vs Magwitch

cards.front: Why does Dickens give Joe uneducated, dialect speech while giving polished language to characters like Pumblechook and Jaggers?
cards.answer: To show that linguistic sophistication does not equal moral superiority — Joe's grammar is poor but his values are faultless.

cards.front: Why does Dickens make Pip sympathetic despite his selfishness and snobbery?
cards.answer: Because his flaws are understandable: a child humiliated by class prejudice internalises that prejudice and becomes what he hates.

cards.front: Name the three means of salvation the lesson identifies.
cards.answer: Law / Grace / Spirit

cards.front: Give the three different understandings of atonement described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Substitutionary atonement / Satisfaction theory / Moral example

cards.front: How does the Holy Spirit help Christians live a holy life, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: It guides them to recognise sin, turn to God, resist temptation, brings comfort, strengthens faith and empowers them to share the gospel.

cards.front: Why do some liberal Christians see Jesus's death as a 'moral example' rather than a payment for sin?
cards.answer: They see it as a supreme act of self-sacrificing love that inspires Christians to live selflessly for others.

title: Earth's Resources: Water, Pollution and Sustainability
subject: separate-sciences-ocr

cards.front: Name the four stages of sewage treatment described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Screening / Primary sedimentation / Biological treatment / Final clarification and sterilisation

cards.front: Name the four ways the lesson says chemistry contributes to sustainable development.
cards.answer: Higher atom economy processes / Renewable and biodegradable materials / Improved recycling technology / More energy-efficient production routes

cards.front: Why is chlorine used more commonly than ozone or UV light for sterilising UK drinking water?
cards.answer: Chlorine is effective, relatively cheap, and its residual effect keeps killing bacteria as water travels through the distribution network, unlike ozone or UV.

cards.front: Why must industrial waste water receive specialised treatment before release?
cards.answer: It may contain heavy metals or toxic organic compounds that need specific treatment before being safely released.

cards.front: What three things does the lesson say unite all Christian views on visions despite differing on channels and authority?
cards.answer: God can communicate with humans / Debate is about the channels used / Debate is about authority they carry
items: Debate is about the channels used
Debate is about authority they carry

cards.front: Why do Humanists say belief in miracles can be harmful?
cards.answer: It encourages people to reject medicine and science in favour of prayer and superstition.

cards.front: How do Christians respond to Hume's argument against miracles?
cards.answer: They say it assumes the conclusion before examining evidence and would dismiss real but surprising historical events.

cards.front: Name the three quenching media used in hardening, and the order of their cooling speed.
cards.answer: Brine (fastest) / Water / Oil (slowest)

cards.front: List the three shared stages of all heat-treatment processes for carbon steel.
cards.answer: Heat to soaking temperature / Hold at temperature (soaking) / Cool at a controlled rate

cards.front: Why does slow furnace cooling in annealing produce a softer, more ductile metal than air cooling?
cards.answer: Slow cooling gives atoms time to form large, coarse grains with very few dislocations, maximising ductility.

cards.front: Why must full through-hardening be avoided for a gear tooth?
cards.answer: It would make the tooth too brittle to withstand bending loads, so it would snap rather than deform.

title: Themes: Family, Truth, Identity and Love
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: Name the four children whose monologues open each season in Things I Know to Be True.
cards.answer: Rosie in Berlin / Pip in the garden / Mark in the gum tree / Ben remembering his parents dancing

cards.front: Why does the connecting-hands staging moment matter to the family theme?
cards.answer: The family joins hands at the exact same instant, showing they stay connected however far apart they scatter.

cards.front: Why is Fran's secret bank account significant to the truth-telling theme?
cards.answer: She kept it secretly so she would know she could leave Bob if she ever needed to.

cards.front: How does Bovell use dramatic irony around Bob's comment about Mark becoming a woman?
cards.answer: Bob names becoming a woman as the one thing that would shock them, not realising this is exactly what is about to happen.

cards.front: Name the four rivers of the Underworld mentioned in the lesson.
cards.answer: Styx / Acheron / Lethe / Phlegethon

cards.front: Name the three regions the judges sent souls to in the Underworld.
cards.answer: Elysium / Asphodel Meadows / Tartarus

cards.front: Why did Heracles seek initiation into the Eleusinian Mysteries before his labour to capture Cerberus?
cards.answer: He sought initiation to prepare himself for entering Hades' kingdom while still alive, linking his myth to the Demeter cult.

cards.front: How does Ovid's portrayal of Hades and Persephone weeping in the Orpheus story show a Roman humanised Underworld?
cards.answer: Ovid shows the Underworld as responsive to emotion, with Hades and Persephone weeping and Tartarus's punishments pausing, a Roman touch.

cards.front: Name the five types of German secondary/primary school mentioned in the lesson.
cards.answer: das Gymnasium / die Realschule / die Hauptschule / die Gesamtschule / die Grundschule

cards.front: Name the three modal verbs the lesson gives for expressing school rules with 'man'.
cards.answer: man muss / man soll / man darf

cards.front: Why does the word order change in 'In der Pause esse ich in der Kantine' compared to starting with the subject?
cards.answer: Because of verb-second word order: starting with a time phrase forces the subject and verb to swap places.

cards.front: Why is school uniform a good discussion topic for German exam tasks, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Because German students don't wear school uniform, so you can compare the British and German systems.

cards.front: What four physical adaptations does regular physical activity cause to the body, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Improved cardiovascular fitness / Increased muscular strength and endurance / Improved flexibility / Improved body composition

cards.front: Why can sports like gymnastics, rowing or wrestling contribute to disordered eating?
cards.answer: Because pressure to achieve a particular body image for weight or aesthetic judging can push athletes towards unhealthy eating habits.

title: The EM Spectrum and its Risks
subject: separate-sciences-ocr-b

cards.front: Name the three essential properties shared by all EM waves.
cards.answer: Transfer energy / Can travel through a vacuum (no medium needed) / Travel at the same speed in a vacuum
items: Can travel through a vacuum (no medium needed)
Travel at the same speed in a vacuum

cards.front: Name the four types of non-ionising EM radiation.
cards.answer: Radio waves / Microwaves / Infrared / Visible light

cards.front: Why can intense microwave beams still cause harm even though microwaves are non-ionising?
cards.answer: Very intense microwave beams can heat body tissue, even though normal exposure levels are low risk.

cards.front: Why is the small risk from a single chest X-ray considered acceptable?
cards.answer: The risk of DNA damage from one chest X-ray is far smaller than the risk of missing an undiagnosed lung condition.

title: Film Music: Writing About an Unfamiliar Cue and Composing to a Brief
subject: music-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four musical choices the lesson suggests for scoring a chase scene.
cards.answer: Fast tempo / Driving string or brass ostinato / Syncopated rhythms / Gradual crescendo and thickening texture

cards.front: Why does the opening semitone ostinato in the Jaws theme sound unsettling?
cards.answer: Because it uses a narrow, repetitive interval played quietly in low strings and tuba, creating dread through simplicity and repetition.

cards.front: How does the Psycho shower scene cue create terror using only strings?
cards.answer: High shrieking violin figures use rapid repeated bowing and sharp accents to imitate stabbing, over dissonant, tightly-spaced harmony.

cards.front: Why should a film music answer describe features stage by stage rather than as a list?
cards.answer: Because describing the time-course shows understanding of the whole cue's journey, not just isolated random details.

cards.front: Name the three chemical weathering processes described in the lesson, each with the mineral they affect.
cards.answer: Hydrolysis breaks down feldspar / Carbonation dissolves calcite / Oxidation affects iron-bearing minerals

cards.front: Name the five sediment transport environments described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Screes / Rivers / Shallow seas / Deep seas / Wind (aeolian) dunes

cards.front: Why does freeze-thaw action break rock apart?
cards.answer: Water in a crack expands about 9% when it freezes, exerting pressure on the crack walls until the rock fragments.

cards.front: Why is wind transport more effective at rounding grains than water transport?
cards.answer: Air provides less cushioning between colliding grains than water, so wind-blown grains round faster over shorter distances.

title: Contemporary UK Film: Aesthetic Style in Focus
subject: film-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Name the five contemporary UK films studied for aesthetic style, with their aesthetic category.
cards.answer: Submarine - indie/art-house / Attack the Block - genre/urban science fiction / Skyfall - blockbuster spectacle / Rocks - social realism / Blinded by the Light - musical drama
items: Attack the Block - genre/urban science fiction
Blinded by the Light - musical drama

cards.front: What four aesthetic choices in the Rocks school-corridor scene create its social-realist feel?
cards.answer: Natural light / Handheld camera / Semi-improvised performance / Retention of imperfect dialogue

cards.front: How does the handheld, following camera in Rocks's corridor scene affect the spectator's experience?
cards.answer: It moves with the girls rather than ahead of them, placing the spectator behind the action so it feels like watching something happening rather than performed.

cards.front: How does the Born to Run lyric-overlay sequence in Blinded by the Light show the protagonist's inner experience?
cards.answer: Song lyrics are superimposed as floating typographic text on screen, making his interior emotional response to the music visible rather than just heard.

title: India and Punjab: Raga, Tala and Bhangra Rhythms
subject: music-ocr

cards.front: Name the three ornamentation techniques the lesson gives for decorating raga melodies.
cards.answer: Meend (smooth slide between pitches) / Gamak (rapid oscillation around a note) / Microtonal inflections

cards.front: Name the three core instrumental roles of Indian Classical music described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Sitar / Tabla / Tanpura

cards.front: Why do skilled performers delay their arrival at the sam in a tala cycle?
cards.answer: To build tension through exciting cross-rhythms and syncopation before landing together in a satisfying moment of resolution.

cards.front: How did British Asian communities transform bhangra from the 1980s onwards?
cards.answer: They fused traditional dhol chaal rhythms with Western instruments and technology like electric guitars, synths, drum machines and samples.

title: Staging and Design: Bringing Salem to the Stage
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: Name the four design areas a designer uses to bring The Crucible to the stage.
cards.answer: Set design / Lighting design / Sound design / Costume design

cards.front: Name the four lighting stages in the sequence for Proctor's torn confession moment in Act 4.
cards.answer: Cold blue-grey wash / Warm amber gobo on hands / Sudden white light from above / Fade to warm light on Elizabeth
items: Fade to warm light on Elizabeth

cards.front: Why might a designer place Danforth on a raised platform in the Act 3 courtroom scene?
cards.answer: Placing the judge higher than everyone else communicates his power spatially, trapping the accused between him above and the audience in front.

cards.front: Why is the off-stage drum in Act 4 considered a design masterstroke?
cards.answer: The audience never sees the executions, only hears the drum's approach, so their imagination fills in what the stage doesn't show.

cards.front: Name the five elements of a strong sales process.
cards.answer: Product knowledge / Speed and efficiency of service / Customer engagement / Responses to customer feedback / Post-sales service

cards.front: Why can defective products still reach customers even when a business uses quality control?
cards.answer: Quality control relies on sampling rather than checking every item, so defects can be missed by the sample.

cards.front: Why is quality assurance described as an investment rather than just a cost?
cards.answer: Because the cost of winning back a lost customer is far higher than the cost of keeping a satisfied one.

title: Collectivisation and the Attack on the Kulaks
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: What were Stalin's three aims for collectivisation?
cards.answer: Feed the cities reliably / Fund industrialisation by exporting grain / Break peasant resistance to Bolshevik rule
items: Break peasant resistance to Bolshevik rule

cards.front: What were the three categories kulaks were divided into by the Politburo in January 1930?
cards.answer: Shot or sent to labour camps / Deported to Siberia, the Urals or Kazakhstan / Expelled from villages and resettled on poor land
items: Shot or sent to labour camps
Deported to Siberia, the Urals or Kazakhstan
Expelled from villages and resettled on poor land

cards.front: Why did Stalin abandon the New Economic Policy in 1927–28?
cards.answer: Peasants withheld grain at low state prices during the procurement crisis, and the NEP could not fund industrialisation on a peasant market economy.

cards.front: Why did Soviet livestock numbers collapse during collectivisation?
cards.answer: Many peasants slaughtered their animals rather than surrender them to the new collective farms.

title: Contraception, Divorce, Gender Equality and Discrimination
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three examples of artificial contraception the lesson gives as forbidden by Catholic teaching.
cards.answer: The contraceptive pill / Condoms / Sterilisation

cards.front: Name the three groups the lesson gives whose views on contraception differ from Catholic teaching.
cards.answer: Most Protestant denominations / Situation ethics (Joseph Fletcher) / Humanists and atheists

cards.front: How do most Protestant churches justify ordaining women as priests?
cards.answer: They argue equality in Christ (Galatians 3:28, 'neither male nor female') outweighs the argument from historical practice.

cards.front: How would situation ethics argue that divorce and remarriage can be the right choice?
cards.answer: If a marriage has irretrievably broken down causing suffering, the most loving course is separation and freedom to remarry.

title: Waves: Properties, Types & the Electromagnetic Spectrum
subject: science-edexcel

cards.front: Name the seven types of wave in the electromagnetic spectrum, in order from longest to shortest wavelength.
cards.answer: Radio waves / Microwaves / Infrared / Visible light / Ultraviolet / X-rays / Gamma rays

cards.front: Name the seven colours of the visible spectrum, in order from longest to shortest wavelength.
cards.answer: Red / Orange / Yellow / Green / Blue / Indigo / Violet

cards.front: How does watching a floating object on water show that waves transfer energy without transferring matter?
cards.answer: The object bobs up and down as waves pass but does not move forward, showing water particles oscillate without travelling with the wave.

cards.front: Why can a glass prism split white light into the visible spectrum?
cards.answer: Different colours (wavelengths) of light are refracted by different amounts as they cross the boundary into the glass.

cards.front: Name the three tones the lesson gives for Tennyson, Owen and Hardy in these war poems.
cards.answer: Tennyson: elevated, heroic register / Owen: bleak, cold and despairing / Hardy: conversational and darkly ironic

cards.front: How does Owen's use of hallucination show the soldiers' state in Exposure?
cards.answer: Soldiers hallucinate about home ('Slowly our ghosts drag home'), suggesting they are already psychologically dead.

cards.front: Why does the repeated 'because' sound unconvincing in The Man He Killed?
cards.answer: The speaker repeats 'because' as though he does not believe his own reasoning for killing a stranger.

cards.front: How does Hardy's simple ballad form affect the impact of The Man He Killed's subject matter?
cards.answer: The neat, deceptively simple ballad stanzas contrast with the killing, making the moral complexity more shocking.

cards.front: Name the four ways of displaying quantitative data given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Frequency table / Bar chart / Histogram / Scatter diagram

cards.front: Name the three types of pattern a scatter diagram can show.
cards.answer: Positive correlation / Negative correlation / No correlation

cards.front: Why is the median a better measure of the 'typical' result than the mean when outliers are present?
cards.answer: Because the median ignores extreme scores, whereas the mean uses every value and gets pulled off target.

cards.front: Why should a calculated mean be rounded to a sensible number of significant figures rather than given with many decimal places?
cards.answer: Because excessive decimal places imply a false level of accuracy that the data doesn't actually support.

title: Eschatology and the Problem of Evil
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: The lesson gives three ways Christians interpret the nature of hell. What are they?
cards.answer: Eternal conscious punishment / Final annihilation of the unrepentant / Universal salvation (universalism)

cards.front: Name the three divergences between Christianity and Islam on life after death given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Purgatory / Nature of salvation / The Trinity

cards.front: Why does the existence of evil create a logical problem for belief in God?
cards.answer: Because an omnipotent God could prevent suffering and a benevolent God would want to, yet suffering still exists.

cards.front: Why does the free will defence not fully explain suffering?
cards.answer: Because it only accounts for moral evil caused by human choices, leaving natural evil like earthquakes and disease unexplained.

cards.front: Name the four Spanish daily meals given in the lesson, in order through the day
cards.answer: el desayuno (breakfast) / la comida (lunch) / la merienda (afternoon snack) / la cena (dinner)

cards.front: Name the three Latin American cultural traditions the lesson describes
cards.answer: la quinceañera / el carnaval / la sobremesa

cards.front: Why do many shops and businesses in Spain still close between about 2pm and 5pm?
cards.answer: Because of the tradition of the siesta, an afternoon rest taken after lunch, especially in southern Spain.

cards.front: Why is Spanish dinner usually later and lighter than in the UK?
cards.answer: Because lunch is the main meal in Spain, so dinner around 9-10pm is a smaller, later meal by comparison.

cards.front: Why does the French King agree to all of Henry's terms in the Treaty of Troyes?
cards.answer: Because of the military defeat at Agincourt, not because Henry's wooing of Katherine won him over.

cards.front: Why does Shakespeare include the English-French language barrier in the wooing scene?
cards.answer: It generates comic confusion but also symbolises the gap between political reality and genuine personal connection.

title: The Marketing Mix and the Four Ps
subject: cambridge-nationals-enterprise-and-marketing

cards.front: Name the four pricing strategies a small business typically uses.
cards.answer: Competitive pricing / Psychological pricing / Price skimming / Penetration pricing

cards.front: What three key product decisions does a start-up need to make?
cards.answer: What exactly are we offering? / What makes it different from rivals? / What quality level will we aim for?
items: What makes it different from rivals?
What quality level will we aim for?

cards.front: How does psychological pricing make a product feel cheaper than it is?
cards.answer: It sets the price just below a round number, such as £9.99 instead of £10.00.

cards.front: Why is starting online and adding physical presence later a sensible approach for a start-up with limited capital?
cards.answer: Physical premises have high fixed costs like rent, rates and utilities, while digital channels are cheaper to set up, making online-first lower risk.

title: Print Advertisements: Quality Street and NHS 111
subject: media-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three persuasive language techniques the lesson identifies in the Quality Street advert's text.
cards.answer: Alliteration / Emotive language / Superlatives

cards.front: Name the three class levels the Quality Street advert layers, from lowest to highest.
cards.answer: The two women / The man in the suit / The Regency characters in the gold frame
items: The Regency characters in the gold frame

cards.front: Why does the gold frame around the man and product in the Quality Street advert create a halo effect?
cards.answer: The gold frame acts as anchorage, elevating the product to something special and linking it to the brand's history.

cards.front: Why is the father positioned as the hero of the NHS 111 advert's narrative?
cards.answer: His dominance in the frame casts him as the hero on a quest to find help, with the NHS framed as the helper.

cards.front: Name the three places in The Woman in Black where Hill repeatedly uses fog to build atmosphere.
cards.answer: At the causeway / At the funeral / Around Eel Marsh House

cards.front: Name the three most terrifying moments in the novel that Hill makes purely auditory (heard, not seen).
cards.answer: The pony and trap drowning ('sucking, churning') / The child's cry / The rocking chair bumping
items: The pony and trap drowning ('sucking, churning')

cards.front: Why does Arthur choose to write his story down rather than tell it aloud on Christmas Eve?
cards.answer: Writing gives him control to shape the story, but also suggests the memory is too painful to speak.

cards.front: Why does learning about the curse later in the novel make Arthur's earlier sightings of the woman more frightening?
cards.answer: Knowing that seeing her means a child will die retrospectively turns each earlier sighting into evidence a child may already have died.

cards.front: Name the five ways a business can respond when competition intensifies.
cards.answer: Cut prices / Improve quality / Widen product range / Improve customer service / Target a different market niche

cards.front: Name the three primary research methods entrepreneurs use to find out about competitors.
cards.answer: Visiting competitor premises / Purchasing their products / Speaking to customers who have used them
items: Speaking to customers who have used them

cards.front: Why did streaming services force traditional DVD rental companies out of business?
cards.answer: They could not adapt quickly enough to the new competition from streaming services.

cards.front: How did Greggs respond to competition from premium artisan bakeries?
cards.answer: It accelerated its value positioning and expanded its range with the vegan sausage roll, rather than trying to become premium.

title: Eschatological Beliefs: Death, Judgement and the Afterlife
subject: religious-studies-ocr

cards.front: Name the three views on the nature of hell described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Conscious eternal separation from God / Annihilation (ceasing to exist) / Universalism (all reconciled to God)

cards.front: Why did Paul insist resurrection is essential to Christian faith in 1 Corinthians 15?
cards.answer: Because if Christ did not rise, then 'your faith is futile', so belief in the afterlife depends on his resurrection.

cards.front: Why does Matthew 25:31-46 show that judgement is based on actions rather than religious profession?
cards.answer: Because Jesus identifies himself with the poor, saying whatever was done for 'the least of these' was done for him, so judgement is ethical.

cards.front: Why does Ruth constantly copy behaviour she has seen on TV at the Cottages?
cards.answer: The clones have no genuine models for adult life, so they construct identities from fragments of popular culture to feel human.

cards.front: Why does Ruth manoeuvre herself into a relationship with Tommy at the Cottages?
cards.answer: Partly because she genuinely cares for him, and partly to stop Kathy from having him.

title: Immune System, Vaccination and Treating Disease
subject: science-ocr-b

cards.front: Name the three ways antibodies destroy pathogens once they bind to antigens.
cards.answer: Agglutination (clumping pathogens together) / Neutralising toxins released by bacteria / Opsonisation (tagging pathogens for destruction)

cards.front: Name the four stages a new drug goes through before it can be licensed.
cards.answer: Preclinical testing on cells and animals / Phase 1 trial / Phase 2 trial / Phase 3 trial
items: Preclinical testing on cells and animals

cards.front: Why does the flu vaccine need updating regularly?
cards.answer: Different strains of flu virus have different surface antigens, so old vaccines no longer match new strains.

cards.front: How does opsonisation help the immune system destroy pathogens?
cards.answer: Antibodies tag the pathogen, marking it so other immune cells cannot miss it and can destroy it.

title: User Groups & Who Participates in Sport
subject: cambridge-nationals-sport-studies

cards.front: Name the twelve user groups recognised in sport participation.
cards.answer: Gender / Ethnic minorities / Retired people and people over 60 / Families with children / Carers / Young children / Teenagers / People with disabilities / Single parents / People who work full-time / Unemployed people / Economically disadvantaged

cards.front: What specific barriers can affect participation for people from ethnic minorities?
cards.answer: Cultural expectations / Language differences / Lack of visible role models / Discrimination

cards.front: Why do families with children often struggle to take part in sport together?
cards.answer: It's hard to find sports all family members enjoy that fit school, childcare and work schedules, and cost of kit, fees and travel adds up.

cards.front: Why does grassroots participation remain low for people with disabilities despite Paralympic inspiration?
cards.answer: Physical access to facilities, specialist coaching and adapted equipment are all critical factors that are often lacking.

cards.front: According to the lesson, what four benefits of physical activity apply specifically to children?
cards.answer: Skill development / Bone density / Socialisation through team sport / Building lifelong habits

cards.front: According to the lesson, what four benefits of physical activity apply specifically to older adults?
cards.answer: Bone density maintenance (reducing osteoporosis risk) / Managing Type 2 diabetes / Reducing loneliness / Maintaining mobility and posture

cards.front: How does regular aerobic exercise reduce the risk of coronary heart disease?
cards.answer: It strengthens the heart muscle, increases stroke volume and improves blood vessel elasticity, reducing fatty deposits narrowing the coronary arteries.

cards.front: How does exercise help the body manage stress physiologically?
cards.answer: It uses up the raised heart rate and glucose from the stress response, releases serotonin and endorphins, and lowers baseline cortisol over time.

title: Place and the Integrated Marketing Mix
subject: business-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four Ps of the marketing mix.
cards.answer: Product / Price / Promotion / Place

cards.front: Why do physical products like furniture or fresh food often benefit from selling through a retailer rather than an e-tailer?
cards.answer: Customers want to see, touch or try these products before buying, which a retailer allows.

cards.front: Why might a premium chocolate brand selling through a budget supermarket need to change its product packaging?
cards.answer: Because the packaging might look cheap next to discount products, undermining the brand image.

title: Poem for My Love — June Jordan
subject: english-literature-ocr

cards.front: Why does Jordan write the poem's opening questions without question marks?
cards.answer: It makes them read as statements of wonder rather than genuine doubt, as if the speaker already knows the answer.

cards.front: Why does the poem's thirteen-line form (one short of a sonnet) suit its theme of love as 'possibility'?
cards.answer: It echoes the sonnet's link with love poetry while refusing to complete the shape, matching love that feels unfinished.

cards.front: How do the poem's shifting pronouns affect who seems to be speaking?
cards.answer: They unsettle who is speaking and being spoken to, widening the poem beyond a single private exchange.

cards.front: Why does the poem's uncertain addressee help it work as a love poem for any reader?
cards.answer: Since nobody knows who it addresses, it stands as a general love poem rather than a private message to one person.

title: Power and Authority: Weber's Three Types
subject: sociology-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four formal agencies of social control mentioned in the lesson.
cards.answer: Police / Courts / Prison system / Schools

cards.front: Name the three informal agencies of social control mentioned in the lesson.
cards.answer: Family / Peer groups / Media

cards.front: How do functionalists view legitimate authority in society?
cards.answer: They see it as a functional necessity for social order, with authority structures serving the common good rather than one group's interests.

cards.front: Why do feminists argue authority structures are patriarchal?
cards.answer: Both traditional authority (inherited male power) and rational-legal authority (laws once denying women votes and jobs) maintained male dominance.

title: Earthquakes in Contrasting Wealth: Nepal & New Zealand
subject: geography-aqa

cards.front: Name the four secondary effects of the Nepal 2015 earthquake given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Avalanches killed 19 climbers / Nearly 8 million people affected / 3 million made homeless / Cholera and dysentery outbreaks in camps
items: Cholera and dysentery outbreaks in camps

cards.front: Name the three long-term responses to the Christchurch earthquake given in the lesson.
cards.answer: CERA set up to coordinate rebuild / Central business district demolished and rebuilt to higher standards / Building code reviewed and tightened / Earthquake education in schools strengthened
items: CERA set up to coordinate rebuild
Central business district demolished and rebuilt to higher standards

cards.front: Why did the CTV building in Christchurch kill so many people despite New Zealand's strict building codes?
cards.answer: It was built in the 1980s but later investigation found design flaws, showing codes only work if enforced and inspected.

cards.front: Why was Nepal's death rate so much higher than Christchurch's even though the size difference only partly explains it?
cards.answer: Building quality was the bigger reason: brick and mud-mortar buildings collapsed while flexible reinforced concrete and timber-frame buildings survived.

cards.front: Name the four deities (other than the Tri-murti) that the lesson says students should know.
cards.answer: Ganesha (remover of obstacles) / Lakshmi (wealth and prosperity) / Hanuman (devotion and service) / Saraswati (learning and wisdom)

cards.front: How does maya cause living beings to misunderstand reality?
cards.answer: Maya causes living beings to mistake the temporary physical world for their true eternal self.

cards.front: Why is Hanuman seen as a model for Hindu devotees?
cards.answer: His total dedication to Rama shows Hindus what it means to love and serve God completely.

cards.front: What four things should each paragraph include in an essay on the extract and whole novel?
cards.answer: A point about Doyle's presentation / A quotation from extract or novel / Analysis of language or structure / A contextual link
items: A quotation from extract or novel

cards.front: Why does Holmes reach for cocaine when Watson announces his engagement?
cards.answer: This juxtaposition shows Holmes is indifferent to love and highlights what each character values and lacks.

cards.front: Name the four types of Tollington characters Syal uses to portray 1960s working-class life.
cards.answer: Nosy neighbours / The local hard man / The neglected children / Well-meaning but clueless white liberals

cards.front: Name the three things the Kumar family represents about the immigrant experience, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Papa's quiet dignity / Mama's cultural preservation / Nanima's traditional wisdom

cards.front: Why does Syal use an unreliable child narrator in Anita and Me?
cards.answer: To create humour, dramatic irony, and emotional depth in the novel.

cards.front: How does Meena's narration create dramatic irony about racism in the novel?
cards.answer: Because of her limited child's understanding, the reader often understands more than Meena about the racism and social tensions around her.

title: Demand on the Biosphere: Food, Water & Energy
subject: geography-edexcel-b

cards.front: Name the four forces the lesson gives for rising demand on the biosphere.
cards.answer: Population growth / Rising affluence / Urbanisation / Industrialisation

cards.front: Give the three examples the lesson uses to support Boserup's theory that population pressure drives innovation.
cards.answer: Medieval shift from two-field to three-field crop rotation / The Green Revolution from the 1960s / Modern precision agriculture (GPS tractors, drip irrigation)
items: Medieval shift from two-field to three-field crop rotation
Modern precision agriculture (GPS tractors, drip irrigation)

cards.front: Why did the Aral Sea dry up?
cards.answer: Soviet planners diverted its two feeder rivers to irrigate cotton fields, so the eastern lobe had dried up completely by 2014.

cards.front: Why is global water demand rising twice as fast as population growth?
cards.answer: Because of meat-rich diets, more factories in industrialising countries, and longer showers in wealthier households.

cards.front: Name the five non-destructive testing (NDT) methods described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Visual inspection / Dye penetrant testing / Ultrasonic testing / Radiographic testing / Magnetic particle inspection

cards.front: Name the three measuring instruments used in quality control mentioned in the lesson.
cards.answer: Vernier caliper / Micrometer / Depth gauge

cards.front: Why do tighter tolerances increase manufacturing cost?
cards.answer: They require more precise machines, more frequent tooling changes and slower cutting speeds.

cards.front: Why is Charpy impact testing critical for offshore and arctic structures?
cards.answer: Low temperatures reduce toughness in many steels, so Charpy testing checks materials will still absorb impact energy safely in the cold.

cards.front: Name the three things Jeanette loses when she leaves home and the church.
cards.answer: Her community / Her identity within the church / Her relationship with her mother

cards.front: Why does Jeanette's mother put her out of the house?
cards.answer: She frames Jeanette's sexuality as demonic, saying she's 'not havin' demons here,' so refuses to let her stay.

cards.front: Why does Winterson refuse to give the novel a neat, triumphant ending?
cards.answer: Because real life doesn't offer resolution — identity is a process, not a destination, so Jeanette is still becoming herself.

title: Montgomery 1955-56: The Boycott That Made King
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: What three demands did the MIA vote to continue the boycott for?
cards.answer: Courteous treatment by drivers / First-come first-served seating with no white-only section / Hiring of Black drivers on Black-majority routes
items: First-come first-served seating with no white-only section
Hiring of Black drivers on Black-majority routes

cards.front: Name the four hardships the lesson says the boycott's discipline survived.
cards.answer: Christmas / Winter rain / Indictments under a 1921 anti-boycott law / The firebombing of King's house

cards.front: Why was Martin Luther King Jr., a newcomer to Montgomery, elected MIA president?
cards.answer: He had a doctorate and a strong preaching voice, but crucially, as a recent arrival, he had few enemies in the city.

cards.front: Why did the Civil Rights Act 1957 fail to bring real change despite being historic?
cards.answer: Lyndon Johnson stripped out its enforcement powers to get past Southern Democratic opposition, so Black voter registration did not move.

cards.front: Name the three false expectations Pip's whole life had been built on.
cards.answer: Miss Havisham was not his patron / He was never intended to marry Estella / His gentleman status was funded by a convict
items: Miss Havisham was not his patron
He was never intended to marry Estella
His gentleman status was funded by a convict

cards.front: Name the three people who attempted to smuggle Magwitch out of England by rowing down the Thames.
cards.answer: Pip / Herbert / Startop

cards.front: Why did Magwitch fund Pip's transformation into a gentleman?
cards.answer: He wanted to prove that even a convict could produce something 'fine', not to gain anything for himself.

cards.front: Why is the failed escape attempt significant in showing Pip's moral growth?
cards.answer: Pip acts selflessly for the first time, caring about saving Magwitch the man rather than the fortune he stands to lose.

title: Elizabeth, Spain and the new world
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Name the three stages of the English attack on the Armada described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Harried up the Channel / Fireships caused panic off Calais / Attacked scattered ships at Gravelines

cards.front: Why did England end up in conflict with Spain by the 1560s?
cards.answer: Religious conflict between Catholic Philip II and Protestant Elizabeth combined with commercial rivalry over Atlantic trade routes.

cards.front: Why did the Spanish Armada lose so many ships trying to return to Spain?
cards.answer: It tried to sail home around Scotland and Ireland, and storms wrecked many ships on that route.

cards.front: How did attacking Spanish treasure fleets help England's war against Spain?
cards.answer: It disrupted the money supply funding Philip II's armies in the Netherlands and his plans to invade England.

cards.front: Name the four states OAPEC named as targets of its 1973 oil embargo.
cards.answer: United States / Netherlands / Portugal / South Africa

cards.front: Name the three effects on Western economies caused by the 1973 oil price shock.
cards.answer: Petrol queues at American gas stations / UK's three-day working week / Fall in Western European industrial output
items: Petrol queues at American gas stations
Fall in Western European industrial output

cards.front: Why did the 1973 oil shock make US administrations more willing to pressure Israel into negotiations?
cards.answer: It caused Western recession, US petrol queues and Britain's three-day week, showing the conflict could hurt the whole world economy.

cards.front: Why was Israel able to invade Lebanon in 1982 without fearing a two-front war?
cards.answer: The 1979 treaty removed Egypt, the largest Arab army, from any future war, so Syria alone could not open a southern front.

cards.front: Name the three euphemisms guardians use to soften the clones' fate.
cards.answer: "Donations" instead of organ harvesting / "Completions" instead of death / "Carers" instead of accomplices

cards.front: Name the three items students traded for at the Hailsham Sales.
cards.answer: Cassette tapes / Jumpers / Ornaments

cards.front: Why does Ishiguro present Kathy's memories of Hailsham with such nostalgia?
cards.answer: So readers share her affection for Hailsham, making the later revelation of its true purpose more devastating.

cards.front: Why does Tommy start creating tiny, intricate animal drawings after learning the Gallery's purpose?
cards.answer: He hopes proving he has a soul through art might earn him a deferral from his donations.

cards.front: Name the five key contextual areas the lesson gives for analysing Blood Brothers.
cards.answer: 1980s Liverpool deindustrialisation / The class system / Russell's working-class background / Housing policy and slum clearance / Russell's purpose as social commentary

cards.front: Name the three sections of a strong Blood Brothers essay's main body, in order.
cards.answer: Opening/Act 1 paragraph / Middle/Development paragraph / Climax/Ending paragraph

cards.front: Why should context be woven into analysis rather than written as a separate paragraph?
cards.answer: A separate context paragraph earns few marks; context must be embedded into analytical paragraphs to score well.

cards.front: How should you use the quotation given at the top of an essay question?
cards.answer: Engage with it as a springboard and reference it, then range across the whole play rather than ignoring it.

cards.front: Name the four purposes the lesson gives for memory-based narration.
cards.answer: Creates authenticity by mimicking real memory / Allows delayed revelation of key facts / Reflects Kathy's psychological state / Creates dramatic irony as readers piece clues together
items: Creates authenticity by mimicking real memory
Allows delayed revelation of key facts
Creates dramatic irony as readers piece clues together

cards.front: How does the novel's three-part structure mirror the clones' lives?
cards.answer: Each part narrows their freedom, from Hailsham's protection to the Cottages' false freedom to the donation cycle's inevitability.

cards.front: Why does Ishiguro use emotionally restrained narrators in both Never Let Me Go and The Remains of the Day?
cards.answer: To create devastating effects through understatement, forcing readers to feel emotions the narrator cannot express.

cards.front: Name the four settings in Coram Boy and what each represents, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Ashbrook House – privilege and tradition / Open roads – lawlessness and danger / Foundling Hospital – institutional care, safety without love / London – opportunity and anonymous cruelty
items: Foundling Hospital – institutional care, safety without love

cards.front: Name the four characters whose perspectives the omniscient narrator moves between in Coram Boy.
cards.answer: Meshak – bewildered, emotional viewpoint / Otis – cold, calculating mind / Alexander – conflicted ambition / Aaron – search for identity

cards.front: How does the dual timeline structure work as a structural argument about class?
cards.answer: By separating the privileged Ashbrook world from the foundling world, it forces the reader to see how class divides keep intimately connected people apart.

cards.front: Why does Gavin use Gothic elements when depicting the buried babies?
cards.answer: They stop the reader distancing themselves emotionally, forcing them to feel the horror of child trafficking rather than just understand it intellectually.

cards.front: According to the lesson, what four problems does holding too much stock cause?
cards.answer: Ties up capital / Occupies warehouse space / Risks obsolescence / Masks inefficiencies in production

cards.front: Name the four advantages of JIT manufacturing given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Reduced warehousing costs / Lower capital tied up in stock / Reduced risk of obsolescence or damage / Ability to respond quickly to demand changes
items: Lower capital tied up in stock
Reduced risk of obsolescence or damage
Ability to respond quickly to demand changes

cards.front: Why does JIT manufacturing work best in stable, predictable production environments?
cards.answer: Because JIT relies on excellent supplier relationships, accurate demand forecasting and a disciplined production schedule to avoid stoppages.

cards.front: How does reducing movement waste improve manufacturing performance?
cards.answer: Redesigning workstation layouts to cut unnecessary movement of people improves operator productivity and reduces the risk of injury.

cards.front: What three types of argument does Mrs Lyons use to persuade Mrs Johnstone to give up a twin?
cards.answer: Practical logic: a better life / Emotion: she'll see him every day / Guilt: too many children already
items: Emotion: she'll see him every day

cards.front: Why is Mrs Lyons presented as Mrs Johnstone's foil?
cards.answer: She contrasts in wealth, class and temperament, highlighting the power imbalance between them.

cards.front: Why does Mrs Johnstone find it almost impossible to refuse Mrs Lyons's request for a twin?
cards.answer: Mrs Lyons's wealth makes her Mrs Johnstone's employer, and the class dynamic gives her power over her.

cards.front: How does the Narrator's ambiguous identity contribute to the play's sense of tragedy?
cards.answer: By never clarifying if he is character, chorus, fate or the devil, Russell shows forces characters cannot escape.

cards.front: Name the four main reasons the lesson gives for the rise in divorce since 1945.
cards.answer: Legal change (Divorce Reform Act 1969) / Secularisation / Changing social attitudes and rising expectations of marriage / The changing status of women
items: Changing social attitudes and rising expectations of marriage

cards.front: Name the five main consequences of divorce given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Financial hardship, particularly for women / Social isolation, particularly for men / Impacts on children's educational and health outcomes / Disruption of extended family relationships / Increase in lone parent families
items: Impacts on children's educational and health outcomes

cards.front: Why do men tend to experience greater social isolation after divorce?
cards.answer: They are less likely to have primary care of children and may have weaker social networks.

cards.front: Why might divorce sometimes be better for children than staying in an unhappy marriage?
cards.answer: Some research suggests parental conflict, not divorce itself, is the key factor affecting children's outcomes.

title: Early Government Policy and the Permanent Indian Frontier
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the four hammer blows the lesson gives for why the Permanent Indian Frontier collapsed in the 1840s.
cards.answer: Pioneer migration on Oregon/California Trails from 1841 / Manifest Destiny doctrine / 1846 Oregon Treaty and 1848 Mexican Cession land gains / 1848 California Gold Rush
items: Pioneer migration on Oregon/California Trails from 1841
1846 Oregon Treaty and 1848 Mexican Cession land gains

cards.front: Name the five nations forced off their lands under the Indian Removal Act.
cards.answer: Cherokee / Chickasaw / Choctaw / Creek / Seminole

cards.front: Why did the 1848 California Gold Rush undermine the Permanent Indian Frontier?
cards.answer: It sent about a quarter of a million migrants overland, carving trails through 'Indian country' that killed buffalo and spread cholera into Plains camps.

cards.front: Why is the 1851 Fort Laramie Treaty described as a move to 'concentration' rather than a genuine peace policy?
cards.answer: It stripped vast territory from nations who had not lost a war and forced them into areas defined by Washington, not true peace.

cards.front: Name the four pricing strategies a start-up needs to know.
cards.answer: Competitive pricing / Psychological pricing / Price skimming / Penetration pricing

cards.front: Why might a very low price make a handmade product feel untrustworthy?
cards.answer: Because price acts as a signal of quality, so an extremely low price suggests the product lacks craft or care.

cards.front: What choice does a business face if its raw material costs rise?
cards.answer: It must absorb the cost, reduce its profit margin, or pass the cost on to customers through a price rise.

cards.front: Name the three separation techniques the lesson gives for separating mixtures.
cards.answer: Filtration / Distillation / Chromatography

cards.front: Why does adding a glowing splint to a gas confirm it is oxygen?
cards.answer: The splint relights because oxygen supports combustion.

cards.front: Why does bubbling carbon dioxide through limewater make it turn milky?
cards.answer: Calcium carbonate, which is insoluble, precipitates when carbon dioxide reacts with the calcium hydroxide.

cards.front: Why must you acidify with dilute nitric acid before testing for halide ions with silver nitrate?
cards.answer: To prevent interference from carbonate or sulfate ions giving a false precipitate.

cards.front: Name the three types of experiment covered in the lesson.
cards.answer: Laboratory experiment / Field experiment / Natural experiment

cards.front: Name the five non-experimental research methods the lesson describes.
cards.answer: Interviews / Questionnaires / Case studies / Observations / Correlations

cards.front: Why do field experiments have higher ecological validity than laboratory experiments?
cards.answer: Behaviour is observed in a natural setting and participants are often unaware they are being studied, reducing demand characteristics.

cards.front: Why are natural experiments useful for studying situations like extreme deprivation?
cards.answer: They allow research into situations that would be unethical or impossible for a researcher to manipulate deliberately.

cards.front: Name the four dative article changes the lesson gives for use with two-way prepositions.
cards.answer: der becomes dem / das becomes dem / die becomes der / die (plural) becomes den + n

cards.front: Why do two-way prepositions take the dative case when describing where furniture is in a room?
cards.answer: Because you are describing location, not movement, so the two-way preposition takes the dative case.

cards.front: Why is the gender of a German room word like 'Schlafzimmer' always 'das'?
cards.answer: Because in a compound noun the gender is always determined by the last word, and 'Zimmer' is 'das'.

cards.front: Name the three zones a Greek temple typically consisted of.
cards.answer: Pronaos (entrance porch) / Cella (inner chamber with cult statue) / Opisthodomos (rear porch, often used as treasury)
items: Opisthodomos (rear porch, often used as treasury)

cards.front: Name the three architectural orders Greek architects developed.
cards.answer: Doric / Ionic / Corinthian

cards.front: Why could Roman temples only be entered from the front, unlike Greek temples?
cards.answer: They stood on a high podium with a frontal staircase as the only entry, fitting their role in a forum where the frontal view mattered most.

cards.front: How does the Roman Composite capital combine features of other orders?
cards.answer: It blends Ionic volutes with Corinthian acanthus leaves, reflecting Roman architects' boldness in mixing the different orders.

title: Interactionist Theory of Crime: Becker and Labelling
subject: sociology-aqa

cards.front: According to Becker, name the three factors the lesson says decide whether a deviant label sticks to someone.
cards.answer: Social characteristics of the actor (class, ethnicity, age, gender) / Discretion of those with formal power (police, teachers, courts) / The social context of the act
items: Social characteristics of the actor (class, ethnicity, age, gender)
Discretion of those with formal power (police, teachers, courts)
The social context of the act

cards.front: Name the three criticisms of labelling theory given by the lesson's Key Fact box.
cards.answer: Marxists: doesn't explain why labels fall on the working class / Feminists: gender shapes labelling and its consequences / Not everyone labelled accepts or acts on the label
items: Marxists: doesn't explain why labels fall on the working class
Feminists: gender shapes labelling and its consequences
Not everyone labelled accepts or acts on the label

cards.front: How can being given a master status lead to a self-fulfilling prophecy?
cards.answer: Rejection from jobs, education and conventional networks makes conventional life harder, so the person identifies with the label and joins deviant groups.

cards.front: According to Heidensohn's chivalry thesis, why might female offenders be treated more leniently by the criminal justice system?
cards.answer: Because they conform to feminine stereotypes, though women who deviate from expected gender roles may be judged more harshly.

title: Components of Fitness and Fitness Tests
subject: physical-education-ocr

cards.front: Name the four components of fitness the lesson says a 100 m sprinter needs.
cards.answer: Reaction time / Power / Speed / Muscular endurance

cards.front: Why is cardiovascular endurance less important for a 100 m sprinter than for a marathon runner?
cards.answer: Because the race duration is too short for the aerobic system to be the limiting factor.

cards.front: Why does simply naming a fitness component without justification fail to earn full marks?
cards.answer: You must name the component, define it, and give a sport-specific reason why it matters for that activity.

cards.front: Name the four main Anglo-Saxon earldoms by the 1060s.
cards.answer: Wessex / Mercia / Northumbria / East Anglia

cards.front: Name the five levels of the Anglo-Saxon social hierarchy, from top to bottom.
cards.answer: King / Earls / Thegns / Ceorls / Slaves

cards.front: Why did Anglo-Saxon kings need to maintain good relationships with their earls?
cards.answer: Kings who lost the support of their leading nobles could face rebellion or even deposition.

cards.front: Why did the Church encourage freeing slaves in Anglo-Saxon England?
cards.answer: Freeing slaves was considered an act of piety by the Church.

cards.front: Name the three structural patterns Hill establishes in Chapters 1-4 of The Woman in Black.
cards.answer: Warning and dismissal / Approach and retreat / Sensory intensification

cards.front: Why is the church almost empty at Mrs Drablow's funeral?
cards.answer: It emphasises Mrs Drablow's isolation and the town's fear of anything connected to Eel Marsh House.

cards.front: Why does Hill use the townspeople's refusal to speak about Eel Marsh House?
cards.answer: Their silence signals a secret too terrible to name, building suspense before Arthur ever arrives there.

cards.front: How does the frame narrative create dramatic irony from the opening pages?
cards.answer: We see the older Arthur unable to tell his story, so we know his cheerful younger self's confidence will be destroyed.

title: Life After Death and the Seven Sacraments
subject: religious-studies-aqa

cards.front: What are the four key elements of Catholic belief about life after death?
cards.answer: Resurrection of the whole person / Personal and Last Judgement / Heaven with God / Purgatory before heaven

cards.front: Why do most Protestants reject the Catholic doctrine of purgatory?
cards.answer: They believe it lacks clear biblical basis and that Christ's atoning death is fully sufficient, so no further purification is needed.

cards.front: Why is purgatory not considered a 'second chance' at salvation in Catholic teaching?
cards.answer: Those in purgatory are already saved and in a state of grace, but undergo purification to prepare for the full joy of heaven.

cards.front: Why do Baptist and evangelical Christians insist on believer's baptism rather than infant baptism?
cards.answer: They see baptism as an outward sign of inward faith that must be freely chosen by a believing adult, not a grace-conferring sacrament.

cards.front: Name the three ideological positions shared by Nazi Germany, fascist Italy and militarist Japan.
cards.answer: Opposed parliamentary democracy / Opposed communism / Opposed 'international finance'

cards.front: Why was Britain reluctant to confront Germany over the Rhineland in March 1936?
cards.answer: Britain was preoccupied with the Abyssinian Crisis and its public leaned toward accepting a 'reasonable' settlement after memories of 1914-18.

cards.front: Why did the loss of the demilitarised Rhineland weaken France's alliance system in eastern Europe?
cards.answer: Without the buffer zone, France could no longer credibly threaten to march into Germany to defend Czechoslovakia or Poland.

cards.front: Why did the British claim that Germany was 'only going into its own back garden' miss the strategic point?
cards.answer: The zone existed not because the land was disputed but to stop German forces attacking France or threatening its eastern allies.

title: Social and cultural effects of the Crusades on Europe
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four channels through which the Crusades affected European society, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Italian trading cities supplying Outremer / The translation movement bringing Arabic/Greek knowledge to universities / Spread of new words and goods through trade / Hardening of religious attitudes (antisemitism and anti-heretic crusades)
items: The translation movement bringing Arabic/Greek knowledge to universities
Spread of new words and goods through trade
Hardening of religious attitudes (antisemitism and anti-heretic crusades)

cards.front: Name the four Rhineland towns whose Jewish communities were massacred in 1096.
cards.answer: Speyer / Worms / Mainz / Cologne

cards.front: Why did the Italian maritime cities grow so wealthy from the Crusades?
cards.answer: They supplied crusader armies with ships, supplies and finance, gaining in return trading concessions like city quarters and tax exemptions in Outremer.

cards.front: Why could crusading ideology that demonised Muslims also lead to violence against Jewish communities in Europe?
cards.answer: The rhetoric of holy war used against Muslims in the Holy Land could easily be redirected toward Jewish minorities living in European towns.

title: Why Food is Cooked and Heat Transfer
subject: food-preparation-and-nutrition-aqa

cards.front: What three families does the lesson group cooking methods into?
cards.answer: Water-based methods / Dry methods / Fat-based methods

cards.front: According to the lesson, what three factors does nutrient loss during cooking depend on?
cards.answer: Temperature / Cooking time / Whether the food is submerged in water
items: Whether the food is submerged in water

cards.front: Why do dry cooking methods like baking and roasting produce more browning than water-based methods?
cards.answer: Because no water is present, browning reactions such as dextrinisation and caramelisation occur more readily, improving colour and flavour.

cards.front: Why does the top of grilled bread toast and brown before the underside does?
cards.answer: Infrared radiation from the glowing element travels downward, heating the top surface directly, while the underside stays pale until turned.

cards.front: Name the six topics OCR states are NOT part of the mental preparation topic.
cards.answer: Arousal and the inverted-U theory / Information processing models / Personality types / Aggression types / Motivation types / Contract to compete

cards.front: What five stages does a diver mentally rehearse in sequence before a dive?
cards.answer: Approach / Hurdle step / Take-off / Tuck position / Entry

cards.front: Why is selective attention closely linked to imagery and positive thinking?
cards.answer: A performer who has clearly imaged the task and has a positive script has less cognitive space for distractions to fill.

cards.front: How does unchallenged negative thinking affect a performer's performance?
cards.answer: It reduces confidence, tightens muscles, narrows attention unhelpfully, and can trigger a self-fulfilling prophecy of poor performance.

cards.front: Name the five fight-or-flight changes adrenaline triggers in the body.
cards.answer: Heart rate increases / Breathing rate increases / Blood diverted from gut to muscles / Glycogen converted to glucose for energy / Pupils dilate
items: Blood diverted from gut to muscles
Glycogen converted to glucose for energy

cards.front: Name the four non-hormonal methods of contraception described.
cards.answer: Condoms / Diaphragms / Copper IUDs / Surgical sterilisation

cards.front: How does negative feedback keep thyroxine levels stable?
cards.answer: High thyroxine makes the pituitary reduce TSH, lowering thyroxine; low thyroxine makes it increase TSH, raising thyroxine.

cards.front: How do hormonal contraceptives like the pill prevent pregnancy?
cards.answer: They maintain high oestrogen and/or progesterone levels, which inhibit FSH production so no egg matures and ovulation doesn't occur.

cards.front: Name the three structural systems that dominate modern construction.
cards.answer: Cellular construction / Rectangular frame construction / Portal frame construction

cards.front: Name the five loads (besides its own weight) a building's structure must carry.
cards.answer: People / Furniture / Wind / Snow / Soil pressure

cards.front: Why can removing a load-bearing wall in a cellular building cause collapse?
cards.answer: The wall carries the floor and roof loads above it, so removing it transfers that load to elements not designed to bear it, risking collapse.

cards.front: How do rigid knee joints let a portal frame span large distances without intermediate supports?
cards.answer: Rigid joints make the frame act as a single unit, allowing rafters to be smaller than a simply supported beam and span long distances.

cards.front: By October 1917, name the five groups the lesson says had abandoned the Provisional Government, and why.
cards.answer: Liberals alienated by leftward coalition / Conservatives alienated by denunciation of Kornilov / Soldiers alienated by failed June Offensive / Peasants alienated by postponed land reform / Workers alienated by inflation and bread queues
items: Conservatives alienated by denunciation of Kornilov
Soldiers alienated by failed June Offensive
Peasants alienated by postponed land reform
Workers alienated by inflation and bread queues

cards.front: Name the three things the lesson gives for why Bolshevik membership surged in 1917.
cards.answer: 'Peace, Land, Bread' slogan matched demands / Order Number 1 committees became recruiting grounds / Kornilov Affair won over workers and soldiers
items: Order Number 1 committees became recruiting grounds
Kornilov Affair won over workers and soldiers

cards.front: How did Order Number 1 end up dissolving discipline in the Russian army at the front?
cards.answer: Soldiers formed committees, refused to attack and voted on obeying orders, leaving officers stripped of authority, sometimes shot.

cards.front: Why did the Kadet-dominated Provisional Government insist on keeping Russia in the First World War?
cards.answer: They believed Russia's honour and Western alliances required victory, and wanted Tsarist war aims like control of Constantinople.

title: The North-South Divide & the UK in the Wider World
subject: geography-aqa

cards.front: Name the four strategies the lesson gives for resolving the north-south divide.
cards.answer: Northern Powerhouse / Devolution deals / Enterprise zones / Levelling Up Fund

cards.front: Name the four areas through which the UK's global links run, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Trade / Culture / Transport links / Political links

cards.front: Why did deindustrialisation hit the north, Midlands, south Wales and central Scotland hardest?
cards.answer: Because that is where coal, steel and shipbuilding industries were concentrated.

cards.front: Why does the EU still matter to UK trade even after Brexit?
cards.answer: It is the closest large market and supply chains built up over forty years cannot easily be redirected.

title: Act 2: Geof, Helen's Return & the Ending
subject: english-literature-aqa

cards.front: Why does Delaney present Geof's everyday domestic tasks as a form of love?
cards.answer: His mundane, unglamorous care — folding nappies, cooking, tidying — is shown as the closest thing to genuine love Jo has experienced since the Boy left.

cards.front: Why is Geof's departure described as the play's cruellest structural repetition?
cards.answer: It repeats the cycle of abandonment: just as the Boy left Jo then Helen failed her, Jo does not fight hard enough to keep Geof, so the one caring relationship is destroyed.

cards.front: How does Delaney use Jo and Geof's household to question what 'family' means?
cards.answer: Helen is Jo's biological mother but fails at every maternal duty, while Geof has no blood tie yet provides care, stability and selfless love.

cards.front: Name the two homophobic insults Helen and Peter use against Geof to question his fitness to be around a child.
cards.answer: An arty little freak / A bloody little pansy

title: The Falklands War and the Miners' Strike
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the five factors the lesson gives for why the miners lost the 1984-85 strike.
cards.answer: Meticulous government preparation with coal stockpiles / Unprecedented police coordination / No national ballot removed legal protection / Nottinghamshire miners kept working, dividing the union / NUM funds sequestrated by courts
items: Meticulous government preparation with coal stockpiles
No national ballot removed legal protection
Nottinghamshire miners kept working, dividing the union

cards.front: Why did Galtieri think Britain would not respond militarily to the Falklands invasion?
cards.answer: He calculated that Britain, with a Conservative government cutting defence spending, would not fight to retake distant islands.

cards.front: How did the Falklands victory affect Thatcher's political standing before the 1983 election?
cards.answer: It transformed her from an unpopular, poll-trailing leader into a national hero, boosting Conservative support dramatically.

cards.front: Why was the Argentine invasion of the Falklands controversial for Britain to respond to militarily?
cards.answer: The sinking of the General Belgrano on 2 May, killing 323, was the most controversial act of the conflict.

cards.front: Name the four character relationships the lesson uses to link to key themes.
cards.answer: Meena and Anita: belonging vs authenticity / Meena and her parents: maintaining culture in a hostile environment / Meena and Nanima: heritage's power to heal / Meena and Sam: racism destroying trust and belonging
items: Meena and Anita: belonging vs authenticity
Meena and her parents: maintaining culture in a hostile environment
Meena and Nanima: heritage's power to heal
Meena and Sam: racism destroying trust and belonging

cards.front: Name the three mistakes Meena makes on her journey to belonging.
cards.answer: Follows Anita into cruelty / Rejects her parents' values / Fails to see the love around her
items: Fails to see the love around her

cards.front: Why does Syal present Papa's dignified response to racism as costly as well as admirable?
cards.answer: Because he absorbs insults he should not have to tolerate, choosing dignity over anger despite the personal cost.

cards.front: How does Nanima manage to communicate with Meena despite not speaking English?
cards.answer: She communicates through touch, gesture, food, and storytelling instead of shared language.

cards.front: Name the three categories of emigrant from the British Isles (1688–c.1730).
cards.answer: Voluntary settlers / Indentured servants / Transported prisoners

cards.front: Why did indentured servants completing their term contribute to colonial instability, as shown by Bacon's Rebellion (1676)?
cards.answer: Freed servants often could not obtain promised land grants, creating a large class of frustrated, landless free men.

cards.front: How did the experience of transported prisoners differ from voluntary settlers in the colonies?
cards.answer: Transported prisoners had no choice of destination, no legal protections, no resources, and faced hard labour as punishment.

cards.front: What four hardware considerations should you check through when selecting hardware for an HCI scenario?
cards.answer: Display (size and touch type) / RAM / Storage / Processing power

cards.front: What are the four screen size categories described, from smallest to largest?
cards.answer: Smartwatch (1–2 inches) / Smartphone (5–7 inches) / Laptop/desktop (13–34 inches) / Smartboard (55–86 inches)

cards.front: Why are LCD screens less energy-efficient than OLED screens?
cards.answer: LCD screens need a backlight to produce an image, while OLED pixels light themselves, using less power.

cards.front: Why do hover states used on desktop menus become irrelevant on a capacitive touchscreen?
cards.answer: Because users interact by direct finger touch rather than a mouse cursor, so there is no equivalent to hovering.

cards.front: Name the four softwood species described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Scots pine / Spruce / Larch / Western red cedar

cards.front: Name the six main types of manufactured board listed in the lesson.
cards.answer: Plywood / MDF / Chipboard / Blockboard / Hardboard / OSB

cards.front: Why must freshly felled (green) timber be seasoned before use?
cards.answer: Green timber has high moisture content and shrinks unevenly as it dries, causing warping, splitting and joint failure.

cards.front: Why is tropical hardwood deforestation considered environmentally damaging?
cards.answer: It destroys biodiversity hotspots, displaces indigenous communities and releases stored carbon.

cards.front: Name the three revision strategies the lesson gives for preparing for the anthology comparison essay.
cards.answer: Quotation cards / Comparison grids / Practice under timed conditions

cards.front: What three things should you decide during the 5-minute planning stage before writing the comparison essay?
cards.answer: Note three comparative points / Choose quotations from both poems / Decide your evaluative conclusion

cards.front: Why should you prepare 3-4 flexible pairings of poems before the exam?
cards.answer: Because the exam names one poem and you choose the comparison, so pairings ready in advance guarantee a strong comparison whatever is named.

cards.front: Why does the lesson say speed in the exam comes from knowing your quotations well?
cards.answer: Because if you already know what to quote, you only need to think about how to use it, saving time.

title: Energy Resources and the Domestic Power Equation
subject: separate-sciences-edexcel

cards.front: What four factors should you consider when comparing energy resources?
cards.answer: Reliability / Environmental impact / Cost / Scalability

cards.front: Name the four main disadvantages of nuclear power given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Radioactive waste storage / High construction costs / High decommissioning costs / Public perception of safety risk

cards.front: Why does using more variable renewables like wind and solar make it harder for the National Grid to balance supply and demand?
cards.answer: Their output depends on weather and daylight rather than demand, so energy storage like pumped-storage hydro is needed to balance supply.

cards.front: Why is hydroelectric power considered highly reliable and able to meet peaks in demand?
cards.answer: Water stored behind a dam can be released to drive turbines whenever extra electricity is needed.

cards.front: Name the four responsibilities of the contracts manager and site manager together.
cards.answer: Coordinate construction site activities / Manage progress and run site meetings / Organise labour, plant and materials / Responsible for health and safety and worker welfare
items: Manage progress and run site meetings
Responsible for health and safety and worker welfare

cards.front: Why does the balance of professional involvement shift once construction begins on site?
cards.answer: The contracts manager and site manager take the lead running the site, while the architect and engineer only make periodic quality-check visits.

cards.front: Why is holding chartered status important for an individual professional if a project goes wrong?
cards.answer: It shows they followed accepted standards and codes of conduct, which matters greatly in legal proceedings.

cards.front: What four consequences does the flag cause across the first four stanzas of 'Flag'?
cards.answer: Brings a nation to its knees / Makes the guts of men grow bold / Dares the coward to relent / Will outlive the blood you bleed
items: Brings a nation to its knees
Makes the guts of men grow bold
Will outlive the blood you bleed

cards.front: What four settings does the flag appear in as the poem escalates from stanza to stanza?
