cards.answer: The pronoun goes before the infinitive instead of before the conjugated verb.

cards.front: Name the six key features of the citadel of Mycenae listed in the lesson.
cards.answer: Lion Gate with lioness relief / Grave Circle A with gold treasures / Palace and megaron at the summit / Cyclopean walls up to twelve metres high / Sally port for covert exits / Underground passage to a cistern
items: Grave Circle A with gold treasures
Palace and megaron at the summit
Cyclopean walls up to twelve metres high

cards.front: Name the four features Mycenae and Tiryns share according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Cyclopean walls / A palace with a megaron / A controlled entrance ramp exposing attackers' right side / Grave monuments nearby
items: A controlled entrance ramp exposing attackers' right side

cards.front: Why was the site of Mycenae chosen for the citadel?
cards.answer: It was defensible, visible, and close to routes linking the Peloponnese to the rest of mainland Greece.

cards.front: Why does the Lion Gate relief show no human figures, gods or battle scenes unlike Egyptian or Mesopotamian art?
cards.answer: It makes its statement through symbol and scale alone rather than narrative imagery.

title: Shabbat, Home Worship and Sacred Texts
subject: religious-studies-aqa

cards.front: What are the five key elements of Shabbat home observance named in the lesson?
cards.answer: Candle lighting / Kiddush / Challah / Synagogue service / Havdalah

cards.front: Name the three daily prayers observant Jews say, in order.
cards.answer: Shacharit (morning) / Mincha (afternoon) / Ma'ariv (evening)

cards.front: Why does the woman of the household light at least two candles on Friday evening?
cards.answer: The two candles symbolise the two aspects of Shabbat: remembering (zachor) and keeping (shamor).

cards.front: Why is the Torah seen as the most authoritative section of the Tenakh?
cards.answer: It is believed to have been directly revealed by God to Moses at Sinai, and is the source of the 613 mitzvot.

cards.front: How does the mask releasing Jack's savagery show what really keeps people civilised?
cards.answer: Removing self-consciousness removes the fear of being judged, revealing that civilised behaviour was only ever maintained by that fear.

cards.front: Why is Piggy punched with his glasses broken after his outburst about the ship?
cards.answer: Speaking truth to power is punished with violence, showing reason and intellect being attacked by force.

cards.front: How does Percival Wemys Madison's forgotten name and address show civilisation fading?
cards.answer: His name and address, standard identification linking him to the adult world, is remembered in Chapter 5 but completely forgotten by Chapter 12.

cards.front: Name the three questions Piggy asks the group in Chapter 5 about what they are.
cards.answer: Humans? / Or animals? / Or savages?

cards.front: Name the three selfless actions that prove Darcy's transformation.
cards.answer: Welcoming the Gardiners at Pemberley / Paying Wickham's debts / Arranging Lydia's marriage without seeking credit
items: Arranging Lydia's marriage without seeking credit

cards.front: Name the four contrasting marriages compared in the novel's resolution.
cards.answer: Charlotte and Collins / Lydia and Wickham / Jane and Bingley / Elizabeth and Darcy

cards.front: Why is Mr Bennet's failure to control Lydia called his greatest parental failure?
cards.answer: His detached, ironic parenting style had real consequences, allowing Lydia's reckless elopement that threatened the whole family's reputation.

cards.front: How did Lady Catherine's intervention ironically help Darcy and Elizabeth?
cards.answer: Her report of Elizabeth's defiant refusal to yield encouraged Darcy to propose to Elizabeth again.

cards.front: Why does Napoleon cut off the hens' food rations during their rebellion?
cards.answer: To punish the hens for refusing to surrender their eggs and force them back into obedience, showing the regime starves its own citizens to control them.

cards.front: How does Napoleon respond to the destruction of the windmill in the Battle of the Windmill?
cards.answer: He declares it a 'great victory,' supported by Squealer's propaganda, showing how totalitarian leaders reframe catastrophic defeats as triumphs.

cards.front: Name the six material categories in design given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Papers and boards / Timber-based materials / Metal-based materials / Polymers / Textile-based materials / Electronic and mechanical systems

cards.front: Why did Alec Issigonis design the Mini with a transverse engine and front-wheel drive?
cards.answer: To maximise interior space in a tiny body, responding to the Suez fuel crisis's demand for a small, fuel-efficient, affordable car.

cards.front: How does Zaha Hadid's use of parametric design and advanced manufacturing affect her buildings and products?
cards.answer: It lets her create fluid, dynamic, curvilinear forms that seem to defy gravity, previously impossible to realise.

cards.front: Name the three main branches of the UK government.
cards.answer: Legislature / Executive / Judiciary

cards.front: What three ceremonial roles does the monarch play in government?
cards.answer: Formally opens Parliament / Gives royal assent to Bills / Invites the PM to form a government
items: Invites the PM to form a government

cards.front: Why is the British constitution described as flexible?
cards.answer: It mixes written laws, historical documents and unwritten conventions, so Parliament can change it simply by passing a new Act.

cards.front: Why can't courts strike down an Act of Parliament in the UK?
cards.answer: Because Parliament is sovereign, holding supreme power to make and unmake any law, which no other body can overrule.

title: Expansion in India: Company to Crown
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the four deeper causes of the 1857 Rebellion given in the lesson, besides the greased cartridges trigger.
cards.answer: Anger at the Doctrine of Lapse / Resentment at evangelical Christian missions / New laws permitting widow remarriage / Annexation of Oudh in 1856
items: Anger at the Doctrine of Lapse

cards.front: Name the three Indian states annexed under Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse between 1848 and 1856.
cards.answer: Satara (1848) / Jhansi (1853) / Nagpur (1854)

cards.front: How did Clive's small army defeat the much larger Nawab's forces at Plassey in 1757?
cards.answer: Clive bribed the Nawab's commander Mir Jafar, who held back his forces, letting Clive's 3,000 men beat 50,000.

cards.front: Why was Warren Hastings impeached after returning to Britain in 1785?
cards.answer: He was accused of corruption for extracting huge sums from the Begums of Oudh and Raja of Benares to pay for war.

title: Smuggling and the Limits of British Authority
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the five types of goods the lesson says were smuggled into the colonies.
cards.answer: Molasses / Tea / Brandy / Wine / Luxury cloth

cards.front: Name the three reasons the lesson gives for why customs collection failed.
cards.answer: Officers were few and underpaid / Juries refused to convict smugglers / Walpole valued colonial markets over enforcement
items: Walpole valued colonial markets over enforcement

cards.front: How did a New England merchant typically evade duties on molasses, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: He bribed the local customs collector with a share of the cargo to falsely certify untaxed French molasses as a legal British import.

cards.front: Why did Walpole tolerate the customs service losing money?
cards.answer: British exports to the colonies grew sharply after 1720, so rising manufactured-goods sales mattered more than lost customs revenue.

cards.front: Why does Viola's disguise as Cesario trap her in an impossible situation?
cards.answer: She falls in love with Orsino who thinks she's a man, while Olivia falls in love with her disguised self.

cards.front: How does Maria's forged letter deceive Malvolio in the subplot?
cards.answer: It is written in Olivia's handwriting and tricks him into believing Olivia loves him, instructing yellow stockings and cross-gartering.

cards.front: Why is the shipwreck described as the play's dramatic catalyst?
cards.answer: It strips Viola of her family, status and female identity, forcing the disguise that creates every comic complication.

title: Stalemate, Armistice and the Cost of Korea
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the three changes in 1953 that broke the deadlock and led to the armistice, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Eisenhower took office and hinted at nuclear weapons / Stalin died in March / Prisoner deadlock broken by neutral commission plan in June
items: Eisenhower took office and hinted at nuclear weapons
Prisoner deadlock broken by neutral commission plan in June

cards.front: Why was a decisive UN advance impossible in Korea after 1951, despite UN technological superiority?
cards.answer: Rugged terrain, dug-in Chinese positions and China's willingness to absorb huge casualties stopped any breakthrough.

cards.front: How did Syngman Rhee try to sabotage the 1953 prisoner deal, and what happened?
cards.answer: He unilaterally released 27,000 anti-communist prisoners, but the US held the line and the deal went ahead.

cards.front: Name the five types of crime psychologists group criminal behaviour into.
cards.answer: Violent crime / Drug-related crime / Acquisitive crime / Sexual offences / Anti-social offences

cards.front: Why might a theory that explains violent crime fail to explain drug-related crime?
cards.answer: Violent crime may stem from a build-up of frustration, while drug-related crime is often linked to addiction or financial pressure instead.

cards.front: Why do psychologists often use official statistics and self-report studies together?
cards.answer: Official statistics give a large-scale reliable picture but miss unreported crime, while self-report studies reveal hidden offending, so combining both builds a fuller picture.

cards.front: Why does the Talmud teach that a wronged person must forgive?
cards.answer: Because once the wrongdoer genuinely seeks forgiveness and makes reparation, the wronged person becomes obligated to forgive.

cards.front: Why do many Quakers register as conscientious objectors instead of fighting?
cards.answer: They believe there is 'that of God' in every person, so killing any human being is always wrong.

cards.front: Why might holding onto resentment be spiritually harmful in Hindu thought?
cards.answer: It may generate negative karma and bind the individual more tightly to the cycle of birth and rebirth (samsara).

cards.front: What three non-combatant roles did many Quakers serve in during the World Wars, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Ambulance units / Hospitals / Farming

cards.front: Name the three main types of single-base mutation described in the lesson. (Higher tier)
cards.answer: Substitution / Insertion / Deletion

cards.front: What are the three possible effects a mutation can have on the protein produced by a gene? (Higher tier)
cards.answer: Harmful / Neutral / Beneficial

cards.front: Why does antibiotic resistance spread through a bacterial population once an antibiotic is introduced?
cards.answer: Random resistance mutations already exist; resistant bacteria survive and reproduce while non-resistant ones die, spreading the trait by natural selection.

cards.front: How can a mutation in a non-coding regulatory region contribute to cancer? (Higher tier)
cards.answer: It can silence a tumour-suppressor gene, reducing the amount of protein made so the cell no longer restrains cell division.

title: Context, User Needs and Design Briefs
subject: design-technology-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four primary research methods the lesson gives for designers gathering first-hand information.
cards.answer: Questionnaires and surveys / Interviews / Observation / Analysis of existing products (disassembly)

cards.front: Name the six areas the lesson says design criteria typically cover in a specification.
cards.answer: Function / User needs / Safety / Materials and manufacturing / Aesthetics / Sustainability

cards.front: Why does a design brief deliberately avoid saying what the solution should look like?
cards.answer: It identifies the user and problem but leaves the solution open for the design process to discover.

cards.front: Why might a portable speaker's design specification be updated after early user testing?
cards.answer: Testing can reveal issues, such as a grip depth too narrow for larger hands, so the specification is refined.

title: Vietnam Before America: France, the Vietcong and the Cold War
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the seven parties that took part in the 1954 Geneva Conference on Vietnam.
cards.answer: France / The Vietminh / The State of Vietnam (Saigon) / The USSR / China / The USA / Britain

cards.front: Why did the French choose to fight at Dien Bien Phu?
cards.answer: They assumed Vietminh artillery could not be brought through the surrounding mountains, so a French garrison supplied by air could crush any attack.

cards.front: Why did Vo Nguyen Giap's forces succeed at Dien Bien Phu despite the French plan?
cards.answer: Thousands of porters disassembled artillery and carried it by bicycle and hand into the hills, with Chinese supplies crossing the border, defeating French assumptions.

cards.front: Why did the USA refuse to intervene directly to save the French at Dien Bien Phu?
cards.answer: Britain refused to support intervention and the US Congress would not authorise unilateral war, so requested airstrikes were declined.

title: Staging and Design: The Flat, the Street and the Band
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: Name the five objects the lesson says do symbolic work across A Taste of Honey.
cards.answer: Flower bulbs / Drink / Hands / Engagement ring / Baby doll

cards.front: What three things does the lesson say every strong design answer for A Taste of Honey must do?
cards.answer: Name a specific moment / Name a specific design element / State the effect on the audience
items: State the effect on the audience

cards.front: Why do sightlines matter when Helen uses direct address?
cards.answer: Every part of the audience needs a clear view of Helen's face during direct address, or the technique loses its force.

cards.front: How does staging configuration change what Helen's direct address can do?
cards.answer: On an end-on stage Helen can address the whole audience as one mass, but on a thrust stage she must turn to sections in turn, making it feel more individually implicated.

cards.front: Name the four limitations of the Florentine Codex as a source for the Nahua perspective, as given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Compiled fifty years after the events / in Spanish colonial conditions / translated and edited by a Spanish friar / informants may have shaped testimony to suit the post-conquest environment
items: Compiled fifty years after the events
Translated and edited by a Spanish friar
Informants may have shaped testimony to suit the post-conquest environment

cards.front: What three things did Cortés's letters to King Charles I emphasise?
cards.answer: Spanish bravery / the justice of the conquest / the need to bring Christianity to the Americas
items: The need to bring Christianity to the Americas

cards.front: Why is Bernal Díaz del Castillo often seen as more reliable than Cortés?
cards.answer: Because he had less to gain from distorting the record than Cortés, who wrote to justify his own expedition.

cards.front: Why do historians debate how far the Nahua voices in the Florentine Codex reflect their true views?
cards.answer: Because Sahagún's aim to convert indigenous people and the changed political context may have shaped what informants said.

cards.front: The lesson gives four reasons why the boarding-school setting works in Never Let Me Go. Name them.
cards.answer: It is enclosed, limiting what the children know / It has authority figures who control information / It is associated with privilege, creating cruel irony / Readers expect enclosed worlds, delaying the horror
items: It is enclosed, limiting what the children know
It has authority figures who control information
It is associated with privilege, creating cruel irony
Readers expect enclosed worlds, delaying the horror

cards.front: What reasons does the lesson give for why the clones in Never Let Me Go don't try to escape?
cards.answer: They have no money / They have no identity documents / They have no knowledge of the outside world / They have internalised their purpose
items: They have no knowledge of the outside world

cards.front: Why does Ishiguro keep the 'normal' humans who benefit from organ donations almost entirely absent from the novel?
cards.answer: By making the clones the most sympathetic characters, he forces readers to confront the ethical questions directly.

cards.front: How does the clones' failure to escape comment on human society more broadly, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: It shows how all humans accept constraining structures like class, work and mortality without questioning them.

cards.front: Name the four key divine attributes given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Omnipotent / Omniscient / Immanent / Transcendent

cards.front: Give the two broad paths the lesson describes for how humans gain knowledge of God.
cards.answer: Special revelation / General revelation

cards.front: Why does Buddhist enlightenment differ from revelation in theistic traditions like Christianity or Sikhism?
cards.answer: The Buddha gained direct insight into the nature of reality himself, rather than receiving a message from a creator God.

cards.front: Why do some religious thinkers argue that the beauty and order of nature is evidence for God?
cards.answer: Many believers hold that nature's beauty and order, such as seasons or the complexity of the cell, communicates something about its creator.

cards.front: What three factors combined to make immigration restriction broadly popular in the 1920s, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Racial prejudice / nativism / Economic anxiety over jobs / Fear of foreign radicals (Red Scare)

cards.front: Why did trade unions like the American Federation of Labor lobby for immigration restrictions after the First World War?
cards.answer: Returning soldiers found immigrants had taken their factory jobs, so unions wanted restrictions to protect wage levels.

cards.front: Why was the trial of Sacco and Vanzetti widely criticised as biased?
cards.answer: Witnesses who gave alibis were dismissed and the judge made prejudicial remarks about their anarchist beliefs and foreign origins.

cards.front: Why did the Palmer Raids target immigrants in particular?
cards.answer: The 1919 bombings were widely blamed on anarchist and communist immigrants, merging fear of radicals with anti-immigration feeling.

title: Establishing Communist Rule and the Korean War, 1949-53
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three parallel hierarchies through which power ran in the new People's Republic.
cards.answer: The CCP under Chairman Mao (set policy) / The State Council under Premier Zhou Enlai (ran government) / The People's Liberation Army (loyal to the party)
items: The CCP under Chairman Mao (set policy)
The State Council under Premier Zhou Enlai (ran government)
The People's Liberation Army (loyal to the party)

cards.front: What three things did the Korean War feed at home in China, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Propaganda (Resist America, Aid Korea campaign) / Repression (campaign against counter-revolutionaries) / Debt (military costs owed to the USSR)
items: Debt (military costs owed to the USSR)

cards.front: How did Mao adapt Marxism-Leninism to fit Chinese conditions?
cards.answer: He made the peasantry the engine of revolution instead of the urban working class, since over 80% of the population worked the land.

cards.front: Why did the Korean War's costs help cause Mao's later break with Khrushchev?
cards.answer: Military costs to the USSR became loans Mao was still repaying in the late 1950s, fuelling resentment and the eventual split.

cards.front: Name the three sources of evidence scientists use to work out what Earth's early atmosphere was like.
cards.answer: Composition of ancient volcanic gases / Chemical signatures in ancient rocks / Comparison with Mars and Venus atmospheres
items: Comparison with Mars and Venus atmospheres

cards.front: List the five gases released by volcanic outgassing that formed Earth's early atmosphere.
cards.answer: Carbon dioxide / Water vapour / Nitrogen / Methane / Ammonia

cards.front: How did rising oxygen levels lead to the formation of the ozone layer?
cards.answer: High-energy UV radiation from the Sun converted some oxygen molecules (O2) into ozone (O3), forming the ozone layer.

cards.front: Why did the ozone layer allow life to colonise the land?
cards.answer: It absorbed most of the Sun's harmful UV radiation, preventing the DNA damage that would otherwise make survival on land very difficult.

title: Dracula and The Lost Boys: Vampires Across Eras
subject: film-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three named sequences from The Lost Boys (1987) suitable for micro-analysis.
cards.answer: The boardwalk-arrival sequence / The cliff-hang gang initiation / The climactic house-fortification finale

cards.front: How does Karl Freund's staircase-descent lighting in Dracula (1931) construct the vampire as 'architectural'?
cards.answer: A single off-axis light source leaves only the steps' edges and a sliver of the figure visible, making Dracula seem part of the castle itself.

cards.front: How does the boardwalk-arrival sequence in The Lost Boys (1987) make the vampire's world seem seductive rather than threatening?
cards.answer: Steadicam movement, saturated neon colours and cuts timed to the rock soundtrack turn the vampire's world into an attractive spectacle, not a static threat.

cards.front: Why is naming a technique without anchoring it to a specific sequence a weak way to answer the comparative-study question?
cards.answer: Without a named sequence the technique cannot support a macro claim about meaning, so the analysis stays vague and unconvincing.

title: The power of the medieval papacy
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four things the medieval Church did in people's daily lives, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Baptised children at birth / Married couples / Heard confessions / Administered last rites at death

cards.front: What three spiritual benefits could a medieval pilgrimage bring?
cards.answer: Earn an indulgence / Demonstrate penance for sins / Strengthen a Christian's faith

cards.front: Why did bishops and abbots hold power beyond their spiritual roles?
cards.answer: They also held land, which made them feudal lords as well as spiritual figures.

cards.front: Why did reports from Jerusalem in the 1070s alarm Western Christians?
cards.answer: Reports said the Seljuk Turks mistreated pilgrims, desecrated churches, and restricted access to the Holy Sepulchre.

cards.front: Name the four paths of yoga the Bhagavad Gita teaches as routes to moksha.
cards.answer: Action (karma yoga) / Knowledge (jnana yoga) / Meditation (astanga yoga) / Devotion (bhakti yoga)

cards.front: Name the four purusharthas (aims of human life) in Hindu teaching.
cards.answer: Dharma (ethical duty) / Artha (material prosperity) / Kama (pleasure and love) / Moksha (liberation)

cards.front: Why does avidya (ignorance) keep the atman trapped in samsara?
cards.answer: Avidya is the mistaken belief that the physical self is the real self, which perpetuates the cycle of rebirth.

cards.front: Why can someone with a lot of harmful karma still reach moksha, according to Hindu teaching?
cards.answer: Karma is not fixed fate; through righteous action, devotion and wisdom a person can change their atman's trajectory.

cards.front: Name the four things the lesson says Emotional weight is carried by in 'Chemistry' rather than explicit statement.
cards.answer: The toy boat / The pond / The meals at the family table
items: The meals at the family table

cards.front: Why does Swift use pathetic fallacy 'in reverse' with the pond in 'Chemistry'?
cards.answer: The still, unchanging pond mirrors grief's frozen quality, contrasting with the turbulent family changes happening above it.

cards.front: How does the narrator's childhood status create tension in the story?
cards.answer: As a child he watches and senses events but cannot act, caught between loyalty to his grandfather and his mother's happiness.

cards.front: Why does the narrator suspect his mother caused the grandfather's death?
cards.answer: She sides with Ralph against her father, and the grandfather becomes marginalised and withdraws before dying, though Swift never confirms this.

cards.front: Name the four steps in treating waste water (sewage treatment).
cards.answer: Screening / Sedimentation / Biological treatment / Final treatment

cards.front: Name the four stages of a product's life assessed in a life cycle assessment.
cards.answer: Extracting raw materials / Manufacturing and packaging / Use / Disposal

cards.front: How does biological treatment clean the effluent during waste water treatment?
cards.answer: Aerobic bacteria break down the organic matter present in the effluent.

cards.front: How does reverse osmosis produce potable water from sea water?
cards.answer: Sea water is forced through a membrane that blocks salt, letting fresh water through.

cards.front: Name the four precautions given in the lesson for handling radioactive sources.
cards.answer: Keep sources in lead-lined containers / Use tongs to handle sources / Wear protective clothing / Minimise exposure time

cards.front: Name the three practical uses of radiation given in the lesson, one for each type.
cards.answer: Gamma: medical tracers and sterilising equipment / Beta: thickness gauges / Alpha: smoke detectors
items: Gamma: medical tracers and sterilising equipment

cards.front: Why does the atomic number decrease by 2 and the mass number decrease by 4 when a nucleus emits an alpha particle?
cards.answer: Because an alpha particle is made of two protons and two neutrons, which are removed from the nucleus.

cards.front: Why does the atomic number increase by 1 when a nucleus emits a beta particle?
cards.answer: Because a neutron in the nucleus turns into a proton, increasing the atomic number by one while mass number stays the same.

cards.front: Besides Noël, Pâques, la fête nationale and Carnaval de Nice, name the four other notable celebrations the lesson mentions.
cards.answer: la fête des Rois (6th January) / la Chandeleur (2nd February) / la fête de la Musique (21st June) / la Toussaint (1st November)
items: la fête de la Musique (21st June)

cards.front: Name the four things families do on the morning of l'Aïd, according to the lesson's example text.
cards.answer: go to the mosque / pray / share a meal / exchange gifts

cards.front: How does the French Easter tradition explain where chocolate eggs come from?
cards.answer: Church bells are said to fly to Rome on Good Friday and return on Easter Sunday, dropping chocolate eggs in gardens for children.

cards.front: How do French people celebrate la fête nationale on 14th July?
cards.answer: There is a military parade on the Champs-Élysées in Paris, fireworks across the country, and people dance in the streets.

cards.front: Name the six key molecules the lesson gives for drawing dot-and-cross diagrams.
cards.answer: Hydrogen (H2) / Hydrogen chloride (HCl) / Water (H2O) / Methane (CH4) / Oxygen (O2) / Carbon dioxide (CO2)

cards.front: What are the four steps for drawing a dot-and-cross diagram?
cards.answer: Write electronic configuration of each atom / Identify electrons needed to fill outer shell / Draw overlapping outer shells with shared electrons / Check each atom has a full outer shell
items: Write electronic configuration of each atom
Identify electrons needed to fill outer shell
Draw overlapping outer shells with shared electrons
Check each atom has a full outer shell

cards.front: Why is graphite used as a lubricant?
cards.answer: Its layers are held together by weak intermolecular forces, so they can slide over each other easily.

cards.front: Why don't simple molecular substances conduct electricity?
cards.answer: They have no free electrons or ions to carry a charge.

title: Peter's Confession, the Transfiguration and Conflicts of Jesus
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three key conflicts of Jesus with the religious authorities given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Healing the paralysed man (forgiving sins) / The Sabbath controversies / The cleansing of the Temple

cards.front: Name the three views the disciples reported when Jesus asked 'Who do people say I am?'
cards.answer: John the Baptist / Elijah / One of the prophets

cards.front: Why did the religious authorities find Jesus's claim to forgive sins so threatening?
cards.answer: Because forgiving sins was something only God could do, so it implied Jesus was claiming divine authority.

cards.front: Why does the Transfiguration show Jesus as the fulfilment of the Law and the Prophets?
cards.answer: Moses represents the Law and Elias represents the Prophets, so their appearance with Jesus shows Israel's scriptures point to him.

cards.front: Name the four processes that drive coastal erosion.
cards.answer: Hydraulic action / Abrasion / Attrition / Solution

cards.front: Name the four factors that shape UK coastal landscapes.
cards.answer: Wave action / Geology / Climate / Human management

cards.front: Why do many UK spits curve at their end?
cards.answer: Secondary wind directions and tidal currents from the estuary mouth bend the growing end of the spit.

cards.front: Why do salt marshes form behind spits?
cards.answer: A spit shelters the water behind it, so waves lose energy and fine sediment settles, letting salt marsh develop.

title: Network Protocols and the TCP/IP Model
subject: computer-science-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four things the lesson says protocols define about communication.
cards.answer: how data is broken into packets / how packets are addressed / how errors are detected / how the two ends signal they've finished
items: how data is broken into packets
how the two ends signal they've finished

cards.front: Why do Ethernet and Wi-Fi both use MAC addresses instead of IP addresses?
cards.answer: They operate at the Link layer, delivering data on the local network, unlike IP addressing which handles routing at the Internet layer.

cards.front: Why is organising the TCP/IP model into layers useful for design?
cards.answer: It keeps the design modular, so a new application protocol can be added without rewriting packet routing, and hardware can change without affecting applications.

cards.front: How does data move through the four TCP/IP layers when it is sent and received?
cards.answer: Sending data passes down Application to Link, each layer adding addressing; receiving data passes back up Link to Application, stripping each layer's information.

title: Religious Experience, Prayer, Design and Cosmological Arguments
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: What three explanations do Atheists and Humanists give for apparently answered prayers?
cards.answer: Coincidence / Confirmation bias (noticing hits, forgetting misses) / The natural course of events

cards.front: Name the four different Christian traditions and their approaches to prayer mentioned in the lesson.
cards.answer: Catholics/Anglicans use set, liturgical prayers / Protestants/evangelicals use informal personal prayer / Pentecostal/charismatic Christians report dramatic healings / Quakers practise silent waiting prayer

cards.front: Why did Hume challenge the cosmological argument's claim that 'every event has a cause'?
cards.answer: Because we only ever observe causation within the universe, not the universe as a whole, so the premise can't be proven by observation.

cards.front: Why do many Christians see fine-tuning as evidence for the design argument?
cards.answer: Because even small changes to the universe's physical constants would make life impossible, which seems to point to intentional design.

title: Indian Wars: Little Crow, Sand Creek and Red Cloud
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three forts the US Army built along the Bozeman Trail in 1866.
cards.answer: Fort Reno / Fort Phil Kearny / Fort C.F. Smith

cards.front: Name the six Indigenous Plains nations the lesson lists as having distinct languages and separate political histories.
cards.answer: Lakota Sioux / Cheyenne / Arapaho / Comanche / Crow / Pawnee

cards.front: Why did the promises of the 1851 Fort Laramie Treaty collapse within a decade?
cards.answer: Settler pressure, gold rushes and broken supply lines undermined the promised annuities and safe passage.

cards.front: How did the Sand Creek Massacre push Red Cloud towards organised armed resistance?
cards.answer: It showed that peaceful treaty arrangements offered no real protection, pushing younger leaders like Red Cloud towards war.

cards.front: Name the four qualities the lesson gives that make Jekyll the embodiment of a Victorian gentleman.
cards.answer: Educated / Charitable / Sociable / Admired by his peers

cards.front: Name the six named characters analysed in this lesson on the novella.
cards.answer: Dr Henry Jekyll / Mr Edward Hyde / Mr Gabriel John Utterson / Dr Hastie Lanyon / Richard Enfield / Poole

cards.front: Why does witnessing Hyde's transformation into Jekyll destroy Lanyon?
cards.answer: Because it violates the boundaries of mainstream, empirical science he trusted, so the revelation itself effectively kills him.

cards.front: Why is Jekyll unable to get rid of Hyde, despite claiming he can whenever he chooses?
cards.answer: Because Hyde is not a separate person but a part of Jekyll himself, so removing Hyde would mean destroying Jekyll.

title: Religious matters: settlement, Catholics and Puritans
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the three groups Puritans split into over how to reform the Church.
cards.answer: Those working for reform inside the Church / Presbyterians who wanted bishops abolished / Separatists who left to form independent congregations
items: Those working for reform inside the Church
Separatists who left to form independent congregations

cards.front: Name the three Catholic-style features the 1559 Settlement kept in church services.
cards.answer: Priests wore vestments / Churches kept altars / Ambiguous wording on communion

cards.front: Why did the 1559 Settlement keep some Catholic-style features in services despite Protestant doctrine?
cards.answer: Elizabeth wanted outward conformity so both Protestants and many Catholics could attend, not enforce inner belief.

cards.front: Why were around 37 London ministers suspended by Archbishop Parker in 1566?
cards.answer: They refused to wear the surplice, the vestment required by the Prayer Book, which Elizabeth ordered enforced.

title: Mains Electricity, Power and the National Grid
subject: separate-sciences-edexcel

cards.front: Why is the live wire in a plug dangerous even when the appliance switch is off?
cards.answer: The live wire stays at about 230 V relative to earth at all times, so touching it drives a current through your body.

cards.front: Why are switches always placed in the live wire rather than the neutral wire?
cards.answer: So that when the switch is open, the appliance and neutral/earth wires are isolated from the high-voltage supply.

cards.front: How does an RCD circuit breaker detect a fault faster than a fuse melts?
cards.answer: It detects tiny imbalances between live and neutral currents, showing leakage to earth, and trips within milliseconds.

cards.front: Give the four voltage levels a step-down transformer sequence reduces mains electricity through before reaching homes.

title: Popular Music: Forms, Hooks and Textures
subject: music-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four types of instrumental backing the lesson gives for melody-and-accompaniment texture in pop.
cards.answer: Block chords / Broken-chord (arpeggiated) pattern / Repeated bass riff (ostinato) / Simple strummed chord loop

cards.front: Name the four exam checklist questions the lesson gives for labelling a pop extract's section.
cards.answer: Is the lyric repeating or changing / Is there a short repeated instrumental idea / Does it build tension or provide contrast / Is the texture thin or thickened
items: Is the lyric repeating or changing
Is there a short repeated instrumental idea
Does it build tension or provide contrast
Is the texture thin or thickened

cards.front: Why does the piano riff in 'Don't Stop Believin'' act as a unifying hook across the whole song?
cards.answer: It recurs as an accompaniment figure under the verses, so it repeats throughout and holds the song together.

cards.front: How does the texture change going into the middle 8 and final chorus in 'Someone Like You'?
cards.answer: Extra instruments and layered backing vocals thicken the texture without ever competing with the lead vocal line.

title: Themes: continuity and change in British entertainment
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the five technologies the lesson gives as step-changes in entertainment access, in order.
cards.answer: Printing press (1476) / Steam railway (1840s) / Cinema (1896) / Radio (1922) / Television (1936)

cards.front: How did religion and changing attitudes shape entertainment across British history?
cards.answer: Religious authority and moral attitudes repeatedly reshaped what leisure was permitted, from Church feast days to Evangelical reform to secularisation ending Sunday trading laws.

cards.front: Why did jousting, falconry and the Grand Tour remain restricted to the wealthy in the medieval and early modern periods?
cards.answer: Access to leisure was shaped by income, so these activities required significant wealth that most people did not have.

title: Context: The Russian Revolution & Orwell's Purpose
subject: english-literature-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three literary levels on which Animal Farm works.
cards.answer: Allegory / Fable / Satire

cards.front: What three causes led to the 1917 Russian revolutions, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Anger over inequality / Food shortages / Russia's catastrophic losses in World War I
items: Russia's catastrophic losses in World War I

cards.front: Why did Stalin win the power struggle against Trotsky after Lenin's death?
cards.answer: Stalin was a cunning political operator who built alliances behind the scenes, while Trotsky was an intellectual focused on spreading world revolution.

cards.front: How did the withdrawal of Animal Farm by Jonathan Cape prove the point Orwell was making?
cards.answer: It showed that even in a democracy, the Ministry of Information could pressure a publisher to silence uncomfortable truths about a powerful ally.

cards.front: Name the three distinctive features that identified a Roman centurion.
cards.answer: Transverse crest on helmet (crista transversa) / Vine stick (vitis) for authority/punishment / Gladius worn on left hip

cards.front: Name the six types of building found in a typical Roman legionary fortress.
cards.answer: Headquarters building (principia) / Commanding officer's house (praetorium) / Barracks blocks / Granaries / Hospital / Bathhouse

cards.front: Why did a legionary's pay and rewards tie his loyalty directly to his general?
cards.answer: Legionaries received salary, campaign booty and land grants from their commanding general, linking their loyalty to him rather than the state.

cards.front: Why did Roman recruits train using weapons heavier than standard issue?
cards.answer: So that when they used their real, lighter weapons in battle, fighting would feel easier by comparison.

cards.front: Name the four propaganda techniques Squealer uses, as identified in the lesson.
cards.answer: Fear / Pseudo-science / Rhetorical questions / Rewriting history

cards.front: How does the pigs' teaching themselves to read and write help them gain power?
cards.answer: It gives them exclusive access to knowledge, letting them exploit the other animals' inability to read.

cards.front: Why do the other animals find Squealer's milk and apples argument 'unanswerable'?
cards.answer: Not because it is logical, but because they cannot articulate a counter-argument and fear Jones's return.

title: Work Done, Elasticity and Hooke's Law
subject: science-aqa

cards.front: Name the steps given for investigating Hooke's law in the required practical.
cards.answer: Hang spring from clamp stand / Measure original length / Add masses one at a time, record new length / Calculate extension by subtracting original length / Plot force-extension graph / Gradient of straight line gives spring constant
items: Add masses one at a time, record new length
Calculate extension by subtracting original length
Gradient of straight line gives spring constant

cards.front: How does a ruler with a pointer (set square) improve the Hooke's law experiment?
cards.answer: It reduces parallax error when measuring the length of the spring.

cards.front: What happens to a spring's force-extension graph and behaviour beyond the limit of proportionality?
cards.answer: The graph curves instead of staying straight, and the spring no longer returns to its original length when the force is removed.

cards.front: What happens to the 200 J of work done pushing a box against friction?
cards.answer: It is transferred to the thermal energy store of the box and floor, warming them slightly.

title: Tea With Our Grandmothers — Warsan Shire
subject: english-literature-ocr

cards.front: The lesson says to learn four things about the poem's 'shape' for the exam. Name them.
cards.answer: Two grandmothers / Three languages / A structure that moves between their stories / The phrase 'tally of surviving'
items: A structure that moves between their stories

cards.front: Name the five other poems in the cluster that the lesson compares Tea With Our Grandmothers to.
cards.answer: Holy Thursday / Baby Song / Prayer / Equilibrium / Theme for English B

cards.front: Why does Shire move between three different languages in Tea With Our Grandmothers?
cards.answer: Because diaspora identity means living inside more than one language and culture at once, which she builds directly into her vocabulary.

cards.front: Why does Shire structure the poem around two grandmothers from opposite ends of the world?
cards.answer: To suggest that survival, ageing and being remembered by the young are universal experiences, not limited to one culture or nationality.

cards.front: Name the four Conflict-cluster themes the lesson says 'Papa-T' explores.
cards.answer: Legacy of empire / Colonised family inheriting an imperial poem / Passing of memory between generations / Tension between obedience and disobedience
items: Colonised family inheriting an imperial poem

cards.front: Name the four poems the lesson compares 'Papa-T' with.
cards.answer: The Destruction of Sennacherib / Colonization in Reverse / Flag / Boat Stealing

cards.front: Why does the grandfather's threat of a 'good lickin' keep the poem's tone warm rather than frightening?
cards.answer: Because the discipline of empire is folded into the discipline of a loving grandfather, making the threat affectionate not menacing.

cards.front: How does D'Aguiar's poem 'talk back' to Tennyson's empire poem rather than simply rejecting it?
cards.answer: It absorbs Tennyson's poem and answers it, letting the grandfather's dialect voice remake the sound of the imperial poem from within.

cards.front: Why does Ralph win the election over Jack in Chapter 1?
cards.answer: The boys vote for his size, attractive appearance, and his holding of the conch, not his competence.

cards.front: Why does Ralph's decision to give Jack control of the choir as hunters matter?
cards.answer: It gives Jack a private army loyal to him rather than the group, planting the seed of later conflict.

cards.front: Why does Piggy call the boys 'a crowd of kids' as the signal fire rages out of control?
cards.answer: Because their excitement and lack of discipline let good intentions become destructive, causing the fire to rage uncontrolled.

cards.front: What three things does Golding highlight about Jack's choir when they first arrive on the island?
cards.answer: Wear black cloaks / Carry a long silver cross each / March in step in two lines / Commanded with arrogance / Forbidden to break formation
items: Carry a long silver cross each
March in step in two lines

cards.front: Name the four local (non-climate) factors that can affect biome distribution.
cards.answer: Altitude / Soil type / Drainage / Rock type

cards.front: Name the three climate factors that shape biome distribution.
cards.answer: Temperature / Precipitation / Sunshine hours

cards.front: Why do tundra plants manage to flower despite the short growing season?
cards.answer: Arctic summers have 24-hour daylight, giving long sunshine hours that let tundra plants flower briefly.

cards.front: Why does cutting down tropical rainforest slow down its own regrowth?
cards.answer: Fewer trees means less transpiration, which reduces local rainfall, which then slows regrowth of the forest.

title: Stalinist economy: collectivisation and Five Year Plans
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: The lesson gives three aims of collectivisation. What were they?
cards.answer: Make agriculture more efficient / Give the state control over food supplies / Free up labour for industrial cities
items: Give the state control over food supplies
Free up labour for industrial cities

cards.front: Why did Stalin believe collectivising agriculture was necessary in 1928?
cards.answer: Independent farmers could hoard grain and resist price controls, so the state needed control of food to feed workers and fund industrialisation.

cards.front: Why did dekulakisation harm Soviet agriculture at the time it needed to improve?
cards.answer: It destroyed the most productive, experienced and capital-owning peasants just as farming most needed their skills.

cards.front: Why did large numbers of women enter Soviet industrial work in the 1930s?
cards.answer: Mainly because of the desperate need for labour in a rapidly industrialising economy, not ideological commitment to equality.

cards.front: Name the four common omissions to look for when comparing a flowchart to its specification.
cards.answer: Missing decision diamond (condition never tested) / Missing output block (action never taken) / Loop arrow pointing to wrong step / Counter that is never reset
items: Loop arrow pointing to wrong step

cards.front: In the worked central heating example, why did the original flowchart waste energy?
cards.answer: It turned the boiler off at any temperature of 18°C or above, instead of running until 21°C as specified.

cards.front: Why can't an engine management system be built using an analogue circuit instead of a microcontroller?
cards.answer: Matching all the sensor variables simultaneously would require an impractically complex analogue circuit.

cards.front: Why do close objects create greater retinal disparity than distant objects?
cards.answer: Because the eyes are set apart, nearby objects produce a larger difference between the two eye images than distant objects do.

cards.front: Why can artists create a convincing sense of depth on a flat painting using linear perspective, relative size and occlusion?
cards.answer: These monocular cues are properties of the light pattern in the scene itself, so they work without needing two eyes or a real 3D scene.

title: Questionnaires, Pilot Studies and Cleaning Data
subject: statistics-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four things a pilot study can catch before the main data collection, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Ambiguous questions / Response categories not exhaustive/mutually exclusive / How long the questionnaire takes / Leading or loaded wording

cards.front: Name the four types of problem the lesson says data cleaning must tackle.
cards.answer: Missing data / Non-responses / Incorrect formats / Extraneous notation or outliers

cards.front: Why must genuine outliers be checked against the original source rather than deleted automatically?
cards.answer: Because they might be real, unusual values rather than errors.

cards.front: Why does asking about sleep on a Monday give different answers to asking mid-week?
cards.answer: Because timing affects responses, as answers change depending on when a question is asked, such as after a weekend.

title: Atman, Samsara and the Purpose of Life
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four stages of life (ashramas) in varnashrama dharma.
cards.answer: Student / Householder / Forest-dweller / Renunciant

cards.front: Name the four realms of rebirth that samsara can span, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Human / Animal / Divine / Hellish

cards.front: Why does a person remain trapped in samsara according to Hindu teaching?
cards.answer: As long as they are driven by desires, attachments and ignorance, they keep generating karma and stay in the cycle of rebirth.

cards.front: How does the cycle of rebirth end and moksha occur?
cards.answer: When all karma is exhausted and the atman recognises its true nature as identical with Brahman or eternally related to Bhagavan, rebirth ends.

title: Feudalism and the Norman Land Settlement
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the four levels of the Norman feudal pyramid, from top to bottom.
cards.answer: King / Tenants-in-chief / Sub-tenants (often knights) / Peasants

cards.front: What four categories of peasant does Domesday Book list?
cards.answer: Villeins / Bordars and cottars / Freemen / Slaves

cards.front: Why could England's small Norman ruling class field thousands of armed knights on demand?
cards.answer: Great honours were sub-divided into dozens or hundreds of knight's fees, each owing fixed military service to its lord.

cards.front: Why did the feudal chain of obligation break down during revolts like 1075 and 1088?
cards.answer: Patronage bound loyalty to landholding, so when that bond snapped at one link the whole chain of obligation shook.

cards.front: Name the three ways Tollington's neighbours react to the racist attack, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Horrified / Indifferent / Sympathetic to Sam

cards.front: How does the Spring Fete change Meena's understanding of racism?
cards.answer: She realises racism isn't just awkward comments or curiosity, but physical, violent danger to her family.

cards.front: Why does Meena's hospital recovery bring her closer to her Punjabi heritage?
cards.answer: Separated from Anita's influence, Meena reconnects with Punjabi stories, food and family instead of chasing Anita's approval.

cards.front: Name the four main categories of renewable technology used in buildings, as covered in this lesson.
cards.answer: Solar / Wind / Heat pumps / Water technologies

cards.front: Name the four water technologies described for reducing mains water use or generating power.
cards.answer: Rainwater harvesting / Grey water re-use / Hydro-generation / Tidal generation

cards.front: Why are heat pumps considered highly efficient?
cards.answer: They move existing heat from a natural source to the building rather than generating heat by burning fuel.

cards.front: Why does a solar thermal system usually still need a backup heating source?
cards.answer: Its output depends on sunshine, so a boiler or immersion heater must top up water temperature in cold or cloudy periods.

cards.front: Name the three things Christopher does as part of his investigation into Wellington's death.
cards.answer: Interviews neighbours methodically / Creates a list of suspects / Reasons about motive and opportunity

cards.front: Why does Christopher keep investigating Wellington's death after Ed tells him to stop?
cards.answer: Not out of defiance, but because he cannot stop applying logic to an unsolved problem.

cards.front: Why does Christopher admire Sherlock Holmes?
cards.answer: Holmes uses logic and deduction rather than emotional intuition, a way of understanding the world Christopher can access.

cards.front: Name the four shocks between 1947 and 1950 that deepened the Red Scare.
cards.answer: Soviet atomic test (August 1949) / 'Loss' of China to Communism (October 1949) / Conviction of Alger Hiss (January 1950) / Start of the Korean War (June 1950)

cards.front: Why did Truman issue the Loyalty Order in March 1947?
cards.answer: He wanted to head off Republican accusations that his administration was 'soft' on Communism.

cards.front: How did J. Edgar Hoover help build public hysteria about Communism before McCarthy?
cards.answer: He fed intelligence on suspected Communists to HUAC and journalists, shaping public anxiety over years.

cards.front: Why did the Alger Hiss case convince many Americans that Communists had infiltrated government?
cards.answer: A senior State Department official was found to have passed secret documents to a Soviet spy, showing infiltration at the highest levels.

cards.front: The lesson names four environmental impacts caused by burning fossil fuels. What are they?
cards.answer: CO2 causing the greenhouse effect and climate change / Sulfur dioxide causing acid rain / Particulates causing respiratory problems / Oil spills damaging marine ecosystems
items: CO2 causing the greenhouse effect and climate change

cards.front: Name the three disadvantages of wind power given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Intermittent (only generates when wind blows) / Visual and noise impact / Can harm birds

cards.front: Why is natural gas sometimes called a 'transition fuel'?
cards.answer: It has about half the carbon footprint of coal per unit of energy, helping countries move towards renewables.

cards.front: How is biomass considered carbon-neutral in theory?
cards.answer: The CO2 absorbed by plants as they grow equals the CO2 released when the biomass is burned.

cards.front: According to the lesson, what three things lured most of the boys to defect to Jack's tribe?
cards.answer: The promise of meat / Excitement / Protection from the beast

cards.front: Why does Golding use sexually violent language to describe the killing of the sow?
cards.answer: To show the hunters are no longer killing for food but for pleasure and dominance.

cards.front: How does Ralph's reaction to Simon's death differ from Piggy's, and why does this matter?
cards.answer: Ralph admits "That was murder" and confronts the horror, while Piggy rationalises it as an accident to protect himself, showing even good characters are complicit.

cards.front: Name the seven characters/character groups and the response to moral crisis each represents in DNA.
cards.answer: Phil - control without conscience / Leah - conscience without action / John Tate - denial / Cathy - sadistic enthusiasm / Richard - discomfort without courage / Adam - dehumanised victim / Mark and Jan - detached narration

cards.front: Why does John Tate's leadership collapse when the group panics after Adam's apparent death?
cards.answer: He relies on denial and intimidation, banning the word 'dead', but controlling language does not control reality, so the group sees he has no plan.

cards.front: How does Kelly show that Cathy was never forced into cruelty by Phil?
cards.answer: Cathy follows Phil's orders with enthusiasm and escalates each act of cruelty herself, showing she was waiting for permission, not coerced.

title: The Position of Women: Flappers and Their Limits
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: According to the lesson, what jobs were 1920s American women concentrated in as 'women's work'?
cards.answer: Secretarial work / Teaching (especially young children) / Nursing / Telephone operating / Retail

cards.front: What factors does the lesson give for why the 19th Amendment passed when it did?
cards.answer: Wyoming gave women the vote in 1869 as a territory / Fifteen states had given women the vote by 1918 / Women's war work in WWI shifted politics / Wilson told the Senate in 1918 it was vital to winning the war
items: Wyoming gave women the vote in 1869 as a territory
Fifteen states had given women the vote by 1918
Women's war work in WWI shifted politics
Wilson told the Senate in 1918 it was vital to winning the war

cards.front: Why did the First World War help persuade politicians to grant women the vote?
cards.answer: Around 25,000 women served as nurses and tens of thousands more did factory work, farming and Red Cross work, proving their contribution and shifting political opinion.

cards.front: Why is the flapper an unreliable image of what life was like for most 1920s American women?
cards.answer: The flapper lifestyle was confined to a small group of young, urban, middle-class white women, while most women were rural, working-class, immigrant or African-American with barely changed lives.

title: Causes of illness and disease over time
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three years the lesson gives for major cholera epidemics in Britain.
What three responses did people use against the Black Death, based on mistaken beliefs?
cards.answer: Burning herbs / Flagellation / Quarantine of towns

cards.front: Why did quarantine accidentally help slow the spread of the Black Death?
cards.answer: It separated infected people from healthy people, reducing contact, even though the real cause (fleas and rats) was unknown.

cards.front: How did killing cats and dogs during the Great Plague possibly make the outbreak worse?
cards.answer: It removed some natural predators of rats, which may have helped the plague spread further.

cards.front: Name the four yugas (ages) in Hindu cosmology, in order.
cards.answer: Satya Yuga / Treta Yuga / Dvapara Yuga / Kali Yuga

cards.front: Name the four main paths of Hindu yoga.
cards.answer: Karma yoga / Jnana yoga / Raja yoga / Bhakti yoga

cards.front: Why does karma explain suffering in Hindu thought?
cards.answer: Because actions performed in previous lives shape a person's present experience, so present suffering results from past karma.

cards.front: Why do worshippers cup their hands over the flame after arti?
cards.answer: To bring the flame's warmth to their faces, symbolising receiving the deity's blessing.

cards.front: Name the four layers of a tropical rainforest, from tallest to shortest.
cards.answer: Emergent layer / Canopy / Understorey / Forest floor

cards.front: Name the five animal adaptations to rainforest life given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Howler monkeys' prehensile tails / Sloths' algae-covered fur for camouflage / Poison dart frogs' bright warning colours / Toucans' huge bills to reach fruit / Jaguars' strong swimming ability
items: Poison dart frogs' bright warning colours
Toucans' huge bills to reach fruit

cards.front: Why does slash-and-burn farming quickly destroy rainforest fertility?
cards.answer: Most nutrients are stored in the living trees, not the soil, so cutting and burning them removes the nutrients entirely.

cards.front: How does cutting down rainforest trees reduce rainfall in the region?
cards.answer: Fewer trees means less transpiration, so less water vapour rises to form clouds, causing less rain and drier conditions.

cards.front: Name the three causes of crime the lesson says many Jews recognise alongside the spiritual dimension.
cards.answer: Poverty / Family breakdown / Lack of moral education

cards.front: Name the three aims of punishment that Jews hold divergent views about.
cards.answer: Retribution / Deterrence / Reformation

cards.front: Why does Isaiah 55:6-8 support restorative justice for offenders?
cards.answer: Because God freely pardons those who turn back to him, so Jews believe offenders should be given the chance to repair harm and rejoin the community.

cards.front: Why do Jews hold divergent views on the death penalty today?
cards.answer: Some see Exodus 21 as justifying it as proportionate retribution for murder, while others follow the Mishnah's caution that courts should rarely execute.

cards.front: Name the four marriages in the novel's resolution.
cards.answer: Elizabeth and Darcy / Jane and Bingley / Charlotte and Collins / Lydia and Wickham

cards.front: What three things does Lady Catherine say Elizabeth lacks?
cards.answer: family / connections / fortune

cards.front: Why does Darcy's secret rescue of Lydia prove his moral transformation is genuine?
cards.answer: He acts out of love, not for public credit, saving the family at great personal cost and asking for nothing in return.

cards.front: Why is Lydia's elopement more than just a romantic subplot?
cards.answer: It is the mechanism that tests whether Darcy's transformation, glimpsed at Pemberley, is genuine.

cards.front: Name the six main factors in material selection the lesson gives.
cards.answer: Functionality / Aesthetics / Availability / Cost / Environmental impact / Social & ethical considerations

cards.front: Name the five material categories the lesson compares for cost.
cards.answer: Timber / Metals / Polymers / Textiles / Papers & boards

cards.front: Why is beech commonly used for kitchen chopping boards?
cards.answer: It is a food-safe, durable hardwood that resists scoring and does not taint food.

cards.front: Why is recycled aluminium seen as a strong environmental choice for drinks cans?
cards.answer: It uses only 5% of the energy needed to produce virgin aluminium.

title: Global Water Insecurity: Surplus, Deficit & Impacts
subject: geography-aqa

cards.front: Name the four impacts of water insecurity described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Waterborne disease and water pollution / Reduced food production / Reduced industrial output / Potential for conflict

cards.front: Name the six factors the lesson gives that affect water availability.
cards.answer: Climate / Geology / Pollution of supply / Over-abstraction / Limited infrastructure / Poverty

cards.front: Why is improving irrigation efficiency seen as the biggest lever for cutting global water demand?
cards.answer: Agriculture uses about 70% of freshwater withdrawals, far more than domestic use, so efficiency gains there cut demand most.

cards.front: Why did Ethiopia's Grand Renaissance Dam create a crisis with Egypt?
cards.answer: Egypt depends on the Nile for about 97% of its fresh water, so filling the dam upstream threatened to reduce its supply.

cards.front: Name the four everyday examples the lesson gives of situations where compression is used.
cards.answer: Streaming music and video / Sending email attachments / Loading images on a web page / Backing up large amounts of data
items: Loading images on a web page
Backing up large amounts of data

cards.front: Name the four benefits the lesson gives of compressing a file.
cards.answer: Downloads and uploads more quickly / Uses less bandwidth / Web pages load sooner / More files fit in an attachment limit or backup drive
items: More files fit in an attachment limit or backup drive

cards.front: How does Huffman coding reduce the number of bits a file needs?
cards.answer: It gives the most common characters the shortest binary codes and rarer characters longer codes, so the file needs fewer bits overall.

cards.front: Why do photographers and musicians keep a lossless master copy instead of only saving a lossy version?
cards.answer: Because lossy compression is not reversible, so re-saving a lossy file repeatedly loses more detail each time.

title: Prison reform: Howard, Fry and the silent and separate systems
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four key proposals John Howard made for prison reform.
cards.answer: Separating different categories of prisoner / Adequate food and healthcare without extortion / Ending the fee system for warders / Ensuring regular inspection
items: Adequate food and healthcare without extortion
Ending the fee system for warders

cards.front: Name the three competing visions of what prison was for in the Victorian debate.
cards.answer: Deterrence / Rehabilitation / Incapacitation

cards.front: Why did transportation shift from America to Australia?
cards.answer: The American Revolution in 1776 ended transportation to the American colonies, causing a prison overcrowding crisis, so Botany Bay was used instead.

cards.front: Why did Pentonville prisoners wear masks when moved between cells?
cards.answer: To prevent recognition between prisoners, keeping them isolated so they could reflect without contamination by other criminals.

title: Cuito Cuanavale, de Klerk and the negotiation begins
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Name the four pressures the lesson gives that pushed de Klerk towards negotiation.
cards.answer: Economic crisis / International isolation / Internal unrest / Failure of 'total strategy' in Angola

cards.front: Why did South Africa's Defence Force get involved in Angola's civil war from the mid-1970s?
cards.answer: It supported UNITA rebels against the Cuban and Soviet-backed MPLA government, as part of its 'total strategy' to prevent a communist state on its border.

cards.front: Why did Mandela insist MK would not surrender its weapons after his release?
cards.answer: He committed the ANC to negotiation but said arms would only be given up once a new democratic constitution was in place.

cards.front: Why do historians describe de Klerk's decision to negotiate as a calculation of survival rather than a conversion to liberalism?
cards.answer: He had been a loyal NP minister, but recognised economic crisis, isolation, unrest and Angola's failure left no viable path except negotiation.

cards.front: Name the four core perspectives GCSE Sociology requires you to know, compare and apply.
cards.answer: Functionalism / Marxism / Feminism / Interactionism

cards.front: Name the three types of feminism described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Liberal feminism / Marxist feminism / Radical feminism

cards.front: Why did Davis and Moore argue that social inequality can serve a functional purpose?
cards.answer: Higher rewards for more demanding roles act as incentives for talented individuals to train for them, filling important positions effectively.

cards.front: Why does Marxist feminism argue women's oppression is tied to capitalism?
cards.answer: Women provide unpaid domestic labour that sustains the workforce, which benefits the capitalist class.

cards.front: Name the three inputs used to control the pick-and-place machine.
cards.answer: Position encoder / Component-present sensor / Placement-complete sensor

cards.front: Name the three outputs used to control the pick-and-place machine.
cards.answer: Vacuum gripper / X-Y positioning motor / Placement actuator

cards.front: Why can't a motor be connected directly to a microcontroller output pin?
cards.answer: The pin only supplies 20–40 mA, far less than a motor draws, so it would damage or destroy the microcontroller.

cards.front: How does a BJT transistor let a microcontroller switch a high-current load?
cards.answer: A small base current from the microcontroller controls a much larger collector-to-emitter current through the load.

title: Customs and Daily Life in German-Speaking Countries
subject: german-aqa

cards.front: Name the five categories Germans sort their rubbish into.
cards.answer: Restmüll (general waste) / Bioabfall (organic waste) / Papier (paper) / Gelber Sack (packaging/plastics) / Glas (glass, sorted by colour)

cards.front: Name the three tracks of the German school system.
cards.answer: Gymnasium (grammar school, leads to Abitur) / Realschule (middle school) / Hauptschule (vocational school)

cards.front: Why are most shops in Germany closed on Sundays?
cards.answer: Because of Sonntagsruhe, a legal requirement for Sunday rest, so only bakeries, petrol stations and some tourist shops can open.

cards.front: How does the Pfand deposit system lead to Germany's high bottle recycling rates?
cards.answer: Customers pay a small deposit on bottles/cans which is refunded when returned, giving recycling rates above 90%.

cards.front: How do you know overflow has occurred when adding two 8-bit binary numbers?
cards.answer: If the addition produces a carry out from the leftmost (most significant) bit, the 8-bit result cannot fit and overflow has occurred.

cards.front: Why do arithmetic and logical right shifts give the same result for a positive number?
cards.answer: A positive number's sign bit is 0, so filling vacated positions with 0 or with a copy of the sign bit is identical.

cards.front: What two things does Mickey discover in the final scene, right before he confronts Eddie?
cards.answer: Eddie is his twin brother / Linda has been seeing Eddie

cards.front: What three 'false stories' does Russell suggest society uses to explain away class inequality?
cards.answer: the myth of meritocracy / the idea poverty is caused by laziness / the belief that the system is fair
items: the idea poverty is caused by laziness
the belief that the system is fair

cards.front: Why does the superstition seem to 'come true' when the twins learn the truth?
cards.answer: Because decades of damage caused by class inequality cannot be undone by a single revelation, not because of supernatural forces.

cards.front: How does the presence of police marksmen deepen Russell's point about the class system?
cards.answer: It suggests the working class are ultimately destroyed by the same institutions that were meant to protect them.

cards.front: Name the four types of grievance that combined to cause the Pilgrimage of Grace.
cards.answer: Religious anger over the dissolution of the monasteries / Fiscal anger at the Subsidy and Statute of Uses / Agrarian protest against rents and enclosures / Northern political resentment of Cromwell and lost autonomy
items: Religious anger over the dissolution of the monasteries
Fiscal anger at the Subsidy and Statute of Uses
Agrarian protest against rents and enclosures
Northern political resentment of Cromwell and lost autonomy

cards.front: What six demands did the Pontefract Articles make in December 1536?
cards.answer: Restore the dissolved monasteries / Repeal the Statute of Uses / Dismiss Cromwell and Cranmer / Condemn heresy / Hold a free Parliament in the north / Recognise Princess Mary as legitimate
items: Hold a free Parliament in the north

cards.front: Why did Robert Aske call the rising a 'pilgrimage' rather than a rebellion?
cards.answer: Because motives among rebels varied, so a religious banner could unite groups with different grievances and mobilise them quickly.

cards.front: How did Bigod's rising give Henry legal cover to crush the Pilgrimage of Grace survivors?
cards.answer: It let Henry rule the first pardon broken by association, justifying martial law and Norfolk's return to punish the rebels.

title: Hosting a Major Sporting Event — Pre-Event & Bidding
subject: cambridge-nationals-sport-studies

cards.front: Name the six criteria a successful Olympic or World Cup bid must address, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Venue and infrastructure / Transport / Security / Accommodation / Legacy planning / Financial viability

cards.front: Name the four pre-event negatives of hosting a major sporting event given in the lesson.
cards.answer: High hosting costs / Displacement of residents / Construction disruption to communities / Political opposition

cards.front: Why are cities becoming increasingly reluctant to enter Olympic bidding races?
cards.answer: Bid campaigns can cost tens of millions of pounds, and cities that lose have spent that money for nothing.

cards.front: Why does infrastructure built for a major event still benefit residents after the event has finished?
cards.answer: New roads, rail lines, airports and broadband built to meet event requirements continue to be used by locals long afterwards.

cards.front: Name the three examples of aerobic activity given in the lesson.
cards.answer: A 10 km run / A long swim / A cycling time trial

cards.front: Name the five recovery methods the lesson describes for after vigorous exercise.
cards.answer: Cool down / Rehydration / Carbohydrate consumption / Ice baths / Massage

cards.front: Why is eating carbohydrates important for recovery after exercise?
cards.answer: It replenishes glycogen stores in the muscles and liver, replacing the glucose fuel broken down during activity.

cards.front: Why is massage particularly valuable for endurance athletes?
cards.answer: They repeatedly use the same muscle groups over long durations, creating chronic tightness that massage relieves by improving circulation and reducing tension.

title: Engagement Patterns in Physical Activity and Sport
subject: physical-education-ocr

cards.front: What four barriers do older adults face in participating in physical activity, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Declining physical capacity / Fewer social networks / Fewer accessible activities / Negative stereotypes about older people

cards.front: Name the four examples of adaptive provision the lesson gives for increasing disabled participation.
cards.answer: Boccia / Sitting volleyball / Goalball / Deaf-friendly coaching

cards.front: Why did grassroots girls' football registrations rise after Beth Mead's hat-trick at the 2022 Women's Euros?
cards.answer: It showed how a visible role model can directly translate into increased grassroots participation among girls.

cards.front: Why are adult women disproportionately affected by caring commitments in relation to sport participation?
cards.answer: Caring responsibilities compete with leisure time, partly explaining why adult women have lower participation in formal sport.

cards.front: Name the four levels of ecosystem organisation, from smallest to largest.
cards.answer: Individual organism / Population (one species) / Community (many species) / Ecosystem (community + abiotic environment)

cards.front: Name the four trophic levels in a food chain, in order.
cards.answer: Producer / Primary consumer (herbivore) / Secondary consumer (carnivore) / Tertiary consumer (top predator)

cards.front: Why did reintroducing wolves to Yellowstone lead to riverside vegetation recovering?
cards.answer: Wolves reduced elk numbers and changed their grazing behaviour, so elk ate less riverside vegetation, allowing it to recover.

cards.front: Why has the introduction of grey squirrels contributed to the decline of red squirrels in the UK?
cards.answer: Grey squirrels are larger and more competitive, so they outcompete red squirrels for the same food sources (interspecific competition).

cards.front: Why does the ascending order of the three prophecies make them so tempting to Macbeth?
cards.answer: It moves from what he already has to what is coming to what seems impossible, so each prediction feels more convincing.

cards.front: How does the natural order idea explain why Macbeth murdering Duncan is so wrong?
cards.answer: Duncan uses organic imagery of planting and growing loyalty, so Macbeth forcing power through violence rejects this natural, patient order.

cards.front: Name the three shallow reasons the poem gives for why the soldier enlisted.
cards.answer: Had drunk a peg after a football match / Told he'd look a god in kilts / Wanted to please his Meg
items: Had drunk a peg after a football match
Told he'd look a god in kilts

cards.front: How does the para-rhyme of 'hymn' and 'him' create meaning in Disabled?
cards.answer: It sounds similar but not identical, setting the boys' happy voices against the broken man and echoing his broken body.

cards.front: Why does Owen set Disabled in a park in the evening rather than on a battlefield?
cards.answer: The ordinary setting shows war's long, quiet aftermath rather than needing a battlefield to show its damage.

cards.front: How does the caesura-heavy ending of Disabled affect the poem's pace?
cards.answer: The repeated question 'Why don't they come?' creates halting pauses that slow the final lines almost to a stop.

cards.front: Name the four things the lesson says St Paul's Cathedral shows about Restoration England.
cards.answer: Disaster / Recovery / The new science / Alliance of Crown and Church

cards.front: Why was Old St Paul's already in poor condition before the Great Fire?
cards.answer: Its spire had been destroyed by lightning in 1561 and never rebuilt, and the nave had been used as cavalry stables under the Commonwealth, leaving the fabric cracked and patched.

cards.front: Why did the clergy reject Wren's Great Model design?
cards.answer: It was a radical centralised church under a dome, too unlike the long nave and choir of English cathedral tradition they insisted on.

cards.front: Why was the coal tax a shrewd way to fund the rebuilding of St Paul's?
cards.answer: It was broad, steady and collected at the port, paid in small amounts by everyone in London who burned coal for heat.

title: Human Life, Ethics and Worship in Buddhism
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: Name the Six Perfections (paramitas) that a Bodhisattva develops, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: generosity / ethics / patience / effort / meditation / wisdom

cards.front: How does metta bhavana meditation develop loving kindness?
cards.answer: It deliberately generates feelings of goodwill, starting with oneself and gradually extending to all beings.

cards.front: Why is tathagatagarbha (Buddha-nature) considered compatible with anatta?
cards.answer: Because Buddha-nature is not a fixed self but a dynamic potential for awakening within beings.

cards.front: Why are mantra recitation and mala beads not the same as praying to a God?
cards.answer: They act as supports for mental training or transformative sacred syllables, not addressing an omnipotent creator deity.

title: Akhand Path, Gurpurbs and Sikh Ceremonies
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: Name the five occasions the lesson gives when the Akhand Path can be performed.
cards.answer: Before and after a birth / At marriages / During gurpurbs / At the start of a new enterprise / During times of difficulty or as respect for the deceased
items: At the start of a new enterprise
During times of difficulty or as respect for the deceased

cards.front: Why do Sikhs light lamps on Divali (Bandi Chhor Divas)?
cards.answer: The people of Amritsar lit the Golden Temple with lamps to welcome home Guru Hargobind after his release from imprisonment.

cards.front: How is the first letter of a child's name chosen at Naam Karan?
cards.answer: A Hukamnama is randomly selected and the first letter of the first word of that hymn gives the child's first letter.

cards.front: Why do Khalsa Sikhs take the surname Singh or Kaur at Amrit Sanskar?
cards.answer: These names abolish caste surnames that marked social position, so all Khalsa Sikhs share one surname expressing equality.

cards.front: Name the three common soldiers Henry meets in disguise before Agincourt.
cards.answer: Williams / Bates / Court

cards.front: In his soliloquy, name the six things Henry says people lay on the king.
cards.answer: Our lives / Our souls / Our debts / Our careful wives / Our children / Our sins

cards.front: Why does Henry order the killing of the French prisoners?
cards.answer: He gives the order on hearing the French have rallied their scattered men, though Gower later cites the killing of the boys as the reason.
